QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.14 Requirements — loss absorption at point of non-viability
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Division 3.2.B Elements of regulatory capital
BANK 3.2.14 Requirements — loss absorption at point of non-viability
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to an additional tier 1 or tier 2 instrument issued by a banking business firm. It sets out additional requirements to ensure loss absorption at the point of non-viability.
(2) The terms and conditions of an instrument must give the Regulatory Authority the discretion to direct that the instrument be written-off or converted to common equity on the happening of a trigger event.
(3) The firm must be able to issue the required number of shares specified in the instrument if a trigger event happens. The issuance of any new shares because of a trigger event must happen before any public sector injection of capital so that capital provided by the public sector is not diluted.
(4) Trigger event, in relation to the firm that issued the instrument, is the earliest of:
(a) a decision of the Regulatory Authority that a write-off (without which the firm would become non-viable) is necessary; and
(b) a decision by the relevant authority in Qatar to make a public sector injection of capital, or give equivalent support (without which injection or support the firm would become non-viable, as determined by that authority).
(5) If the firm is a member of a financial group and the firm wishes the instrument to be included in the group’s capital in addition to its solo capital, the trigger event must be the earliest of:
(a) the decision in subrule (4) (a);
(b) the decision in subrule (4) (b);
(c) a decision, by the relevant authority in the firm’s home jurisdiction, that a write-off (without which the firm would become non-viable) is necessary; and
(d) a decision, by the relevant authority in the jurisdiction of the financial regulator that regulates the parent entity of the firm, to make a public sector injection of capital, or give equivalent support, in that jurisdiction (without which injection or support the firm would become non-viable, as determined by that authority).
(6) Any compensation paid to the holder of an instrument because of a write-off must be paid immediately in the form of common shares (or the equivalent for non-joint-stock companies).
(7) If the firm is a member of a financial group, any common shares paid as compensation to the holder of the instrument must be common shares of the firm or of the parent entity of the group.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.16 Criteria for third party interests — common equity tier 1 capital
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Division 3.2.C Inclusion of third parties’ interests
BANK 3.2.16 Criteria for third party interests — common equity tier 1 capital
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) For rule 3.2.8 (e), a common share, issued by a consolidated subsidiary of a banking business firm and held by a third party as a non-controlling interest, may be included in the firm's CET 1 capital if:
(a) the share would be included in the firm's CET 1 capital had it been issued by the firm; and
(b) the subsidiary that issued the share is itself a deposit-taker or investment dealer (or an equivalent entity in its home jurisdiction).
(2) The amount to be included in the consolidated CET 1 capital of a banking business firm is calculated in accordance with the following formula:

NCI — ((CET1s — Min) × SS)


where:

NCI is the total of the non-controlling interests of third parties in a consolidated subsidiary of the firm.

CET1s is the amount of CET 1 capital of the subsidiary.

Min is the lower of:

(a) 1.07 × (minimum CET 1 capital requirement of the subsidiary); and
(b) 1.07 × (the part of the consolidated minimum CET 1 capital requirement that relates to the subsidiary).
SS means the percentage of the shares in the subsidiary (being shares included in CET 1 capital) held by those third parties.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2015-3 (as from 1st January 2016).

(1) For rule 3.2.10(c), an instrument (including a common share) issued by a consolidated subsidiary of a banking business firm and held by a third party as a non-controlling interest may be included in the firm's additional tier 1 capital if the instrument would be included in the firm's additional tier 1 capital had it been issued by the firm.

Note Any amount already included in CET 1 capital must not be included in additional tier 1 capital — see rule 3.2.10(c).
(2) The amount to be included in the consolidated additional tier 1 capital of a banking business firm is calculated in accordance with the following formula:

NCI — ((T1s — Min) × SS)

where:

NCI is the total of the non-controlling interests of third parties in a consolidated subsidiary of the firm.

T1s is the amount of additional tier 1 capital of the subsidiary.

Min is the lower of:

(a) 1.07 × (minimum additional tier 1 capital requirement of the subsidiary); and
(b) 1.07 × (the part of the consolidated minimum additional tier 1 capital requirement that relates to the subsidiary).
SS means the percentage of the shares in the subsidiary (being shares included in additional tier 1 capital) held by those third parties.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.18 Criteria for third party interests — tier 2 capital
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Division 3.2.C Inclusion of third parties’ interests
BANK 3.2.18 Criteria for third party interests — tier 2 capital
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) For rule 3.2.12 (c), an instrument (including a common share and any other tier 1 capital instrument) issued by a consolidated subsidiary of a banking business firm and held by a third party as a non-controlling interest may be included in the firm's tier 2 capital if the instrument would be included in the firm's tier 2 capital had it been issued by the firm.

Note Any amount already included in CET 1 capital or additional tier 1 capital must not be included in tier 2 capital — see rule 3.2.12 (c).
(2) The amount to be included in the consolidated tier 2 capital of a banking business firm is calculated in accordance with the following formula:

NCI — ((T2s — Min) × SS)

where:

NCI is the total of the non-controlling interests of third parties in a consolidated subsidiary of the firm.

T2s is the amount of tier 2 capital of the subsidiary.

Min is the lower of:

(a) 1.07 × (minimum tier 2 capital requirement of the subsidiary); and
(b) 1.07 × (the part of the consolidated minimum tier 2 capital requirement that relates to the subsidiary).
SS means the percentage of the shares in the subsidiary (being shares included in tier 2 capital) held by those third parties.

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.19 Treatment of third party interests from special purpose vehicles
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Division 3.2.C Inclusion of third parties’ interests
BANK 3.2.19 Treatment of third party interests from special purpose vehicles
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) An instrument issued out of a special purpose vehicle and held by a third party must not be included in a banking business firm's CET 1 capital. Such an instrument may be included in the firm's additional tier 1 or tier 2 capital (and treated as if it had been issued by the firm itself directly to the third party), if:
(a) the instrument satisfies the criteria for inclusion in the relevant category of regulatory capital; and
(b) the only asset of the special purpose vehicle is its investment in the capital of the firm and that investment satisfies the criterion in rule 3.2.11(16) or 3.2.13(11) for the immediate availability of the proceeds.
(2) An instrument described in subrule (1) that is issued out of a special purpose vehicle through a consolidated subsidiary of a banking business firm may be included in the firm's consolidated additional tier 1 or tier 2 capital if the instrument satisfies the criteria in rule 3.2.17 or 3.2.18, as the case requires. Such an instrument is treated as if it had been issued by the subsidiary itself directly to the third party.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).

BANK 3.2.21 Approach to valuation for regulatory adjustment

A banking business firm must use the same approach for valuing regulatory adjustments to its capital as it does for balance-sheet valuations. An item that is deducted from capital must be valued in the same way as it would be for inclusion in the firm’s balance sheet.

BANK 3.2.23 How adjustments are to be made
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
A regulatory adjustment to a banking business firm’s regulatory capital may be either a deduction from that capital or the derecognition of an item for the calculation of the capital.

Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.24 Corresponding deduction approach
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Subdivision 3.2.D.2 Adjustments to common equity tier 1 capital
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
If this Division requires a deduction to be made using the corresponding deduction approach, a banking business firm must make the deduction from the category of regulatory capital that the holding would qualify as if the firm itself had issued the relevant instrument (or, if the firm does not have sufficient regulatory capital in that category, from the next higher category). For that purpose, CET 1 capital is the highest category of regulatory capital, additional tier 1 capital is the next highest, and tier 2 is the lowest.

Note    For these rules, the 3 categories of regulatory capital are CET 1 capital, additional tier 1 capital and tier 2 capital — see rule 3.2.7 (4).

Amended by QFCRA RM/2015-3 (as from 1st January 2016).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.25 Goodwill and intangible assets
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Subdivision 3.2.D.2 Adjustments to common equity tier 1 capital
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
A banking business firm must deduct, from its CET 1 capital, the amount of its goodwill and other intangible assets (except mortgage servicing rights). The amount must be net of any related deferred tax liability that would be extinguished if the goodwill or assets become impaired or derecognised under IFRS or any other relevant accounting standards.

Note    For the treatment of mortgage servicing rights, see rule 3.2.36.

Amended by QFCRA RM/2015-3 (as from 1st January 2016).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.26 Deferred tax assets that rely on future profitability
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Subdivision 3.2.D.2 Adjustments to common equity tier 1 capital
BANK 3.2.26 Deferred tax assets that rely on future profitability
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to deferred tax assets of a banking business firm if the assets depend on the future profitability of the firm to be realised, but does not apply to such assets that relate to temporary differences.
(2) For each deferred tax asset to which this rule applies, the firm must deduct, from its CET 1 capital, the full amount of the asset net of any deferred tax liability that may be netted against it under subrules (3) to (5).
(3) A deferred tax asset may be netted against a deferred tax liability only if:
(a) the asset and the liability relate to taxes levied by the same taxation authority; and
(b) that authority explicitly permits offsetting.
(4) A deferred tax liability must not be used for netting if it has already been netted against a deduction of goodwill or other intangible assets, or defined benefit pension assets.
(5) A deferred tax liability that may be netted must be allocated pro rata between deferred tax assets deducted under this rule and those to which the treatment in rule 3.2.36 is applied.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.30 Gains and losses from changes to own credit risk
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Subdivision 3.2.D.2 Adjustments to common equity tier 1 capital
BANK 3.2.30 Gains and losses from changes to own credit risk
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) In the calculation of a banking business firm’s CET 1 capital:
(a) the firm must derecognise all unrealised gains and unrealised losses that have resulted from changes in the fair value of liabilities because of changes in the firm’s own credit risk; and
(b) in relation to derivative liabilities, the firm must derecognise all accounting valuation adjustments that arise from the firm’s own credit risk.
(2) The firm must not offset valuation adjustments that arise from the firm’s own credit risk against such adjustments that arise from its counterparties’ credit risk.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.31 Defined benefit pension fund assets
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Subdivision 3.2.D.2 Adjustments to common equity tier 1 capital
BANK 3.2.31 Defined benefit pension fund assets
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must deduct, from its CET 1 capital, the amount of a defined benefit pension fund that is an asset on the firm’s balance sheet. The amount must be net of any related deferred tax liability that would be extinguished if the asset were to become impaired or derecognised under IFRS or any other relevant accounting standards.
(2) The firm may apply to the Regulatory Authority for approval to offset from the deduction any asset in the fund to which the firm has unrestricted and unfettered access. Such an asset must be assigned the risk-weight that would be assigned to it if it were owned directly by the firm.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.32 Investments in own shares and capital instruments
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Subdivision 3.2.D.2 Adjustments to common equity tier 1 capital
BANK 3.2.32 Investments in own shares and capital instruments
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must deduct, from its CET 1 capital, any investment in its own common shares or own capital instruments (except instruments that have been derecognised under IFRS or any other relevant accounting standards). The firm must also deduct any of its own common shares or instruments that it is contractually obliged to purchase.
Note For the meaning of investment, see rule 3.2.22. In this rule (and elsewhere in this Division), investment includes an indirect or synthetic holding.
(2) The firm must apply the corresponding deduction approach to make the deductions required by this rule.
Note For the corresponding deduction approach, see rule 3.2.24.
(3) For this rule, a gross long position may be deducted net of a short position in the same underlying exposure only if the short position involves no counterparty risk.
(4) For this rule, the firm must look through its holdings of index securities to determine its exposures to its own shares. However, if the firm finds it operationally burdensome to look through those holdings and monitor its exact exposure to its own shares, the firm may use a conservative estimate of such exposures if the Regulatory Authority so approves.
(5) The firm may net a gross long position in its own shares resulting from a holding of index securities against a short position in those shares resulting from a short position in the same underlying index if the maturity of the short position matches the maturity of the long position.
Guidance
In such cases, the short positions may involve counterparty credit risk (which will be subject to the relevant counterparty credit risk charge).
(6) This rule applies to an investment whether it is held in the firm’s banking book or trading book.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.content_text: (1) A banking business firm must deduct, from its CET 1 capital, any investment in its own common shares or own capital instruments (except instruments that have been derecognised under IFRS or any other relevant accounting standards). The firm must also deduct any of its own common shares or instruments that it is contractually obliged to purchase. Note For the meaning of investment , see rule 3.2.22 . In this rule (and elsewhere in this Division), investment includes an indirect or synthetic holding. (2) The firm must apply the corresponding deduction approach to make the deductions required by this rule. Note For the corresponding deduction approach, see rule 3.2.24 . (3) For this rule, a gross long position may be deducted net of a short position in the same underlying exposure only if the short position involves no counterparty risk. (4) For this rule, the firm must look through its holdings of index securities to determine its exposures to its own shares. However, if the firm finds it operationally burdensome to look through those holdings and monitor its exact exposure to its own shares, the firm may use a conservative estimate of such exposures if the Regulatory Authority so approves. (5) The firm may net a gross long position in its own shares resulting from a holding of index securities against a short position in those shares resulting from a short position in the same underlying index if the maturity of the short position matches the maturity of the long position. Guidance In such cases, the short positions may involve counterparty credit risk (which will be subject to the relevant counterparty credit risk charge). (6) This rule applies to an investment whether it is held in the firm’s banking book or trading book. Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015). Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.33 Treatment of reciprocal cross-holdings in banking, financial and insurance entities
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Subdivision 3.2.D.2 Adjustments to common equity tier 1 capital
BANK 3.2.33 Treatment of reciprocal cross-holdings in banking, financial and insurance entities
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must deduct, from its regulatory capital, reciprocal cross-holdings in the shares (or other instruments that qualify as capital) of a banking, financial or insurance entity if the firm’s holding has the effect of artificially inflating the firm’s capital position.
Guidance
The firm should seek guidance from the Regulatory Authority as to whether an entity is a financial entity. However, a financial entity might be involved in (for example) financial leasing, issuing credit cards, portfolio management, investment advisory, custodial and safekeeping services and other similar activities that are ancillary to the business of banking.
(2) The firm must apply the corresponding deduction approach to make the deductions required by this rule.
Note For the corresponding deduction approach, see rule 3.2.24.
(3) For this rule, the provision by a banking business firm of support, by way of a guarantee or some other capital enhancement, to such an entity is to be treated as an investment by the firm in the entity.

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.34 Non-significant investments in unconsolidated banking, financial or insurance entities
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Subdivision 3.2.D.3 Deductions from categories of regulatory capital
BANK 3.2.34 Non-significant investments in unconsolidated banking, financial or insurance entities
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to an investment by a banking business firm in the capital of a banking, financial or insurance entity that is outside the scope of regulatory consolidation, if the investment is not a significant investment.

Note For the meaning of financial entity, see rule 3.2.33 (1), guidance.

(2) For this rule and rules 3.2.35 and 3.2.36, significant investment means:

(a) an investment representing more than 10% of the issued common shares, or other instruments that qualify as capital, of the entity; or
(b) if the entity is affiliated with the firm, an investment representing any amount of the issued common shares, or other instruments that qualify as capital, of the entity.
Note For the meaning of affiliated, see subrule (10) (b).
(3) For this rule, the firm must look through its holdings of index securities to determine its exposures to such instruments. However, if the firm finds it operationally burdensome to look through those holdings and monitor its exact exposure to such instruments, the firm may use a conservative estimate of such exposures if the Regulatory Authority so approves.
(4) Underwriting positions held for longer than 5 business days must be included in the investments to be deducted. Underwriting positions held for 5 business days or less must be excluded.
(5) The amount to be deducted is the firm’s net long position in the relevant investments (that is, the gross long position net of any short position in the same underlying exposure, if the maturity of the short position either matches the maturity of the long position or has a residual maturity of at least 1 year). The firm may also net gross long positions arising through holdings of index securities against short positions in the same underlying index if the maturity of the short position either matches the maturity of the long position or has a residual maturity of at least 1 year.
Guidance
In such cases, the short positions may involve counterparty credit risk (which will be subject to the relevant counterparty credit risk charge).

(6) If the total of all such holdings, in aggregate and on a net long basis, is more than 10% of the firm’s CET 1 capital (after applying all the adjustments required by rules 3.2.25 to 3.2.33), the amount to be deducted from each category of the firm’s regulatory capital is to be calculated as follows:

(a) the total amount to be deducted under this rule is the excess amount (that is, the amount by which the total of all such holdings, in aggregate and on a net long basis, is more than 10% of the firm’s CET 1 capital, after applying all the adjustments required by rules 3.2.25 to 3.2.33);
(b) the amount to be deducted from the firm’s CET 1 capital is the excess amount multiplied by the percentage of the holding that is made up of instruments that would qualify as CET 1 capital if issued by the firm itself;
(c) the amount to be deducted from the firm’s additional tier 1 capital is the excess amount multiplied by the percentage of the holding that is made up of instruments that would qualify as additional tier 1 capital if issued by the firm itself;
(d) the amount to be deducted from the firm’s tier 2 capital is the excess amount multiplied by the percentage of the holding that is made up of instruments that would qualify as tier 2 capital if issued by the firm itself;
(e) if the firm does not have enough of a particular category of regulatory capital to make a deduction required by any of paragraphs (b) to (d), the deduction must be made from the next higher category of regulatory capital.

(7) Any amount of a holding to which this rule applies that is not deducted from regulatory capital must be risk-weighted.

Note For the risk-weighting of such holdings, see Part 4.4 (standardised approach to credit risk) for amounts held in the banking book and Part 6.5 (market risk, traded equity positions) for amounts held in the trading book
(8) This rule applies to an investment whether it is held in the firm’s banking book or trading book.
(9) With the Regulatory Authority’s prior written approval, the firm may exclude from the deductions, for a period specified by the Authority, investments made in the course of resolving a distressed institution or providing financial assistance to reorganise such an institution.

(10) For subrule (2):

(a) the definition of affiliate in the Glossary does not apply;

(b) an entity is affiliated with a banking business firm if:

(i) the firm controls the entity;
(ii) the entity controls the firm; or
(iii) the firm and the entity are under common control; and
(c) control has the meaning given by the applicable accounting standard.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2015-3 (as from 1st January 2016).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2024-1 (as from 1st July 2024).

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.35 Significant investments in unconsolidated banking, financial or insurance entities
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Subdivision 3.2.D.3 Deductions from categories of regulatory capital
BANK 3.2.35 Significant investments in unconsolidated banking, financial or insurance entities
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) This rule applies in relation to a significant investment by a banking business firm in the capital of a banking, financial or insurance entity that is outside the scope of regulatory consolidation.

Note For the meaning of financial entity, see rule 3.2.33 (1), guidance.
(2) Underwriting positions held for longer than 5 business days must be included in the investments to be deducted. Underwriting positions held for 5 business days or less must be excluded.
(3) For this rule, the firm must look through its holdings of index securities to determine its exposures to such instruments. However, if the firm finds it operationally burdensome to look through those holdings and monitor its exact exposure to such instruments, the firm may use a conservative estimate of such exposures if the Regulatory Authority so approves.

(4) The total, on a net long basis, of all such holdings that are not common shares is to be deducted from the firm’s regulatory capital. The amount to be deducted from each category of that capital is to be calculated as follows:

(a) the amount to be deducted from the firm’s CET 1 capital is the total amount of the holding multiplied by the percentage of the holding that is made up of instruments that would qualify as CET 1 capital if issued by the firm itself;
(b) the amount to be deducted from the firm’s additional tier 1 capital is the total amount of the holding multiplied by the percentage of the holding that is made up of instruments that would qualify as additional tier 1 capital if issued by the firm itself;
(c) the amount to be deducted from the firm’s tier 2 capital is the total amount of the holding multiplied by the percentage of the holding that is made up of instruments that would qualify as tier 2 capital if issued by the firm itself;
(d) if the firm does not have enough of a particular category of regulatory capital to make a deduction required by any of paragraphs (a) to (c), the deduction must be made from the next higher category of regulatory capital.
(5) The total, on a net long basis, of all such holdings that are common shares are subject to recognition up to a threshold and deduction above the threshold in accordance with rule 3.2.36.
(6) For this rule and rule 3.2.36, a capital instrument issued by the entity must be treated as common shares if the instrument would not meet the criteria for CET 1 capital, additional tier 1 capital or tier 2 capital if issued by the firm itself.

(7) Any amount of a holding to which this rule applies that is not deducted from regulatory capital must be risk-weighted.

Note For the risk-weighting of such holdings, see Part 4.4 (standardised approach to credit risk) for amounts held in the banking book and Part 6.5 (market risk, traded equity positions) for amounts held in the trading book.
(8) This rule applies to an investment whether it is held in the firm’s banking book or trading book.
(9) With the Regulatory Authority’s prior written approval, the firm may exclude from the deductions, for a period specified by the Authority, investments made in the course of resolving a distressed institution or providing financial assistance to reorganise such an institution.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2024-1 (as from 1st July 2024).

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.36 Threshold deductions
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Subdivision 3.2.D.3 Deductions from categories of regulatory capital
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to the following kinds of asset:

(a) a significant investment in the common shares of a banking, financial or insurance entity that is outside the scope of regulatory consolidation;
(b) mortgage servicing rights;

(c) deferred tax assets that arise from temporary differences (for example, allowance for credit losses).

Note For the treatment of other deferred tax assets, see rule 3.2.26.
(2) When a banking business firm calculates its CET 1 capital, the firm may recognise each kind of asset to which this rule applies only up to 10% of the firm’s CET 1 capital (calculated after applying all other adjustments) but this is subject to subrule (4).
(3) The firm must deduct, from its CET 1 capital, the amount by which any of the 3 kinds of asset exceeds 10% of its CET 1 capital (after applying all the other regulatory adjustments required to its CET 1 capital).
(4) When a banking business firm calculates its CET 1 capital, the firm may recognise the total of all 3 kinds of assets to which this rule applies only up to 15% of the firm’s CET 1 capital (calculated after applying all other adjustment including limiting the recognition of any kind of those assets to 10% of the firm’s CET 1 capital).

(5) The firm must deduct, from its CET 1 capital, the amount by which the total of the 3 kinds of asset (after any limitation applied under subrule (2)) exceeds 15% of its CET 1 capital (after applying all the other regulatory adjustments required to its CET 1 capital).

Note 1 Any amount of such assets that is not deducted from CET 1 capital must be risk-weighted at 250% — see rule 4.4.86.
Note 2 For the general treatment of investments in unconsolidated banking, financial or insurance entities, see rules 3.2.34 and 3.2.35.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2024-1 (as from 1st July 2024).

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.37 Higher capital requirement imposed on overseas branch
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Subdivision 3.2.D.3 Deductions from categories of regulatory capital
BANK 3.2.37 Higher capital requirement imposed on overseas branch
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) If a banking business firm has an overseas branch, the firm must deduct, from its CET 1 capital, any capital requirement imposed on the branch by:
(a) the Regulatory Authority; or
(b) the financial regulator in the jurisdiction in which the branch is located.
(2) If both the Authority and the other financial regulator impose such a requirement, the firm must deduct the higher of the 2 requirements from its CET 1 capital.
(3) Subrules (1) and (2) do not apply if the overseas branch is included in the firm’s consolidated returns.
(4) Despite subrule (3), if the financial regulator in the jurisdiction in which an overseas branch of a banking business firm is located imposes a capital requirement on the branch, the firm must deduct, from its CET 1 capital, the amount of any shortfall between the actual capital held by the branch and that capital requirement.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2015-3 (as from 1st January 2016).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.38 Certain exposures protected by guarantees or credit derivatives
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Subdivision 3.2.D.3 Deductions from categories of regulatory capital
BANK 3.2.38 Certain exposures protected by guarantees or credit derivatives
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
If an exposure of a banking business firm is covered by an eligible guarantee or eligible credit derivative, but the coverage is subject to a materiality threshold (below which the protection provider is not obliged to pay on the occurrence of a credit event), the firm must deduct, from its CET 1 capital, so much of the exposure as is below the threshold.

Guidance

A guarantee by a banking business firm’s parent entity may be an eligible guarantee if the parent entity is an eligible guarantor — see rules 4.5.26 and 4.5.27.

Note Eligible guarantee is defined in rule 4.5.27. Eligible credit derivative is defined in rule 4.5.34.

Amended by QFCRA RM/2015-1 (as from 1st July 2015).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.39 Excesses of large exposures
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK Subdivision 3.2.D.3 Deductions from categories of regulatory capital
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
If a banking business firm has breached a large exposure limit (see rule 5.2.9), then, unless the Regulatory Authority has given approval for the excess, the firm must either:

(a) obtain eligible collateral (in accordance with either the simple approach or the comprehensive approach) for the amount by which the limit was exceeded; or
Note For eligible collateral in the simple approach, see rule 4.5.12; for eligible collateral in the comprehensive approach, see rule 4.5.12.
(b) deduct that amount from its CET 1 capital.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2015-3 (as from 1st January 2016).

BANK 3.2.40 Firms may use estimates or exclude deductions
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) If it is impractical for a banking business firm to examine and monitor the firm's exposures to the capital of entities concerned (including through holdings of indexed securities), the firm may apply to the Regulatory Authority for approval to use an estimate of such exposures. The authority will grant such an approval only after the firm satisfies the authority that the estimate is conservative, well-founded and reasonable.
(2) A banking business firm may also apply to the Regulatory Authority for approval not to deduct an investment made to resolve, or provide financial assistance to reorganise, a distressed entity.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2015-3 (as from 1st January 2016).

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.2.41 Deductions from common equity tier 1 capital
doc_path: BANK Part 3.2 Initial and ongoing capital requirements
BANK 3.2.41 Deductions from common equity tier 1 capital
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) In addition to the other deductions to CET 1 capital under this Chapter, deductions may be required to CET 1 capital under the threshold deduction rule.
(2) The threshold deduction rule provides recognition for particular assets that are considered to have some limited capacity to absorb losses. The following items come within the threshold deduction rule:
(a) significant investments in the common shares, or other instruments that qualify as CET 1 capital, of an unconsolidated entity concerned;
(b) mortgage servicing rights;
(c) deferred tax assets that relate to temporary differences (for example, allowance for credit losses).
(3) Instead of full deduction, the items that come within the threshold deduction rule receive limited recognition when calculating CET 1 capital. The total of each of the items in subrule (2) do not require adjustment from CET 1 capital and are risk-weighted at 300% (for items listed on a recognised exchange) or 400% (for items not so listed) provided that:
(a) each item is no more than 10% of the firm's CET 1 capital (net of all regulatory adjustments except those under this Subdivision); or
(b) in total, the 3 items are no more than 15% of the firm's CET 1 capital (net of all regulatory adjustments except those under this Subdivision).
(4) A banking business firm must deduct from CET 1 capital any amount in excess of the threshold in subrule (3)(a) or (b).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2015-3 (as from 1st January 2016).

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK Part 3.3 Capital buffers and other requirements
doc_path: BANK Part 3.3 Capital buffers and other requirements
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.content_text: BANK Part 3.3 Capital buffers and other requirements

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.3.1 Introduction
doc_path: BANK Part 3.3 Capital buffers and other requirements
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) The capital adequacy framework contains 2 additional measures for conserving capital through the capital conservation buffer and the counter-cyclical capital buffer.
(2) The capital conservation buffer promotes the conservation of capital and the build-up of a buffer above the minimum in times of economic growth and credit expansion, so that the buffer can be drawn down in periods of stress. It imposes an obligation to restrict a firm's distributions when capital falls below the capital conservation buffer minimum.
(3) The counter-cyclical capital buffer is a macroprudential tool that can be used to mitigate the build-up of a system-wide risk such as excess aggregate credit growth. It is intended to ensure that the banking system has a buffer of capital to protect it against future potential losses.
(4) These 2 buffers and other requirements on capital are set out in this Part.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2015-3 (as from 1st January 2016).

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.3.2 Capital conservation buffer
doc_path: BANK Part 3.3 Capital buffers and other requirements
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm whose risk-based capital requirement is higher than its base capital requirement must maintain a minimum capital conservation buffer of:
(a) 2.5% of the firm's total risk-weighted assets; or
(b) a higher amount that the Regulatory Authority may, by written notice, set from time to time.
(2) A firm's capital conservation buffer must be made up of CET 1 capital above the amounts used to meet the firm's CET 1 capital ratio, tier 1 capital ratio and regulatory capital ratio in rule 3.2.6(2).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.3.3 Capital conservation ratios
doc_path: BANK Part 3.3 Capital buffers and other requirements
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) If a banking business firm's capital conservation buffer falls below the required minimum, the firm must immediately conserve its capital by restricting its distributions.

Note A payment made by a firm that does not reduce its CET 1 capital is not a distribution for the purposes of this Part. Distributions include, for example, dividends, share buybacks and discretionary bonus payments.
(2) This rule sets out, in column 3 of table 3.3.3, the minimum capital conservation ratios for banking business firms that are required to maintain a capital conservation buffer. Capital conservation ratio is the percentage of earnings that a firm must not distribute if its CET 1 capital ratio falls within the corresponding ratio in column 2 of that table.
(3) Earnings means distributable profits calculated before deducting elements subject to the restrictions on distributions. Earnings must be calculated after notionally deducting the tax that would have been payable had none of the distributable items been paid.

Note The effect of calculating earnings after tax is that the tax consequence of the distribution is reversed out.
(4) A banking business firm must have adequate systems and controls to ensure that the amount of distributable profits and maximum distributable amount are calculated accurately. The firm must be able to demonstrate that accuracy if directed by the Regulatory Authority.
(5) If the firm is a member of a financial group, the capital conservation buffer applies at group level.

Table 3.3.3 Minimum capital conservation ratios

column 1 item column 2 CET1 capital ratio column 3 minimum capital conservation ratio (% of earnings)
1 4.5% to 5.125% 100
2 > 5.125% to 5.75% 80
3 > 5.75% to 6.375% 60
4 > 6.375% to 7.0% 40
5 >7% 0



Examples of application of table

Assume that a firm's minimum CET 1 capital ratio is 4.5% and an additional 2.5% capital conservation buffer (which must be made up of CET 1 capital) is required for a total of 7% CET 1 capital ratio. Based on table 3.3.3:

1 If a firm's CET 1 capital ratio is 4.5% or more but less than 5.125%, the firm needs to conserve 100% of its earnings.
2 If a firm's CET 1 capital ratio is 5.125% or more but less than 5.75%, the firm needs to conserve 80% of its earnings and must not distribute more than 20% of those earnings by way of dividends, share buybacks and discretionary bonus payments.
3 A firm with a CET 1 capital ratio of more than 7% can distribute 100% of its earnings.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2018-1 (as from 1st May 2018).

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.3.4 Powers of Regulatory Authority
doc_path: BANK Part 3.3 Capital buffers and other requirements
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) The Regulatory Authority may impose a restriction on capital distributions by a firm even if the amount of the firm’s CET 1 capital is greater than its CET 1 capital ratio and required capital conservation buffer.
(2) The Regulatory Authority may, by written notice, impose a limit on the period during which a banking business firm may operate within a specified capital conservation ratio.
(3) A banking business firm may apply to the Regulatory Authority to make a distribution in excess of a limit imposed by this Part. The authority will grant approval only if it is satisfied that the firm has appropriate measures to raise capital equal to, or greater than, the amount the firm wishes to distribute above the limit.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.3.5 Counter-cyclical capital buffer
doc_path: BANK Part 3.3 Capital buffers and other requirements
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) If imposed by the Regulatory Authority, the counter-cyclical capital buffer would require a firm to have additional CET 1 capital against possible future losses from system-wide risks such as excess credit growth.
(2) The Regulatory Authority may, by written notice, require banking business firms to have additional CET 1 capital as a counter-cyclical capital buffer. The buffer set by the authority will not exceed 2.5% of total risk-weighted assets.
(3) The Regulatory Authority will notify banking business firms of any decision to set, or increase, a counter-cyclical capital buffer within a reasonable period of not more than 1 year before the date when the decision takes effect. However, a decision to remove or decrease a counter-cyclical capital buffer will take effect immediately.
(4) If a counter-cyclical capital buffer applies to a firm, the capital conservation ratios (and capital distribution restrictions) in rule 3.3.3 apply to the firm as if its minimum capital conservation buffer were increased by the amount of the counter-cyclical capital buffer.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2015-3 (as from 1st January 2016).

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.3.6 Capital reductions
doc_path: BANK Part 3.3 Capital buffers and other requirements
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must not reduce its capital and reserves without the Regulatory Authority's written approval.

Examples of ways to reduce capital
•   a share buyback or the redemption, repurchase or repayment of capital instruments issued by the firm
•   trading in the firm's own shares or capital instruments outside an arrangement agreed with the authority
•   a special dividend.
(2) A banking business firm planning a reduction must prepare a forecast (for at least 2 years) showing its projected capital after the reduction. The firm must satisfy the authority that the firm's capital will still comply with these rules after the reduction.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 3.3.7 Authority can require other matters
doc_path: BANK Part 3.3 Capital buffers and other requirements
BANK 3.3.7 Authority can require other matters
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
Despite anything in these rules, the Regulatory Authority may require a banking business firm to have capital resources, comply with any other capital requirement or use a different approach to, or method for, capital management. The authority may also require a firm to carry out stress-testing at any time.

Note Under FSR, article 16, the Regulatory Authority may modify or waive the application of a prudential requirement to an authorised firm or firms.

Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.1.1 Introduction
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) This Chapter sets out the requirements for a banking business firm’s credit risk management policy and practice (including credit risk assessments and the use of ratings from ECRAs) to implement the risk-based framework for capital adequacy and the early identification and management of problem assets.
(2) This Chapter also deals with the following means to determine regulatory capital and control or mitigate credit risk:
(a) the standardised approach for calculating the firm’s credit risk capital requirement;
Note The standardised approach was previously called the risk-weighted assets approach.
(b) CRM techniques;
(c) provisioning.
(3) To guard against abuses and to address conflicts of interest, this Chapter requires transactions with related parties to be at arm’s length.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.1.2 Meaning of credit risk
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
Credit risk is:

(a) the risk of default by a counterparty; and
(b) the risk that an asset will lose value because its credit quality has deteriorated.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.1.2 Guidance
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
Credit risk may result from exposures on or off the balance sheet, including loans and advances, investments, inter-bank lending, derivative transactions, SFTs and trading activities. It can exist in both the trading book and the banking book.

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.1.3 General requirements — management of credit risk and problem assets
doc_path: BANK 4.1.3 General requirements — management of credit risk and problem assets
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must manage credit risk by adopting a prudent credit risk management policy that allows its credit risk to be identified, measured, evaluated, managed and controlled or mitigated.
(2) The policy must also provide for problem assets to be recognised, measured and reported. The policy must set out the factors that must be taken into account in identifying problem assets.
Note 1 For the full requirements as to the firm’s credit risk management policy, see Part 4.2.
Note 2 Additional risk management requirements apply to banking business firms’ exposures to central counterparties — see rules 4.6A.40 and 4.6A.41.
(3) Problem assets includes non-performing assets (see rule 4.7.10) and other assets for which there is reason to believe that the firm may not be able to collect the amounts due in full or in accordance with the assets’ terms.
(4) A banking business firm must ensure that it has an adequate understanding of the risk profile and characteristics of each of its counterparties, both at origination and regularly (at least annually) afterwards.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.1.4 Capital and credit risk
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must have capital to cover credit risk. The necessary amount of capital is the firm’s credit risk capital requirement.
Guidance
1 The firm’s credit risk capital requirement is part of its risk-based capital requirement — see rule 3.2.5.
2 Under rule 3.2.3, a banking business firm must have, at all times, capital at least equal to its minimum capital requirement (defined in that rule). The firm’s minimum capital requirement cannot be lower than its risk-based capital requirement, of which the credit risk capital requirement is a major part. Therefore, the firm must know its credit risk capital requirement at all times.
(2) A banking business firm’s credit risk capital requirement is the sum of the following components:
(a) the total of the firm’s risk-weighted assets for each of the following:
(i) exposures in the banking book (except those mentioned in subparagraphs (ii) to (iv)), calculated using the standardised approach (see Divisions 4.4.B and 4.4.C);
(ii) unsettled transactions and failed trades, in both the banking book and the trading book (see Subdivision 4.4.B.12);
(iii) defaulted exposures, in both the banking book and the trading book (see Subdivision 4.4.B.13);
(iv) securitisation exposures in the banking book (see Divisions 4.6.E, 4.6.F and 4.6.G);
(b) the firm’s capital requirements for counterparty credit risk, for exposures in both the banking book and the trading book (see Part 4.6A).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2014-2 (as from 1st January 2015).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
A banking business firm’s governing body is responsible for approving and periodically (at least annually) reviewing the firm’s credit risk strategy and significant credit risk policies. The firm’s credit risk strategy must reflect the firm’s risk appetite and the level of profit that the firm expects to achieve for incurring various credit risks.

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
A banking business firm’s senior management is responsible for implementing the credit risk strategy approved by the firm’s governing body and for developing policies and procedures for identifying, measuring, monitoring and controlling credit risk. The policies and procedures must address credit risk in all of the firm’s activities and at the level of both individual credits and the portfolio.

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
A banking business firm must identify and manage the credit risk that is inherent in all of the firm’s products and activities. The firm must ensure that the risks of a product or activity new to it:

(a) are subject to adequate risk management procedures and controls before the product is introduced or the activity undertaken; and
(b) are approved in advance by the firm’s governing body or the governing body’s appropriate committee.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.17 Credit risk management framework
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.1 Establishing appropriate credit risk environment
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
A banking business firm must implement a credit risk management framework that is appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of the firm’s business. The framework must include:

(a) a credit risk appetite statement (see rule 4.2.18);
(b) a credit risk management strategy (see rule 4.2.19);
(c) clearly defined and documented roles, responsibilities and formal reporting structures to manage credit risk, and policies and procedures to support those roles, responsibilities and structures;
(d) a designated credit risk management function;
(e) a management information system that is adequate, both under normal circumstances and in periods of stress, to measure, assess and report on credit risk; and
(f) an independent review process to ensure that the framework is effective to identify, measure, evaluate, monitor, report, and control or mitigate credit risk.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.18 Credit risk appetite statement
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.1 Establishing appropriate credit risk environment
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must maintain an appropriate and well-documented credit risk appetite statement. The statement must set out:

(a) the degree of credit risk that the firm is prepared to accept (its credit risk appetite);
(b) the maximum level of credit risk that the firm is willing to operate within (its credit risk tolerance);
(c) the process for ensuring that the credit risk tolerance is set at an appropriate level;
(d) the process for monitoring compliance with the credit risk tolerance and for taking appropriate action if it is breached; and
(e) the timing and process for reviewing the credit risk appetite and tolerance.
(2) The firm need not have a separate credit risk appetite statement if the firm’s overall risk appetite statement (required by CTRL, rule 7.1.5) includes a credit risk appetite statement that complies with subrule (1).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)
Amended by QFCRA RM/2024-4 (as from 1st October 2025)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.19 Credit risk management strategy
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.1 Establishing appropriate credit risk environment
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must maintain an appropriate and well-documented credit risk management strategy that describes the objectives guiding the firm’s credit origination, credit assessment and approval activities and adopts the necessary policies and processes for conducting those activities.
(2) The strategy must reflect the firm’s credit risk appetite, credit risk profile and the market and macroeconomic conditions.
(3) The strategy must describe the firm’s willingness to accept credit risk based on exposure type, economic or industry sector, geographical location, currency and maturity, and must include the overall characteristics that the firm wants to achieve in its credit portfolio.
(4) The strategy must take into account the sustainability of earnings from the firm’s credit risk activities, including an acceptable risk/reward trade-off that takes into account estimates of the cost of capital.
(5) The firm need not have a separate credit risk management strategy document if the document that sets out the firm’s overall risk management strategy (required by CTRL, rule 7.1.3 (5) (b)) includes a statement of the firm’s credit risk management strategy that complies with subrules (1) to (4).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)
Amended by QFCRA RM/2024-4 (as from 1st October 2025)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.20 Role of governing body in credit risk management
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.1 Establishing appropriate credit risk environment
BANK 4.2.20 Role of governing body in credit risk management
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm’s governing body must review and approve the firm’s credit risk appetite and credit risk management strategy. The governing body must do so at least annually.
(2) The governing body must regularly challenge, and seek assurance and evidence from, the firm’s senior management that the firm’s credit risk policies, processes and practices are consistent with its credit risk appetite and credit risk management strategy.
(3) The governing body must obtain sufficient information to find out whether the firm’s credit risk profile is consistent with the firm’s credit risk management strategy or not, and if it is not must require the firm’s senior management to take appropriate and timely action.
(4) The governing body must ensure that the firm’s senior management has the capability and resources to manage the firm’s credit risk activities appropriately, and that such activities operate within the firm’s credit risk appetite, credit risk management strategy and credit risk policies.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.21 Role of senior management in credit risk management
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.1 Establishing appropriate credit risk environment
BANK 4.2.21 Role of senior management in credit risk management
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm’s senior management is responsible for implementing the credit risk management strategy approved by the firm’s governing body and for developing and implementing appropriate policies and processes to identify, measure, monitor, report and control or mitigate credit risk.
(2) The policies and processes must address credit risk in all of the firm’s activities and at the level of both individual exposures and the portfolio.
(3) The senior management’s responsibility for implementing the credit risk management strategy and developing and implementing the firm’s credit risk policies includes ensuring:
(a) that the firm’s credit origination, credit assessment and approval activities conform to the strategy and policies;
(b) that written processes are developed that are consistent with the strategy and policies;
(c) that responsibilities for credit origination, credit assessment and credit approval and review are clearly and properly assigned;
(d) that the strategy, policies and processes are effectively communicated throughout the firm;
(e) that all the relevant personnel:
(i) clearly understand the firm’s approach to originating, assessing, approving and managing credit risk; and
(ii) are held accountable for complying with the policies and processes; and
(f) that there is a regular independent internal review of the firm’s credit origination, credit assessment, credit approval and credit management functions.
(4) The reviews required by paragraph (3) (f) must be carried out independently from the business function concerned — for example, by the firm’s independent risk management and compliance function, or an independent internal audit function or qualified external party.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

(2) The policies and processes must address credit risk in all of the firm’s activities and at the level of both individual exposures and the portfolio. (3) The senior management’s responsibility for implementing the credit risk management strategy and developing and implementing the firm’s credit risk policies includes ensuring: (a) that the firm’s credit origination, credit assessment and approval activities conform to the strategy and policies; (b) that written processes are developed that are consistent with the strategy and policies; (c) that responsibilities for credit origination, credit assessment and credit approval and review are clearly and properly assigned; (d) that the strategy, policies and processes are effectively communicated throughout the firm; (e) that all the relevant personnel: (i) clearly understand the firm’s approach to originating, assessing, approving and managing credit risk; and (ii) are held accountable for complying with the policies and processes; and (f) that there is a regular independent internal review of the firm’s credit origination, credit assessment, credit approval and credit management functions. QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.22 Credit risk policies and processes
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.1 Establishing appropriate credit risk environment
BANK 4.2.22 Credit risk policies and processes
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must implement prudent and well-documented policies and processes to identify, measure, monitor, report and control or mitigate credit risk. The full credit life-cycle must be considered, including credit origination, the initial and subsequent credit assessment and approval processes and the continuing monitoring and management of the firm’s credit exposures and portfolio.
(2) The policies must address target markets, portfolio mix, price and non-price terms, the structure of limits, approval authorities and overrides, the processing of waivers or exceptions, and reporting.
(3) The policies must be well-documented, clearly defined, consistent with prudent practices and applicable laws and regulations, and adequate for the nature, scale and complexity of the firm’s activities.
(4) The firm must implement the policies within the context of the relevant internal and external factors such as the firm’s market position, personnel capabilities and technology.
(5) The firm must have appropriate operational capacity and business systems to support the credit risk management strategy before the strategy is implemented.
(6) The firm must have prudent and well-documented policies and processes for the early identification and management of problem exposures, including non-performing and forborne exposures and other transactions, and the maintenance of adequate provisions.
(7) The firm must have appropriate credit risk practices, including an effective system of internal control, to consistently determine adequate provisions in accordance with the firm’s stated policies and processes and the applicable accounting standard.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.23 Internal risk appetite limits
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.1 Establishing appropriate credit risk environment
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must implement appropriate policies and processes to ensure that its credit portfolio is adequately diversified, given the firm’s target markets and credit risk management strategy.
(2) In particular, the policies must establish targets for the firm’s portfolio mix and must set prudent limits on the firm’s exposures to:
(a) higher-risk borrowers;
(b) higher-risk credit products and activities; and
(c) particular industry sectors and geographical locations.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.24 Country and transfer risk
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.1 Establishing appropriate credit risk environment
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm that originates credit exposures in geographical locations other than Qatar must have prudent policies and processes for identifying, evaluating, measuring, monitoring, reporting and controlling or mitigating country risk and transfer risk.
Guidance
Country risk or sovereign risk covers all the risks arising from the economic, political and social environments of a foreign country that may have potential consequences for foreigners’ debt and equity investments in that country. Transfer risk focuses more specifically on a borrower’s capacity to obtain the foreign exchange necessary to service its cross-border debt and other contractual obligations.
(2) The monitoring of country risk factors must take into account:
(a) the potential for default by foreign borrowers because of country-specific economic factors; and
(b) the enforceability of agreements, including the timing and ability to realise collateral under the relevant legal framework.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.25 Credit assessment and approval process
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.2 Operating under sound credit granting process
BANK 4.2.25 Credit assessment and approval process
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must establish sound credit assessment and approval criteria. The criteria must set out:
(a) the borrowers that are eligible for credit;
(b) the extent and nature of credit that the firm is willing to provide; and
(c) the terms and conditions that the exposures would be subject to.
(2) The firm must undertake a comprehensive assessment of a borrower’s credit risk that considers, and is proportionate to, the nature, type and size of the exposure. The firm must use experienced credit judgement in adopting a scalable and flexible approach to its assessment of a borrower’s credit risk.
(3) The firm must assess credit risk primarily on the strength of a borrower’s capacity to repay. The firm must not rely unduly on collateral instead of comprehensive credit assessment.
(4) The firm must not rely unduly on external credit ratings. The firm must obtain adequate information about a borrower to undertake a comprehensive credit assessment.
(5) The firm must properly consider a borrower’s integrity and reputation and its legal capacity to assume liability.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.26 Credit assessment — exposures to individuals
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.2 Operating under sound credit granting process
BANK 4.2.26 Credit assessment — exposures to individuals
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) For an exposure to an individual, a banking business firm’s credit assessment must consider the following matters, so far as relevant:
(a) the purpose and structure of the exposure;
(b) the borrower’s sources of repayment;
(c) the borrower’s current risk profile;
(d) the borrower’s expenses;
(e) the borrower’s repayment history and capacity, assessed under various scenarios such as:
(i) an increase in interest rates;
(ii) a change from a fixed interest rate to a floating interest rate (or vice versa);
(iii) a decrease in the borrower’s income or cash flows, particularly for less stable sources of income or cash flow; and
(iv) for an exposure with an interest-only period that subsequently reverts to principal and interest payments —a principal and interest basis of repayment;
(f) the proposed terms and conditions of the exposure, including covenants designed to limit to an acceptable level the firm’s exposure to changes in the borrower’s risk profile;
(g) if applicable, the adequacy and enforceability of collateral, guarantees and other risk mitigants, under various scenarios.
(2) For paragraphs (1) (b) to (e), the firm must make reasonable inquiries about, and must take reasonable steps to verify:
(a) the borrower’s sources of repayment; and
(b) the borrower’s commitments and total indebtedness.
(3) For paragraph (1) (d), the firm:
(a) must collect reasonable estimates of the borrower’s expenses; and
(b) must not use expense benchmarks as a substitute for reasonable enquiries about the borrower’s expenses.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.27 Credit assessment — exposures other than to individuals
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.2 Operating under sound credit granting process
BANK 4.2.27 Credit assessment — exposures other than to individuals
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) For an exposure other than to an individual, a banking business firm’s credit assessment must include consideration of the following matters, if relevant:
(a) the purpose and structure of the exposure;
(b) the borrower’s sources of repayment;
(c) the borrower’s current risk profile;
(d) the borrower’s repayment history and capacity, assessed under various scenarios such as:
(i) an increase in interest rates;
(ii) a change from a fixed interest rate to a floating interest rate (or vice versa);
(iii) a decrease in income or cash flows, particularly for less stable sources of income or cash flow; and
(iv) for an exposure with an interest-only period that subsequently reverts to principal and interest payments —a principal and interest basis of repayment;
(e) the proposed terms and conditions of the exposure (including covenants designed to limit to an acceptable level the firm’s exposure to changes in the borrower’s risk profile);
(f) if applicable, the adequacy and enforceability of collateral, guarantees and other risk mitigants, under various scenarios;
(g) the borrower’s business expertise, its economic or industry sector and its position within that sector;
(h) the borrower’s historical financial and future cash flows;
(i) the borrower’s equity capital invested in the business;
(j) the availability and enforceability of risk mitigants other than collateral, such as hedging and insurance.
(2) For paragraphs (1) (b) and (c), the firm must make reasonable inquiries about, and must take reasonable steps to verify:
(a) the borrower’s sources of repayment, income and cash flows; and
(b) the borrower’s commitments and total indebtedness.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.28 Collateral and guarantees
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.2 Operating under sound credit granting process
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must have prudent credit risk policies covering:
(a) the acceptability of various forms of collateral;
(b) appropriate processes for valuing collateral (including valuing before entering into an exposure and the continuing valuing of collateral, if appropriate); and
(c) an appropriate process to ensure that collateral is, and continues to be, enforceable and realisable.
(2) The firm must ensure that all valuations are appraised independently of the firm’s credit origination, assessment and approval process.
(3) The valuation of collateral must reflect fair values, taking into account market conditions such as the time taken to liquidate or realise collateral.
(4) The firm must ensure that the valuation of collateral such as land takes into account, so far as possible, the likelihood of external events that may affect the valuation of the asset taken as collateral.
(5) The firm must have appropriate mechanisms for regularly assessing the value of collateral, guarantees and other risk mitigants.
(6) The firm must establish appropriate limits on LTV ratio to minimise the risk that an asset that has been taken as collateral will be insufficient to cover any repayment shortfall. The firm must ensure that there is appropriate scrutiny of any instances of lending with a high LTV ratio.
(7) In relation to guarantees, the firm must appropriately evaluate the level of coverage that is provided in relation to the credit quality of the guarantor and the legal enforceability of the guarantee. For exposures to individuals in particular, the firm must ensure that a guarantor clearly understands the risks involved.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.29 Credit approval and experienced credit judgement
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.2 Operating under sound credit granting process
BANK 4.2.29 Credit approval and experienced credit judgement
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must have a clearly established process for:
(a) approving new exposures (including prudent credit standards);
(b) renewing and refinancing existing exposures; and
(c) identifying the appropriate approval authority for an exposure of a particular size and complexity.
(2) The firm must document the credit assessment and approval process and must identify the approval authority for each exposure, so that it is clear which individual is accountable for each credit decision.
(3) The firm must ensure that personnel involved in the credit assessment and approval process have appropriate experience and knowledge to exercise prudent credit judgement commensurate with the nature, scale and complexity of the relevant transaction.
(4) The firm must have prudent credit risk policies and processes in relation to overrides or waivers of, and exceptions to, the firm’s credit risk policies. The policies and processes must provide:
(a) clear identification of approval authorities; and
(b) limits to the maximum level of allowable overrides, waivers or exceptions.
(5) There must be regular reports to the firm’s relevant internal governance bodies and review functions about exposures that originated as overrides or waivers of, or exceptions to, the firm’s credit risk policies, or were otherwise not in compliance with those policies.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.3 Maintaining appropriate credit administration, measurement and monitoring process
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.3 Maintaining appropriate credit administration, measurement and monitoring process

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.30 Credit administration, measurement and monitoring
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.3 Maintaining appropriate credit administration, measurement and monitoring process
BANK 4.2.30 Credit administration, measurement and monitoring
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must have an appropriate system to administer its credit portfolio.
(2) The system must take into account:
(a) the efficiency and effectiveness of the firm’s credit administration, including its monitoring of documentation, contractual requirements, covenants and collateral;
(b) the accuracy and timeliness of the information provided to the firm’s management information systems;
(c) the adequate segregation of duties;
(d) the adequacy of controls over all of the firm’s credit administration processes; and
(e) compliance with the firm’s credit risk policies and processes, and with applicable laws and regulations.
(3) The firm must ensure that its credit administration system captures all the information necessary to ascertain a borrower’s current financial condition, and sufficient information to track all credit decisions made and the history of each exposure. The firm’s credit risk review function must determine that credit administration is complete and that all approvals and other necessary documents have been obtained.
(4) The firm must have an appropriate system to monitor the condition of individual exposures, including determining whether the relevant credit loss provisions are sufficient.
(5) The firm must have an appropriate system to monitor the overall composition and quality of the firm’s credit portfolio.
(6) The firm must have an appropriate information system and analytical techniques that enable the firm’s management to measure the credit risk inherent in all of its activities on and off the firm’s balance sheet. The system must provide adequate information on the composition of the firm’s credit portfolio, including identifying any concentrations of risk.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.31 Credit risk grading systems
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.3 Maintaining appropriate credit administration, measurement and monitoring process
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must have an internal credit risk grading system that is appropriate for the nature, scale and complexity of the firm’s operations.
(2) The firm must have prudent policies and processes governing the development, validation, operation and oversight of its credit risk grading system.
(3) The credit risk grading system must extend to as much of the firm’s credit portfolio as possible, including off-balance-sheet exposures.
(4) The system must meaningfully assess and differentiate risk and must be able to rank risk consistently and through time. A sufficient number of risk grades must be included to ensure that the system adequately captures gradation of risk.
(5) The definitions and criteria for each risk grade must be plausible and intuitive.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.title: BANK 4.2.32 Stress testing
doc_path: BANK Subdivision 4.2.B.3 Maintaining appropriate credit administration, measurement and monitoring process
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.document_html:
(1) A banking business firm must take into consideration potential future changes in economic conditions when assessing individual exposures and its credit portfolio, and must assess its credit risk exposures under stressed conditions.
(2) The firm must undertake regular portfolio-level and risk-specific stress testing of its credit exposures.
(3) The complexity and granularity of the firm’s stress testing must take into account the nature, scale and complexity of the firm’s credit portfolio. The firm must carry out stress testing at a sufficiently granular level to be adequately sensitive to the risk characteristics of different types of exposures.
(4) The scenarios used for stress testing must include severe but plausible adverse conditions.
(5) The firm must consider the results of stress testing in its overall limit-setting and monitoring process.
(6) Stress testing analyses must include contingency plans for actions that the firm’s governing body and senior management may take in particular scenarios.
(7) The stress testing arrangements must include well-documented and sound policies and processes governing the stress testing programme. The arrangements must provide for the timely communication of information to the firm’s governing body and senior management about scenarios, key assumptions, results and capital effects.
(8) Stress testing models must be appropriately validated and checked independently or by an appropriately qualified external party.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2023-5 (as from 1st July 2024)
QFCRA Rules :: Banking Business Prudenti.content_text: (1) A banking business firm must take into consideration potential future changes in economic conditions when assessing individual exposures and its credit portfolio, and must assess its credit risk exposures under stressed conditions.
