QFCRA Rules :: Customer and Investor Pro.title: Glossary
QFCRA Rules :: Customer and Investor Pro.document_html:
(see r 1.1.5)

advertisement: see rule 4.2.1.

associate of a person (A) means any of the following:

(a) if A is a legal person — a legal person in the same corporate group as A;
(b) any other person whose business or domestic relationship with A might reasonably be expected to give rise to a community of interest between them that may involve a conflict of interest in dealing with third parties.

Note Legal person, corporate group and person are defined in this glossary.

authorisation means an authorisation granted under FSR, Part 5.

authorised firm means a person that has an authorisation.

business day means a day that is not a Friday, Saturday, or a public or bank holiday in Qatar.

business customer: see rule 1.2.3.

calendar month means a period beginning at the start of any day of one of the 12 named months of the year and ending:

(a) at the end of the day before the corresponding day of the next named month; or
(b) if there is no corresponding day — at the end of the last day of next named month.

carrying out contracts of insurance: see rule 6.1.2.

COLL means the Collective Investment Schemes Rules 2010.

collective investment fund: see rule 5.1.2.

company means:

(a) a company incorporated under the Companies Regulations of the QFC; or
(b) a legal person incorporated under the law of a jurisdiction outside the QFC, the liability of each of member of which is limited to the amount of the member's capital contribution or guarantee.

complaint: see rule 3.8.1.

compliance officer for an authorised firm means the individual who exercises the compliance oversight function (as described in CTRL, rule 1.2.13) for the firm.

COND means the Conduct of Business Rules 2007, as in force at any time before 1 January 2020.

contract of insurance: see rule 6.1.2.

corporate group means the following:

(a) a legal person (A);
(b) any parent entity of A;
(c) any subsidiary (direct or indirect) of A or of any parent entity of A.

Note Legal person, parent entity and subsidiary are also defined in this glossary.

CTRL means the Governance and Controlled Functions Rules 2020.

customer: see rule 1.2.1.

customer dispute resolution scheme means the scheme by that name established under the Customer Dispute Resolution Scheme Rules 2019.

day means a period of 24 hours starting at midnight.

deposit: see rule 7.1.2.

deposit-taking: see rule 7.1.2.

deposit-taking business: see rule 7.1.2.

durable medium means a medium that:

(a) allows information to be addressed personally to the recipient;
(b) enables the recipient to store information in a way that is accessible for future reference and for a period of time adequate for the purposes of the information; and
(c) allows the information to be reproduced unchanged.

effecting contracts of insurance: see rule 6.1.2.

eligible counterparty: see rule 1.2.10.

employee of an authorised firm means an individual who is the firm's employee for the purposes of the Employment Regulations of the QFC.

entity means any kind of entity, and includes, for example, any person.

execute a transaction includes:

(a) to carry the transaction into effect or perform it; and
(b) to instruct another person to execute it.

FSR means the Financial Services Regulations.

GENE means the General Rules 2005.

general insurance contract: see rule 6.1.2.

governing body: an authorised firm's governing body is:

(a) in the case of such a firm that is a company or limited liability partnership incorporated in the QFC, or a partnership constituted under the Partnership Regulations 2007 — its board of directors or the body (whatever it is called) that, under the firm's constitutional document, has the responsibility of overseeing the firm's business in or from the QFC; and

(b) in the case of a firm that is a branch:

(i) that part of the board of directors of the firm that has the responsibility of overseeing the firm's business in or from the QFC;
(ii) if the firm does not have that part of the board described in subparagraph (i) — that part of the firm's membership, committee of management or other body (whatever it is called) that has the responsibility of overseeing the firm's business in or from the QFC; or
(iii) if the firm does not have the board or body described in subparagraphs (i) and (ii) — the person or persons delegated by the board, membership, committee or other body with the responsibility of overseeing the firm's business in or from the QFC.

group policy means an insurance contract that covers a defined group of persons (for example, the members of a society or professional body, or the employees of an employer).

initial disclosure document: see rule 4.4.1.

insurance business: see rule 6.1.2.

insurance mediation business: see rule 6.1.2.

investment advice: see rule 5.1.2.

investment business: see rule 5.1.2.

investment intermediary: see rule 5.1.2.

investment manager: see rule 5.1.2.

investment mediation business: see rule 5.1.2.

issuer means:

(a) for a security other than a unit in a collective investment fund — the person that issued, or is to issue, the security;
(b) for a unit in a collective investment fund — the operator of the collective investment fund or the fund manager (within the meaning of PROF) of the professional investor fund, as the case requires; and
Note Operator of a collective investment fund and professional investor fund are defined in this Glossary.

jurisdiction means any kind of legal jurisdiction, and includes, for example:

(a) the State of Qatar;
(b) a foreign country (whether or not an independent sovereign jurisdiction), or a state, province or other territory of a foreign country; and
(c) the QFC or a similar jurisdiction.

key information document: see rule 5.4.1.

legal person means an entity (other than an individual) on which the legal system of a jurisdiction confers rights and imposes duties, and includes, for example, any entity that can own, deal with or dispose of property.

life insurance contract: see rule 6.1.2.

long term care insurance contract: see rule 6.1.2.

long term insurance contract: see rule 6.1.2.

managing investments: see rule 5.1.2.

material interest: see rule 3.5.1.

non-investment insurance contract: see rule 6.1.2.

operator of a collective investment fund means the person (however described) responsible for managing the fund and fund property, and includes the operator of a collective investment scheme within the meaning of COLL.

overseas regulator means a regulatory or governmental authority, body or agency in a jurisdiction outside the QFC (whether in the State of Qatar or elsewhere).

packaged investment product: see rule 5.1.2.

parent entity, for a legal person (A), means any of the following:

(a) a legal person that holds a majority of the voting power in A;
(b) a legal person that is a member of A (whether direct or indirect, or though legal or beneficial entitlement) and alone, or together with 1 or more legal persons in the same corporate group, holds a majority of the voting power in A;
(c) a parent entity of any legal person that is a parent entity of A.

Note Legal person and corporate group are defined in this glossary.

person means:

(a) an individual (including an individual occupying an office or position from time to time); or
(b) a legal person.

PROF means the Professional Investor Funds Rules 2022.

professional investor fund: see PROF, rule 1.2.1.

pure protection contract: see rule 6.1.2.

QFC means Qatar Financial Centre.

QFC insurance intermediary means an authorised firm that is an insurance intermediary.

QFC insurer means an authorised firm that is an insurer.

regulated activity means an activity that is a regulated activity under FSR.

Note See FSR, article 23 (1) and Schedule 3, Part 2; the Islamic Banking Business Prudential Rules 2015, rule 1.1.4; and the Investment Management and Advisory Rules 2014, rule 1.1.3A.

regulated exchange means an exchange:

(a) that is incorporated or otherwise established in a jurisdiction outside the QFC; and
(b) that is regulated as an exchange by an overseas regulator in that jurisdiction.

regulated financial institution means a person that is not an authorised firm but is authorised, in a jurisdiction outside the QFC, by an overseas regulator to carry on a financial service.

Regulatory Authority means the Qatar Financial Centre Regulatory Authority.

remuneration means remuneration in any form, including benefits of any kind.

retail customer: see rule 1.2.2.

risk management officer for an authorised firm means the individual who exercises the risk management function (as described in CTRL, rule 1.2.12) for the firm.

soft commission agreement: see rule 3.5.10.

specified product: see rule 5.1.2.

subsidiary: a legal person (A) is a subsidiary of another legal person (B) if B is a parent entity of A.

Note Legal person and parent entity are defined in this glossary.

tied agent means a QFC insurance intermediary that represents only 1 insurer and is able to advise only on the policies offered by that insurer.

unit in a collective investment fund: see rule 5.1.2.

QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.title: CDRS 4 Purpose of these rules
QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.document_html:
These rules establish, in accordance with FSR, article 86 (2), an independent body for dealing with complaints by authorised firms' customers. The scheme set out in these rules may be referred to as the customer dispute resolution scheme.

Derived from QFCRA RM/2019-3 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.title: CDRS 5 Establishment of Independent Adjudicator
QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.document_html:
(1) The Independent Adjudicator is constituted by 1 or more members appointed by the Regulatory Authority from time to time.
(2) The Adjudicator is not a part of the Authority and is not subject to direction by the Authority.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2019-3 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.title: CDRS 6 Qualifications for appointment as member of Independent Adjudicator
doc_path: CDRS 6 Qualifications for appointment as member of Independent Adjudicator
QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.document_html:
(1) An individual is qualified for appointment as a member of the Independent Adjudicator if the Regulatory Authority is satisfied that he or she meets high standards of relevant professional knowledge, integrity and competence.
(2) The Regulatory Authority is solely responsible for assessing an individual's professional knowledge (and its relevance), and his or her integrity and competence.

QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.document_html:
(1) A member of the Independent Adjudicator is to be appointed by written instrument. An appointment may be for a fixed period or for the adjudication of a particular complaint.
(2) The terms of a member's appointment (including terms about ending the appointment) are as agreed between the member and the Regulatory Authority.

QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.title: CDRS 8 Who is eligible to apply to the Independent Adjudicator?

CDRS 8 Who is eligible to apply to the Independent Adjudicator?
QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.document_html:
A person is eligible to apply to the Independent Adjudicator if:

(a) the person (the applicant) is (or was) one of the following:
(i) a retail customer of an authorised firm;
(ii) a business customer (as defined in CIPR) of an authorised firm (but only if the applicant's business has no more than 20 employees);
(iii) an individual who is or was a beneficiary under a group policy issued by an authorised firm;
(iv) an individual who is a surviving dependent of a deceased retail customer of an authorised firm;
(v) a legal personal representative of a deceased retail customer of an authorised firm;
(vi) a widow or widower of a deceased retail customer of an authorised firm;
(vii) an individual who is entitled to benefit from an insurance contract issued to a retail customer of an authorised firm;
(b) the applicant has made a complaint to the authorised firm concerned, or a complaint was made to the firm by:
(i) if the applicant is an individual who is or was a beneficiary under a group policy issued by the firm — the person to whom the policy was issued;
(ii) if the applicant is an individual who is a surviving dependent of a deceased retail customer of the firm — that customer;
(iii) if the applicant is a legal personal representative of a deceased retail customer of the firm — that customer;
(iv) if the applicant is a widow or widower of a deceased retail customer of the firm — that customer;
(v) if the applicant is an individual who is entitled to benefit from an insurance contract issued to a retail customer of the firm — that customer; and
(c) either:
(i) the response period for the complaint has not ended, but the firm has given a final response to the complaint and the applicant is not satisfied with that response; or
(ii) the response period for the complaint has ended.

Note See the glossary for the definition of response period.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2019-3 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.title: CDRS 9 When to apply
doc_path: CDRS Part 3 Application for Independent Adjudicator's review of decisions
QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.document_html:
(1) An application may be made to the Independent Adjudicator within 4 calendar months after:
(a) a final response is received (even if it was given after the end of the response period); or
(b) the response period has ended without the firm having given any response.
(2) The Adjudicator may accept, consider and decide an application made after the end of the period allowed by subrule (1) if the Adjudicator is satisfied that there is sufficient reason for the delay in applying.

QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.title: CDRS 12 Firm must cooperate in adjudication
doc_path: CDRS 12 Firm must cooperate in adjudication
QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.document_html:
(1) An authorised firm whose action or decision is the subject of an application to the Independent Adjudicator must participate in the adjudication process and must cooperate fully with the Adjudicator.
(2) In particular, the Authority may request the firm to provide further information or copies of documents. The firm must comply with such a request.
(3) The Authority may publish, on an approved website, procedures for making a complaint to the Adjudicator and for the operation of this scheme.
(4) To the fullest possible extent, the principles in the General Rules 2005, Part 1.2, apply to an authorised firm in its relationship with the Adjudicator. For that purpose, the Adjudicator is taken to be a regulator.
Note The General Rules 2005, Part 1.2, contains provisions about the conduct of authorised firms in relation to their conduct of regulated activities in or from the QFC.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2019-3 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.title: CDRS 13 Adjudicator's process
QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.document_html:
(1) The Independent Adjudicator must observe the principles of procedural fairness.
(2) The Adjudicator is not bound by the technical law of evidence, but may inform itself about any matter in any way that it thinks appropriate. In particular, the Adjudicator may rely, without further inquiry, on information or documents given to the Adjudicator by the Regulatory Authority.
(3) The Adjudicator is not obliged to grant an oral hearing to any party.
(4) The Adjudicator must make a decision in accordance with the substantial equity and fairness of the matter. In particular, the Adjudicator may decide that a party may not rely on a contractual provision if it would be inequitable or unfair to do so.

Example

In deciding the equity and fairness of a matter, the Adjudicator might take into account any of the following:
•   imbalances of power or information between the parties
•   the parties' actual intentions
•   the sincerity of each party
•   whether or not any consent given was truly an informed consent.
(5) The Adjudicator must give its decision in writing and must transmit it through the Authority.
(6) If there is more than 1 member of the Adjudicator, a decision by any member is valid for all purposes as a decision of the Adjudicator.

Guidance

It is expected that only rarely, if ever, would a complaint be decided otherwise than by a single member of the Adjudicator.
(7) Subject to this rule, the Adjudicator may determine its own procedure.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2019-3 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.title: CDRS 14 Adjudicator's powers
QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.document_html:
(1) The Independent Adjudicator may direct an authorised firm to pay compensation, of no more than QR 400,000, to an applicant for losses and expenses that the applicant has actually incurred as a result of the actions by the firm that gave rise to a complaint.
(2) The Adjudicator has no power to award costs in relation to an application, nor to award compensation or damages other than as set out in subrule (1).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2019-3 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.title: CDRS 15 Effects of Independent Adjudicator's decision
doc_path: CDRS 15 Effects of Independent Adjudicator's decision
QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.document_html:
(1) After the Independent Adjudicator has given a decision, the applicant may accept the decision or refuse to accept it, but must do either within 21 days after being notified of it. The Adjudicator may extend the period for acceptance (either before or after the period has ended) if the Adjudicator is satisfied that there is sufficient reason to do so.
(2) If the applicant does not accept the decision within the 21-day period (or any extension of it), the applicant is taken to have refused to accept the decision.
(3) If the applicant refuses (or is taken to have refused) to accept the decision, the decision is of no effect.
(4) If the applicant accepts the decision, the decision is binding on both the applicant and the authorised firm concerned.
(5) The firm must comply with the decision (and in particular must pay the applicant any compensation awarded) as soon as reasonably practicable.
(6) A decision is final and is not subject to appeal.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2019-3 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.title: CDRS 16 Transitional
QFCRA Rules :: Customer Dispute Resoluti.document_html:
(1) The Independent Adjudicator established under COND, rule 8.1.2, is continued in existence.
(2) The appointment of a member of the Adjudicator under COND, rule 8.1.4, continues in effect according to its terms.
(3) An application under COND, Chapter 8, made to the Adjudicator before the commencement of these rules continues to have effect as an application under these rules.
(4) A decision of the Adjudicator (including a decision to award compensation) made on such an application continues to have effect as a decision of the Adjudicator, as if made under these rules.
(5) In this rule:

COND means the Conduct of Business Rules 2007 (as in force immediately before 1 January 2020).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2019-3 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 1.1.2 Purpose of rules
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) These rules establish a regulatory framework for the establishment and operation of:
(a) derivatives exchanges; and
Note For the meaning of derivative in these rules, see rule 1.2.1 and the glossary.
(b) central counterparties (CCPs) to clear and settle transactions in derivatives.
(2) These rules are based on:
(a) the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures established by the Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures and the International Organization of Securities Commissions;
(b) the criteria established for a qualifying central counterparty in Capital requirements for banks’ exposures to central counterparties, published by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision as part of its capital framework standard; and
(c) the European Union’s framework for non-EU central counterparties (that is, third-country central counterparties subject to regulation in the European Union) which must be recognised with the European Securities and Markets Authority.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

(2) A note in or to these rules is explanatory and is not part of these rules. However, examples and guidance are part of these rules.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 1.1.10 Declaration of regulated activities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
For FSR, article 23 (2), each of the following activities is a regulated activity:

(a) operating a derivatives exchange;
Note An authorised firm that is authorised to conduct the regulated activity of operating a derivatives exchange is referred to generally in these rules as an authorised derivatives exchange. See rule 1.2.3. An authorised derivatives exchange is permitted to allow trading only in derivatives that are approved derivatives (see rules 1.2.1 and 3.1.12 (3)) and are within the scope of its authorisation.
(b) operating a central counterparty for clearing and settling transactions in approved derivatives.
Note An authorised firm that is authorised to conduct the regulated activity of operating a central counterparty for clearing and settling transactions in approved derivatives is referred to generally in these rules as an authorised CCP. See rule 1.2.4. An authorised CCP is permitted to clear and settle transactions only in derivatives that are approved derivatives (see rules 1.2.1 and 3.1.12 (5)) and are within the scope of its authorisation.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 1.2.1 What is an approved derivative?
doc_path: DMEX 1.2.1 What is an approved derivative?
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
In these rules:

approved derivative means an arrangement or product (such as a future, an option, a warrant or a contract for differences) whose value derives from, and is dependent on, the value of an underlying asset, but only if the arrangement or product:

(a) relates to a specified product (within the meaning of FSR. Schedule 3, Part 3); and
(b) is specified by the Regulatory Authority, by notice on an approved website, as an approved derivative.
Note For the meaning of approved website, see the Interpretation and Application Rules 2005, rule 3.1.2.

Guidance

A reference in these rules to a derivative that is actually being traded (or cleared and settled), or is proposed to be traded (or cleared and settled), in or from the QFC by an authorised market entity is normally to be read as a reference to an approved derivative, since no other derivatives may be traded, or cleared and settled, under these rules.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 1.2.3 What is an authorised derivatives exchange?
doc_path: DMEX 1.2.3 What is an authorised derivatives exchange?
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
In these rules:

authorised derivatives exchange means an authorised firm that is authorised to conduct, in or from the QFC, the regulated activity of operating a derivatives exchange (that is, the regulated activity mentioned in rule 1.1.10 (a)).

Guidance

An exchange provides:

• a centralised market (whether primary, secondary or both); and
• a non-discretionary system or mechanism (whether order-driven, quote-driven or a combination of both) enabling the market to operate by face-to-face trading (open outcry), electronic trading or other means.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 1.2.4 What is an authorised CCP?
doc_path: DMEX 1.2.4 What is an authorised CCP?
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
In these rules:

authorised CCP means an authorised firm that is authorised to conduct, in or from the QFC, the regulated activity of operating a central counterparty for clearing and settling transactions in derivatives (that is, the regulated activity mentioned in rule 1.1.10 (b)).

Guidance

1 A central counterparty or CCP interposes itself between the counterparties to contracts for derivatives traded in a market, becoming the buyer to every seller and the seller to every buyer, and so ensures that open contracts are performed.
2 A CCP becomes the counterparty to a trade through novation, an open-offer system or another legally binding arrangement.
3 CCPs have the potential to significantly reduce risks to participants through the multilateral netting of trades and by imposing more-effective risk controls on all participants. For example, CCPs typically require participants to provide collateral (in the form of initial margin and other financial resources) to cover current and potential future exposures.
4 CCPs may also mutualise certain risks through devices such as default funds. As a result of their potential to reduce risks to participants, CCPs can reduce systemic risk in the markets they serve. The effectiveness of a CCP’s risk controls and the adequacy of its financial resources are critical to achieving those benefits.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 1.2.5 Who are members of an authorised market entity?

(1) Subject to subrule (2), a person who has been granted access to the facilities of an authorised market entity in accordance with the entity’s rules is a member of the entity.
(2) If a member of an authorised market entity allows a client to have direct electronic access (for example, by allowing the client to use the member’s trading code) to the entity’s trading facilities, that granting of access does not of itself make the client a member of the entity.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 2.1.1 Application of principles
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The principles in this Chapter apply to an authorised market entity in relation to its conduct, in or from the QFC, of a regulated activity mentioned in rule 1.1.10.
(2) The principles also apply to the activities of such an entity carried on outside the QFC, if the activities:
(a) relate to 1 or more regulated activities carried on by the entity in or from the QFC; and
(b) are capable of having an effect on any of the following:
(i) confidence in the financial system operating in or from the QFC;
(ii) the entity’s ability to comply with the requirements of these rules as to financial resources;
(iii) the entity’s fitness and propriety to be an authorised market entity.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 2.1.14 Principle 13 — relations with regulators
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
The entity must deal with all relevant regulators in an open and cooperative way, and must keep the Regulatory Authority promptly informed of anything that relates to the entity and about which the Authority would reasonably expect to be informed.

Guidance

1 The principles in this Chapter are drawn up in accordance with FSR, article 15 (3), and are part of these rules.
2 The principles are a general statement of the standards expected of authorised market entities. They apply directly to the conduct of business, and the operation and financial standing, of such entities.
3 The principles are not exhaustive of the standards expected. Complying with the principles does not absolve such an entity from failing to observe other requirements in these rules, and observing other applicable requirements in these rules is not necessarily complying with the principles.
4 Such an entity’s failure to comply adequately with the principles is likely to affect the Regulatory Authority’s assessment of the entity’s fitness and propriety. A breach of the principles could form the basis of action by the Authority.

This Chapter applies in relation to:

(a) an application for an authorisation to conduct, in or from the QFC, either of the regulated activities mentioned in rule 1.1.10; and
(b) an application for the variation or withdrawal of such an authorisation.

Note 2 An entity that is licensed (however described) in a jurisdiction outside the QFC or the State of Qatar to conduct either of the activities of operating a derivatives exchange and operating a central counterparty may apply to the Regulatory Authority under Chapter 11 to be recognised to conduct the corresponding regulated activity in or from the QFC.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 3.1.6 Form etc of applications
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 3 Authorisation — requirements and process
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An application for an authorisation:
(a) must be in the form required by the Regulatory Authority;
(b) must include a copy of the applicant’s constitution;
(c) must include particulars of:
(i) the applicant’s organisation, structure and practices; and
(ii) its governing body; and
(d) must include any other information required by these rules or by the Authority.
(2) If an applicant for an authorisation intends to conduct the regulated activity of operating a derivatives exchange, the application must specify the type or types of approved derivative that the applicant proposes to admit to trading.
(3) If an applicant for an authorisation intends to conduct the regulated activity of operating a CCP, the application must specify the type or types of approved derivative transactions in which the applicant proposes to clear and settle.
(4) If an applicant for an authorisation intends to conduct its business in accordance with Shari’a, the application must include:
(a) a statement to that effect; and
(b) a statement of the names of the proposed members of the applicant’s Shari’a supervisory board.
Guidance
An applicant whose application states that it intends to conduct its business in accordance with Shari’a must, if the application is granted, conduct its entire business in accordance with Shari’a, and its authorisation will include a condition to that effect (see rule 3.1.12 (2)). So-called Islamic windows will not be approved. See also CTRL, Part 9.4, as applied by rule 12.1.2.
(5) An application for the variation or withdrawal of an authorisation:
(a) must be in the form required by the Authority; and
(b) must include any information required by these rules or by the Authority.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 3.1.9 Consideration by Regulatory Authority
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 3 Authorisation — requirements and process
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) In considering an application under this Part, the Regulatory Authority:
(a) may make any enquiries that it considers appropriate;
(b) may ask the applicant to give it more information;
(c) may ask the applicant to give it information on how the applicant intends to ensure that the applicant will comply with a particular requirement;
(d) may ask the applicant to verify, in any way that the Authority specifies, any information that the applicant has given to it; and
(e) may take into account any or all of the following:
(i) the applicant’s connection with any person who is (or, if the applicant were an authorised firm, would be) a controller of the applicant;
(ii) anything that the Authority reasonably considers may harm, or may have harmed, the integrity or reputation of the QFC;
(iii) any other information that the Authority reasonably considers to be relevant.
(2) When the Authority is considering the fitness and propriety of an authorised market entity or applicant, it may take into account whether or not the other members of the entity’s or applicant’s corporate group act in accordance with the principles in Chapter 2.
(3) This rule does not limit what the Authority may do, or the matters that the Authority may take into account, in considering such an application.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.content_text: (1) In considering an application under this Part, the Regulatory Authority : (a) may make any enquiries that it considers appropriate; (b) may ask the applicant to give it more information; (c) may ask the applicant to give it information on how the applicant intends to ensure that the applicant will comply with a particular requirement; (d) may ask the applicant to verify, in any way that the Authority specifies, any information that the applicant has given to it; and (e) may take into account any or all of the following: (i) the applicant’s connection with any person who is (or, if the applicant were an authorised firm, would be) a controller of the applicant; (ii) anything that the Authority reasonably considers may harm, or may have harmed, the integrity or reputation of the QFC ; (iii) any other information that the Authority reasonably considers to be relevant. QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 3.1.10 Criteria for grant of authorisation
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 3 Authorisation — requirements and process
DMEX 3.1.10 Criteria for grant of authorisation
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) To be granted an authorisation, an applicant must demonstrate, to the Regulatory Authority’s satisfaction, that:
(a) the applicant is fit and proper to be an authorised market entity (see rule 3.1.11);
(b) if the authorisation is granted, the applicant:
(i) will have sufficient financial resources;
(ii) will have an appropriate governance and management structure;
(iii) will have appropriate systems and controls;
(iv) will have the required number of approved individuals to exercise the required controlled functions; and
(v) will have appropriate risk management arrangements;
(in each case, as required by the relevant provisions of these rules) to conduct its business as an authorised market entity; and
(c) if the authorisation is granted, the applicant as an authorised market entity:
(i) will continue to satisfy the criteria in paragraphs (a) and (b); and
(ii) will be able to fulfil its other obligations under these rules.
(2) The Authority must reject an application for an authorisation unless the applicant demonstrates, to the Authority’s satisfaction, that:
(a) the applicant satisfies the criteria in subrule (1) that apply to it;
(b) the applicant’s other business activities are not incompatible with conducting the activity;
(c) the applicant’s legal form is suitable for the activity;
(d) the applicant will conduct its business soundly and prudently;
(e) the applicant has made arrangements, satisfactory to the Authority, for clearing and settling transactions; and
(f) if the applicant proposes to have transactions cleared by a CCP outside Qatar — the CCP is a recognised CCP (see Chapter 11).
(3) Subrule (2) does not limit the grounds on which the Authority may reject such an application.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 3.1.11 Consideration of applicant’s fitness and propriety
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 3 Authorisation — requirements and process
DMEX 3.1.11 Consideration of applicant’s fitness and propriety
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
In deciding whether an applicant is fit and proper to be an authorised market entity, the Regulatory Authority may consider any 1 or more of the following matters:

(a) the extent to which the applicant’s constitution and organisation provide for effective governance;
(b) the applicant’s resources, policies and procedures for continuing to satisfy the authorisation criteria and fulfilling its obligations under these rules;
(c) the applicant’s connection with its controllers or any other person;
(d) the applicant’s connection with its outsourced service providers;
(e) the types of derivatives traded, cleared or settled (or to be traded, cleared or settled) on or through the applicant’s facilities;
(f) the educational or other qualifications or experience of the applicant’s employees, taking into account their duties in connection with the establishment or operation of a market;
(g) the applicant’s policies and procedures for ensuring that it employs only individuals who are honest and show integrity;
(h) the fitness and propriety, integrity, qualifications and competence of the applicant’s approved individuals;
(i) the applicant’s remuneration structure and strategy;
(j) any matter that may harm, or may have harmed, the integrity or reputation of the QFC;
(k) the applicant’s activities, and the associated risks and accumulation of risks that those activities pose to the Authority’s regulatory objectives;
(l) the extent to which the applicant’s regulatory and listings functions are independent of, and segregated from, its commercial functions (in terms of both governance and operations);
(m) the applicant’s policies and procedures for identifying and managing conflicts and potential conflicts between its commercial interest and its functions;
(n) the applicant’s arrangements to ensure that its board of directors has effective oversight of the applicant’s functions;
(o) the cumulative effect of factors any one of which on its own is not enough to give reasonable cause to doubt that the applicant is fit and proper to be an authorised market entity;
(p) any other matter that the Authority reasonably considers to be relevant.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 3.1.12 Grant of authorisation
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 3 Authorisation — requirements and process
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) If the Regulatory Authority decides to grant an authorisation, the Authority may impose any condition or restriction on the authorisation that it considers appropriate.
(2) In particular, in the case of an applicant whose application states that the applicant intends to conduct its business in accordance with Shari’a, the Authority must impose a condition on the authorisation that the whole of the applicant’s business in the QFC must be conducted in accordance with Shari’a.
Guidance
Islamic windows are not permitted in the QFC. See CTRL, Part 9.4, as applied by rule 12.1.2.
(3) It is a condition of the authorisation of an authorised derivatives exchange that the exchange trades only approved derivatives.
(4) In the authorisation of an authorised derivatives exchange, the Authority must specify the type or types of approved derivative that may be traded on the exchange.
(5) It is a condition of the authorisation of a central counterparty that the exchange may clear and settle transactions only in approved derivatives.
(6) In the authorisation of a central counterparty, the Authority must specify the type or types of approved derivative in which transactions may be cleared and settled.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 3.1.14 Continued effect of rules etc after withdrawal of authorisation
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 3 Authorisation — requirements and process
DMEX 3.1.14 Continued effect of rules etc after withdrawal of authorisation
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) This rule applies if the Regulatory Authority:
(a) grants an application for the withdrawal of an authorisation; or
(b) on its own initiative, withdraws an authorisation.
(2) For 6 years after the date on which the withdrawal takes effect, the Authority may exercise any function in relation to the applicant under the QFC Law, FSR, these rules, and any other law, regulations or rules applying in the QFC, that it could have exercised if the authorisation had not been withdrawn.
(3) For this rule, the provisions of the QFC Law, FSR, and any other law, regulations or rules applying in the QFC, have effect as if they were provisions of these rules.
(4) For this rule, the provisions of these rules (including the provisions mentioned in subrule (3)) apply as if:
(a) a reference to an authorised firm or authorised market entity were a reference to the entity whose authorisation was withdrawn; and
(b) all other necessary changes were made.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.1 Meaning of non-executive director etc
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.A Board of directors — composition and qualifications
DMEX 4.2.1 Meaning of non-executive director etc
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
In these rules:

independent non-executive director of an authorised market entity means a non-executive director:

(a) who is not made ineligible by rule 4.2.2 to be an independent non-executive member of the entity’s board of directors; or
(b) who has been approved by the Regulatory Authority to exercise the non-executive governance function for the entity on the basis of an application referred to in rule 4.2.3.

non-executive director of an authorised market entity means a member of the entity’s board of directors who has no responsibility for implementing the board’s decisions or policies.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.2 Ineligibility as independent non-executive member of board of directors
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.A Board of directors — composition and qualifications
DMEX 4.2.2 Ineligibility as independent non-executive member of board of directors
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An individual is ineligible to be an independent non-executive member of an authorised market entity’s board of directors if:

(a) he or she is (or has been during the last 3 years):
(i) an employee of the entity; or
(ii) an employee, board member, owner, partner or controller of a consultant to the entity (including the entity’s external auditor);
(b) he or she is related by blood or marriage to a member of the entity’s senior management;
(c) within the last 3 years, he or she, or any of his or her relatives by blood or marriage, has had, directly or indirectly, 1 or more substantial commercial or financial transactions with the entity;
(d) he or she is receiving, or has received during the last 3 years, remuneration from the entity (otherwise than as a member of its board of directors);
(e) he or she:
(i) owns 1% or more of the shares of the entity; or
(ii) is a representative of a legal person that owns 5% or more of the shares of the entity or another company in its corporate group;
(f) he or she has been a member of the board for longer than 9 consecutive years; or
(g) he or she might reasonably be taken to have a conflict of interest because of a personal or business relationship with:
(i) a member of the board, the individual who exercises the senior executive function for the entity, or a member of the entity’s senior management; or
(ii) a major shareholder of the entity.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.3 Approval to exercise non-executive governance function despite ineligibility as independent non-executive member of board
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.A Board of directors — composition and qualifications
DMEX 4.2.3 Approval to exercise non-executive governance function despite ineligibility as independent non-executive member of board
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) This rule applies if:
(a) under rule 4.2.2, an individual is ineligible to be an independent non-executive member of an authorised market entity’s board of directors; but
(b) the board nonetheless considers that the individual:
(i) should be approved to exercise the non-executive governance function for the entity; and
(ii) should be treated as being eligible to be an independent non-executive member of the board.
(2) With its application for the Authority’s approval of the individual for the non-executive governance function, the board must provide:
(a) a clear statement of its reasons for holding the opinion referred to in subrule (1) (b); and
(b) appropriate supporting evidence.
Guidance
The statement could include evidence of the individual’s providing constructive challenge, strategic guidance and specialist advice, and holding the entity’s management to account, in the board’s discussions.

doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.A Board of directors — composition and qualifications
DMEX 4.2.4 Directors to be approved individuals
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
A director of an authorised market entity must be an individual who is approved to exercise the appropriate controlled function, as follows:

(a) for an executive director — the executive governance function;
(b) for a non-executive director — the non-executive governance function.
Note INDI, Chapters 3 and 5, applies to the approval of individuals to perform the executive governance and non-executive governance functions — see rules 1.1.9 (5) and 5.1.1.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.5 Number of directors
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.A Board of directors — composition and qualifications
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must ensure that its board of directors is of sufficient size and expertise to adequately oversee the operation of the entity.
(2) The board must be made up of:
(a) at least 5 directors; or
(b) a greater number directed by the Regulatory Authority.
(3) In a direction under paragraph (2) (b), the Authority may specify how many executive directors or independent non-executive directors (or both) that the relevant entity’s board must have.
(4) A majority of the directors must be non-executive directors, and at least 1 of the non-executive directors must be an independent non-executive director.
(5) In the case of an authorised market entity that is a subsidiary, the majority of its directors may be directors or senior executives of the parent entity or another member of the corporate group. However, the entity must still have at least 2 independent non-executive directors.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.6 Board competencies
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.A Board of directors — composition and qualifications
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
The directors of an authorised market entity must have an appropriate mix of relevant competencies, and as a whole must have the necessary skills to oversee the entity effectively.

Guidance
Relevant competencies include financial markets, financial analysis, financial stability issues, financial reporting, information technology, strategic planning, risk management, compensation, regulation, corporate governance and management skills.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.7 Chair of the board
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.A Board of directors — composition and qualifications
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The chair of an authorised market entity’s board of directors must be a non-executive director.
Guidance
The Regulatory Authority expects that the chair of an authorised market entity that is not a subsidiary will be an independent non-executive director.
(2) If the chair is not an independent non-executive director, the entity must be able to demonstrate how its governance arrangements will satisfy the need for independent oversight of the entity’s senior management.
Guidance
The independent oversight referred to in subrule (2) could be provided by, for example, nominating a senior independent non-executive director with explicit responsibilities in this regard.
(3) The chair must not have been an employee of the entity during the previous 5 years.
(4) The chair is responsible for the following:
(a) setting the board’s agenda and ensuring that every agenda item (particularly any item dealing with strategic and risk issues) receives sufficient attention;
(b) ensuring that every director receives background information in time for each meeting and that that information is thorough, relevant and accurate;
(c) encouraging transparent and candid debate by promoting contributions by all the directors, particularly the non-executive directors and independent non-executive directors.

(4) The chair is responsible for the following: (a) setting the board’s agenda and ensuring that every agenda item (particularly any item dealing with strategic and risk issues) receives sufficient attention; (b) ensuring that every director receives background information in time for each meeting and that that information is thorough, relevant and accurate; (c) encouraging transparent and candid debate by promoting contributions by all the directors, particularly the non-executive directors and independent non-executive directors . Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.8 Training and competency of directors
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.A Board of directors — composition and qualifications
DMEX 4.2.8 Training and competency of directors
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) A director of an authorised market entity must regularly update and refresh his or her skills and knowledge.
(2) An authorised market entity’s board of directors must ensure that:
(a) a suitable induction programme is offered to every newly-appointed director to help him or her to understand the duties and role of a director; and
(b) regular updates and training are offered to each director to maintain his or her competency for that role.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.9 Periodic assessments of performance etc
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.A Board of directors — composition and qualifications
DMEX 4.2.9 Periodic assessments of performance etc
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s board of directors must regularly assess (with the assistance of external experts, if necessary) the performance of the board as a whole, of its committees and of each director. The assessments:
(a) must review the board’s structure, size and composition and the structures and coordination of the committees;
(b) must consider:
(i) rotating the members and chairs of committees periodically; and
(ii) limiting individuals’ tenure on the board or a committee;
(c) must assess each committee’s performance against its terms of reference; and
(d) must assess each director’s suitability, taking into account his or her performance on the board.
(2) The board must carry out such an assessment at least annually.
(3) The board must periodically review its own governance practices and procedures, must determine where improvements may be needed, and must make any necessary changes. The board may do so either separately or as part of an assessment required by subrule (1).
(4) The board must use the results of the assessments and reviews required by subrules (1) to (3) as part of its efforts to continue to improve the board.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.10 Frequency of board meetings
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.A Board of directors — composition and qualifications
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s board of directors must meet:
(a) at least every 3 months; or
(b) more frequently, if the Regulatory Authority so directs.
(2) In a direction under paragraph (1) (b), the Authority may specify how often the board must meet, or how long may pass between meetings, or both, taking into account the nature, scale and complexity of the entity’s operations.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.11 Boards of authorised CCPs — special rules
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.A Board of directors — composition and qualifications
DMEX 4.2.11 Boards of authorised CCPs — special rules
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to an authorised CCP's board of directors.
(2) The board must invite 1 or more representatives of the clients of the CCP’s clearing members to attend, as observers, any board meeting at which matters referred to in rule 9.3.13 are to be dealt with. An invited representative may speak, but not vote, at a meeting.
Note Rule 9.3.13 deals with segregation and portability of the positions of authorised CCPs’ users’ customers, and any collateral provided to it in relation to those positions.
(3) The board of directors of an authorised CCP must make the minutes of its meetings available to the CCP’s auditor and to the Regulatory Authority.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.14 Allocation of responsibilities by board
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.B Board of directors — role and obligations
DMEX 4.2.14 Allocation of responsibilities by board
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s board of directors is primarily responsible for all of the entity’s operations at all times. The entity’s senior management is responsible for implementing the board’s business strategy consistently with the board’s policies and risk appetite, under the board’s supervision.
(2) The board must give the individual who exercises the senior executive function for the entity a written document that sets out his or her responsibilities. The individual must acknowledge, in writing, having received that document, and must confirm in the acknowledgement that he or she understands those responsibilities and undertakes to carry them out.
(3) The board retains any responsibility that it does not specifically allocate.
(4) The allocation of a responsibility by the board does not remove or reduce the board’s duty to oversee:
(a) the individual who exercises the entity’s senior executive function; and
(b) the entity’s senior management.
(5) The board:
(a) must ensure that the entity’s business can be adequately managed by the board, the individual who exercises the entity’s senior executive function and the entity’s senior management; and
(b) must consider whether any member of the entity’s senior management (other than the individual who exercises the senior executive function) ought to be ordinarily resident in Qatar to exercise his or her functions properly.
Note These rules already require the individuals who exercise the following controlled functions to be ordinarily resident in Qatar:
• the senior executive function — see rule 4.3.4 (2)
• the risk management function — see rule 5.2.7 (2)
• the compliance oversight function — see rule 5.2.10 (2).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.B Board of directors — role and obligations
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity’s board of directors:

(a) must ensure that it has access to sufficient information and independent advice about the entity’s affairs to make informed decisions and discharge its responsibilities effectively; and
(b) must be mindful of the legitimate interests of shareholders, customers and other stakeholders when making decisions.

DMEX 4.2.18 General obligations — culture and values
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity’s board of directors must play the leading role in establishing the entity’s corporate culture and values.

Guidance
To comply with this obligation, the board may need to develop and oversee a code of conduct or code of ethics for all employees that defines acceptable and unacceptable behaviour, and reminds them not to engage in illegal or unethical activity.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.19 General obligations — own structure
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.B Board of directors — role and obligations
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity’s board of directors:

(a) must have a well-designed governance structure;
Guidance
The board should maintain and periodically update rules, by-laws or other similar documents setting out its organisation, rights, responsibilities and key activities.
(b) must allocate sufficient time and attention for its members to perform their duties effectively; and
(c) must consider how it can best perform its role, and in particular whether to establish 1 or more committees to make recommendations to the board on matters about which the board must make decisions.
Note Division 4.2.C requires the board to establish certain committees.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.20 General obligations — oversight
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.B Board of directors — role and obligations
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity’s board of directors:

(a) must provide effective oversight of the entity’s senior management and the individual who exercises the entity’s senior executive function;
(b) must hold the senior management and that individual accountable for their actions;
(c) must set out the possible consequences (including dismissal) if those actions are not aligned with the board’s performance expectations;
(d) must deal prudently with any conflicts of interest that arise, by ensuring that no individual or group of individuals unduly influences the board’s decision-making;
(e) must approve the organisational structure and corporate governance framework through which the entity is managed and controlled;
(f) must ensure that the entity has succession plans for its key functions;
(g) must establish direct and independent contact with the entity’s audit and risk management functions;
(h) must ensure that the entity has effective policies, procedures and controls to deter, prevent, detect, report and remedy fraud, and must ensure that appropriate resources are allocated for that purpose; and
(i) must maintain transparency and disclosure.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.21 General obligations — subsidiaries
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.B Board of directors — role and obligations
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) If an authorised market entity has 1 or more subsidiaries, wherever incorporated, the entity’s board of directors must ensure that the entity seeks to promote good governance in those subsidiaries.
(2) The entity’s board must ensure that it is aware of the material risks and issues that affect both the entity and its subsidiaries. The board must exercise adequate oversight over the subsidiaries while respecting the subsidiaries’ legal and governance responsibilities.
(3) In particular, the entity’s board must ensure that it understands the purpose, structure, governance and unique risks of the entity’s subsidiaries.
(4) The entity’s board:
(a) must establish a group structure (including the legal entity and business structure) and a corporate governance framework with clearly defined roles and responsibilities, at the parent company level and at the subsidiary level, as appropriate, based on the complexity and significance of each subsidiary;
(b) must define an appropriate subsidiary board and management structure that takes into account the material risks to which the group, its businesses and its subsidiaries are exposed;
(c) must assess whether the group’s corporate governance framework:
(i) includes adequate policies, processes and controls; and
(ii) addresses risk management across the businesses and legal entity structures;
(d) must ensure that the framework includes appropriate processes and controls to identify and address potential intragroup conflicts of interest (such as those arising from intragroup transactions);
(e) must approve policies and clear strategies for establishing new structures and legal entities, and must ensure that the policies and strategies are consistent with the policies and interests of the group;
(f) must assess whether there are effective systems to exchange information among the various entities, to manage the risks of the subsidiaries and of the group as a whole, and to ensure that the group is effectively supervised;
(g) must allocate sufficient resources to monitor the subsidiaries’ compliance with all applicable legal, regulatory and governance requirements;
(h) must maintain an effective relationship with the Regulatory Authority and, through the subsidiaries’ boards or direct contact, with the regulators of all of the subsidiaries; and
(i) must establish an effective internal audit function that ensures that audits are carried out within or for all the subsidiaries and parts of the group and the group as a whole.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.22 Specific obligations — approving and updating strategic and business plans
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.B Board of directors — role and obligations
DMEX 4.2.22 Specific obligations — approving and updating strategic and business plans
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s board of directors:
(a) must approve a strategic plan and a business plan, each appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of the entity’s business; and
(b) must update the plans regularly to take account of changes in the business environment.
(2) The plans may be combined in 1 document.
Note There is a separate requirement for a business resilience and continuity plan — see rule 4.2.26.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.23 Specific obligations — appointment etc of individual for senior executive function or internal auditor
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.B Board of directors — role and obligations
DMEX 4.2.23 Specific obligations — appointment etc of individual for senior executive function or internal auditor
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) This rule applies in relation to:
(a) an individual who is approved to exercise the senior executive function for an authorised market entity; and
(b) an authorised market entity’s internal auditor.
(2) A decision about the appointment, remuneration, disciplining or dismissal, or the assessment of the performance, of an individual in relation to whom this rule applies may be made only by:
(a) the entity’s board of directors;
(b) any relevant committee of the board; or
(c) the chair of the board, after consulting the board.

DMEX 4.2.24 Specific obligations — appointment etc of individuals for risk management function or compliance oversight function
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:

(2) A decision about the appointment, remuneration, disciplining or dismissal, or the assessment of the performance, of an individual in relation to whom this rule applies may be made only by: (a) the entity’s board of directors ; (b) any relevant committee of the board; or (c) the entity’s senior management, after consulting the board or any relevant committee of the board. QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.25 Specific obligations — remuneration policy
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.B Board of directors — role and obligations
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s board of directors must establish and maintain, for itself and the whole entity, a remuneration policy that is appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of the entity’s business.
Note Appropriate records must be kept of the entity’s remuneration policies and procedures — see GENE, rule 6.1.1.
(2) The policy must set out the entity’s remuneration arrangements, including:
(a) the objectives and structure of any performance-based component;
(b) performance measures that are in line with the entity’s risk management strategy;
(c) the forms and mix of remuneration; and
Examples
1 fixed and variable components
2 cash and equity-related benefits
3 termination payments.
(d) eligibility for, and the timing of, payments.
(3) The policy:
(a) must be aligned with the entity’s culture, its risk appetite statement, its long-term strategic direction and viability, its financial goals and its overall safety and soundness; and
Note For the requirement for a risk appetite statement, see rule 7.1.3 (4) (a).
(b) must appropriately balance risk and reward.
(4) The forms and mix of remuneration (in particular, performance-based remuneration) must be consistent with sound risk management.
(5) The timing of payments must take into account the timeframes within which risks associated with individuals’ performance are likely to materialise.
(6) The policy must permit any performance-based component of an individual’s remuneration (or such a component of the remuneration of a class of individuals) to be deferred or reduced (including reduced to zero) if necessary:
(a) to protect the entity’s financial soundness; or
(b) to respond to significant unexpected or unintended consequences of the entity’s activities.
(7) If the policy provides for part of an individual’s remuneration to be based on his or her performance, it must provide for that part to be repayable to the entity by an individual who has received it, if the entity later becomes satisfied that:
(a) the individual failed to meet the relevant performance measures; or
(b) by excessive risk-taking, he or she contributed significantly to a negative financial performance by the entity.
(8) The policy must prohibit an individual who has received deferred remuneration in the form of equity in the entity, or in any other form that is linked to the entity’s equity, from hedging his or her economic exposures to the resultant equity price risk before the equity or other remuneration is fully vested.
(9) A remuneration package offered by the entity (including any performance-based component):
(a) must encourage behaviour that supports the entity’s long-term financial soundness and its risk management strategy;
(b) must align remuneration with prudence in risk-taking; and
(c) must incorporate adjustments to reflect:
(i) the outcomes of the entity’s activities;
(ii) the risks related to those activities, taking into account the cost of the associated capital; and
(iii) the time necessary for the outcomes of those activities to be reliably measured.
(10) The remuneration of the non-executive directors of an authorised CCP must not be linked to the CCP’s business performance.
(11) The entity’s board must periodically review the remuneration policy.
Guidance
1 Guaranteed bonuses should generally not be offered because such bonuses are not consistent with sound risk management and performance-based rewards.
2 Remuneration payments should be linked to performance over time and should be designed in a way that does not reward failure.
3 Any deferral of payment to an individual must take into account the risks associated with his or her performance that may materialise during the period of deferment — for example:
• the risk of an increase in the cost of capital required to support the risks that he or she took
• uncertainties in the timing and likelihood of future revenues and expenses).
4 The application of any deferral of payment may vary depending on:
• the level of seniority or responsibility of the individual to whom the payment is due
• the nature of risks to which the entity is exposed
• any other relevant matters.
5 Nothing in rule 4.2.25 prevents an entity from adopting the remuneration policy of a member of the entity’s corporate group, provided that:
• the policy is approved by the entity’s board
• the policy complies with rule 4.2.25.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.26 Specific obligations — business resilience and continuity plan
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.B Board of directors — role and obligations
DMEX 4.2.26 Specific obligations — business resilience and continuity plan
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s board of directors must approve a business resilience and continuity plan to ensure, so far as practicable, that, in the event of an interruption, the entity can continue to fulfil its obligations under the law applicable in the QFC.
Note 1 For the requirements as to the plan’s content, see rule 7.1.13.
Note 2 For the meaning of law applicable in the QFC, see the glossary.
(2) The board must keep the plan under review and must ensure that the plan is tested at intervals determined by the board.
(3) The interval between tests must be appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of the entity’s business but must not be longer than 18 months.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.27 Specific obligations — avoiding or mitigating conflicts of interest
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.B Board of directors — role and obligations
DMEX 4.2.27 Specific obligations — avoiding or mitigating conflicts of interest
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s board of directors must ensure that each part of the entity’s corporate governance framework, and each part of its risk management framework, is designed:
(a) to avoid conflicts of interest (or to mitigate such conflicts if it is not possible to avoid them); and
(b) to deal effectively with any conflict of interest that arises.
(2) The frameworks must require that:
(a) any conflict of interest that arises must be reported:
(i) to the entity’s senior management; and
(ii) if it is not addressed within a reasonable time by the senior management, to the board; and
(b) every 6 months, the entity’s senior management must give the board a written summary of all the conflicts of interest that the senior management addressed during the previous 6 months.
(3) In this rule and rule 4.2.28, a reference to an entity’s board of directors may be read as a reference to any board committee or other body (whatever it is called) that is responsible for the entity’s corporate governance framework and risk management framework in relation to conflicts of interest and periodic review.
Guidance
A conflict of interest involving a member of the entity’s board of directors is to be dealt with under the board’s own conflicts policy, governance manual or terms of reference.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.28 Specific obligations — periodic review of corporate governance framework
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.B Board of directors — role and obligations
DMEX 4.2.28 Specific obligations — periodic review of corporate governance framework
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s board of directors must ensure that the entity’s corporate governance framework and risk management framework are reviewed at least once in every 3 years by:
(a) the entity’s internal auditor; or
(b) an independent and objective external reviewer.
Note For the meaning of board of directors in this rule, see rule 4.2.27 (3).
(2) The person who carries out the review must report in writing to the board within 30 days after the review is completed.
(3) The entity must give a copy of the report to the Regulatory Authority within 30 days after the board receives the report.
(4) The Authority may direct an authorised market entity to carry out more frequent reviews than subrule (1) requires.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.B Board of directors — role and obligations
DMEX 4.2.30 Specific obligations — independence of certain employees
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity’s board of directors must ensure that each employee to whom a responsibility is allocated within the entity’s internal controls and assurance framework is sufficiently free from influence for the framework to be effective in achieving its purposes.

Note For the requirements relating to an authorised market entity’s internal controls and assurance framework, see Part 5.2.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.31 Obligations of individual members of board of directors
doc_path: DMEX Division 4.2.B Board of directors — role and obligations
DMEX 4.2.31 Obligations of individual members of board of directors
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
A member of an authorised market entity’s board of directors:

(a) must act in good faith, honestly and reasonably;
(b) must exercise due care and diligence;
(c) must act in the best interests of the entity and the entity’s members, clients and customers, putting those interests ahead of his or her own interests;
(d) must exercise independent judgment and objectivity in decision-making, taking proper account of the interests of the entity and its members, clients and customers; and
(e) must not use his or her position to gain undue personal advantage or cause detriment to the entity.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.32 Board committees to be established
doc_path: DMEX 4.2.32 Board committees to be established
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s board of directors must establish the following committees:
(a) a nominations committee;
(b) a remuneration committee;
(c) an audit committee;
(d) a risk committee.
(2) The chair of each committee must be an independent non-executive director.
(3) With the written approval of the Regulatory Authority, the entity:
(a) may combine the nominations committee and the remuneration committee; and
(b) may combine the audit committee and the risk committee.
(4) Each committee must have clear terms of reference setting out its role and objectives and the authority delegated to it by the board.
(5) Each committee:
(a) must report regularly to the board; and
(b) must circulate its minutes to every member of the board.

An authorised market entity’s nominations committee is to be responsible for making recommendations to the board for the appointment of new board members, individuals to exercise the senior executive function, and members of the entity’s senior management.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.34 Remuneration committee
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s remuneration committee is to be responsible for developing, adopting and overseeing a remuneration policy for the entity, and in particular for the remuneration of the board members and senior management.
Note For the requirements about the remuneration policy, see rule 4.2.25.
(2) All of the members of the remuneration committee must be non-executive directors.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.35 Audit committee
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s audit committee is to be responsible for:
(a) adopting and overseeing the entity’s policy on internal audit and financial reporting;
(b) reviewing the results of the audit process with management and external auditors;
(c) overseeing the entity’s internal auditors and interacting with the external auditors;
(d) making decisions (or recommendations to the board or shareholders) about the appointment, remuneration and dismissal of external auditors;
(e) reviewing and approving the scope and frequency of audit;
(f) receiving significant audit reports and ensuring that the entity’s senior management promptly takes any corrective action that is necessary to address control weaknesses, non-compliance with policies, laws and regulations, and other problems;
(g) overseeing the establishment of accounting policies and practices;
(h) reviewing third-party opinions on the design and effectiveness of the overall internal controls and assurance framework; and
(i) if the entity is an authorised Islamic market entity:
(i) reviewing the effectiveness of its systems and controls for monitoring compliance with Shari’a (including reviewing the reports of internal Shari’a reviews and the Shari’a supervisory board to ensure that appropriate action has been taken); and
(ii) ensuring that the entity’s reporting of financial information complies with internationally recognised accounting standards that comply with Shari’a.
(2) A majority of the members of the audit committee must be non-executive directors.
(3) The chair of the board must not be a member of the audit committee.
(4) The audit committee must meet at least 4 times a year.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.36 Risk committee
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s risk committee is to be responsible for:
(a) advising the board on the entity’s overall risk appetite, overseeing senior management’s implementation of the entity’s risk management strategy, reporting on the entity’s risk culture, and interacting with and overseeing the entity’s risk management function;
Note For the requirements relating to the risk management strategy, see rule 7.1.6.
(b) overseeing the entity’s strategies for:
(i) the management of the entity’s capital and liquidity; and
(ii) dealing with all the relevant risks;
to ensure that the strategies are consistent with the entity’s risk appetite; and
(c) receiving regular reports about:
(i) the entity’s risk profile;
(ii) measurement against the approved risk appetite and risk limits; and
(iii) any breaches of risk limits and action taken as a result of such breaches.
(2) A majority of the members of the risk committee must be non-executive directors.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.37 Risk committee — additional requirements for authorised CCPs
doc_path: DMEX 4.2.37 Risk committee — additional requirements for authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP’s risk committee must include at least 1 independent non-executive director.
(2) The committee chair is to be an independent non-executive director of the CCP.
(3) The CCP’s management must not attempt to influence the committee’s advice.
(4) The CCP’s board must clearly determine:
(a) the committee’s mandate;
(b) governance arrangements to ensure that the committee is able to advise the board independently;
(c) the committee’s operational procedures; and
(d) in relation to the members referred to in rule 4.2.38:
(i) the admission criteria; and
(ii) the election procedures for those members.
(5) The committee’s governance arrangements must provide that:
(a) the committee is to report directly to the board rather than to the chief executive officer; and
(b) the committee is to meet regularly.
(6) The members of the committee must keep their proceedings confidential (except for appropriate reporting to the board and the Regulatory Authority).
(7) If the committee chair determines that a member has an actual or potential conflict of interest in relation to a matter that is before the committee, that member must not vote on the matter.
(8) An authorised CCP must promptly inform the Authority of any decision of the CCP’s board in which the board decided not to follow the committee’s advice.
