QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.content_text: (1) An authorised CCP’s risk committee must include at least 1 independent non-executive director . (2) The committee chair is to be an independent non-executive director of the CCP. (3) The CCP’s management must not attempt to influence the committee’s advice. (4) The CCP’s board must clearly determine: (a) the committee’s mandate; (b) governance arrangements to ensure that the committee is able to advise the board independently; (c) the committee’s operational procedures; and (d) in relation to the members referred to in rule 4.2.38 : (i) the admission criteria; and (ii) the election procedures for those members . QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.38 Risk committee of CCP — representatives of clearing members
doc_path: DMEX 4.2.38 Risk committee of CCP — representatives of clearing members
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must appoint:
(a) at least 1 representative of its clearing members; and
(b) at least 1 representative of its clients;
to its risk committee as members.
(2) Neither the representatives of the clearing members nor the representatives of the CCP’s clients (nor the total of both together) are to be a majority of the committee’s members.
(3) The appointment by an authorised CCP of a member of its risk committee under subrule (1) does not constitute the member as a member of the CCP’s board. The member may speak and vote at the committee’s meetings.
(4) To avoid doubt, rule 4.2.37 (6) and (7) apply to a member appointed under subrule (1).

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.2.39 Risk committee of CCP — employees as observers
doc_path: DMEX 4.2.39 Risk committee of CCP — employees as observers
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP’s risk committee may invite employees of the CCP and external independent experts to attend its meetings as observers.
(2) The appointment of an observer to the risk committee under subrule (1) does not constitute the observer as a member of the committee. Such an observer may speak but not vote at its meetings.
(3) Rule 4.2.37 (6) applies to such an observer as if he or she were a member of the committee.

The Regulatory Authority may attend the meetings of an authorised CCP’s risk committee as an observer and may require the entity to inform the Authority of the committee’s activities and decisions. A representative of the Authority may speak at the committee’s meetings but may not vote.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX Part 4.3 Senior management — role and obligations
doc_path: DMEX Part 4.3 Senior management — role and obligations
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
Notes for Part 4.3

1 The senior management of an authorised market entity is made up of the individuals who are approved to exercise the controlled functions mentioned in rule 4.3.1.
2 The individuals who are approved to exercise the internal control and assurance functions (risk management function, compliance oversight function and internal audit function) also form part of an authorised market entity’s senior management, and those controlled functions are specifically further dealt with in in Chapter 5. That Chapter also contains the general provisions about the performance of controlled functions for an authorised market entity and the application of INDI.
3 The individual who is approved to exercise the MLRO function is also a member of senior management. For the MLRO function, see the Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism Rules 2019, which apply to an authorised market entity — see rule 1.1.7 (2).

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.3.1 What is authorised market entity’s senior management?
doc_path: DMEX Part 4.3 Senior management — role and obligations
DMEX 4.3.1 What is authorised market entity’s senior management?
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity’s senior management is made up of:

(a) each individual who is approved to exercise 1 or more of the following controlled functions for the entity:
(i) the senior executive function;
(ii) the finance function;
(iii) the senior management function;
(iv) the MLRO function;
(v) the risk management function;
(vi) the compliance oversight function;
(vii) the internal audit function; and
(b) any other individual who, in the Regulatory Authority’s opinion, has overall responsibility for the day-to-day management of the entity’s business in or from the QFC.
Guidance
1 FSR, article 31 (2), provides that, subject to that article, the Regulatory Authority may:
“(a) impose or vary such conditions, restrictions and requirements on an Authorisation as the Regulatory Authority shall consider appropriate; or
(b) require a Person specified in the condition, restriction or requirement to take or refrain from taking such action as the Regulatory Authority considers appropriate …”.
2 For this Part, the powers in FSR article 31 enable the Authority, for example, to direct an entity:
• to appoint an individual who is ordinarily resident in Qatar to exercise a controlled function, even if this Part does not require the individual to be so resident
• to appoint an individual to exercise a controlled function even if this Part does not require the entity to appoint such an individual.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.3.2 Senior management’s collective responsibilities
doc_path: DMEX Part 4.3 Senior management — role and obligations
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The members of an authorised market entity’s senior management are collectively responsible for implementing the corporate governance framework and risk management framework approved by the entity’s board of directors, and for overseeing the entity’s daily operations.
(2) The members of the entity’s senior management:
(a) must ensure that the implementation of the frameworks is in accordance with these rules;
(b) must discharge their management responsibilities conscientiously and prudently;
(c) must maintain clear decision-making procedures to the extent appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of the entity’s business;
(d) must actively promote a strong governance and risk management culture throughout the entity; and
(e) must establish and maintain policies and procedures that enable them to be satisfied that any individual who is to act for the entity is suitable to do so, having regard to:
(i) the role that he or she is to have in the entity; and
(ii) the law applicable in the QFC.
Note For the meaning of law applicable in the QFC, see the glossary.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.3.3 Duties of individuals towards entity
doc_path: DMEX Part 4.3 Senior management — role and obligations
DMEX 4.3.3 Duties of individuals towards entity
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
Each member of an authorised market entity’s senior management owes the following duties to the entity:

(a) to act for the entity’s benefit;
(b) to avoid any conflict between his or her interests and those of the entity (or, if it is not possible to avoid such a conflict, to mitigate it);
(c) to have, and to maintain, the knowledge and skills that are reasonably expected of an individual who holds a similar appointment, and carries out similar functions, in the senior management of the entity;
(d) to carry out his or her functions diligently.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.3.6 Allocation of responsibilities by individual who exercises senior executive function
doc_path: DMEX Part 4.3 Senior management — role and obligations
DMEX 4.3.6 Allocation of responsibilities by individual who exercises senior executive function
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The individual who exercises the senior executive function for an authorised market entity must give each other individual who exercises a controlled function (other than the executive governance function, the non-executive governance function or the MLRO function) for the entity a written document that sets out that other individual’s responsibilities.
(2) Each such other individual must acknowledge, in writing, having received that document, and must confirm in the acknowledgement that he or she understands those responsibilities and undertakes to carry them out.
(3) The allocation of a responsibility by the individual who exercises the senior executive function does not remove or reduce that individual’s duty to exercise oversight of the other controlled functions.
(4) The individual who exercises the entity’s senior executive function must not attempt, in a document referred to in subrule (1), to restrict, limit or compromise any right, duty, responsibility or authority conferred by these rules or any other Rules on an individual who exercises any other controlled function.
(5) The individual who exercises the senior executive function retains any responsibility that he or she does not specifically allocate.
(6) The scope of the responsibilities allocated to an individual who exercises a controlled function for the entity must not be less than the scope of the controlled function as set out in these rules and INDI.
(7) The individual who exercises the entity’s senior executive function must obtain the approval of the entity’s board of directors (or that of the board’s audit committee) of the content of the document given to the individual who exercises the internal audit function.
(8) The individual who exercises the entity’s senior executive function must consult with the board or the board’s risk committee in relation to the content of the document to be given to the individual who exercises the risk management function.
(9) The allocation of responsibilities referred to in this rule is separate from operational authorities and limits exercised by the individual who exercises the entity’s senior executive function and the entity’s senior management (such as limits on loan approvals, underwriting, claims handling, investments, or signing cheques).

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.3.7 Allocation of responsibilities to senior management
doc_path: DMEX Part 4.3 Senior management — role and obligations
DMEX 4.3.7 Allocation of responsibilities to senior management
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must allocate responsibility for all aspects of its business among the members of its senior management in such a way that at all times:
(a) every significant area of its business is subject to an appropriately senior level of management and supervision;
(b) the role, and the extent of the responsibilities, of every member of its senior management is clear; and
(c) the business and affairs of the entity can be effectively monitored and controlled by its senior management and board of directors.
(2) In adopting and maintaining management structures, the entity must take into account all the relevant factors, including the following:
(a) the nature, scale and complexity of each aspect of its business;
(b) any actual or potential conflicts of interest that may arise as a result of the allocation of the relevant responsibilities;
(c) the ability, qualifications and experience of the relevant senior managers.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 4.3.8 Records of allocation of responsibilities etc
doc_path: DMEX Part 4.3 Senior management — role and obligations
DMEX 4.3.8 Records of allocation of responsibilities etc
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must make a record of all allocations of responsibilities, and all adoptions of management structures. The entity must retain the record for at least 6 years after the allocation or adoption.
(2) If a responsibility is allocated to more than 1 individual, the entity must clearly show how the responsibility is shared or divided between the individuals. The records must show that the relevant members of the entity’s senior management are aware of, and have accepted, the allocation of responsibilities.

doc_path: DMEX Part 4.3 Senior management — role and obligations
DMEX 4.3.9 Management information and business plan
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must ensure that its senior management receives the information that is necessary to identify, measure, manage and control risks in a timely and reliable way.
(2) The entity must plan its business appropriately so as to identify, measure, manage and control risks.
Note The entity must have a written business plan that is regularly updated to take account of changes in the business environment — see rule 4.2.22.

doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX 5.1.2 Authority of certain controlled functions
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to:
(a) each individual who exercises an internal control and assurance function for an authorised market entity; and
Note For the internal control and assurance functions, see Part 5.2.
(b) each employee who is allocated responsibilities within such an entity’s corporate governance framework and its risk management framework.
(2) An authorised market entity must ensure that each individual to whom this rule applies has all of the following:
(a) the necessary authority to exercise the function or carry out his or her duties;
(b) access to all the necessary information, documents and records of the entity;
(c) appropriate access to the entity’s board of directors and senior management.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.1.3 Exercise of 2 or more controlled functions by same individual
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX 5.1.3 Exercise of 2 or more controlled functions by same individual
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) Subject to subrule (2), an individual may exercise 2 or more controlled functions for an authorised market entity if (but only if):
(a) the entity’s board of directors confirms to the Regulatory Authority in writing that it is satisfied that:
(i) the individual’s exercise of the functions in combination:
(A) does not give rise to any internal or external conflict of interest; and
(B) does not compromise the independence, objectivity and effectiveness of the exercise of any of the functions;
(ii) the individual’s combined exercise of the functions will not increase the entity’s risk of non-compliance with the law applicable in the QFC or any other applicable law; and
Note For the meaning of law applicable in the QFC, see the glossary.
(iii) it is appropriate, having regard to the nature, scale and complexity of the entity’s business, for the individual to exercise both or all of the controlled functions; and
(b) the Authority is satisfied that:
(i) the conditions in paragraphs (a) (i), (ii) and (iii) have been met; and
(ii) the individual can adequately exercise the functions in combination.
(2) An authorised market entity must not combine the internal audit function with any other controlled function.
(3) At least once in every year, the entity’s senior management must review:
(a) the entity’s policies, procedures and controls for combining the functions, including its procedures for assessing:
(i) whether it is feasible to continue to combine the functions;
(ii) the risk in doing so; and
(iii) the likely effect of doing so on the entity’s business; and
(b) the combined exercise of the functions, to satisfy itself that:
(i) the combined exercise does not compromise the independence, objectivity and effectiveness of the exercise of each function;
(ii) no internal or external conflict of interest arises;
(iii) the combined exercise has not increased, and will not increase, the entity’s risk of non-compliance with the law applicable in the QFC or any other applicable law; and
Note For the meaning of law applicable in the QFC, see the glossary.
(iv) the combined exercise continues to be appropriate, having regard to the nature, scale and complexity of the entity’s business.
(4) The senior management must report the results of a review under subrule (3) to the entity’s board of directors within 30 days after the review is completed.
(5) If the Regulatory Authority is satisfied that it is no longer appropriate for 2 or more controlled functions to be exercised for an authorised market entity by the same individual, the Authority may, by written notice, direct the entity to do either or both of the following:
(a) stop combining the functions;
(b) appoint 1 or more individuals to exercise any of the functions.
(6) In particular, the Authority may give a direction under subrule (5) if the Authority considers that:
(a) the continued performance by the individual of both or all the functions:
(i) is no longer appropriate, having regard to the nature, scale and complexity of the entity’s business;
(ii) has given rise, or is likely to give rise, to an internal or external conflict of interest; or
(iii) has compromised, or is likely to compromise, the independence, objectivity and effectiveness of the performance of any of the functions;
(b) the individual is performing any of the functions at a standard that is below the standard at which a reasonable person who has the necessary skills, knowledge and experience would be expected to perform that function; or
(c) the combined performance of the functions by the individual has impaired, or is likely to impair, the entity’s compliance with the requirements applicable to the conduct of its business in or from the QFC.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX Part 5.2 Internal controls and assurance
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.2 Internal controls and assurance
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
Note for Part 5.2

An authorised market entity’s internal controls and assurance framework is made up of the policies, processes, tasks, behaviours and other aspects of its organisation that, taken together:

• enable the entity to respond appropriately to business, operational, financial, compliance and other risks, and so facilitate its effective operation
• safeguard the entity’s assets and ensure that its liabilities are identified and managed
• ensure the quality of the entity’s internal and external reporting (which requires proper records and processes that generate a flow of timely, relevant and reliable information from internal and external sources)
• ensure that the entity complies with the applicable laws, regulations and rules, and with its internal policies.

DMEX 5.2.1 Objectives of internal controls and assurance framework
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity must establish and maintain an internal controls and assurance framework to ensure that:

(a) the entity’s business is conducted efficiently;
(b) the entity’s assets are safeguarded;
(c) fraud and other unlawful acts are prevented or detected;
(d) risk is managed effectively;
(e) the entity’s financial records are accurate and complete; and
(f) the preparation of the entity’s financial statements is timely.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.2.2 Independence of internal control and assurance functions etc
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.2 Internal controls and assurance
DMEX 5.2.2 Independence of internal control and assurance functions etc
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
The requirement in rule 4.2.30 (that each individual who exercises an internal control and assurance function is sufficiently free from influence to be effective in achieving the function’s purpose) is satisfied if reasonable measures have been taken to ensure that:

(a) no such individual is remunerated in a way that would tend to undermine his or her independence and objectivity in exercising the function;
Note For the requirements about the remuneration policy, see rule 4.2.25.
(b) no such individual is involved in performing a function that generates, or is intended to generate, revenue for the entity;
(c) no such individual is limited or restricted as to the matters that he or she can investigate or report on in the exercise of his or her function;
(d) the reports and conclusions of such an individual can be honest and candid, without fear of reprisal; and
(e) pressure or influence is not applied to such an individual to modify his or her reports or conclusions.
Guidance
An authorised market entity’s internal control and assurance functions cannot be effective unless their exercise is independent. Independent means, broadly, that the individual who exercises such a function is not subjected to pressure to mould or manipulate his or her conclusions or results. An internal control and assurance function that produces only results that are convenient to the entity’s board of directors or management would not be regarded as satisfying rule 5.2.2.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.2.4 Certain individuals’ obligation to raise matters promptly
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.2 Internal controls and assurance
DMEX 5.2.4 Certain individuals’ obligation to raise matters promptly
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) This rule applies in relation to every individual who is approved to exercise an internal control and assurance function for an authorised market entity.
(2) The entity’s policies, procedures and controls must provide that every such individual:
(a) must promptly raise significant matters directly with the entity’s board of directors, the chair of the board, or any relevant committee of the board; and
(b) must promptly tell any other individual to whom this rule applies if the first individual becomes aware of a risk that might have (or a number of risks that, taken together, might have) a significant effect on:
(i) the entity’s risk management strategy; or
(ii) the other individual’s functions.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.2.5 Reports about internal control and assurance functions
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.2 Internal controls and assurance
DMEX 5.2.5 Reports about internal control and assurance functions
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must ensure that each internal control and assurance function makes periodic written reports to the entity’s board of directors, or a relevant committee of the board, about the matters mentioned in subrule (2).
(2) The matters are the following:
(a) how each internal control and assurance function is performing against the entity’s policies, procedures and controls for the function;
(b) the shorter-term and longer-term objectives of each internal control and assurance function, and the progress made in achieving those objectives;
(c) the resources of staff, equipment, time and budget allocated to the internal controls and assurance framework and an analysis of the adequacy of those resources;
(d) any material deficiency, material weakness or material failure of an internal control and assurance function, and the response to the deficiency, weakness or failure.
Guidance
The board or committee could also take into account:
• reports by the internal audit function that cover the other internal control and assurance functions
• reports commissioned from third parties in relation the internal control and assurance functions.
(3) The board or committee must determine:
(a) how often such a report must be made; and
(b) how serious a deficiency, weakness or failure must be to require it to be reported under subrule (2) (d).
Note Under GENE, rule 4.1.3 (2) (g), an authorised market entity must immediately tell the Regulatory Authority about any material deficiency, material weakness or material failure in the entity’s internal control and assurance functions.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.2.8 What makes up authorised market entity’s risk management function?
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.2 Internal controls and assurance
DMEX 5.2.8 What makes up authorised market entity’s risk management function?
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s risk management function is made up of:
(a) the individual who is approved to exercise the risk management function for the entity;
(b) any other employees who are allocated to the function;
(c) the part of the entity’s resources (other than staff) allocated to the function;
(d) the entity’s risk management strategy;
(e) the entity’s risk management policies; and
(f) the records that the entity keeps in relation to risk management.
Note For the requirements relating to the risk management strategy, see rule 7.1.4.
(2) The purpose of an authorised market entity’s risk management function is to monitor and control the entity’s risk exposure.
(3) The risk management function must provide for the timely monitoring of, advising on, investigating and reporting on all reasonably foreseeable material risks.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.2.11 What makes up authorised market entity’s compliance oversight function?
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.2 Internal controls and assurance
DMEX 5.2.11 What makes up authorised market entity’s compliance oversight function?
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s compliance oversight function is made up of:
(a) the individual who is approved to exercise the compliance oversight function for the entity;
(b) any other employees who are allocated responsibilities within the function;
(c) the part of the entity’s resources (other than staff) allocated to the function;
(d) the entity’s compliance policies and procedures; and
(e) the records that the entity keeps in relation to compliance matters.
Note Appropriate records must be kept of policies and procedures — see GENE, rule 6.1.1.
(2) The purposes of an authorised market entity’s compliance oversight function are the following:
(a) to ensure that the entity complies with:
(i) decisions of the Regulatory Authority;
(ii) the entity’s internal policies, procedures and controls; and
(iii) requirements and standards applicable to the entity under the law applicable in the QFC or any other applicable law;
Note For the meaning of law applicable in the QFC, see the glossary.
(b) to ensure that the entity’s business is conducted ethically and responsibly;
(c) to minimise the risk of the entity or its facilities being used in the furtherance of financial crime.
Guidance
The compliance oversight function includes:
• monitoring and assessing the adequacy and effectiveness of the entity’s compliance policies and procedures
• participating in the process of approving new products or significant changes to existing products
• monitoring and assessing the extent to which it complies with those policies and procedures
• monitoring and assessing the adequacy and effectiveness of measures taken to correct any deficiencies
• reporting to the entity’s board of directors as necessary
• maintaining and updating the entity’s compliance policies and procedures in conjunction with the entity’s senior executive function and senior management
• providing advice and support to the entity’s senior executive function and senior management about compliance issues.
Note For the meaning of financial crime, see the Glossary.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.2.12 Authorised market entities to have internal audit function
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.2 Internal controls and assurance
DMEX 5.2.12 Authorised market entities to have internal audit function
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must establish and maintain an internal audit function.
(2) An authorised market entity’s internal audit function must be appropriate to:
(a) the nature, scale and complexity of the entity’s business; and
(b) the entity’s risk profile and legal status.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.2.13 Authorised market entities to have internal auditor
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.2 Internal controls and assurance
DMEX 5.2.13 Authorised market entities to have internal auditor
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity must have an individual who is approved to exercise the internal audit function for the entity.

Guidance

1 For an entity that is part of a corporate group, the corporate group internal audit function may be used to perform the function for the entity. This means that the entity is not required to have a dedicated resource for the internal audit function. The work to be undertaken by the internal audit function would depend on the agreed risk-based audit plan for the entity and the corporate group-wide auditor would be best placed to decide that work.

2 Nothing in this rule prevents an entity from appointing a corporate group employee to the internal audit function.

Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.2.14 What makes up authorised market entity’s internal audit function?
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.2 Internal controls and assurance
DMEX 5.2.14 What makes up authorised market entity’s internal audit function?
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s internal audit function is made up of:
(a) the entity’s internal auditor;
(b) any other employees who are allocated responsibilities within the function;
(c) the part of the entity’s resources (other than staff) allocated to the function;
(d) the entity’s audit charter and risk-based audit plan; and
(e) the records that the entity keeps in relation to internal audit.
Note For other audit requirements applicable to authorised market entities, see GENE, Part 9.5.
(2) The purpose of an authorised market entity’s internal audit function is to provide independent assurance of:
(a) the adequacy and effectiveness of the entity’s policies and procedures, and the documentation about them, for the entity as a whole, its corporate group, each subsidiary (if any) and each part of the entity (such as a business unit, business area or department);
(b) the reliability and integrity of information and the means used to identify, measure, classify and report such information;
(c) the accuracy and currency of the identification of risks and the agreed actions to address them;
(d) the safeguarding of the entity’s assets and the assets of its clients and other stakeholders;
(e) the existence of those assets;
(f) whether the entity’s assets are appropriately segregated from the assets of its clients and other stakeholders; and
(g) the performance of the entity’s external auditors, to the extent requested by its board of directors and consistent with applicable law.
(3) The internal audit function must carry out regular assessments of the entity’s internal audit policies, procedures and controls and incorporate any necessary improvements.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.2.15 Authority of internal auditor
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.2 Internal controls and assurance
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity’s internal audit policies, procedures and controls must provide that:

(a) the entity’s internal auditor, and any employee who is allocated responsibilities within the internal audit function, must be allowed access to, and must be permitted to review, any information, documents and records of the entity that he or she considers necessary to carry out an audit or other review; and
(b) the internal auditor has the authority:
(i) to undertake, on his or her own initiative, a review of any area or any function of the entity consistently with the internal audit function’s purpose;
(ii) to require an appropriate management response to an internal audit report, including the development of a suitable remediation or mitigation plan or other follow-up plan; and
(iii) to decline to undertake an audit or review, or take on any other duty, that he or she believes is inconsistent with the internal audit function’s purpose or the entity’s internal audit policies and procedures.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.3.1 Obligation to have proper market surveillance etc
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.3 Market surveillance and enforcement
DMEX 5.3.1 Obligation to have proper market surveillance etc
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must have rules, procedures and appropriate surveillance to ensure that its facilities afford proper protection to investors.
(2) In deciding whether an authorised market entity has complied with subrule (1), the Regulatory Authority may take into account the extent to which the entity’s rules and procedures, and its arrangements for monitoring and overseeing the use of its facilities:
(a) include appropriate measures to prevent the use of its facilities for abusive or improper purposes;
(b) provide appropriate safeguards for investors against fraud or misconduct, recklessness, negligence or incompetence by users of its facilities;
(c) enable users of its facilities to monitor their use of the facilities;
(d) enable users of the facilities to raise queries about any use of the facilities that they are reported to have made;
(e) enable users of the facilities to comply with regulatory or legal requirements; and
(f) provide appropriate arrangements to reduce the risk that the facilities will be used in ways that are incompatible with regulatory or legal requirements.
(3) In subrule (2):
appropriate, in relation to an authorised market entity and its facilities, means appropriate in relation to:
(a) the nature and scale of the facilities;
(b) the types of persons who will use the facilities; and
(c) the use that will be made of the facilities.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.3.2 When are arrangements appropriate?
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.3 Market surveillance and enforcement
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity has appropriate arrangements for monitoring and enforcing compliance with its rules if:
(a) the entity has the ability:
(i) to monitor and oversee the use of its facilities;
(ii) to assess its members’ compliance with its rules;
(iii) to assess the significance of any non‐compliance;
(iv) to take appropriate disciplinary action against a member that contravenes the entity’s rules;
(v) to suspend a member’s access to its facilities;
(vi) to refer members’ or others’ conduct to other appropriate authorities for possible action or further investigation;
(vii) to enforce its rules against users (other than members) of its facilities;
(viii) to retain authority over a former member for at least 1 year after the end of the member’s membership; and
(ix) to take action against a supplier of services to a member (for example, a warehouse) whose performance or conduct may be critical to ensuring that the member complies with the entity’s rules;
(b) the departments that are responsible for monitoring and overseeing the use of the entity’s facilities and enforcing compliance with its rules are appropriately located and managed and are adequately resourced; and
(c) the entity has arrangements to make disciplinary decisions (including any arrangements for hearings) and the arrangements for appeals from the entity’s decisions in those matters.
(2) A reference in subrule (1) to an authorised market entity’s rules includes, where appropriate, its settlement arrangements.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.3.3 Obligation to detect financial crime etc
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.3 Market surveillance and enforcement
DMEX 5.3.3 Obligation to detect financial crime etc
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must operate an effective market surveillance program and appropriate measures to identify, monitor, deter and prevent conduct that may amount to market misconduct, financial crime or money laundering on and through the entity’s facilities.
(2) If an authorised market entity has reason to suspect that market misconduct, financial crime or money laundering may have been committed on or through its facilities, the entity must immediately report the relevant facts to the Regulatory Authority in writing.
Note For the meaning of financial crime, see the Glossary.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.3.4 Discipline, monitoring and enforcement
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.3 Market surveillance and enforcement
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must have policies and procedures to ensure that:
(a) compliance with its business rules is monitored and enforced;
(b) complaints by or about its members are investigated;
(c) disciplinary action can be taken; and
(d) financial and other penalties can be imposed.
(2) The entity’s policies and procedures for monitoring compliance with its business rules must include:
(a) adequate oversight of activities conducted on or through its facilities; and
(b) processes to detect non-compliance.
(3) An authorised market entity must have policies and procedures for:
(a) investigating complaints to the entity about the conduct of persons in the course of using the entity’s facilities; and
(b) the fair, independent and impartial resolution of appeals against decisions of the entity.
(4) In the case of an authorised market entity that is an authorised derivatives exchange, the policies and procedures must include effective arrangements for monitoring transactions to identify disorderly trading conditions or market abuse.
(5) The entity’s policies and procedures for disciplinary action must include:
(a) a fair and clear policy on financial and other penalties; and
(b) processes for appeals.
(6) The entity may modify, withdraw or suspend a member’s or other person’s access to its facilities.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 5.3.5 Application of financial penalties
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 5 Controlled functions and internal controls and assurance framework
DMEX Part 5.3 Market surveillance and enforcement
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
If an authorised market entity’s arrangements under this Part provide for the imposition of financial penalties, the arrangements must ensure that any penalty paid is applied only in 1 or more of the following ways:

(a) to meet the expenses incurred by the entity in investigating the breach in relation to which the relevant penalty was imposed, or in the course of any appeal against the entity’s decision in relation to the breach;
(b) for the benefit of users of the entity’s facilities;
(c) for charitable purposes.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

doc_path: DMEX Part 6.1 Capital and other financial resources

DMEX 6.1.1 Monitoring financial resources — all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must have policies and procedures to enable it to determine and monitor whether its financial resources comply with the requirements in this Part. For that purpose, the entity must take the following matters into account:
(a) the nature, scale, complexity, activities and risks of its operations;
(b) the operational, counterparty, market and settlement risks to which it is exposed;
(c) the amount, composition and legal position of its financial resources;
(d) its ability to access additional financial resources if necessary;
(e) any other matter that is relevant and appropriate.
(2) An authorised market entity must monitor and manage the concentration of its credit and liquidity exposures to banks and its members.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

doc_path: DMEX Part 6.1 Capital and other financial resources
DMEX Division 6.1.B Financial resources — authorised derivatives exchanges
DMEX 6.1.3 Financial resources — authorised derivatives exchanges
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The minimum financial resources for an authorised derivatives exchange are:
(a) capital of an amount equal to half its estimated gross operating costs for the next 12 months; or
(b) another amount determined by the Regulatory Authority.
(2) For the purposes of calculating its capital requirements, an authorised derivatives exchange:
(a) must calculate its operational expenses in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standards (or other accounting standards approved by the Regulatory Authority); and
(b) must use the most recent audited information from its annual financial statement.
(3) When estimating its gross operating costs for the next 12 months, an authorised derivatives exchange must include any penalty payments for which it may become liable as part of any other arrangement (including an outsourcing arrangement) that is necessary to enable it to function as an authorised market entity.
(4) An authorised derivatives exchange must have sufficient liquid assets (in addition to the minimum financial resources required by subrule (1)) to ensure that there is no significant risk that it will be unable to meet its liabilities as they fall due. The exchange must maintain those additional financial resources at all times.
(5) The assets held by an authorised derivatives exchange to comply with this rule must be liquid enough and of high enough quality to enable the exchange to meet its current and projected operating expenses under a range of adverse scenarios, including adverse market conditions.
(6) If the assets are cash, the financial institution that holds them:
(a) must be a banking business firm authorised in the QFC or a bank authorised in the State of Qatar that is acceptable to the Regulatory Authority; or
(b) must be supervised by an overseas regulator that is acceptable to the Authority.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.1.4 Financial resources — authorised CCPs
doc_path: DMEX Part 6.1 Capital and other financial resources
DMEX Division 6.1.C Financial resources — authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The minimum capital for an authorised CCP is the greater of the following amounts:
(a) US $10,000,000;
(b) the sum of the following amounts:
(i) the capital required to cover its winding down or restructuring (see rule 6.1.6);
(ii) the capital required to cover operational risk and legal risk (see rule 6.1.7);
(iii) the capital required to cover credit risk, counterparty credit risk, market risk and business risk (so far as they are not covered by the CCP’s margins and default fund) (see rule 6.1.8).
(2) For the purposes of calculating its capital requirements, an authorised CCP:
(a) must calculate its operational expenses in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standards (or other accounting standards approved by the Regulatory Authority); and
(b) must use the most recent audited information from its annual financial statement.
(3) Capital that an authorised CCP holds for the purposes of complying with this rule must be capital that would qualify as tier 1 capital:
(a) if the CCP is an authorised Islamic market entity — under IBANK, Part 3.2, if the CCP were an Islamic banking business firm; or
(b) in any other case — under BANK, Part 3.2, if the CCP were a banking business firm.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.1.5 Calculating capital requirements — estimate of period required for winding down or restructuring
doc_path: DMEX Part 6.1 Capital and other financial resources
DMEX Division 6.1.C Financial resources — authorised CCPs
DMEX 6.1.5 Calculating capital requirements — estimate of period required for winding down or restructuring
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must estimate the period (in months) that would be necessary to wind down or restructure its activities. The estimated period must be long enough to ensure that, even in stressed market conditions, it would be possible to wind down or restructure the CCP’s activities in an orderly way, including reorganising its operations, liquidating its clearing portfolio or transferring its clearing activities to another clearing house.
(2) In estimating the period, the CCP must take into account the liquidity, size, and maturity structure of its positions, the types of approved derivatives that it clears and any possible cross-border obstacles.
(3) However, the estimated period must not be less than 6 months.
(4) The CCP must notify the Regulatory Authority of the estimated period.
(5) The CCP must revise its estimate of the period necessary for winding down or restructuring its activities whenever there is a significant change in the assumptions underlying the estimate, and must notify the Authority of the new estimated period.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.1.8 Capital requirements — credit risk, counterparty credit risk, market risk and business risk
doc_path: DMEX Part 6.1 Capital and other financial resources
DMEX Division 6.1.C Financial resources — authorised CCPs
DMEX 6.1.8 Capital requirements — credit risk, counterparty credit risk, market risk and business risk
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP’s capital requirement for credit risk, counterparty credit risk, market risk and business risk is the sum of the following amounts:
(a) to cover credit risk (including counterparty credit risk) — an amount equal to 8% of its risk‐weighted assets for credit risk (calculated in accordance with subrule (2));
(b) to cover market risk — an amount equal to its capital requirements for market risk (calculated in accordance with subrule (3));
(c) to cover business risk — an amount equal to the greater of:
(i) the estimate approved under subrule (4): and
(ii) 25% of the CCP’s annual gross operational expenses.
(2) For paragraph (1) (a), the amount to cover credit risk must be calculated:
(a) if the CCP is an authorised Islamic market entity — in accordance with IBANK, Parts 4.4 and 4.5, as if the CCP were an Islamic banking business firm; and
(b) in any other case — in accordance with BANK, Parts 4.4 and 4.5, as if the CCP were a banking business firm.
(3) For subrule (1) (b), the amount to cover market risk must be calculated:
(a) if the CCP is an authorised Islamic market entity — in accordance with IBANK, Chapter 6, as if the CCP were an Islamic banking business firm; and
(b) in any other case — in accordance with BANK, Chapter 6, as if the CCP were a banking business firm.
(4) For subrule (1) (c) (i), for each financial year an authorised CCP must submit to the Regulatory Authority for approval an estimate of the capital necessary to cover losses during the year resulting from business risk, based on reasonably foreseeable adverse scenarios relevant to its business model. The estimate must be submitted before the beginning of the year.
Guidance
The capital required by rule 6.1.8 is not intended to cover losses referred to in rule 6.1.10.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.1.9 Reporting capital shortfall
doc_path: DMEX Part 6.1 Capital and other financial resources
DMEX Division 6.1.C Financial resources — authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) In this rule:
(a) the notification threshold for an authorised CCP is 110% of its minimum financial resources (see rule 6.1.4); and
Example
For an authorised CCP that is required to hold only the minimum capital of US$10,000,000, the notification threshold would be US$11,000,000.
(b) a reference to the capital of an authorised CCP is a reference to the total of its capital that would qualify as tier 1 capital (see rule 6.1.4 (3)).
(2) If the capital of an authorised CCP falls below the notification threshold, the CCP must immediately notify the Regulatory Authority.
(3) The notification must include:
(a) the reasons why the CCP’s capital has fallen below the threshold;
(b) a statement of the short‐term prospects for the CCP’s financial situation; and
(c) a comprehensive description of the measures that the CCP intends to take to ensure that it complies with rule 6.1.4 in future.
(4) The CCP must update the notification every week, until its capital is again above the notification threshold.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.1.10 Other financial resources — authorised CCPs
doc_path: DMEX Part 6.1 Capital and other financial resources
DMEX Division 6.1.C Financial resources — authorised CCPs
DMEX 6.1.10 Other financial resources — authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must maintain sufficient pre-funded available financial resources to cover losses that are greater than the losses to be covered by margin requirements and the CCP’s default fund. Those resources:
(a) must include dedicated resources of the CCP;
(b) must be freely available to it; and
(c) must be separate from the financial resources that the CCP uses to meet the requirement for financial resources in rule 6.1.4.
Note For the obligations of a CCP regarding margin, see rule 9.3.11.
(2) The additional financial resources referred to in subrule (1), together with the CCP’s default fund, must be sufficient at all times to enable the CCP to withstand, under extreme but plausible market conditions, the default of at least the 2 clearing members to which it has the largest exposures.
(3) An authorised CCP may require non-defaulting clearing members to provide additional funds in the event of a default of another clearing member.
Note An authorised CCP must also maintain a minimum level of liquidity to cover its liquidity risks. See rule 7.2.4.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.2.1 Employees
doc_path: DMEX Part 6.2 Other resources — all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) A reference in this rule to an employee of an authorised market entity includes any individual whose services are available to the entity to operate and supervise its facilities in connection with the entity’s business.
(2) An authorised market entity must have sufficient employees to operate and supervise its facilities.
(3) The entity must ensure that each employee:
(a) is fit and proper to perform his or her duties;
(b) is properly trained for those duties; and
(c) is properly trained in the requirements of the legislation applicable in the QFC.
(4) The entity must have policies and procedures:
(a) to satisfy itself that each employee is suitable to be an employee, having regard to the role that he or she has, or is to have, in the entity; and
(b) to ensure that each employee continues to be fit and proper to perform his or her duties.
(5) The entity must keep a record, for each employee, of:
(a) his or her fitness and propriety for the duties that he or she performs; and
(b) his or her training assessments.
(6) The entity must retain the record for an employee for at least 6 years after he or she ceases to be an employee.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.2.2 Information technology resources
doc_path: DMEX Part 6.2 Other resources — all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must have sufficient information technology resources to operate and supervise its facilities.
(2) The entity must satisfy the Regulatory Authority that those resources are established and maintained to ensure:
(a) their performance and capacity;
(b) their reliability and integrity;
(c) their security;
(d) the confidentiality of the data in the entity’s information technology systems; and
(e) the entity’s connectivity to its members.
(3) The entity must not give a person access to its facilities unless the person’s information technology systems are compatible with those of the entity.
(4) The entity must have policies and procedures to evaluate, select and monitor its information technology systems. The policies and procedures must provide for:
(a) problem management and systems change;
(b) the testing of the systems before going live, in accordance with internationally accepted testing standards;
(c) monitoring and reporting on the systems’ performance, availability and integrity;
(d) adequate measures to ensure:
(i) that the systems are resilient and not failure-prone;
(ii) that the entity’s business can continue even if a system fails;
(iii) that the systems are protected from damage, tampering, misuse and unauthorised access; and
(iv) the integrity of data that is part of, or is being processed through, the systems; and
(e) any other matter that is necessary to evaluate, select and monitor the systems.
(5) The entity must comply with the requirements in Schedule 1 for the purposes of:
(a) testing the adequacy and effectiveness of its own systems; and
(b) assessing the adequacy and effectiveness of its members’ systems.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.3.1 Meaning of outsourcing
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
In these rules:

outsourcing, for an authorised market entity, means an arrangement that involves the entity relying on a separate service provider (including a member of the entity’s corporate group) for the exercise of a function that relates to a regulated activity of the entity and would otherwise be exercised by the entity, but does not include the following arrangements:

(a) arrangements to provide advisory services (for example, the provision of legal advice), audit services, personnel training services, billing services, and physical security;
(b) supply arrangements and functions (including, for example, the supply of electricity or water and the provision of catering and cleaning services);
(c) the purchase of standardised services (for example, market information services and the provision of prices);
(d) the appointment of an employee of the entity’s corporate group to exercise a controlled function for the entity.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.3.2 Obligation to have outsourcing policy
doc_path: DMEX 6.3.2 Obligation to have outsourcing policy
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s board of directors must establish and maintain an outsourcing policy.
(2) The policy must at least provide for:
(a) whether the entity will outsource any function at all; and
(b) what functions may be outsourced.
Note Appropriate records must be kept of policies and procedures — see GENE, rule 6.1.1.
(3) A policy that the entity will not outsource any function satisfies subrule (1).
(4) The board must review, at least once in every 2 years, the entity’s outsourcing policy and procedures, including:
(a) its procedures for:
(i) assessing the feasibility of a proposed outsourcing and the risks that the outsourcing poses to the entity’s business; and
(ii) costing any proposed material outsourcing; and
Note Material outsourcing is defined in rule 6.3.6.
(b) the criteria for selecting service providers.
(5) In this rule and rule 6.3.3, a reference to an entity’s board of directors may be read as a reference to any board committee or other body (whatever it is called) that, or any individual (however the responsibility might have been delegated) who, is responsible for the entity’s outsourcing policy.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.3.3 Responsibility for outsourced functions
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The outsourcing of a function by an authorised market entity does not relieve the entity’s board of directors from any obligation in relation to the function under the law applicable in the QFC.
Note 1 For the meaning of “board of directors” in this rule, see rule 6.3.2 (5).
Note 2 For the meaning of law applicable in the QFC, see the glossary.
(2) The board remains responsible for ensuring:
(a) that all requirements are complied with in relation to the function; and
(b) that the function is otherwise properly exercised.
(3) The board must exercise due skill, care and diligence in carrying out its obligations in relation to outsourced functions.

endnotes: Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.3.4 Outsourcing arrangements
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity may enter into an outsourcing arrangement only if:
(a) the entity’s board of directors has approved the entity’s outsourcing policy; and
(b) the arrangement:
(i) is permitted by the policy;
(ii) will not reduce the entity’s ability to fulfil its obligations to depositors, policyholders, clients and other stakeholders;
(iii) will not increase the entity’s risk of non-compliance with the law applicable in the QFC or any other applicable law; and
Note For the meaning of law applicable in the QFC, see the glossary.
(iv) will not affect the Regulatory Authority’s ability to appropriately supervise the entity.
Example for paragraph (b) (iv)
The place where the service provider is located, or that place’s legal system, could prevent the Authority from appropriately supervising the entity.
(2) The arrangement must be in writing.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.3.5 Review of outsourcing of controlled functions
doc_path: DMEX 6.3.5 Review of outsourcing of controlled functions
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) This rule applies if an authorised market entity outsources the exercise of a controlled function.
(2) The senior management of the entity must review the arrangements for the outsourcing every year, to ensure that the independence, objectivity and effectiveness of the exercise of the function are not adversely affected.
(3) The senior management must report the results of the review to the entity’s board of directors.
Note The outsourcing of a function by an authorised market entity does not relieve the entity from any obligation in relation to the function (see rule 6.3.3 (1)). The entity’s board is ultimately responsible for ensuring that the entity carries out the entity’s obligations under these rules (see rule 4.2.12).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX Division 6.3.B Material outsourcing arrangements
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.content_text: DMEX Division 6.3.B Material outsourcing arrangements

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.3.6 Meaning of material outsourcing
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
In these rules:

material outsourcing, for an authorised market entity, means the outsourcing of a function of such importance that weakness or failure in the exercise of the function would cast serious doubt on:

(a) the entity’s ability to comply with:
(i) any regulations, rules or principles; or
(ii) any condition, restriction or requirement of its authorisation;
(b) its financial performance or position; or
(c) its ability to continue in business.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.3.7 Due skill in material outsourcing
doc_path: DMEX 6.3.7 Due skill in material outsourcing
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The senior management of an authorised market entity must exercise due skill, care and diligence in selecting, entering into, managing and exiting from a material outsourcing.
(2) Before entering into a material outsourcing, the senior management:
(a) must assess the risks that the outsourcing poses to the entity’s business; and
(b) must satisfy themselves that the service provider selected has the ability and capacity to perform the relevant function reliably and professionally at the start and during the life cycle of the outsourcing.
(3) For this rule, the senior management must take into account at least the following matters:
(a) whether the service provider is regulated, to what extent, and by whom;
(b) whether the function is subject to specific regulation or supervision;
(c) the risk that the service provider’s service may become unavailable because of the number of other persons using the service provider;
(d) the financial stability and expertise of the service provider;
(e) any conflict of interest that might arise from the provision of the function by the service provider.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.3.8 Written agreement for material outsourcing
doc_path: DMEX 6.3.8 Written agreement for material outsourcing
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The written agreement (required by rule 6.3.4 (2)) between an authorised market entity and a service provider for a material outsourcing must require the service provider:
(a) to deal with the Regulatory Authority in an open and co-operative way in relation to matters relating to the entity under the material outsourcing; and
(b) to grant the Authority access to the entity’s books, records and data in the possession or control of the service provider.
Guidance
The Authority expects authorised market entities to be able to demonstrate that the outsourced function is being performed effectively. The Authority may seek documentary evidence about the service provider’s performance.
(2) The agreement must include, if appropriate, provisions as to:
(a) the law applicable to the agreement;
(b) the reporting or notification requirements on the service provider and the means for measuring quantitative and qualitative performance by the service provider;
(c) access by the entity and its internal and external auditors to the entity’s books, records and data while they are in the possession or control of the service provider;
(d) the obligation to protect confidential information and personal data (that is, any information relating to an individual who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identification number or to 1 or more factors specific to the individual’s physical, physiological, mental, economic, cultural or social identity);
(e) the rules for subcontracting, if the arrangement permits it;
(f) the termination rights of each party; and
(g) contingency arrangements.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.3.9 Regulatory Authority to be notified of certain matters
doc_path: DMEX 6.3.9 Regulatory Authority to be notified of certain matters
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must not enter into a material outsourcing unless it gives the Regulatory Authority at least 30 business days’ prior written notice of its intention to enter into the outsourcing.
(2) If the outsourcing permits subcontracting to a third party, the entity must give the Authority notice of that fact.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 6.3.10 Additional information about material outsourcing
doc_path: DMEX 6.3.10 Additional information about material outsourcing
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The Regulatory Authority may, by written notice to an authorised market entity, require the entity to give the Authority, within a stated reasonable period, information about a material outsourcing (or proposed material outsourcing) that the Authority reasonably needs to enable it to decide whether the outsourcing complies with this Chapter.
(2) The power given by this rule is additional to the Authority’s other powers.
Note See for example FSR, article 48 (Powers to obtain documents and information).

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX Chapter 7 Risk management
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.content_text: DMEX Chapter 7 Risk management

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
Guidance
The Regulatory Authority will take into account an authorised market entity’s risk profile in assessing the appropriateness of the entity’s risk management framework, and the entity’s compliance with this Chapter. In particular, the Authority will consider:

• the nature, scale and complexity of the entity’s operations in the QFC
• whether or not the entity is included in a risk management framework for its parent entity or corporate group.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.1.1 What is risk management?
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
Risk management, for an authorised market entity, includes some or all of the following, according to the nature, scale and complexity of the entity’s business:

(a) identifying, assessing and reporting risk management information (including information dealing with issues of corporate strategy, mergers and acquisitions, and major projects and investments) to the entity’s board of directors and its senior executive function and senior management in a timely way;
(b) assessing risk positions, risk exposures, the steps being taken to manage them and, if appropriate, pre-defined risk limits;
(c) participating in the process of approving new products or significant changes to existing products;
(d) preparing periodic reports to the board setting out an overview of risk management during the relevant period, sending a copy of each such report to the entity’s internal auditor and making the report available to the entity’s external auditors;
(e) assessing risk events and identifying appropriate remedial action;
(f) assessing changes in the entity’s risk profile;
(g) identifying available resources to manage the entity’s risks;
(h) facilitating business continuity planning and disaster recovery for the entity;
(i) developing and maintaining external relationships relevant to risk management in the entity;
(j) developing and maintaining effective risk management communication within the entity;
(k) monitoring and assessing the adequacy and effectiveness of the entity’s risk management policies, procedures and controls.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.1.2 What is the risk management framework?
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
DMEX 7.1.2 What is the risk management framework?
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity’s risk management framework is the totality of systems, structures, policies, processes and people within the entity that identifies, measures, evaluates, monitors, reports on and controls or mitigates internal and external sources of material risks. Material risks are risks that could have a significant effect (financial or non-financial) on the entity, on its stakeholders or on the interests of its customers.

Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.1.3 Entities to have risk management framework
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
DMEX 7.1.3 Entities to have risk management framework
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must have a documented risk management framework.
(2) An authorised market entity’s risk management framework must enable the entity to develop and implement strategies, policies, procedures and controls to manage the different types of material risks, and must provide the entity’s board of directors with a comprehensive entity-wide view of such risks.
(3) The framework must be appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of the entity’s business.
(4) An authorised market entity’s risk management framework must reflect the entity’s business objectives and the business plan approved by the entity’s board of directors, and must include all of the following:
(a) a risk appetite statement;
(b) a risk management strategy;
(c) a risk-management function dedicated to the framework;
(d) a management information system to support the framework;
(e) a robust review process to ensure that the framework remains effective.
Note For the requirement for the board to approve the business plan, see rule 4.2.22 (1) (a).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.1.4 Risks to be addressed
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity’s risk management framework must address at least the following risks (so far as material to the entity’s operations):

(a) credit or asset risk;
(b) liquidity risk;
(c) market/investment risk;
(d) operational risk;
(e) strategy and planning risk;
(f) technology risk;
(g) cybersecurity risk;
(h) market conduct risk;
(i) money laundering and terrorism financing risk;
(j) compliance, legal, reputational and regulatory risk;
(k) any other risks that, singly or in combination, could have a significant effect on the entity.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.1.5 Risk appetite statement
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must have a documented risk appetite statement. A risk appetite statement is a high-level qualitative statement that clearly captures the entity’s attitude to, and its level of acceptance of, different risks.
(2) The entity’s risk appetite is the aggregate level and types of risk that the entity is willing to assume to achieve its strategic objectives and business plan. In setting its risk appetite, the entity must not breach its obligations or constraints determined by regulatory capital requirements, or liquidity or other needs.
(3) If appropriate, the statement must specify quantitative measures.
(4) The entity’s board of directors must review and approve the statement every year.
Guidance
The qualitative and quantitative measures referred to in this rule should reflect those expressed in the entity’s risk management strategy (see rule 7.1.6 (2) (c)).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.1.6 Risk management strategy
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s risk management strategy must be appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of the entity’s business.
(2) The strategy:
(a) must provide for assessing material risks;
(b) must set out policies and procedures for monitoring, prioritising and managing major risk exposures;
(c) must include both quantitative and qualitative considerations; and
(d) must provide for monitoring significant changes to the entity’s risk profile.
(3) The strategy must include:
(a) objectives and principles, and the allocation of responsibility, for dealing with risk across the entity;
(b) defining and categorising the types of risk to which the entity is exposed;
(c) processes (covering contingency planning, business continuity, crisis management and fraud) for identifying, assessing, monitoring, managing and reporting on risks;
(d) a process for obtaining and recording the approval of the entity’s board of directors of any material change to, or deviation from, the strategy; and
(e) a process for obtaining a direction by the board to settle any major question of the interpretation of the strategy.
(4) The entity must ensure that the strategy:
(a) is recorded in writing;
(b) is kept up to date to take into account new internal and external circumstances; and
(c) is reviewed at least once in every year.
(5) If the entity is part of a corporate group, the entity’s board must know the implications for the entity of any group-wide risk management strategy.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.1.7 Entities must provide appropriate training
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
DMEX 7.1.7 Entities must provide appropriate training
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity’s senior management must ensure that appropriate risk management training is available to employees at all levels throughout the entity. The training that is provided to an employee must be appropriate to the employee’s seniority, role and responsibilities.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.1.8 Independence of certain employees
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must ensure that each employee who is allocated responsibilities within the entity’s risk management framework is sufficiently free from influence for the framework to be effective in achieving its purposes.
(2) The requirement in subrule (1) is satisfied if reasonable measures have been taken to ensure that:
(a) no such employee is remunerated in a way that would tend to undermine his or her independence and objectivity in performing his or her duties;
Note For the requirements relating to an entity’s remuneration policy, see rule 4.2.25.
(b) no such employee is involved in performing a function that generates, or is intended to generate, revenue for the entity;
(c) no such employee is limited or restricted as to the matters that he or she can investigate or report on in the exercise of his or her function;
(d) the reports and conclusions of such an employee can be honest and candid, without fear of reprisal; and
(e) pressure or influence is not applied to such an employee to induce him or her to modify his or her reports or conclusions.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.content_text: (1) An authorised market entity must ensure that each employee who is allocated responsibilities within the entity’s risk management framework is sufficiently free from influence for the framework to be effective in achieving its purposes. (2) The requirement in subrule (1) is satisfied if reasonable measures have been taken to ensure that: (a) no such employee is remunerated in a way that would tend to undermine his or her independence and objectivity in performing his or her duties; Note For the requirements relating to an entity’s remuneration policy, see rule 4.2.25 . (b) no such employee is involved in performing a function that generates, or is intended to generate, revenue for the entity; (c) no such employee is limited or restricted as to the matters that he or she can investigate or report on in the exercise of his or her function; (d) the reports and conclusions of such an employee can be honest and candid, without fear of reprisal; and (e) pressure or influence is not applied to such an employee to induce him or her to modify his or her reports or conclusions. QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.1.9 Regular review of systems and controls
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
DMEX 7.1.9 Regular review of systems and controls
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must regularly review its systems and controls. The frequency of the reviews must be appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of the entity’s business, but a review must be done at least once in every year.
(2) The entity must submit written findings of each review to the entity’s board of directors. A copy of each report must be kept for at least 6 years after the date on which the report is submitted to the board.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.1.10 Cybersecurity risks
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must have systems and controls to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, that it is protected against, and resilient to, cybersecurity risks.
(2) The systems and controls must cover:
(a) governance in relation to cybersecurity risks;
(b) the identification of such risks;
(c) protection against cyber attacks;
(d) the detection of cyber attacks;
(e) the entity’s response to and recovery from cyber attacks;
(f) testing the relevant systems (see rule 6.2.2 (5) and Schedule 1);
(g) situational awareness; and
(h) learning and evolving.
(3) The entity must take into account, so far as is appropriate for the nature, scale and complexity of its operations, the guidance in the document Guidance on cyber resilience for financial market infrastructures, published jointly by the Bank for International Settlements and the International Organization of Securities Commissions in June 2016.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)
