QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.1.11 Management of general business risks
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
DMEX 7.1.11 Management of general business risks
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity must have robust management and control systems to identify, monitor, and manage general business risks, including losses from poor execution of its business strategy, negative cash flows, or unexpected and excessively large operating expenses.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.1.12 Operational risk
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must establish a robust framework to identify, monitor, and manage operational risk, with appropriate systems, policies, procedures and controls.
(2) An authorised market entity’s board of directors must clearly define the roles and responsibilities for addressing operational risk and must approve the entity’s operational risk management framework. Systems, operational policies, procedures, and controls must be reviewed, audited, and tested periodically and after significant changes.
(3) An authorised market entity must have clearly defined operational reliability objectives, and must have policies that are designed to achieve those objectives.
(4) An authorised market entity must ensure that it has scalable capacity that is adequate to handle increasing stress volumes and to achieve its service-level objectives.
(5) An authorised market entity must have comprehensive physical and information security policies that address all potential vulnerabilities and threats.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.1.13 Business resilience and continuity plan
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
DMEX 7.1.13 Business resilience and continuity plan
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must have a business resilience and continuity plan to address events that would pose a significant risk of disrupting its operations, including events that could cause a widespread or major disruption. The plan:
(a) must set out:
(i) objectives, policies, procedures and responsibilities to deal with internal and external business disruptions; and
(ii) measures to ensure timely resumption of service levels;
(b) must include policies and procedures for event and crisis management;
(c) must incorporate the use of a secondary site;
(d) must contain appropriate emergency rules for force majeure events;
(e) must be designed to ensure that critical information technology systems can resume operations within 2 hours after a disruptive event; and
(f) must set out business continuity procedures for its members and other users of its facilities after a disruptive or force majeure event.
Note The plan must be reviewed and approved by the entity’s board — see rule 4.2.26.
(2) The plan must be designed to enable the entity to complete settlement by the end of the day of a disruption, even in extreme circumstances.
(3) The plan must be subjected to periodic review and scenario testing.
Note The entity’s board has specific obligations in relation to testing — see rule 4.2.26 (2) and (3).
(4) The Regulatory Authority may direct the entity to test the plan at any time in a way that the Authority considers appropriate.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.1.14 Other operational systems and controls
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.1 Obligations of all authorised market entities
DMEX 7.1.14 Other operational systems and controls
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must identify, monitor, and manage the risks that key users, other market entities, and service and utility providers might pose to its operations.
(2) In addition, an authorised market entity must identify, monitor, and manage the risks that its operations might pose to other market entities.
(3) An authorised market entity must have an incident management procedure to record, report, analyse and resolve all operational incidents.
(4) An authorised market entity must have clearly defined operational reliability objectives and policies to achieve those objectives.
(5) An authorised market entity must have a scalable operational capacity adequate to handle increasing stress volumes, service‐level objectives and historical data.
(6) An authorised market entity must have a comprehensive physical and information security policy, standards, practices and controls to identify, assess and manage security threats and vulnerabilities and to protect data from loss and leakage, unauthorised access and other processing risks.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX Part 7.2 Particular obligations of authorised CCPs
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.2 Particular obligations of authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
Guidance — risk management

An authorised CCP is subject to the general risk management provisions in Part 7.1. However, because of the nature of a CCP’s business, certain special obligations apply to it.
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.content_text: Guidance — risk management An authorised CCP is subject to the general risk management provisions in Part 7.1 . However, because of the nature of a CCP’s business, certain special obligations apply to it.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.2.1 General obligation as to risk management
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.2 Particular obligations of authorised CCPs
DMEX 7.2.1 General obligation as to risk management
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised CCP must have procedures to identify all sources of risk that may affect its on‐going functions. It must consider the likelihood of potential adverse effects on its revenues or expenses and its level of capital.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.2.2 Operational risk management
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.2 Particular obligations of authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must have a well-documented assessment and management system for operational risk with clear responsibilities assigned for it. The system must identify the CCP’s exposures to operational risk and must track relevant operational risk data, including material loss data.
(2) The system must be reviewed regularly by an independent expert who has the necessary knowledge to do so.
(3) The system must be closely integrated into the CCP’s risk management processes. Its output must be an integral part of the process of monitoring and controlling the CCP’s operational risk profile.
(4) The CCP must implement a system for reporting to senior management that provides operational risk reports to relevant functions within the CCP. The CCP must have procedures for taking appropriate action according to the information in the reports.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.2.3 Legal risk
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.2 Particular obligations of authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must have a well-founded, clear and enforceable legal basis for every significant aspect of its activities in every jurisdiction in which it operates.
(2) An authorised CCP must have rules, procedures and contractual arrangements that are appropriate for the nature, scale and complexity of its operations, and are legally enforceable.
(3) An authorised CCP that operates in 2 or more jurisdictions:
(a) must identify and mitigate the risks that arise from doing business in each jurisdiction, including the risks that arise from conflicts between the laws in those jurisdictions; and
(b) must ensure that the rules, procedures and arrangements referred to in subrule (2) provide a high degree of confidence that actions taken by the CCP under those rules and procedures will not be reversed, stayed or rendered void.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.2.4 Liquidity risk
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.2 Particular obligations of authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP:
(a) must determine the minimum amount of liquid financial resources that it needs;
(b) must maintain sufficient such resources in all the relevant currencies to give it a high degree of confidence that it will be able to effect same-day, intra-day or multi-day settlement, as applicable, of its payment obligations, under a wide range of stress scenarios;
(c) must ensure that the resources held to meet its minimum liquid financial resources requirement are available when needed;
(d) must have a well-documented rationale to support the amount and form of the resources that it maintains for those purposes; and
(e) must make appropriate arrangements to ensure that it continues to maintain that amount and form of those resources.
(2) In addition, a CCP that is involved in activities with a more-complex risk profile, or that is systemically important in 2 or more jurisdictions, must consider maintaining additional liquidity resources sufficient to cover a wider range of potential stress scenarios that must include the default of the 2 users and their affiliates that would generate the largest aggregate payment obligation to the CCP in extreme but plausible market conditions.
(3) An authorised CCP must have a robust framework for managing its liquidity risks. The framework must enable it to manage liquidity risks arising from its users and other parties (such as settlement banks, custodian banks, and liquidity providers).
(4) The framework must include:
(a) rules, policies and procedures:
(i) that will enable it to meet its payment obligations on time even after an individual or combined default of its users and other parties mentioned in subrule (2); and
(ii) to address unforeseen and possibly uncovered liquidity shortfalls without the need to unwind or revoke transactions or delay settling its payment obligations;
(b) effective operational and analytical tools to identify, measure and monitor its settlement and funding flows on a continuing and timely basis; and
(c) rigorous due diligence procedures in relation to its liquidity providers, to provide a high degree of confidence that each provider:
(i) has sufficient information to assess, understand and manage its own liquidity risks; and
(ii) can perform as required by the provider’s commitment.
(5) An authorised CCP:
(a) must regularly review the adequacy of the amount that it has determined to be its minimum liquid financial resources;
(b) must regularly test the sufficiency of those resources by rigorous stress testing; and
(c) must regularly test its procedures for accessing its liquid financial resources at a liquidity provider.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.2.5 Liquidity requirements — general obligations
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.2 Particular obligations of authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) For the purpose of meeting its minimum liquid resource requirement, an authorised CCP’s qualifying liquid resources in a currency include:
(a) cash at the central bank of issue and at creditworthy commercial banks;
(b) committed lines of credit;
(c) committed foreign exchange swaps;
(d) committed repos;
(e) highly marketable collateral held in custody; and
(f) investments that are readily available and convertible into cash with prearranged funding arrangements that would be highly reliable even in extreme but plausible market conditions.
(2) If an authorised CCP has access to routine credit at a central bank, the CCP may count that access as part of its minimum liquidity requirement, but only to the extent that:
(a) the CCP has collateral that is eligible for pledging to (or for conducting other appropriate forms of transactions with) the central bank; and
(b) the credit will be available when needed.
(3) An authorised CCP may supplement its qualifying liquid resources with other liquid resources in other forms. However, those other resources must be in the form of assets that are likely to be saleable or acceptable as collateral for lines of credit, swaps, or repos on an ad hoc basis after a default, even if that saleability or acceptability cannot be reliably prearranged or guaranteed in extreme market conditions.
(4) Even if an authorised CCP does not have access to routine central bank credit, the CCP must still take account of what collateral is typically accepted by the relevant central bank, because such assets are more likely to be liquid in stressed circumstances. An authorised CCP must not assume, as part of its liquidity plan, that emergency central bank credit will be available to it.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.2.6 Liquidity providers — required due diligence
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.2 Particular obligations of authorised CCPs
DMEX 7.2.6 Liquidity providers — required due diligence
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must obtain a high degree of confidence, through rigorous due diligence, that each provider of its minimum required qualifying liquid resources (whether a user of the CCP or an external party):
(a) has sufficient information to understand and to manage its associated liquidity risks; and
(b) has the capacity to perform as required under its commitment.
(2) An authorised CCP may take into account a liquidity provider’s potential access to credit from the central bank of issue for a particular currency, if relevant to assessing the provider’s performance reliability in relation to the currency.
(3) An authorised CCP must regularly test its procedures for accessing its liquid resources at a liquidity provider.

DMEX 7.2.7 Liquidity management — use of central bank accounts

An authorised CCP that has access to central bank accounts, payment services, or securities services must use those services (if it is practicable to do so) to improve its management of liquidity risk.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.2.8 Liquidity management — testing
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.2 Particular obligations of authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must determine and regularly test the sufficiency of its liquid resources through rigorous stress testing.
(2) An authorised CCP must have clear procedures:
(a) to report the results of its stress tests to appropriate decision makers at the CCP; and
(b) to use these results to evaluate the adequacy of, and adjust, its liquidity risk management framework.
(3) In conducting stress testing, an authorised CCP must consider a wide range of relevant scenarios. The scenarios must include:
(a) relevant peak historic price volatilities;
(b) shifts in other market factors such as price determinants and yield curves;
(c) multiple defaults over various time horizons;
(d) simultaneous pressures in funding and asset markets; and
(e) a spectrum of forward-looking stress scenarios in a variety of extreme but plausible market conditions.
(4) The scenarios:
(a) must also take into account the design and operation of the CCP;
(b) must include all the other entities that might pose material liquidity risks to the CCP (such as settlement banks, nostro agents, custodian banks, liquidity providers, and linked market entities); and
(c) where appropriate, must cover a multiday period.
(5) In all cases, an authorised CCP:
(a) must document its supporting rationale for the amount and form of total liquid resources that it maintains; and
(b) must have appropriate governance arrangements.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.content_text: (1) An authorised CCP must determine and regularly test the sufficiency of its liquid resources through rigorous stress testing. (2) An authorised CCP must have clear procedures: (a) to report the results of its stress tests to appropriate decision makers at the CCP; and (b) to use these results to evaluate the adequacy of, and adjust, its liquidity risk management framework. (3) In conducting stress testing, an authorised CCP must consider a wide range of relevant scenarios. The scenarios must include: (a) relevant peak historic price volatilities; (b) shifts in other market factors such as price determinants and yield curves; (c) multiple defaults over various time horizons; (d) simultaneous pressures in funding and asset markets; and (e) a spectrum of forward-looking stress scenarios in a variety of extreme but plausible market conditions. (4) The scenarios: (a) must also take into account the design and operation of the CCP; (b) must include all the other entities that might pose material liquidity risks to the CCP (such as settlement banks, nostro agents, custodian banks, liquidity providers, and linked market entities); and (c) where appropriate, must cover a multiday period. (5) In all cases, an authorised CCP : (a) must document its supporting rationale for the amount and form of total liquid resources that it maintains; and (b) must have appropriate governance arrangements. Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.2.9 Obligation to measure and assess liquidity etc
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.2 Particular obligations of authorised CCPs
DMEX 7.2.9 Obligation to measure and assess liquidity etc
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) In as near as possible to real time, an authorised CCP must measure and assess its liquidity and credit exposures to:
(a) each of its clearing members; and
(b) any other CCP with which it has concluded an interoperability arrangement.
(2) An authorised CCP must ensure that it has access, in a timely way and on a non-discriminatory basis, to the relevant sources of price information to measure its exposures effectively.
(3) An authorised CCP must comply with subrules (1) and (2) without incurring unduly high costs.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.2.10 Credit risk management
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.2 Particular obligations of authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must establish and implement a robust process to manage:
(a) its current, and possible future, credit risk and market risk exposures to its users and other market counterparties; and
(b) credit risks arising from its payment, clearing, and settlement processes.
(2) An authorised CCP must regularly carry out:
(a) stress-tests using models that contain standards and predetermined parameters and assumptions; and
(b) comprehensive and thorough analysis of those models, and the parameters and assumptions, to ensure that the models are appropriate to decide the necessary level of default protection under current and evolving market conditions;
as appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of its operations.
(3) An authorised CCP:
(a) must undertake the analysis required by subrule (2) (b) at least every 2 months, or more frequently if:
(i) the transactions cleared or markets served display high volatility or become less liquid; or
(ii) the size or concentration of positions held by its participants increase significantly; and
(b) must carry out a full validation of its risk-management models at least once in every year.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.2.11 Stress-testing
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.2 Particular obligations of authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must maintain an appropriate programme of stress-testing.
(2) The programme must cover at least the following:
(a) identifying risks, including:
(i) sources of credit risk, and risks related to credit exposures and credit resources;
(ii) sources of liquidity risk, and risks related to liquidity exposures and liquidity resources;
(b) developing comprehensive scenarios, including:
(i) scenarios using historical data;
(ii) forward-looking scenarios;
(iii) the use of end-of-day, intraday and intra-period price and position movements; and
(iv) changes in relationships between products and asset classes;
(c) calculating and aggregating stress test results;
(d) the treatment of customer exposures.
(3) The programme must implement, so far as is appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of the CCP’s operations, the guidance in:
(a) section 3 of the document Final report — Resilience of central counterparties (CCPs): Further guidance on the PFMI, published jointly by the Bank for International Settlements and the International Organization of Securities Commissions in July 2017; and
(b) if the CCP is an authorised Islamic market entity — the IFSB’s guiding principles on stress-testing for institutions offering Islamic financial services.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 7.2.12 Custody and investment risk
doc_path: DMEX Part 7.2 Particular obligations of authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must have effective means to address risks relating to:
(a) the custody of its own assets; and
(b) its investments.
(2) An authorised CCP:
(a) must hold its own assets with authorised firms, or with 1 or more entities that are authorised or licensed by an overseas regulator to hold deposits or provide custody services, as appropriate;
(b) must be able to have prompt access to its assets when required; and
(c) must understand, and must regularly evaluate, its exposures to the entities that hold its assets.
(3) An authorised CCP must ensure that:
(a) its investment strategy is consistent with its overall risk-management strategy, and is fully disclosed to its users; and
(b) its investments are subject to minimal credit, market, and liquidity risks.
(4) The investments must be secured by, or be claims on, high-quality obligors, allowing for quick liquidation with little or no adverse price effect.

doc_path: DMEX Part 7.2 Particular obligations of authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised CCP’s business continuity plan must be designed to enable the CCP to complete settlement by the end of a day of disruption, even in extreme circumstances.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 8.1.1 Obligation to have rules
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must make rules in accordance with this Chapter. The rules must be clear and fair and must be legally enforceable against the entity’s members.
(2) A reference in this Part to an authorised market entity’s rules includes its business rules (which are dealt with in Part 8.2) and its default rules (which are dealt with in Part 8.3).
Guidance
An authorised derivatives exchange’s business rules include its listing rules (see rules 8.2.2 and 8.2.3). An authorised CCP’s business rules include its access rules (see rule 8.2.5) and its clearing rules (see rule 8.2.6).
(3) Nothing in this Chapter prevents an authorised market entity from combining its business rules and its default rules in 1 document.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 8.1.2 Making and amending rules
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) Before an authorised market entity makes rules:
(a) it must publish a draft of the proposed rules, and must invite comments from its members and other market participants on the draft;
(b) it must give proper consideration to any comments that it receives; and
(c) it must obtain the Regulatory Authority’s approval of the proposed rules.
(2) The Authority may, on application by the entity, dispense with the requirement for market consultation in exceptional cases, such as the following:
(a) urgent cases (that is, cases in which, because of time constraints, it is desirable and in the best interests of the relevant market for the rules to be made without consultation);
(b) minor or technical amendments, such as amendments:
(i) to correct technical or logical errors;
(ii) to correct inconsistencies or anomalies; or
(iii) to clarify a rule;
(c) if the Authority is satisfied that the delay that would be involved in holding the consultation would adversely affect:
(i) the financial system operating in or from the QFC; or
(ii) the interests of members or investors.
(3) Subrules (1) and (2) apply to the making of an amendment to existing rules. However, for an amendment to existing rules, the entity must also publish the text of the rules as they are proposed to be amended.
(4) When submitting a proposed amendment of its rules to the Authority, the entity:
(a) must set out the text of the amendment (including a marked-up version of the rules as to be amended, for comparison);
(b) must give an explanation of the reasons for the amendment; and
(c) must state the proposed effective date of the amendment.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 8.2.1 Rules about membership and members’ obligations

DMEX 8.2.1 Rules about membership and members’ obligations
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity’s business rules must set out the members’ and other users’ obligations:
(a) arising from the entity’s constitution and other administrative arrangements;
(b) when conducting activities on or through its facilities; and
(c) about professional standards that must be imposed on employees and agents of members and other users of its facilities.
(2) The business rules must include:
(a) criteria for:
(i) admitting members; and
(ii) giving other persons access to its facilities;
(b) a regime to prevent market abuse and financial crime;
(c) measures (such as transaction monitoring, risk assessment, training, and imposing financial or other penalties) to ensure that the entity’s members, and other users of the entity’s facilities, comply with the rules;
(d) appropriate provision for enforcing any limit-fixing direction that the entity issues;
(e) a statement that members and other users of its facilities may make a protected report under GENE, Chapter 4A, against the entity; and
(f) any other matters necessary for the proper functioning of the authorised market entity and the facilities operated by it.
(3) The rules must not include or approve any restrictive practice that may prevent effective competition for business in approved derivatives.
Note The rules must have been approved by the Regulatory Authority — see rule 8.1.2 (1) (c).

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 8.2.2 Rules about admitting approved derivatives to trading etc
doc_path: DMEX 8.2.2 Rules about admitting approved derivatives to trading etc
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) As part of its business rules, an authorised derivatives exchange must make clear rules (listing rules) about admitting approved derivatives to trading on markets that it operates.
(2) The listing rules must set out clear and objective criteria according to which approved derivatives can be admitted to trading, or traded, on its facilities.
(3) The listing rules must cover:
(a) how to apply for the listing of an approved derivative;
(b) decision-making on an application;
(c) procedures for admitting approved derivatives to the exchange’s official list, including:
(i) requirements to be met before an approved derivative is admitted to the list; and
(ii) agreements in connection with admitting approved derivatives to the list;
(d) procedures for enforcing the agreements referred to in paragraph (c) (ii);
(e) procedures for discontinuing or suspending a listing;
(f) standards of conduct that must be observed in connection with the admission of an approved derivative to the list and continuing the admission of an approved derivative to the list;
(g) anything that must be done, or not done, in connection with the admission of an approved derivative to the list or continuing the admission of an approved derivative to the list;
(h) how to deal with any conflict of interest that arises or could arise when a person seeks to have an approved derivative admitted to the list; and
(i) any other matters necessary or desirable for the proper operation of the listing process and of the market in approved derivatives admitted to the list.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 8.2.3 Rules about design of approved derivatives admitted to trading etc
doc_path: DMEX 8.2.3 Rules about design of approved derivatives admitted to trading etc
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The listing rules of an authorised derivatives exchange must ensure that the contract for an approved derivative that is to be traded on its facilities is designed so that the derivative can be priced in an orderly way and settled effectively.
(2) The listing rules must include all of the following design specifications for approved derivative contracts that are to be traded on the exchange’s facilities:
(a) minimum price fluctuations (price ticks);
(b) maximum price fluctuations (daily price limits), if any;
(c) last trading day;
(d) settlement procedures;
(e) trading months;
(f) position limits, if any;
(g) reportable levels;
(h) trading hours.
(3) The listing rules must require such a contract to satisfy the following conditions:
(a) its terms must be clear and unambiguous, and must enable a correlation between the price of the derivative and the price of the underlying;
(b) either:
(i) the price of the underlying must be reliable and publicly available or ascertainable; or
(ii) if the price is not otherwise publicly available — the contract must be likely to provide a means of disclosing to the market, or enabling the market to assess, the price of the underlying;
(c) sufficient information of a kind needed to value the derivative must be publicly available or ascertainable;
(d) the arrangements for determining the settlement price of the contract must be such that the price properly reflects the underlying or reference price.
(4) In subrule (3), a reference to the price of the underlying includes any other value measure.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 8.2.4 Error trades
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An error trade is the execution of an order resulting from either or both of the following:
(a) an erroneous order entry;
(b) a malfunction of the system of an authorised market entity or a member of such an entity.
(2) An authorised derivatives exchange’s business rules must include comprehensive error trade policies and procedures that set out the extent to which transactions can be cancelled:
(a) by the exchange at its sole discretion;
(b) at the request of a member; or
(c) with the consent of the members involved.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 8.2.5 Access rules
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) As part of its business rules, an authorised CCP must make clear and non‐discriminatory rules, based on objective criteria, to govern access to its facilities.
(2) The rules may provide for the CCP to refuse access to those facilities on legitimate commercial grounds.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 8.2.6 Rules about approved derivatives cleared etc
doc_path: DMEX 8.2.6 Rules about approved derivatives cleared etc
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) As part of its business rules, an authorised CCP must make rules (clearing rules) setting out clear and objective criteria according to which approved derivative contracts can be cleared or settled on its facilities.
(2) An authorised CCP must ensure that an approved derivative is cleared on its facilities only if it is traded on:
(a) an exchange operated by a recognised market entity; or
(b) a market in an approved jurisdiction.
Note For the approved jurisdictions, see rule 1.1.11.
(3) For the purposes of considering whether to allow the clearing of an approved derivative referred to in subrule (2) (b), the CCP may take into account:
(a) the degree of standardisation of the terms and operational processes of the approved derivative contract concerned;
(b) the volume and liquidity of the derivative; and
(c) the availability of fair, reliable and generally accepted pricing information for the derivative.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 8.3.1 Default rules
doc_path: DMEX Division 8.3.A All authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) Default rules of an authorised market entity are rules that enable the entity to take action on an unsettled market contract if:
(a) a member of the entity, or a person who has been granted access to the entity’s facilities, is a party; and
(b) the member or person is, or appears to be, unable to meet its obligations under the contract.
Examples of actions that may be taken
close-out open positions
discharge the rights and liabilities arising from contracts that a person granted access cannot, or may not, be able to fulfil.
(2) An authorised market entity must have default rules.
Note The rules must have been approved by the Regulatory Authority — see rule 8.1.2 (1) (c).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 8.3.2 Authorised CCPs — default rules
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) In this rule:
member of an authorised CCP includes a member that is another authorised market entity.
(2) An authorised CCP’s default rules must clearly define and specify:
(a) the circumstances that constitute a default (addressing both financial and operational default);
(b) how the CCP may treat different types of default;
(c) how to identify a default (including both automatic and discretionary default scenarios, and how, in a discretionary default scenario, the discretion is to be exercised);
(d) any changes to normal settlement practice in a default scenario;
(e) the management of transactions at different stages of processing;
(f) the expected treatment of proprietary and client transactions and accounts;
(g) the probable sequence of actions that the CCP may take;
(h) the roles, obligations and responsibilities of the various parties, including the CCP, the defaulting member and the CCP’s other members;
(i) how to address a defaulting member’s obligations to its clients;
(j) how to allocate any credit losses that the CCP faces as a result of a default;
(k) how stress events are to be dealt with;
(l) a regime to discharge the remaining rights and liabilities of a defaulting member and for the defaulting member to pay or be paid a sum of money determined, in accordance with the rules, by offsetting all the relevant rights, assets and liabilities on the relevant account;
(m) a regime for the certification by or on behalf of the CCP, separately for each account of a defaulting member, of the sum finally payable (or that no sum is payable);
(n) the CCP’s segregation and portability arrangements, including how to determine the value at which client positions will be transferred;
(o) provisions to ensure that losses that arise as a result of the default of a member, or threaten the CCP’s solvency, are allocated with a view to ensuring that the CCP can continue to provide its services, and conduct its activities, in accordance with its authorisation; and
(p) any other ways to contain the effect of a default.
Note An authorised CCP must establish a default fund — see rule 9.3.12.
(3) An authorised CCP’s default rules must set out:
(a) the amount that each member must contribute to the CCP’s default fund (or how to calculate that amount); and
(b) the arrangements for the payment of members’ contributions.
(4) The default rules may provide for the following in the event that a member of the CCP defaults:
(a) effecting the transfer and closing‐out of the member’s assets or proprietary or client positions to the CCP, a non‐defaulting member, a receiver, a third party or a bridge financial company;
(b) the auction of any position or asset of the defaulting member in the market;
(c) the application of the proceeds of liquidation, and other funds and assets of the member;
(d) the use of a default contribution fund to cover the obligation.
(5) An authorised CCP must review and test its default rules and procedures at least once in every year, and after any material change to the rules and procedures, to ensure that they remain practical and effective.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 8.3.3 Authorised CCPs’ default rules in relation to certain non-members
doc_path: DMEX 8.3.3 Authorised CCPs’ default rules in relation to certain non-members
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) In its default rules, an authorised CCP may make the same or similar provision, in relation to certain non‐members (designated non-members), as in relation to members.
(2) If an authorised CCP’s default rules make such provision, the CCP must have adequate procedures for:
(a) designating the non-members, or classes of non-members, in relation to which such provision applies
(b) keeping the designation of such a non-member or class under review; and
(c) withdrawing a designation.
(3) The procedures must be designed to ensure that:
(a) if a person’s failure to meet its obligations under a contract would adversely affect the operation of the market, the person is not, or does not remain, designated; and
(b) if such a failure by a person in a class of persons would adversely affect the operation of the market, the class is not, or does not remain, designated.
(4) The CCP must have adequate arrangements:
(a) for notifying a person or class that has been designated of the designation or the withdrawal of the designation; and
(b) if a class of persons has been designated, or the designation of a class of persons has been withdrawn, for ascertaining the persons that fall within the class.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.1 Adequacy and appropriateness of systems and controls
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
DMEX 9.1.1 Adequacy and appropriateness of systems and controls
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must ensure that its systems and controls:
(a) are adequate to ensure that its operations are conducted at all times in accordance with the law applicable in the QFC;
Note For the meaning of law applicable in the QFC, see the glossary.
(b) are adequate and suitable for the performance of its functions;
(c) are adequate to meet contingencies and disasters; and
(d) are appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of its business.
(2) An authorised market entity must have systems and controls for each of the following matters or functions:
(a) promptly and accurately transmitting information to the users of its facilities;
(b) identifying, assessing and managing its risks;
(c) the fitness and propriety of its employees;
(d) identifying and managing conflicts of interest;
(e) operating its functions;
(f) outsourcing;
(g) publishing price, volume and other market-related information;
(h) supervising and monitoring transactions effected on or through its facilities;
(i) how transactions are effected, cleared and settled;
(j) safeguarding and administering assets;
(k) internal and external audit;
(l) allocating responsibility for complying with decisions and directions of the Regulatory Authority;
(m) monitoring the adequacy of its resources.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.2 Organisation
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must establish internal management and organisational structures, policies and procedures, including:
(a) mapping out reporting lines;
(b) procedures for reporting and communicating information, policies and decisions to all relevant levels of the entity;
(c) clear and documented allocation of responsibilities;
(d) procedures to monitor and control delegation and outsourcing;
(e) segregating responsibility for functions in relation to which conflicts of interest may arise; and
(f) internal checks and balances such as hierarchical controls, cross-checking and joint responsibilities.
(2) The entity must document the policies and procedures and must communicate them to all of its employees.
(3) The entity:
(a) must adopt and document clear decision-making policies and procedures; and
(b) must establish internal mechanisms to ensure compliance with the policies and procedures required by subrule (1),
as appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of its business.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.3 Persons that may be admitted as members
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
DMEX 9.1.3 Persons that may be admitted as members
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity may admit a person as a member if the person is:
(a) an authorised firm;
(b) a State licensed entity;
Note For State licensed entity, see Chapter 10.
(c) a recognised firm.
Note For recognised firm, see rule 11.1.3.
(2) An authorised market entity may admit any other person as a member but must notify the Regulatory Authority if it does so.
Example of persons that might be admitted as members
a person that carries on the relevant activities:
• for its own account
• for the account of another legal person in the same corporate group, if the group’s main business is not the provision of financial services.
(3) An authorised market entity must not admit a person as a member under subrule (2) unless the person:
(a) undertakes in writing:
(i) to comply with the legislation applicable in the QFC in relation to the person’s use of the entity’s facilities;
Note For the meaning of legislation applicable in the QFC, see the glossary.
(ii) to submit unconditionally to the supervision of the Regulatory Authority, and the Authority’s disciplinary processes and procedures, in relation to any matter that arises out of or relates to the person’s use of the entity’s facilities; and
(iii) to submit unconditionally to the jurisdiction of the Regulatory Tribunal and the Civil and Commercial Court in relation to any proceedings that arise out of or relate to the person’s use of the entity’s facilities; and
(b) appoints an authorised firm or licensed firm as its agent to accept service of legal process in the QFC, and ensures that the appointment continues in effect while ever the person is a member of the market entity.
(4) In paragraph (3) (b):
licensed firm means an entity that holds a licence under the QFC Law, article 11, to carry on a permitted activity in or from the QFC.
(5) Before admitting a person as a member, an authorised market entity must undertake due diligence to satisfy itself that the person:
(a) is of sufficiently good repute;
(b) is sufficiently competent and experienced;
(c) has appropriate standards of conduct for the members of its staff who will be permitted to use the entity’s order entry system; and
(d) has organisational arrangements, and financial and technological resources, that are no less than those of an authorised market entity that provides similar financial services.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.4 Members’ access to facilities
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must not allow a person to have access to its facilities unless:
(a) if the person is conducting a regulated activity in or from the QFC — the person is authorised to conduct that activity; and
(b) the access is granted in accordance with the entity’s business rules and on the basis of criteria that have been approved by the Regulatory Authority and are designed to protect:
(i) the orderly functioning of the facilities; and
(ii) the interests of investors.
(2) If a member of an authorised market entity allows a client to have direct electronic access (for example, by allowing the client to use the member’s trading code) to the entity’s trading facilities, the member must adequately control the client’s access.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.5 General safeguards for investors
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must have policies and procedures, and an effective monitoring program, to ensure that activities conducted on or through its facilities are conducted in a fair, orderly and transparent way so as to afford proper protection to investors.
(2) The monitoring program must include systems for the coordinated monitoring of all activities conducted on or through its facilities and, so far as practicable, similar or related activities conducted elsewhere.
(3) The entity must ensure that there are policies and procedures:
(a) to prevent its facilities being used improperly, recklessly or negligently;
(b) to allow users to monitor activities conducted on or through the facilities, and raise queries about those activities; and
(c) to enable users to comply with regulatory requirements.

DMEX 9.1.6 Market abuse and financial crime — detection and reporting
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity:

(a) must operate measures to detect, deter and prevent market abuse and financial crime on or through the entity’s facilities; and
(b) must promptly report any suspected or actual market abuse or financial crime to the Regulatory Authority.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.7 Transparency
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must have policies and procedures for giving sufficient information to the users of its facilities to enable them to have an accurate understanding of:
(a) the risks of using its facilities; and

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.9 Handling complaints
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must have effective policies and procedures to investigate and resolve complaints made against it.
(2) Those policies and procedures must provide for:
(a) acknowledging a complaint promptly and fairly;
(b) considering the complaint objectively; and
(c) sending a timely response to the complainant.
(3) The entity must establish and maintain a register of complaints made against it and how each complaint is resolved. The record for a complaint must be retained for at least 6 years after the date on which the complaint is resolved.
(4) Any communication that an authorised market entity sends to the complainant in response to a complaint against it must state that if the complainant is not satisfied with the entity’s response, the complainant may report the matter to the Regulatory Authority.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.11 Authorised derivatives exchanges — notifications about proposed changes in approved derivatives traded

DMEX 9.1.11 Authorised derivatives exchanges — notifications about proposed changes in approved derivatives traded
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised derivatives exchange must give, to persons who have been granted access to its facilities, reasonable advance notice of any proposal of any of the following kinds:
(a) a proposal to admit to trading, on or through its facilities, an approved derivative that it has not previously traded, but is approved to trade;
(b) a proposal to suspend an approved derivative from trading;
(c) a proposal to restore an approved derivative to trading;
(d) a proposal to cease trading an approved derivative.
(2) An authorised derivatives exchange must give, to persons who have been granted access to its facilities, notice of any proposal to apply for the variation of its authorisation to admit to trading, on or through its facilities, an approved derivative that it is not authorised to trade.
(3) A notice under subrule (2) must be given when the exchange applies to the Authority for its approval of the variation, and must include the same information about the proposal as the exchange gave the Authority.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.13 How notifications to Regulatory Authority to be given
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
DMEX Division 9.1.E Obligations about notifications to Regulatory Authority
DMEX 9.1.13 How notifications to Regulatory Authority to be given
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) A notification to the Regulatory Authority required by this Division may be given:
(a) orally; or
(b) in writing;
whichever is more appropriate in the circumstances.
(2) A notification required by this Division must be in English.
(3) If an authorised market entity gives a notification to the Authority orally, it must confirm that notification in writing without delay.
(4) A written notification must contain the entity’s name and its authorisation number.
(5) A written notification must be sent to the Authority as follows:
(a) by email at the address specified by the Authority;
(b) delivered:
(i) by post to the current address of the Authority;
(ii) by hand to the current address of the Authority; or
(iii) by fax to a number specified by the Authority.
(6) A written notification must be signed by the individual who performs the senior executive function or the executive governance function for the entity concerned.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.14 Changes in core details
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
DMEX Division 9.1.E Obligations about notifications to Regulatory Authority
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity must give the Regulatory Authority reasonable advance notice of any change to any of the following:

(a) the entity’s name;
(b) any business or trading name under which the entity conducts an authorised derivatives exchange or authorised CCP in or from the QFC;
(c) the address of the entity’s principal place of business in the QFC;
(d) its legal structure;
(e) any material matter in relation to an approved individual, such as any of the following:
(i) the individual’s changing of his or her name;
(ii) the relevant controlled function being performed for the entity by a different individual;
(iii) anything relevant to an approved individual’s fitness and propriety.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.15 Events etc to be notified
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
DMEX Division 9.1.E Obligations about notifications to Regulatory Authority
DMEX 9.1.15 Events etc to be notified
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity must immediately notify the Regulatory Authority if it becomes aware, or has reasonable grounds to believe, that any of the following may have occurred or may be about to occur:

(a) anything affecting the entity that casts doubt on the entity’s fitness and propriety;
(b) anything affecting an approved individual who performs a controlled function for the entity that casts doubt on the entity’s or individual’s fitness and propriety;
(c) a matter that could have a significant adverse effect on the entity’s reputation;
(d) a matter that could result in serious adverse financial consequences to:
(i) the financial system operating in or from the QFC;
(ii) the QFC itself; or
(iii) another authorised firm;
(e) a proposed restructuring, merger, acquisition, reorganisation or business expansion that could have a significant effect on the entity’s risk profile or resources;
(f) any material change in the entity’s controllers;
(g) any action that would result in a material change in the entity’s capital adequacy or solvency;
(h) legal proceedings against the entity (in any jurisdiction);
(i) a change in delegations within the entity;
(j) a change in the entity’s fees or charges;
(k) an exercise of default rules by the entity;
(l) a significant failure in the entity’s systems or controls, including a failure report by its auditor;
(m) a contravention of a relevant requirement, and the action that the entity is taking to rectify the contravention;
Note Contravention of a relevant requirement is defined in the Glossary.
(n) a contravention of any of the authorisation criteria by the entity or any of its employees;
(o) disciplinary action against the entity in any jurisdiction;
(p) a significant contravention of a relevant requirement by a member of the entity;
(q) the inability of a member to meet a requirement of the entity.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.16 Fraud, irregularities and other misconduct
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
DMEX Division 9.1.E Obligations about notifications to Regulatory Authority
DMEX 9.1.16 Fraud, irregularities and other misconduct
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity must notify the Regulatory Authority immediately of any of the following:

(a) it becomes aware that an employee may have committed a fraud;
(b) it becomes aware that a member may have committed a fraud;
(c) it becomes aware that a serious fraud has been committed against it;
(d) it has reason to believe that a person is acting with intent to commit a serious fraud against it;
(e) it identifies significant irregularities in its accounting or other records, whether or not there is evidence of fraud;
(f) it suspects that an employee who is connected with the entity’s regulated activities may be guilty of serious misconduct that casts doubt on his or her honesty or integrity;
(g) it becomes aware of any serious market abuse or financial crime.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity must immediately notify the Regulatory Authority of any of the following:

(a) the granting or refusal of an application for, or the revocation of, the entity’s licence to operate an exchange or clearing house in a jurisdiction outside the QFC;
(b) the entity’s becoming aware that an overseas regulator has begun an investigation into its affairs or the affairs of any of its members;
(c) an overseas regulator’s appointing inspectors (however called) to investigate the entity’s affairs;
(d) an overseas regulator’s imposing disciplinary measures or disciplinary sanctions on the entity.

doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
DMEX Division 9.1.E Obligations about notifications to Regulatory Authority
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must immediately notify the Regulatory Authority if:
(a) it has investigated a complaint that has arisen in connection with its performance of, or its failure to perform, any of its functions; and
(b) the conclusion is that the entity:
(i) must pay compensation to a person; or
(ii) must remedy the matter that the complaint was about.
(2) The entity must prepare a report about its investigation and conclusion and must give the Authority a copy of the report (including any recommendations) as soon as practicable after it is finalised.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.21 Failures in backup information technology systems
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
DMEX Division 9.1.E Obligations about notifications to Regulatory Authority
DMEX 9.1.21 Failures in backup information technology systems
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must immediately notify the Regulatory Authority if a back-up information technology system fails in such a way that, if the entity’s main information technology system were also to fail, the entity would be unable to operate any of its facilities during its normal hours of operation.
(2) The entity must immediately notify the Authority of:
(a) the action that it is taking to restore the operation of the back-up system; and
(b) when it expects the operation of that system to be restored.

doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
DMEX Division 9.1.E Obligations about notifications to Regulatory Authority
DMEX 9.1.24 Disciplinary action taken against others
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must immediately notify the Regulatory Authority:
(a) at the start of any disciplinary action that the entity takes against a person for contravening its business rules; or
(b) of the lodgement of an appeal against any such action.
(2) A notification under subrule (1) (a) must include:
(a) the name of the person disciplined;
(b) details of the disciplinary action; and
(c) the entity’s reasons for taking the action.
(3) A notification under subrule (1) (b) must include the name of the appellant and the grounds of the appeal.
(4) An entity to which subrule (1) (b) applies must notify the Authority of the outcome of the appeal.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.25 Contraventions
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
DMEX Division 9.1.E Obligations about notifications to Regulatory Authority
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised market entity must immediately notify the Regulatory Authority if it obtains information tending to suggest that a person:
(a) has been conducting, in or from the QFC, an activity that contravenes the general prohibition in the QFC Law, article 10;
(b) has engaged in market abuse; or
(c) has engaged in financial crime.
(2) The notification must include the full details necessary for the Authority to investigate or assess the issue.
Note If an issue of financial crime arises, the Authority may be obliged, under the general law of Qatar, to report the matter to the prosecuting authorities of the State of Qatar.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.28 Winding up, bankruptcy and insolvency

DMEX 9.1.28 Winding up, bankruptcy and insolvency
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised market entity must immediately notify the Regulatory Authority of any of the following:

(a) the calling of a meeting to consider a resolution to wind up the entity;
(b) the making of an application to dissolve the entity or strike it from the register maintained by the Companies Registration Office of the QFC;
(c) the presentation of a petition for its winding up;
(d) the entity making, or proposing to make, a composition or arrangement with its creditors;
(e) the making of an application to commence insolvency proceedings against it;
(f) the appointment of a receiver, administrator or provisional liquidator to it under the law of any jurisdiction.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.1.30 Reports — general
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.1 Operating obligations — all authorised market entities
DMEX Division 9.1.E Obligations about notifications to Regulatory Authority
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) Unless a rule states otherwise, an authorised market entity:
(a) must include, in each report that it gives the Regulatory Authority, the entity’s name and authorisation number;
(b) must ensure that the Authority receives the report by 5 pm on:
(i) the day on which it is due; or
(ii) if that day is not a business day — the next business day after that day.
(2) A report is not taken to have been received by the Authority until:
(a) it has been received by email at the address specified by the Authority; or
(b) it has been duly signed by the signatories specified in the relevant rule (or in accordance with subrule (3)) and delivered:
(i) by post to the current postal address of the Authority;
(ii) by hand to the current street address of the Authority; or
(iii) by fax to a number specified by the Authority.
(3) If a rule does not specify the signatory for a report, the report must be signed by the individual who performs the senior executive function or executive governance function for the entity concerned.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.2.2 Obligation to maintain proper market
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.2 Operating obligations — authorised derivatives exchanges
DMEX 9.2.2 Obligation to maintain proper market
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised derivatives exchange:
(a) must ensure that the market that it operates is fair, orderly and transparent; and
(b) must have policies and procedures that ensure that an approved derivative is not admitted to trading in that market unless:
(i) there is a proper market in the derivative (see subrule (2)); and
(ii) the derivative has been admitted to the exchange’s official list.
(2) For there to be a proper market in an approved derivative, all of the following conditions must be satisfied:
(a) market information (including the pre-trade and post-trade disclosure of orders) is available, on a fair basis, to persons engaged in dealing;
(b) the derivative is capable of genuine and legitimate trading;
(c) there is a sufficient range and number of investors willing and able to generate adequate supply of, and demand for, the derivative;
(d) if appropriate, there is a sufficiently liquid underlying cash market;
(e) enough information is publicly available to enable market participants to make a reasonably informed judgement about the value of the derivative and the risks associated with it;
(f) the rules of the authorised derivatives exchange concerned allow trading in the derivative to be discontinued or suspended:
(i) if the issuer has not complied with its disclosure obligations; or
(ii) in other circumstances in which it is appropriate to discontinue or suspend trading;
(g) liquidity incentive schemes are offered only in accordance with rule 9.2.6;
(h) there are controls to prevent volatility in the market that is not the result of market forces (see rule 9.2.10);
(i) error trades are managed (see rule 9.2.12);
(j) there is a fair and non-discretionary algorithm for matching orders on its facilities.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.2.3 Admission of approved derivatives to trading
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.2 Operating obligations — authorised derivatives exchanges
DMEX 9.2.3 Admission of approved derivatives to trading
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised derivatives exchange must ensure that a derivative is not admitted to trading on its facilities unless the design of the derivative contract satisfies the relevant provisions of the exchange’s rules.
(2) Before an authorised derivatives exchange admits a derivative to trading, it must do the following:
(a) verify that the derivative contract satisfies the provisions referred to in subrule (1);
(b) ensure that the exchange has appropriate supervisory arrangements to monitor trading and settlement in the derivative;
(c) satisfy itself that settlement can be effected in accordance with the derivative contract.
(3) The exchange must have arrangements:
(a) to verify that the issuers of derivatives comply with the market’s disclosure obligations; and
(b) to assist the users of the market to obtain information that is published under the market’s disclosure obligations.
(4) The exchange must have arrangements to regularly review whether such derivatives comply with the exchange’s admission requirements.
(5) The exchange must have policies and procedures for the continuing development and review of the contract designs.
(6) If the exchange admits a derivative to trading on its facilities without obtaining the consent of its issuer, and the derivative has been admitted to trading on another market, the exchange:
(a) must inform the issuer as soon as is reasonably practicable; and
(b) may not require the issuer to demonstrate compliance with its disclosure obligations.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.2.5 Transaction recording

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised derivatives exchange must include in the records of each transaction effected on or through its facilities, or of each transaction reported to it, all of the following:

(a) the facility on or through which the transaction is effected;
(b) the order type;
(c) the name, price and quantity of the derivative traded;
(d) the name of the exchange member;
(e) the time of receipt of the order, instruction or report;
(f) the time at which the transaction is effected;
(g) the due date of the transaction or its expiry date;
(h) the facility on or through which the transaction is to be cleared and settled;
(i) how the transaction was settled.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.2.6 Liquidity incentive schemes
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.2 Operating obligations — authorised derivatives exchanges
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) In this rule:
liquidity incentive scheme means an arrangement that is intended to provide liquidity in a market or in relation to a particular type of derivative.

Guidance
Liquidity incentive schemes are arrangements under which an exchange offers financial incentives to market-makers. Such incentives might include rebates, stipends, waivers of membership or transaction fees, payments for routing order flows and other forms of soft dollar benefits.
(2) An authorised derivatives exchange must not operate a liquidity incentive scheme unless:
(a) participation in the scheme is limited to:
(i) members of the exchange;
(ii) members’ clients; and
(iii) other persons who satisfy subrule (3); and
(b) the Regulatory Authority has approved the scheme.
(3) A person satisfies this subrule if:
(a) the relevant exchange has undertaken due diligence to ensure that the person is of sufficiently good repute and has adequate competencies and organisational arrangements; and
(b) the person has agreed in writing to comply with the exchange’s business rules.
Guidance
The exchange should do the following:
• verify the identity of the person and its beneficial owners and directors for the purposes of complying with the AML requirements
• assess the character, good standing, knowledge, experience and skills of the person and its directors and employees
• assess whether the control framework that the person has created for the scheme is adequate to ensure that trading occurs in accordance with the exchange’s business rules.
(4) At least 10 business days before an authorised derivatives exchange first operates a liquidity incentive scheme, the exchange must give the Authority a notice that sets out:
(a) the details of the scheme;
(b) the benefits to the exchange and its members and other users that will result from the scheme;
(c) a certificate by the exchange that the scheme complies with subrule (2) (a); and
(d) the date on which the scheme is intended to become operative.
(5) If the Authority does not approve the proposed scheme, the exchange may refer the matter to the Regulatory Tribunal for review.
(6) The exchange must, as soon as practicable, announce the introduction of the scheme, including the date on which it becomes operative and any other relevant information.
Guidance
An exchange need not publish any details about the scheme that are reasonably to be regarded as commercially sensitive. However, it should disclose as much as it thinks appropriate to keep its market well informed about the scheme.

Guidance Liquidity incentive schemes are arrangements under which an exchange offers financial incentives to market-makers. (2) An authorised derivatives exchange must not operate a liquidity incentive scheme unless: (a) participation in the scheme is limited to: (i) members of the exchange; (ii) members’ clients; and (iii) other persons who satisfy subrule (3); and (b) the Regulatory Authority has approved the scheme. (3) A person satisfies this subrule if: (a) the relevant exchange has undertaken due diligence to ensure that the person is of sufficiently good repute and has adequate competencies and organisational arrangements; and (b) the person has agreed in writing to comply with the exchange’s business rules. Guidance The exchange should do the following: • verify the identity of the person and its beneficial owners and directors for the purposes of complying with the AML requirements • assess the character, good standing, knowledge, experience and skills of the person and its directors and employees • assess whether the control framework that the person has created for the scheme is adequate to ensure that trading occurs in accordance with the exchange’s business rules. (4) At least 10 business days before an authorised derivatives exchange first operates a liquidity incentive scheme, the exchange must give the Authority a notice that sets out: (a) the details of the scheme; (b) the benefits to the exchange and its members and other users that will result from the scheme; (c) a certificate by the exchange that the scheme complies with subrule (2) (a); and (d) the date on which the scheme is intended to become operative. (5) If the Authority does not approve the proposed scheme, the exchange may refer the matter to the Regulatory Tribunal for review. (6) The exchange must, as soon as practicable, announce the introduction of the scheme, including the date on which it becomes operative and any other relevant information. Guidance An exchange need not publish any details about the scheme that are reasonably to be regarded as commercially sensitive. However, it should disclose as much as it thinks appropriate to keep its market well informed about the scheme. Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.2.8 Pre-trade disclosures
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.2 Operating obligations — authorised derivatives exchanges
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised derivatives exchange must publish all of the following information about the derivatives being traded on its facilities:
(a) the current bid and offer prices and volume;
(b) the depth of trading interest (including any actionable indication of interest) shown at the prices and volumes advertised through its systems for the derivatives;
(c) any other information about the derivatives that would promote transparency in trading.
Guidance
1 An actionable interest is a message from one member to another in a trading system about available trading interest that contains all necessary information to agree on a trade.
2 An authorised derivatives exchange should use an adequate mechanism so that pre-trade information is available to the public easily and uninterrupted, at least during business hours. The exchange may charge a reasonable fee for the information that it publishes.
(2) The information must be published in real time, on reasonable commercial terms and on a non-discriminatory basis.
Guidance
1 An authorised derivatives exchange may seek a waiver or modification of this rule in relation to transaction orders if:
• the order size is pre-determined and exceeds a pre-set and published level
• details of the exemption are set out in the exchange’s business rules.
2 In deciding whether to grant such a waiver or exemption, the Regulatory Authority will take into account:
• the size of the order, compared with the normal market size for the derivative concerned
• the effect that the exemption would have on price discovery, fragmentation, fairness and overall market quality
• whether there is sufficient transparency relating to trades executed without pre-trade disclosure as a result of dark orders, whether or not they are entered in transparent markets
• whether the exchange supports transparent orders by giving priority to transparent orders over dark orders, for example by executing such orders at the same price as transparent orders
• whether there is adequate disclosure of details relating to dark orders available to members and other participants on the exchange’s facilities to enable them to understand how their orders will be handled and executed. (A dark order is an order that is executed on an execution platform without pre-trade transparency.)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.2.10 Volatility and large trading volumes
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.2 Operating obligations — authorised derivatives exchanges
DMEX 9.2.10 Volatility and large trading volumes
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised derivatives exchange must have policies and procedures to ensure that its trading systems:
(a) are resilient;
(b) have adequate capacity to deal with large volumes of orders and messages; and
(c) can operate in an orderly way under conditions of market stress.
(2) The exchange’s policies and procedures must enable it:
(a) to reject orders that exceed pre-determined volume and price thresholds;
(b) to temporarily halt the trading of a particular derivative on its facilities if there is a significant price movement for the derivative on its facilities or a related market during a short period; and
(c) to cancel, vary or correct any transaction.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.2.11 Messaging systems and pre-trade controls
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.2 Operating obligations — authorised derivatives exchanges
DMEX 9.2.11 Messaging systems and pre-trade controls
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised derivatives exchange must have adequate arrangements (including technology):
(a) to prevent the breaching of capacity limits for messaging;
(b) to require its members to apply pre-trade controls to their clients; and
(c) to permit only its members to modify the parameters of any pre-trade controls.
(2) The exchange must publish the details of the arrangements.
Guidance
1 To comply with rule 9.2.11, an authorised derivatives exchange:
• might provide a way to “throttle” orders to prevent breaches of its capacity
• might prohibit “naked” or “unfiltered” access to its facilities by members’ clients (that is, where the clients’ orders do not pass through pre-trade controls)
• might require members to have appropriate pre-trade controls on their clients’ orders, including in-built and automatic rejection of orders outside specified limits.
2 Pre-trade controls that an authorised derivatives exchange requires from its members should contain:
• price or size parameters: members should be able to automatically block or cancel orders that do not meet the set price or size limits order-by-order or over a specified period
• controls around permission to trade: members should be able to block or cancel orders immediately as soon as they are aware that a trader’s trade permissions have been breached
• effective risk management: members should be able to block or cancel orders automatically where the trades pose risks that compromise the relevant member’s own risk management; such controls should be applied as necessary and appropriate to exposures to individual clients or derivatives or groups of clients or derivatives, exposures of individual traders, trading desks or the member as a whole
• reporting obligations: members should be obliged to notify the exchange about significant risks that may affect fair and orderly trading, and major incidents, as soon as they become aware of such a risk or incident
• overriding of pre-trade controls: each member should have procedures and arrangements for dealing with orders that have been automatically blocked by the member’s pre-trade controls, but that the member may re-submit; such procedures and arrangements should serve to warn the member’s compliance and risk management functions that controls have been overridden and require their approval for the overriding
• training on order entry procedures: members should ensure that employees who use the order entry system have adequate training on order entry procedures before they are allowed to use the system
• monitoring and accessibility of knowledgeable and mandated staff: members should monitor their orders in as close to real time as possible, (including from a cross-market perspective) for signs of disorderly trading; such monitoring should be done by staff who understand the member’s trading flow, and they should be accessible to the exchange and have the necessary authority to take necessary and appropriate remedial action; a member should ensure that its compliance staff are able to follow closely the member’s electronic trading activity so that they can quickly respond to and correct any failures or regulatory breaches
• control of messaging traffic: members should have control of messaging traffic to the exchange, particularly to ensure that any messaging limits imposed by the exchange on the members are not exceeded (messaging limits are limits imposed by an exchange on its members for the transmission of orders to ensure that the exchange’s capacity to deal with such orders is not exceeded).

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.2.12 Error trades
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.2 Operating obligations — authorised derivatives exchanges
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised derivatives exchange must have policies and procedures:
(a) to prevent or minimise error trades;
(b) to identify and rectify error trades promptly; and
(c) to identify whether error trades are related to disorderly market activity.
Note For the meaning of error trade, see rule 8.2.4 (1).
(2) An authorised derivatives exchange must be able:
(a) to reject an order that is clearly erroneous; and
(b) to cancel, amend or correct an error trade.
