QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.2.13 Clearing and settlement
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.2 Operating obligations — authorised derivatives exchanges
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised derivatives exchange must have policies and procedures:
(a) for the timely discharge of the rights and liabilities of the parties to the transactions effected on or through its facilities; and
(b) to monitor compliance with its business rules in relation to the clearing and settlement of such transactions.
(2) The exchange must notify its members and other users of its facilities about the policies and procedures.
(3) An authorised derivatives exchange must not use a clearing house outside the QFC, or a CCP that is not a recognised market entity.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.2.16 Authorised derivatives exchanges — transaction recording and reporting
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.2 Operating obligations — authorised derivatives exchanges
DMEX 9.2.16 Authorised derivatives exchanges — transaction recording and reporting
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised derivatives exchange must have systems and procedures:
(a) to report the details of any derivative contract that has been concluded using its facilities, and of any modification or termination of such a contract, to:
(i) a trade repository that the exchange is satisfied would meet the standards for such a repository under EMIR; or
(ii) if there is no such trade repository — the Authority;
(b) to make such reports no later than the working day after the conclusion, modification or termination of the relevant contract;
(c) to include in such a report the following details:
(i) the parties to the relevant contract;
(ii) if the beneficiary of the rights and obligations arising from the contract is not a party, the name of the beneficiary;
(iii) the main characteristics of the contract, including its type, underlying maturity, notional value, price, and settlement date; and
(d) to keep appropriate records of each such report (including the date on which, and the time at which, each report was made).
(2) A report must be to a technical standard that would satisfy the applicable requirements under EMIR.
(3) The exchange must keep a record of any derivative contract that has been concluded using its facilities, and any modification of it, for at least 5 years after the termination of the contract.
(4) No liability resulting from a disclosure referred to in this rule lies with the exchange or any of its directors or employees.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.3.3 Beginning or ceasing clearing or settling
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.3 Operating obligations — authorised CCPs
DMEX 9.3.3 Beginning or ceasing clearing or settling
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must have policies and procedures to allow it:
(a) to begin clearing or settling, on or through its facilities, a type of derivative that it has not previously cleared or settled, but is authorised to clear or settle; or
(b) to cease clearing or settling a type of derivative on or through its facilities.
(2) Subject to subrule (3), an authorised CCP must obtain the approval of the Regulatory Authority:
(a) before beginning to clear or settle, on or through its facilities, a type of derivative that it has not previously cleared or settled, but is authorised to clear or settle; or
(b) before ceasing to clear or settle a type of derivative or generally.
(3) When submitting information to the Authority for the purposes of subrule (1), the CCP must give the following information:
(a) a description of the type of derivative concerned and its terms;
(b) the name of the trading facility for the type of derivative.
(4) The CCP need not obtain approval under subrule (1):
(a) in an emergency that threatens the orderly functioning of its facilities; or
(b) if the delay caused by obtaining approval:
(i) would be contrary to the principle of promoting fair, orderly and transparent markets; or
(ii) would adversely affect:
(A) the financial system operating in or from the QFC; or
(B) the interests of members or investors.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised CCP must include in the records of each transaction that is cleared or settled on or through its facilities, or reported to it, all of the following:

(a) the name of the derivative traded and the price, quantity and date of the transaction;
(b) the names and, if appropriate, the roles of the parties to the transaction;
(c) the facilities on which the transaction was effected and on which it was cleared or settled;
(d) if applicable, the time at which novation takes place;
(e) the due date and manner of settlement of the transaction.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.3.5 Transaction reporting
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.3 Operating obligations — authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must ensure that the details of any derivative contract that it has concluded, and of any modification or termination of such a contract, are reported to:
(a) a trade repository that the exchange is satisfied would meet the standards for such a repository under EMIR; or
(b) if there is no such trade repository — to the Authority.
(2) A report must be to a technical standard that would satisfy the applicable requirements under EMIR.
(3) A report under subrule (1) must be made no later than the working day after the conclusion, modification or termination of the relevant contract.
(4) The details that must be reported under subrule (1) are the following:
(a) the parties to the relevant contract;
(b) if the beneficiary of the rights and obligations arising from the contract is not a party, the name of the beneficiary;
(c) the main characteristics of the contract, including its type, underlying maturity, notional value, price, and settlement date.
(5) An authorised CCP may delegate the reporting of the details of derivative contracts.
(6) An authorised CCP must ensure that the details of derivative contracts are reported without duplication.
(7) An authorised CCP must keep appropriate records of each report under this rule (including the date on which, and the time at which, the report was made).

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.3.6 Money settlement
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.3 Operating obligations — authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP may conduct its money settlements using commercial bank money only if the Regulatory Authority so approves.
(2) Subrules (3) to (6) apply to an authorised CCP that conducts its money settlements using commercial bank money.
(3) The CCP must adopt appropriate measures to minimise and strictly control the credit and liquidity risks that arise from its use of settlement banks.
(4) The CCP must establish strict criteria for the use of settlement banks. The criteria must take into account, for each bank, its creditworthiness, its capitalisation, its access to liquidity, its operational reliability, and the standard of regulation and supervision that applies to it.
(5) The CCP must monitor adherence to the criteria for the use of settlement banks.
(6) The CCP:
(a) must conduct its money settlements using only assets that carry little or no credit or liquidity risk;
(b) must monitor, manage, and limit its credit and liquidity risks that arise from settlement banks;
(c) must monitor and manage the concentration of credit and liquidity exposures to its settlement banks; and
(d) must ensure that its legal agreement with a settlement bank:
(i) specifies clearly when transfers on the bank’s books are expected to occur and when they are final; and
(ii) ensure that funds received are transferable as soon as possible (if not intra-day, at least by the end of the day) to enable the CCP and its users to manage their credit and liquidity risks.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.3.7 Collateral
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.3 Operating obligations — authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to an authorised CCP that requires collateral to manage its own, or its users’, credit risks arising in the course of (or for the purposes of) its payment, clearing, and settlement processes.
(2) The CCP:
(a) must accept only collateral with low credit, liquidity, and market risks; and
(b) must set and enforce appropriately conservative haircuts and concentration limits.
(3) The CCP must establish and implement a collateral management system that is well designed and operationally flexible. The system must provide for the following:
(a) limiting the assets that it accepts as collateral to those with low credit, liquidity, and market risks;
(b) prudent valuation practices and haircuts:
(i) that are regularly tested; and
(ii) that take into account stressed market conditions;
(c) so far as is practicable and prudent, establishing stable, conservative haircuts that are appropriate in stressed market conditions;
(d) avoiding concentrated holdings of assets that would significantly impair its ability to liquidate the assets quickly without significant adverse price effects;
(e) if it accepts cross-border collateral, mitigating the risks associated with such collateral.
(4) The system must ensure that the collateral can be used in a timely way.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.3.8 Settlement finality
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.3 Operating obligations — authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must have adequate arrangements to ensure the clear and certain final settlement of:
(a) its users’ obligations, including payments and transfer instructions; and
(b) its own obligations.
(2) The arrangements must ensure that if a transaction cannot be settled intra-day or in real time, it is settled no later than the end of its value date.
(3) The arrangements must clearly define:
(a) the point at which the final settlement of a transaction occurs; and
(b) the point after which the parties to the underlying contract may not revoke unsettled payments, transfer instructions, or other obligations.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.3.9 Notifications about trading
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.3 Operating obligations — authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must notify persons who have been granted access to its facilities about any proposal of either of the following kinds for which it has sought the Regulatory Authority’s approval:
(a) to clear or settle, on or through its facilities, a type of derivative that it has not previously cleared or settled, but is authorised to clear or settle;
(b) to cease clearing or settling:
(i) a type of derivative; or
(ii) derivatives generally.
(2) A notice under subrule (1) must be given at the time the CCP seeks the Regulatory Authority’s approval, and must include the same information as the CCP gave the Authority.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.3.10 Compliance procedures
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.3 Operating obligations — authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
An authorised CCP must have adequate compliance procedures to ensure that:

(a) users’ compliance with its rules is monitored and enforced;
(b) any complaints about its operations or about a user of its facilities are promptly investigated;
(c) if appropriate, action resulting in financial or other penalties can be taken;
(d) there are appropriate appeal procedures; and
(e) that the Regulatory Authority is notified of matters about which, under these rules, the Authority must be notified.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.3.11 Margin system
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.3 Operating obligations — authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP:

(a) must have a margin system that meets the requirements in subrule (2);
(b) must mark users’ positions to market, and collect variation margin, at least daily, to limit the build-up of current exposures;
(c) must have the necessary authority and operational capacity to make intra-day margin calls and payments (both scheduled and unscheduled) to users; and
(d) must regularly review and validate its margin system to ensure that the system operates effectively and as intended.

(2) The margin system:

(a) must set margin levels that are appropriate for the risks and particular attributes of each derivative, portfolio, and market that the CCP serves;
(b) must use a reliable source of timely price information, and must also use procedures and sound valuation models for circumstances in which price information is not readily available or is unreliable; and

(c) must adopt initial margin models and parameters:

(i) that are risk-based; and
(ii) that generate margin requirements sufficient to cover the CCP’s exposures to users in the period between the last margin collection and the close-out of positions after a user defaults.

(3) An authorised CCP:

(a) must establish and implement a margin management system;
(b) must adopt a policy of daily (and, if appropriate, intra‐day) calculation and collection of variation margin, based on models and parameters, that manages current and potential future exposures; and

(c) must analyse and review the performance of the margin model and overall margin coverage by:

(i) rigorous daily back-testing to evaluate whether there are any exceptions to its initial margin coverage;
(ii) sensitivity analyses, carried out at least monthly and more frequently, as appropriate, to determine the impact of varying important model parameters including the most volatile periods that have been experienced by the markets it serves and extreme changes in the correlations between prices; and
(iii) an assessment of the theoretical and empirical properties of its margin model for all derivatives that it clears.
(4) If the CCP calculates margins at the level of members’ portfolios, the initial margins must be applied to each portfolio’s distribution of future exposures. If the CCP calculates margins at more granular levels, the initial margins must be applied to the corresponding distribution of future exposures.

(5) The initial margins must use models:

(a) that rely on conservative estimates of the time horizons for effectively hedging or closing-out the particular types of derivatives that the CCP clears, even in stressed market conditions; and
(b) that have an appropriate method for measuring credit exposure that accounts for product risk factors and portfolio effects across products, and (so far as practicable and prudent) limits the need for destabilising procyclical changes.
(6) An authorised CCP may allow offsets or reductions in required margin across products that it clears or between products that it and another authorised CCP clear, if the risk of 1 product is significantly and reliably correlated with the risk of the other.
(7) If 2 or more authorised CCPs are authorised to offer cross‐margining, they must have appropriate safeguards and harmonised overall risk‐management systems.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)
Amended by QFCRA RM/2025-1 (as from 1st October 2025)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.3.12 Default fund
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.3 Operating obligations — authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must maintain a pre-funded default fund to cover losses arising from the default of 1 or more clearing members that exceed the losses to be covered by margin requirements. The CCP must establish a minimum below which the size of the default fund is not to be allowed to fall under any circumstances.
(2) The default fund must be sufficient to enable the CCP to withstand, under extreme but plausible market conditions, the default of:
(a) the clearing member to which it has the largest exposure; or
(b) the clearing members to which it has the second and third largest exposures, if the sum of its exposures to those clearing members is greater than the exposure referred to in paragraph (a).
(3) An authorised CCP must establish the minimum contribution to the default fund and the criteria to calculate each clearing member’s contribution. A clearing member’s contribution must be proportional to the CCP’s exposure to the member.
(4) To ensure that its default fund is adequate to withstand any likely default, an authorised CCP must develop a range of possible future scenarios, including scenarios of extreme but plausible market conditions, and must test the fund’s adequacy under those scenarios. The scenarios must take into account:
(a) the most volatile periods that have been experienced in the markets for which the CCP provides its services; and
(b) the possibility of sudden sales of financial resources and rapid reductions in market liquidity.
(5) An authorised CCP may establish a separate default fund for each type of derivative that it clears.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 9.3.13 Segregation and portability
doc_path: DMEX Part 9.3 Operating obligations — authorised CCPs
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An authorised CCP must have systems and procedures to enable the segregation and portability of positions of its users’ customers, and any collateral provided to it in relation to those positions.
(2) The systems and controls must provide for the following:
(a) segregation and portability arrangements that effectively protect the positions and collateral of users’ customers from the default or insolvency of the relevant member or other users;
(b) if the CCP offers additional protection of customers’ positions and collateral against the concurrent default of both the relevant member and other users — any necessary measures to ensure that the additional protection is effective;
(c) account structures that enable the CCP to readily identify the positions of a user’s customers, and to segregate their collateral.
(3) An authorised CCP must publish to its users its rules, policies and procedures about the segregation and portability of positions and collateral.
(4) The requirement to distinguish assets and positions in accounts is satisfied if:
(a) the assets and positions are recorded in separate accounts;
(b) netting between positions recorded in different accounts is prevented; and
(c) the assets that cover the positions recorded in an account are not exposed to losses connected to positions recorded in another account.
(5) An authorised CCP must offer to keep:
(a) records and accounts that enable users of its facilities to distinguish the CCP’s assets and positions from those held for the account of its clients (“omnibus client segregation”); or
(b) records and accounts that enable users of its facilities to distinguish assets and positions held for the account of a specific client from those held for the account of other clients (“individual client segregation”).
(6) If a user so requests, an authorised CCP must offer the user the possibility of opening more accounts in the user’s own name or for the account of their clients.
(7) An authorised CCP must publish to the users of its facilities, its rules, policies and procedures about the segregation and portability of the positions and related collateral of users’ clients facilities. The publication must disclose how to determine the value at which client positions will be transferred.
(8) An authorised CCP must also disclose whether:
(a) segregated assets and client collateral are held by the CCP or by 1 or more unaffiliated third‐party custodians;
(b) the CCP takes a title transfer or a security interest;
(c) it has a right of use or re‐use of clients’ collateral and when;
(d) clients’ collateral is protected on an individual or omnibus account basis; and
(e) there are any legal, operational or other constraints that would impair its ability to segregate or transfer the positions (and related collateral) of a user’s clients.
(9) An authorised CCP must structure its portability arrangements in a way that makes it highly likely that the positions and collateral of a defaulting user’s customers will be transferred to 1 or more other users.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 10.1.1 Application of Chapter 10
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 10 Entities licensed etc by Qatar Central Bank or QFMA
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) This Chapter applies to:
(a) while a supervisory MoU is in effect between the Regulatory Authority and the Qatar Central Bank — an entity that is licensed (however described) by the Bank to conduct, in the State of Qatar outside the QFC, an activity that corresponds to a derivatives market activity; and
(b) while a supervisory MoU is in effect between the Authority and the QFMA — an entity that is licensed (however described) by the QFMA to conduct, in that State, an activity that corresponds to a derivatives market activity.
(2) An entity to which this Chapter applies is called, in these rules, a State licensed entity.

DMEX 10.1.3 Entities may carry on activities etc
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) A State licensed entity may conduct a derivatives market activity in or from the QFC if:
(a) its licence from the Qatar Central Bank or the QFMA authorises it to conduct, in the State of Qatar outside the QFC, an activity corresponding to that activity; and
(b) the Bank or the QFMA, as the case requires, has notified the Regulatory Authority that it has no objection to the entity’s conducting the activity in and from the QFC under the relevant supervisory MoU.
(2) An entity that conducts a derivatives market activity as permitted by subrule (1) is taken to hold an approval for the purposes of the QFC Law, article 11 (2).

DMEX 11.1.3 Definitions — recognised market entity etc
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
In these rules:

recognised market entity means an entity that operates an exchange or central counterparty in a jurisdiction outside the State of Qatar and has been granted recognition as a recognised market entity by the Regulatory Authority.

recognised firm means an entity:

(a) that is a member of, or a participant in, an exchange or central counterparty in a jurisdiction outside the State of Qatar; and
(b) that has been granted recognition as a recognised firm by the Authority.

recognised person means a recognised market entity or recognised firm.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 11.1.5 Application for recognition
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 11 Recognition — entities licensed or authorised outside the State of Qatar
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An applicant for recognition as a recognised market entity or recognised firm must submit an application to the Regulatory Authority that demonstrates, to the Authority’s satisfaction, that the applicant satisfies the recognition criteria for a recognised market entity or a recognised firm.
(2) The application must include:
(a) an acknowledgement that the following laws, regulations and rules will apply to it in relation to its activities in the derivatives market in the QFC if recognition is granted, and an unconditional undertaking to comply with those laws, regulations and rules:
(i) the QFC Law and Regulations made under it (and in particular FSR, article 82);
(ii) the AML/CFT Law and any regulations made under it;
Note The AML/CFT Law of the State of Qatar (and any regulations made under it) applies to a recognised person as it does to any other entity that operates within the State.
(iii) other Laws and Regulations of the State of Qatar that are applicable in the QFC;
(iv) Chapter 13 (Market abuse) and Chapter 15 (Fees) of these rules;
(b) unconditional undertakings:
(i) to submit to the Authority’s exercise of its functions in relation to supervision and investigations (under FSR, Part 8) and disciplinary and enforcement proceedings (under FSR, Part 9), in relation to the applicant’s operations in the QFC; and
(ii) to comply with any directions given by the Authority in relation to those operations; and
(iii) to submit to the jurisdiction of the Regulatory Tribunal and the Civil and Commercial Court in relation to any proceedings in the QFC arising out of or related to those operations;
(c) if the applicant’s home jurisdiction is not an approved jurisdiction — a comparative analysis of the regulatory requirements applicable to the applicant in its home jurisdiction compared with those under these rules and those in the IOSCO Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures;
Note For the approved jurisdictions, see rule 1.1.11.
(d) if the law or practice in the applicant’s home jurisdiction requires the applicant to have, in that jurisdiction, 1 or more individuals approved by an overseas regulator to perform a function that is the equivalent of a controlled function:
(i) a list of those functions and the names of the individuals; and
(ii) details of the approval of each individual.
(3) If the applicant becomes aware of a material change in circumstances that is reasonably likely to be relevant to its application, it must immediately inform the Regulatory Authority of the change.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 11.1.6 Recognition criteria for recognised market entities
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 11 Recognition — entities licensed or authorised outside the State of Qatar
DMEX 11.1.6 Recognition criteria for recognised market entities
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
The recognition criteria for a recognised market entity are that:

(a) the applicant has its head office and registered office outside the QFC and the State of Qatar;
(b) the applicant is licensed or authorised (however described) to operate an exchange or central counterparty in an approved jurisdiction, or in another jurisdiction acceptable to the Regulatory Authority;
Guidance
In particular, the Regulatory Authority expects a recognised person to have AML/CFT controls that are substantially equivalent to those required in the QFC. For example, the Authority would expect a recognised person to have:
• a written policy in relation to AML/CFT
• a money laundering reporting officer
• a reporting framework
• record-keeping requirements
• an appropriate training programme.
(c) if the applicant is regulated by an overseas regulator in a jurisdiction that is not an approved jurisdiction:
(i) the regulatory regime in that jurisdiction is broadly equivalent to the Authority’s regulatory regime;
(ii) adequate arrangements exist, or will exist, for cooperation between the Authority and the overseas regulator; and
(iii) the applicant operates to a standard that would reasonably satisfy the authorisation criteria for authorised market entities;
(d) if the applicant operates a central counterparty — it is a qualifying central counterparty, as defined in the document entitled “CRE50 — Counterparty credit risk definitions and terminology”, published by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and in effect from 15 December 2019 (as amended and in effect from time to time); and
(e) the applicant has given the acknowledgement and undertakings required by rule 11.1.5 (2) (a) and (b).

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 11.1.7 Recognition criteria for recognised firms
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 11 Recognition — entities licensed or authorised outside the State of Qatar
DMEX 11.1.7 Recognition criteria for recognised firms
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The recognition criteria for a recognised firm are that:
(a) it is licensed or authorised (however described) to trade on or use the facilities of an exchange in an approved jurisdiction, or in another jurisdiction acceptable to the Regulatory Authority;
Note For the approved jurisdictions, see rule 1.1.11.
(b) subject to subrule (2), it conducts business in a jurisdiction other than the QFC or the State of Qatar, and has its head office and registered office outside the QFC and that State;
(c) if it is regulated by an overseas regulator in a jurisdiction that is not an approved jurisdiction:
(i) in relation to the trading referred to in paragraph (a), it is regulated by an overseas regulator acceptable to the Authority;
(ii) the law under which it is authorised is broadly equivalent to the Authority’s regulatory regime, as it applies to a member of an authorised market entity; and
(iii) adequate arrangements exist, or will exist, for cooperation between the Authority and the overseas regulator referred to in subparagraph (i); and
(d) when using the facilities of an exchange in the QFC, it does not exceed the scope of the activities that it is licensed or authorised, by its overseas regulator, to conduct; and
(e) it has given the acknowledgement and undertakings required by rule 11.1.5 (2) (a) and (b).
(2) Paragraph (1) (b) does not apply to an applicant that has a branch that is an authorised firm.
(3) If a recognised firm has a branch that is an authorised firm, nothing in this rule prevents the member from conducting a regulated activity in or from the QFC through the branch.
(4) In this rule:
branch means the local office in the QFC of a company or limited liability partnership that is incorporated in a jurisdiction outside the QFC.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 11.1.8 Matters that Regulatory Authority may take into account
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 11 Recognition — entities licensed or authorised outside the State of Qatar
DMEX 11.1.8 Matters that Regulatory Authority may take into account
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
In considering whether an applicant satisfies the relevant recognition criteria, the Regulatory Authority may take into account any or all of the following:

(a) the licence that the applicant holds;
(b) the applicant’s rules and practices;
(c) if the applicant is not regulated by an overseas regulator in an approved jurisdiction — the regulatory regimes and legal systems (including insolvency laws and default provisions) that the applicant is subject to;
(d) in the case of an applicant for recognition as a recognised CCP:
(i) the need to ensure that the applicant, if recognised, would provide, for participants in the market, protection at least equivalent to the protection that would be provided by an authorised CCP;
(ii) the applicant’s 12-month business plan for the operations it proposes with the relevant authorised derivatives exchange;
(iii) whether the applicant understands the nature of the functions that it will exercise for the authorised derivatives exchange and its significance for the applicant’s ability to satisfy its recognition criteria;
(iv) if the applicant is not regulated by an overseas regulator in an approved jurisdiction — whether the legal framework under which the applicant operates provides for reciprocity through an effective equivalent system for the recognition of CCPs authorised under third-country legal regimes; and
(e) any other matter that the Authority reasonably considers to be relevant.

DMEX 11.1.9 Condition as to derivatives traded etc

(2) It is a condition of the recognition of a recognised market entity that proposes to conduct a central counterparty in or from the QFC that the entity allows the clearing and settling of transactions only in approved derivatives.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 11.1.10 Recognised persons subject to obligation to comply with Shari’a
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 11 Recognition — entities licensed or authorised outside the State of Qatar
DMEX 11.1.10 Recognised persons subject to obligation to comply with Shari’a
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) This rule applies in relation to an applicant for recognition that is subject, under the law of its home jurisdiction or otherwise, to an obligation to comply with Shari’a in some or all of its operations.
(2) If the Regulatory Authority grants recognition to the applicant, it is a condition of the recognition that the applicant, in the whole of the conduct of its business in and from the QFC, complies with Shari’a (as Shari’a would apply to the applicant in its home jurisdiction).
Guidance
A successful applicant for recognition is not permitted to operate an Islamic window in the QFC even if it would be permitted to do so in its home jurisdiction.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 11.1.11 Notification and reporting requirements — general
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 11 Recognition — entities licensed or authorised outside the State of Qatar
DMEX 11.1.11 Notification and reporting requirements — general
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) A recognised person must notify the Regulatory Authority immediately of any event that may cause it to be unable to satisfy the recognition criteria.
(2) A recognised person must give the Authority a report at least once a year, on a date or dates agreed with the Authority, that contains:
(a) a statement confirming that the person continues to be licensed or authorised (however described) in its home jurisdiction;
(b) a statement confirming that the person satisfies the other recognition criteria, and has done so throughout the period to which the statement relates;
(c) particulars of any changes during that period to:
(i) its constitution;
(ii) its organisation, structure and practices; or
(iii) its governing body;
(iv) any individual mentioned in the list required by rule 11.1.5 (2) (d); and
(d) particulars of any action taken against the person during that period by an overseas regulator, or a law enforcement authority in any jurisdiction, even if that action:
(i) has not been made public; or
(ii) is not of a kind of which the Authority would reasonably expect to be notified.
(3) A recognised person must promptly give the Authority a copy of its annual report and accounts (and, if it is a member of a corporate group, of the consolidated annual report and accounts of the corporate group), at the same time as it provides them to the overseas regulator by which it is regulated in its home jurisdiction.
(4) A recognised person must give the Regulatory Authority a copy of its annual report for a financial year no later than the earliest of the following times:
(a) 4 months after the end of the financial year;
(b) the time when the report is sent to the person’s shareholders.
(5) A recognised person that is a member of a corporate group must give the Regulatory Authority a copy of the group’s consolidated annual report for a financial year no later than the latest of the following:
(a) 4 months after the end of the financial year;
(b) the time when the report is sent to the person’s members or shareholders;
(c) the time when the report is sent to the group’s shareholders.
(6) A recognised person must give the Authority a copy of any information:
(a) that it has provided to the overseas regulator by which it is regulated in its home jurisdiction; and
(b) that is relevant to any regulated activity that it conducts in or from the QFC.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 11.1.13 Notification and reporting requirements ― action by other regulators etc
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 11 Recognition — entities licensed or authorised outside the State of Qatar
DMEX 11.1.13 Notification and reporting requirements ― action by other regulators etc
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
A recognised person must notify the Regulatory Authority immediately of any of the following:

(a) the granting, modification or variation of a licence in its home jurisdiction or any other jurisdiction (if the licence relates to operating a clearing house or settlement facility);
(b) the revocation, withdrawal or refusal of such a licence;
(c) the granting, withdrawal or refusal of an application for, or the revocation of, its membership of a clearing house in another jurisdiction;
(d) its becoming aware that an overseas regulator has started an investigation into its affairs;
(e) the appointment, by an overseas regulator, of an investigator (however described) to investigate its affairs;
(f) the imposition, by an overseas regulator, of disciplinary measures on it in relation to its financial services.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 11.1.14 Notification and reporting requirements — insolvency and dissolution
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 11 Recognition — entities licensed or authorised outside the State of Qatar
DMEX 11.1.14 Notification and reporting requirements — insolvency and dissolution
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
A recognised person must notify the Regulatory Authority immediately of any of the following:

(a) the calling of a meeting to consider a resolution for winding up the person;
(b) an application to dissolve it, or to strike it from the corporate register in its home jurisdiction;
(c) the presentation of a petition for its winding up;
(d) its making, or proposing to make, a composition or arrangement with its creditors;
(e) an application under the law of any jurisdiction commencing insolvency proceedings or proceedings for the appointment of a receiver, administrator or provisional liquidator;
(f) any other event or matter relating to its insolvency or potential insolvency.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 11.1.15 Communications to Regulatory Authority
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 11 Recognition — entities licensed or authorised outside the State of Qatar
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) A recognised person must conduct its communication with the Regulatory Authority in English.
(2) A recognised person must take reasonable steps to ensure that all the information that it provides to the Authority:
(a) is factually accurate or, in the case of an estimate or judgement, is fairly and properly based; and
(b) is complete (that is, it includes everything that the Authority would reasonably expect to be notified about).
(3) A recognised person must notify the Authority immediately if it becomes aware, or has information that reasonably suggests, that it has or may have provided the Authority with information:
(a) that was or may have been false, misleading, incomplete or inaccurate; or
(b) that has or may have changed significantly.
(4) The notification must include details of the information concerned, an explanation of why the information was or may have been provided and the correct information.
(5) Unless a rule states otherwise, a recognised person must ensure that each notification that it gives the Authority:
(a) is in writing;
(b) includes the recognised person’s name; and
(c) is sent:
(i) by post to the current postal address of the Authority;
(ii) by email to an address specified by the Authority; or
(iii) by fax to a number specified by the Authority.
(6) A recognised person must ensure that, if the person sends a communication to the Authority, the person obtains confirmation from the Authority that the Authority has received the communication.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 11.1.16 Automatic termination of recognition
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 11 Recognition — entities licensed or authorised outside the State of Qatar
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) If a recognised person ceases to be licensed or authorised (however described) in its home jurisdiction, it ceases to be recognised in the QFC.
(2) In a case mentioned in subrule (1), the Regulatory Authority may give any directions that are necessary:
(a) to enable the person’s outstanding market contracts to be closed out or settled; and
(b) to protect the interests of the person’s members, clients or customers.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 11.1.17 Revocation of recognition
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 11 Recognition — entities licensed or authorised outside the State of Qatar
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The Regulatory Authority may revoke the recognition of a recognised person if any of the following happens:
(a) the person ceases to satisfy any of the recognition criteria other than the criterion of being licensed or authorised (however described) in its home jurisdiction;
Note Loss of the person’s licence in its home jurisdiction automatically terminates the person’s recognition — see rule 11.1.16.
(b) the person breaches an undertaking by it referred to in rule 11.1.5 (2) (b) (and, in particular, if the breach would amount to a contravention of a relevant requirement if the person were an authorised firm);
Note Contravention of a relevant requirement is defined in the Glossary.
(c) action is taken against the person by an overseas regulator, or a fiscal authority or law enforcement authority in any jurisdiction;
(d) the person fails to comply with a condition imposed by rule 11.1.9, or a condition imposed under rule 11.1.10 (2);
(e) the person fails to comply with rule 11.1.12, 11.1.13 or 11.1.14;
(f) an event mentioned in rule 11.1.14 happens in relation to the person;
(g) the person notifies the Authority that the person no longer wishes to be recognised.
(2) A notice by a recognised person referred to in paragraph (1) (g) must include details of the arrangements that the person has made to settle or close out the person’s outstanding market contracts and protect the interests of its members, clients or customers.
(3) If the Authority revokes the recognition of a recognised person, the Authority may give any directions that are necessary:
(a) to enable the person’s outstanding market contracts to be closed out or settled; and
(b) to protect the interests of the person’s members, clients or customers.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 11.1.18 Continued effect of rules etc after withdrawal or revocation of recognition
doc_path: DMEX Chapter 11 Recognition — entities licensed or authorised outside the State of Qatar
DMEX 11.1.18 Continued effect of rules etc after withdrawal or revocation of recognition
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) This rule applies if the Regulatory Authority:
(a) grants an application for the withdrawal of the recognition of a recognised person; or
(b) on its own initiative, revokes the recognition of such a person.
(2) For 6 years after the date on which the withdrawal or revocation takes effect, the Authority may exercise any function in relation to the person under the QFC Law, FSR, these rules, and any other law, regulations or rules applying in the QFC, that it could have exercised if the recognition had not been withdrawn or revoked.
(3) For this rule, the provisions of the QFC Law, FSR, and of any other law, regulations or rules applying in the QFC, have effect as if they were provisions of these rules.
(4) For this rule, the provisions of these rules (including the provisions mentioned in subrule (3)) apply as if:
(a) a reference that is taken to be a reference to an authorised firm or authorised market entity were a reference to the person whose recognition was withdrawn or revoked; and
(b) all other necessary changes were made.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 12.1.2 Authorised Islamic market entities — application of CTRL, Chapter 9
doc_path: DMEX 12.1.2 Authorised Islamic market entities — application of CTRL, Chapter 9
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) CTRL, Chapter 9, applies to an authorised Islamic market entity as set out in this rule.
(2) For that application, a reference in CTRL, Chapter 9 to an Islamic financial institution is to be treated as a reference to an authorised Islamic market entity.
(3) For that application, CTRL, rules 9.2.3 and 9.2.4, are taken to be omitted and the following rule inserted:
“9.2.3 Evaluation of information given to authorised market entity
An authorised Islamic market entity’s governing body must evaluate the suitability and effectiveness of the information and reports that it and the entity’s senior management receive under this Chapter. The test of suitability and effectiveness is whether the information and reports are suitable for effectively overseeing and implementing the principles and requirements set out in this Chapter.”.
Note CTRL, rule 9.2.4, deals with stress-testing. For the requirements in relation to stress-testing for an authorised CCP that is an authorised Islamic market entity, see rule 7.2.11 (3).

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.1.1 Definitions etc for Chapter 13
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) For this Chapter:
deal includes:
(a) entering into, offering to enter into, or refraining from entering or offering to enter into, an agreement in relation to a derivative, and
(b) exercising, or not exercising, a right conferred by a derivative.
related instrument: a financial instrument is related to a derivative if the price or value of the instrument depends on, or has an effect on, the price or value of the derivative.
(2) In this Chapter, a reference to conduct includes a failure to act.
Examples
Failing to correct another person’s incorrect assumption Omitting details from a statement otherwise correct but misleading without the details
(3) For the purposes of this Chapter, information about a derivative is also information about a related instrument.
Guidance
Information about a derivative is information relevant to the derivative’s price or value. The value of a derivative affects the value of a related instrument. For example, information that is relevant to the present value of a derivative would be relevant to the value of a future in the derivative (a related instrument).

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.1.2 Application of Chapter 13 in relation to conduct
doc_path: DMEX 13.1.2 Application of Chapter 13 in relation to conduct
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
This Chapter applies to a person’s conduct in relation to a derivative if:

(a) the derivative has been admitted to trading on an exchange in the QFC;
(b) an application has been made for its admission to trading on an exchange in the QFC; or
(c) it is related to a derivative referred to in paragraph (a) or (b).

Guidance — application of Chapter 13 in relation to State licensed entities and recognised market entities

FSR, article 82, applies to any person carrying on business in or from the QFC. In that application, this Chapter applies in relation to:

• a State licensed entity (see rule 10.1.4 (2))
• a recognised market entity (see rule 11.1.4 (2)).

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.1.5 Establishing that conduct does not contravene FSR, art 82
doc_path: DMEX 13.1.5 Establishing that conduct does not contravene FSR, art 82
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
If a provision of this Chapter says that a kind of conduct is to be regarded as contravening a provision of FSR, article 82, a particular instance of such conduct contravenes that provision of that article unless the person concerned is shown to have been acting properly according to:

(a) a normal or customary practice of the relevant market that is accepted as such by the Regulatory Authority;
(b) the listing rules of the relevant exchange;
(c) any Law, regulations or Rules applicable in the QFC; or
(d) any exemption or justification specified in this Chapter and applicable to the conduct.

(1) For FSR, article 83 (1) and these rules:
inside information, in relation to a derivative, means information that:
(a) is precise (see subrule (2));
(b) is not generally available (see subrule (3));
(c) relates, directly or indirectly, to the derivative or its issuer; and
(d) would, if generally available, be likely to have a significant effect (see subrule (4)) on the price of the derivative or a related instrument.
(2) For paragraph (a) of the definition of inside information, information is precise if:
(a) it describes circumstances that exist or may reasonably be expected to come into existence, or an event that has occurred or may reasonably be expected to occur; and
(b) it is specific enough to enable a conclusion to be drawn about the possible effect of the circumstances or event on the price of a derivative or a related instrument.
(3) For paragraph (b) of that definition, information is generally available if, for example:
(a) it has been disclosed to the market through a regulatory announcement service or otherwise in accordance with the rules of the market or a requirement in a law;
(b) it is available in records that are open to inspection by the public (whether or not a fee is payable);
(c) it is otherwise generally available, including through the Internet or another publication (whether or not a fee is payable), or is derived from information that has been published;
(d) members of the public can obtain it by observation without infringing rights or obligations of privacy, property or confidentiality; or
(e) it can be obtained by analysing or developing other information that is generally available.
(4) For paragraph (d) of that definition, information is taken to be likely to have a significant effect on the price of a derivative or a related instrument if (and only if) it is information of a kind that a reasonable investor would be likely to use as part of the basis of an investment decision.
Guidance
Information of the following kinds about pending orders may be inside information:
• that derivatives of a particular kind have been, or are to be, bought or sold, or that their purchase or sale is under consideration or is the subject of negotiation;
• that derivatives of a particular kind have not been, or are not to be, bought or sold;
• information about the quantity of derivatives bought or sold or whose purchase or sale is under consideration or is the subject of negotiation;
• information about the price (or range of prices) at which derivatives have been, or are to be, bought or sold or the price (or range of prices) at which derivatives, whose purchase or sale is under consideration or is the subject of negotiation, may be bought or sold;
• information about the identity of the persons involved or likely to be involved in any capacity in a purchase or sale.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.3.1 Meaning of insider
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) In this Part:
insider means a person who has inside information, if:
(a) the person obtained the information as a result of:
(i) the person’s membership of an administrative, management or supervisory body of an issuer of derivatives;
(ii) the person’s holding in the capital of an issuer of derivatives;
(iii) the person’s having access to the information through the exercise of the person’s employment, profession or duties;
(iv) the person’s criminal activities; or
(b) the person obtained the information by other means and knows, or could reasonably be expected to know, that the information is inside information.
(2) For paragraph (b) of the definition of insider, a person could reasonably be expected to know that information is inside information if:
(a) a normal and reasonable person in the person’s position would know, or should have known, that the person from whom he or she received the information was an insider; and
(b) a normal and reasonable person in the person’s position who has inside information would have known that it is inside information.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.3.2 What is insider dealing?
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
Each of the following paragraphs describes conduct that is to be regarded as contravening FSR, article 82 (1) and (3):

(a) a person who has inside information uses that information to acquire or dispose of, for his or her own account or for the account of another person, directly or indirectly, a derivative to which that information relates;
(b) a person enters an order and afterwards obtains inside information and amends or cancels the order based on that information;
(c) a person who has inside information recommends that another person deal, or induces another person to deal, on the basis of that information.

Examples of conduct that, in the Regulatory Authority’s opinion, would contravene FSR, article 82

1 A is the CEO of a company that is about to release its semi-annual financial report. The report will disclose an outstanding claim that will have a significant effect on the company’s financial results. A passes this information on to family members who instruct their broker to sell their shares in the company. The Authority considers that the family members would have contravened FSR, article 82 (1) (dealing on the basis of inside information), and A would have contravened FSR, article 82 (2) (disclosing inside information).
2 B, an employee of an oil and gas company, knows through his employment that the company is about to enter into a joint venture agreement with another company that could be very lucrative for his employer. Before the joint venture is disclosed to the market, B buys shares in his employer based on his expectation that the price of the shares will rise significantly after the new joint venture is announced.
3 C, an employee of a firm that is an advisor to a company, D, becomes aware of negotiations for a takeover of D that is likely to be announced to the market imminently. C buys shares in D based on his expectation that the takeover will soon be announced.
4 D, a dealer on the trading desk of a firm dealing in derivatives, accepts a large order from a client to acquire a long position in certain futures. Before executing the order, D trades for the firm and on her personal account by taking a long position in those futures, based on her expectation that she will be able to sell them at a profit because of the significant price increase that will result from the execution of her client’s order. Both trades would contravene article 82 (1) (dealing on the basis of inside information).
4 Investment bank E has been in discussions with an issuer about a potential issue of new derivatives by the issuer. In order to gauge potential investor interest and the terms of the issue, E raises the issue with a potential investor, F, to see if F would be prepared to commit to purchasing some of the derivatives. F uses this inside information to deal in related derivatives.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.3.3 Attempts to deal
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) An attempt to deal is to be regarded as contravening FSR, article 82 (1) if the dealing, had it been completed, would have been regarded as contravening that article.
(2) For subrule (1), a person has attempted to deal if the person takes a substantial step toward dealing but, for reasons that the person does not intend, the dealing is not completed.
Guidance
“Attempting to deal” covers situations where a person who has inside information takes steps to enter into a transaction but the transaction is not executed. For example, if an insider places an order with a broker or instructs another person (such as an investment adviser) to place an order with a broker, but the order is not executed for some reason beyond the person’s control.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.3.4 Conduct that does not amount to insider dealing — general
doc_path: DMEX Division 13.3.B Conduct that does not amount to insider dealing
DMEX 13.3.4 Conduct that does not amount to insider dealing — general
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
Conduct is not to be regarded as contravening FSR, article 82 (1) if:

(a) the person concerned is participating in a liquidity incentive scheme;
(b) the person concerned reasonably believes that the relevant inside information has been disclosed to the market;
(c) the relevant dealing occurs in the performance of an underwriting agreement for the relevant derivative;
(d) the dealing occurs in the performance of a person’s functions as a liquidator or receiver; or
(e) in the case of the execution, by a person who has inside information, of a client order — the person executes the order without giving the information to the client, or otherwise advising or encouraging the client, in relation to the transaction.
Note in relation to conduct in accordance with an accepted practice of the relevant market, see rule 13.1.5.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.3.5 Market-making and authorised counterparties
doc_path: DMEX Division 13.3.B Conduct that does not amount to insider dealing
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) Dealing by a person is not to be regarded as contravening FSR, article 82 (1) if the dealing is on the person’s own account and is solely in the course of the legitimate performance of the person’s functions as a market-maker (see subrule (2)), or any other counterparty that is approved by the relevant exchange.
(2) A person’s dealing in a derivative is likely to be in the course of the legitimate performance of the person’s functions as a market-maker if:
(a) the person holds itself out as willing and able to buy and sell derivatives of that kind at prices that the person determines the person generally and continuously rather than for a particular transaction, and the dealing is either of that kind, or is to hedge a risk arising from such a dealing; and
(b) inside information that is held by the person or persons who make the decision to deal is limited to information about a person’s pending orders.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.3.6 Execution of client orders
doc_path: DMEX Division 13.3.B Conduct that does not amount to insider dealing
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The execution by a person (person A) of an unsolicited client order (see subrule (2)) in a derivative while person A has inside information about the derivative is not to be regarded as contravening FSR, article 82 (1) if person A:
(a) has not disclosed the inside information to the client nor procured the client to deal in the derivative; and
(b) has not otherwise advised or encouraged the client in relation to the order.
(2) A dealing by a person (person A) in a derivative is likely to be in the course of the execution of an unsolicited client order if any of the following paragraphs are satisfied:
(a) the dealing is initiated by the client;
(b) person A has agreed with the client that person A will act in a particular way when carrying out or arranging the carrying out of the order;
(c) person A’s conduct is with a view to facilitating or ensuring the effective carrying out of the order;
(d) person A’s behaviour is reasonable by the standards of conduct of the market, and proportional to any risk undertaken by person A;
(e) the relevant trading by person A on behalf of the client either has no effect on the price, or there has been adequate disclosure to the client that trading will take place without objection from the client;
(f) person A has complied with any applicable conduct of business obligations relating to the execution of the order.
(3) However, it is an indication that person A’s dealing is not the proper execution of an unsolicited client order that the inside information is not limited to information about a person’s pending orders.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.3.7 Effect of information barriers
doc_path: DMEX Division 13.3.B Conduct that does not amount to insider dealing
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
A dealing by an entity is not to be regarded as contravening FSR, article 82 (1) (even though the entity has, at the time, inside information relevant to the dealing) if:

(a) at the time, the entity has in operation an effective information barrier that is reasonably capable of ensuring that:
(i) the information will not be communicated to the individual who makes the decision to deal; and
(ii) no advice about the dealing will be given to the individual by an insider;
(b) the information is not communicated; and
(c) no such advice is given.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

doc_path: DMEX Part 13.4 Disclosure of inside information
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
Examples of conduct that could contravene FSR, article 82 (2)

• a director of an issuer discloses inside information to another individual in a social context
• the selective briefing of analysts by directors of issuers
• B is the CEO of a company that is about to release its annual financial report, which will disclose an outstanding claim that will have a significant effect on the company’s financial results; B tells family members who have no role in the company
• an employee of an issuer selectively briefs analysts about developments relating to the issuer that have not yet been disclosed to the market
• the chairman of a company announces his resignation to a journalist before the information has been disclosed to the market as a whole.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.4.1 Disclosures that do not contravene FSR, article 82 (2)
doc_path: DMEX Part 13.4 Disclosure of inside information
DMEX 13.4.1 Disclosures that do not contravene FSR, article 82 (2)
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) Each of the following paragraphs describes a disclosure of inside information that is to be regarded as not contravening FSR, article 82 (2):
(a) a disclosure that is required or permitted under the legislation applicable in the QFC;
Note For the meaning of legislation applicable in the QFC, see the glossary.
(b) a disclosure to the Regulatory Authority to fulfil a legal or regulatory obligation or otherwise to assist the Authority to perform its functions;
(c) a disclosure in the course of making a report under GENE, Chapter 4A (Protected reporting);
(d) a disclosure to an overseas regulator to fulfil a legal or regulatory obligation or otherwise for the purpose of assisting that regulator to perform its functions;
(e) a disclosure to a court in the course of legal proceedings.
(2) A disclosure is made in the proper course of a person’s employment, profession or duties if, for example:
(a) the disclosure is otherwise in fulfilment of a legal obligation;
(b) the disclosure is reasonable for any of the following purposes:
(i) to enable the recipient to perform the proper functions of his or her employment, profession or duties;
(ii) to facilitate, or seek advice about, a transaction;
Example
a disclosure to a professional adviser
(c) to facilitate a commercial, financial or investment transaction;
(d) if the information disclosed is information about a person’s pending orders:
(i) the person (A) who makes the disclosure does so only to the extent necessary to offer to dispose of a derivative to, or acquire it from, the person who received the information, and solely for that purpose; and
(ii) it is reasonable for A to make the disclosure to enable A to perform the proper functions of A’s employment, profession or duties.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX Part 13.5 Market manipulation
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
Guidance for Part 13.5

An order or transaction is likely to be regarded as contravening FSR, article 82 (4) if:

• it is executed in a particular way to create a false or misleading impression;
• it does not appear to have a legitimate economic rationale;
• the person concerned has another, illegitimate, reason for undertaking it;
• its main purpose appears to be to induce others to trade in, or bid for, a derivative; or to position or move the price of a derivative.
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.content_text: Guidance for Part 13.5 An order or transaction is likely to be regarded as contravening FSR, article 82 (4) if: • it is executed in a particular way to create a false or misleading impression; • it does not appear to have a legitimate economic rationale; • the person concerned has another, illegitimate, reason for undertaking it; • its main purpose appears to be to induce others to trade in, or bid for, a derivative ; or to position or move the price of a derivative .

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.5.1 Market manipulation — false or misleading impression as to supply of, or demand for, or price or value of, derivatives
doc_path: DMEX 13.5.1 Market manipulation — false or misleading impression as to supply of, or demand for, or price or value of, derivatives
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) Each of the following paragraphs describes conduct that is to be regarded as contravening FSR, article 82 (4) (A) by giving, or being likely to give, a false or misleading impression as to the supply of, or demand for, or as to the price or value of, 1 or more derivatives:
(a) buying or selling derivatives at the close of the market, with the intention of misleading investors who act on the basis of closing prices;
(b) entering orders with the intention of creating a false perception of demand or supply;
(c) “wash trades” — that is, the sale or purchase of a derivative without change in beneficial interest or market risk, or if the transfer of beneficial interest or market risk is only between parties acting in collusion, with the intention of creating a false appearance of trading activity;
(d) “layering” — that is, submitting multiple orders in relation to a derivative away from one side of the order book with the intention of executing a trade on the other side of the order book, if the initial manipulative orders will be removed after that trade has taken place;
(e) “momentum ignition” — that is, entering orders or a series of orders in relation to a derivative that are intended to start or exacerbate a trend, and to encourage other participants to accelerate or extend the trend, with the intention of creating an opportunity to unwind or open a position at a favourable price;
(f) “quote stuffing” — that is, entering large numbers of orders (or cancellations of, or updates to, orders) for a derivative with the intention of creating uncertainty for other market participants, slowing down their trading processes, camouflaging a strategy, disrupting or delaying the trading process or making it more difficult to identify genuine orders on the trading system.
Guidance
Although some of the above paragraphs describe conduct that is more commonly associated with algorithmic trading, such as high frequency trading, the Regulatory Authority considers that the conduct described could amount to abusive conduct even if carried out manually.
(2) In considering whether particular conduct contravenes FSR, article 82 (4) (A) by giving, or being likely to give a false or misleading impression as to the supply of, demand for, or price of, a derivative, the Regulatory Authority may take into account the following matters:
(a) the extent to which orders to trade given, or transactions undertaken, represent a significant proportion of the daily volume of transactions in the derivative on the market concerned, and in particular whether those activities lead to a significant change in the price of the derivative;
(b) the extent to which orders to trade given, or transactions undertaken, by persons with a significant buying or selling position in the derivative lead to significant changes in its price;
(c) whether transactions undertaken leave the beneficial ownership of the derivative unchanged;
(d) the extent to which orders to trade given, or transactions undertaken, include position reversals in a short period;
(e) the extent to which orders to trade given, or transactions undertaken, are concentrated in a short period in the trading session and lead to a price change that is subsequently reversed;
(f) the extent to which orders to trade change the representation of the best bid or offer prices in the derivative on a market, or more generally the representation of the order book available to market participants, and are removed before they are executed;
(g) the extent to which orders to trade are given, or transactions are undertaken, at or around a specific time when reference prices, settlement prices and valuations are calculated and lead to price changes that have an effect on such prices and valuations;
(h) the extent to which orders to trade given or transactions undertaken by persons are preceded or followed by the dissemination of false or misleading information by those persons;
(i) any other matter that the Authority reasonably considers to be relevant.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.5.2 Market manipulation — creating artificial price for derivatives
doc_path: DMEX 13.5.2 Market manipulation — creating artificial price for derivatives
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) Each of the following paragraphs describes conduct that is to be regarded as contravening FSR, article 82 (4) (B) by creating an artificial price for a derivative:
(a) “marking the open” and “marking the close” — that is, buying or selling a derivative near the reference time of a trading session (for example, at opening or closing time) or at the end of a particular period (for example, at the end of the quarter or a financial year) with the intention of artificially increasing, decreasing or maintaining a reference price (such as the opening price or closing price) or mislead investors as to that price;
(b) a person (or 2 or more persons acting in collusion) entering both buy and sell orders for a derivative at, or nearly at, the same time, with the same price and quantity, with the intention of artificially positioning the price of the derivative at a particular level;
(c) a person (or 2 or more persons acting in collusion) entering transactions or orders to trade that secure a dominant position over the supply of, or demand for, a derivative or its underlying, with the intention of directly or indirectly fixing a purchase or sale price or creating other unfair trading conditions;
(d) creating a floor (or ceiling) in the price pattern — that is, carrying out transactions or orders to trade in such a way as to create an obstacle to the price of a derivative falling below or rising above a certain level (for example, to ensure that a derivative’s settlement price is above a particular strike price);
(e) entering into transactions or placing orders in relation to a derivative on an exchange with the intention of artificially influencing:
(i) the price of a related instrument on that exchange; or
(ii) the price of the derivative or a related instrument on another exchange.
(2) In considering whether a person’s conduct contravenes FSR, article 82 (4) (B) by securing an abnormal or artificial price for a derivative, the Authority may take into account the following matters:
(a) the extent to which the person has a direct or indirect interest in the price or value of the derivative;
(b) the extent to which movements in price, rate or option volatility, and the volatility of those factors for the derivative, are outside their normal intra-day, daily, weekly or monthly range;
(c) whether the person has successively and consistently increased or decreased the person’s bid or offer, or the price the person has paid, for the derivative;
(d) any other matter that the Authority reasonably considers to be relevant.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.6.1 Fictitious devices etc
doc_path: DMEX Part 13.6 Use of fictitious devices
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) Each of the following paragraphs describes conduct that is to be regarded as contravening FSR, article 82 (5):
(a) a person takes advantage of access (whether occasional or regular) to the media by voicing an opinion about a derivative (or indirectly about its issuer, if applicable) while having previously taken a position on, or submitted 1 or more bids in relation to, that derivative (with the intention of subsequently profiting from the effect of the opinion on the price of the derivative) without having simultaneously disclosed that conflict of interest to the public in a proper and effective way;
(b) a person enters into a transaction or series of transactions in relation to a derivative that are designed to conceal the ownership of the derivative, so that disclosure requirements are circumvented by the holding of the derivative in the name of a colluding party, and disclosures are misleading in relation to the true underlying holding;
(c) “pump and dump” — that is, taking a long position in a derivative and then disseminating misleading positive information about the derivative with a view to increasing its price.
(2) Paragraph (1) (b) does not apply to a nominee holding.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.6.2 Determining whether or not behaviour amounts to use of fictitious device
doc_path: DMEX Part 13.6 Use of fictitious devices
DMEX 13.6.2 Determining whether or not behaviour amounts to use of fictitious device
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
The Regulatory Authority may take the following matters into account in determining whether or not a fictitious device or other form of deception or contrivance has been used:

(a) a person gives orders to trade, submits a bid or undertakes a transaction in a derivative and before or after doing so the person (or a connected person) disseminates false or misleading information about the derivative;
(b) a person gives orders to trade, submits a bid or undertakes a transaction in a derivative and before or after doing so the person (or a connected person) produces or disseminates research or investment recommendations that are erroneous or biased or demonstrably influenced by material interest.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX Part 13.7 Disseminating false or misleading information
doc_path: DMEX Part 13.7 Disseminating false or misleading information
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
Guidance

1 To contravene FSR, article 82 (6), it is not necessary for any transaction to be entered into.
2 A statement that contravenes FSR, article 82 (6), could be made in a variety of ways — for example:
• through a regulatory announcement service;
• through media such as the radio, a newspaper or television;
• through the internet, including social media;
• through a market information service such as a trading terminal;
• by telling another person orally.
3 Examples of conduct that may contravene FSR, article 82 (6):
• spreading a rumour, when the person doing so knew or ought to have known that the rumour was false or misleading;
• recklessly submitting false or misleading information about a derivative through a regulatory announcement service.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.7.1 Truth and falsity of statements for Part 13.7
doc_path: DMEX Part 13.7 Disseminating false or misleading information
DMEX 13.7.1 Truth and falsity of statements for Part 13.7
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) For this Part, a statement is a false statement or a misleading statement if it is objectively false or misleading, whether or not the person who makes it:
(a) knows it to be false or misleading; or
(b) ought reasonably to have known that it is false or misleading (see subrule (3)).
(2) For this Part, the truth or falsity of a statement must be judged as a whole. A reference in this Part to a false or misleading statement includes a statement every part of which is true, but which omits 1 or more facts without which the statement as a whole is untrue or misleading.
(3) A person who makes a false or misleading statement ought reasonably to have known that the statement is false or misleading if a reasonable person in the same position would or should have known, in all the circumstances, that the statement is false or misleading.

QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.title: DMEX 13.7.2 False statement etc inducing a person to deal
doc_path: DMEX Part 13.7 Disseminating false or misleading information
DMEX 13.7.2 False statement etc inducing a person to deal
QFCRA Rules :: Derivatives Markets and E.document_html:
(1) The making of a false statement is to be regarded as contravening FSR, article 82 (6), if:
(a) the person (person A) who makes the statement:
(i) does so with the intention of inducing another person to deal; or
(ii) is reckless or negligent as to whether making the statement may induce another person to deal; and
(b) another person’s dealing would be to person A’s advantage.
(2) For subrule (1):
(a) it is sufficient that the statement is made, and does not matter who the statement is made to;
(b) it is sufficient that person A’s intention is that some other person deal (or that person A is reckless or negligent as to whether some other person may be induced to deal), and does not matter that person A:
(i) has no specific intention as to who must deal; or
(ii) gives no thought as to who may be induced to deal; and
(c) it does not matter that person A has no specific intention about which derivative must be dealt in, nor that any dealing that results is not in the derivative about which person A made the statement.
Examples of conduct that may contravene FSR, article 82:
• a person (person A) circulates marketing information about a derivative to a small group of potential investors; the information includes exaggerated claims about the potential future performance of the derivative when person A knows or ought to know that there is no reasonable basis for making the claims
• a person (person C), a financial adviser who is managing investments for a client, records false or misleading information about the value of investments in the client’s portfolio; person C’s purpose is to ensure that portfolio account statements sent to the client show the value of the portfolio to be higher than its actual value, to induce the client to provide funds to buy further derivatives.
(3) For this rule:
(a) a person is negligent in relation to the effect of a statement if the person gives no thought to the effect of the statement; and
(b) a person is reckless in relation to the effect of a statement if the person knows that the statement may have a particular effect but makes the statement anyway.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2023-1 (as from 1st April 2023)
