QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.2.10 Duties owed to firm by senior management
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.2 Governance — controlled functions and corporate governance framework
INMA 9C.2.10 Duties owed to firm by senior management
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
Each member of a wholesale advisory firm’s senior management owes the following duties to the firm:

(a) to carry out their functions diligently;
(b) to have, and to maintain, the knowledge and skills that may reasonably be expected of an individual who holds a similar appointment, and who carries out similar functions, in the firm’s senior management;
(c) to act for the firm’s benefit; and

(d) if there is a conflict, or a potential conflict, between the member’s interests and the interests of the firm:

(i) to avoid the conflict; or
(ii) if it is not possible to avoid the conflict—to mitigate the conflict.

INMA 9C.2.17 Principle 4 — review of corporate governance framework
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
The approved individual for a wholesale advisory firm’s senior executive function must ensure that the firm reviews its corporate governance framework appropriately, and does so sufficiently often to ensure:

(a) that the framework remains effective;
(b) that, except as allowed under rule 9C.2.18 or 9C.2.19, the functions within the framework remain independent; and
(c) if any gaps or weaknesses in the framework are identified—that any necessary corrective actions are taken in a timely manner.
Note A firm’s corporate governance framework includes the firm’s risk management framework and the firm’s internal controls and assurance framework, see rule 9C.2.7 (1) (a) and (b).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.2.18 Performance of 2 or more controlled functions by same individual
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.2 Governance — controlled functions and corporate governance framework
INMA Division 9C.2.D Governance principles and performance of functions
INMA 9C.2.18 Performance of 2 or more controlled functions by same individual
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) An individual may perform 2 or more controlled functions (combined functions) for a wholesale advisory firm only if:

(a) the firm’s senior executive confirms in writing to the Regulatory Authority that the senior executive is satisfied the individual’s performance of the combined functions:

(i) does not cause a material conflict;
(ii) does not increase the firm’s risk of non-compliance with the law applicable in the QFC, or any other applicable law; and
(iii) is not inappropriate, having regard to the nature, scale and complexity of the firm’s business;

(b) the Authority is satisfied that:

(i) the conditions under paragraph (a) have been met; and
(ii) the individual is able to perform the combined functions adequately; and
(c) the Authority has not given a direction in relation to the individual under subrule (2).

(2) If the Authority is satisfied that it is no longer appropriate for an individual to perform combined functions for a wholesale advisory firm, the Authority may, by written notice, direct the firm to do either or both of the following:

(a) stop combining the functions;
(b) appoint 1 or more other individuals to perform any of the functions.

(3) In particular, the Authority may give a direction under subrule (2) if it is satisfied of any of the following:

(a) that the individual’s continued performance of the combined functions for the firm:

(i) is no longer appropriate, having regard to the nature, scale and complexity of the firm’s business; or
(ii) has caused, or is likely to cause, a material conflict;
(b) that the individual is performing any of the combined functions at a standard that is below the standard at which a reasonable person, having the necessary skills, knowledge and experience, would be expected to perform that function; or
(c) that the performance of the combined functions by the individual has impaired, or is likely to impair, the firm’s compliance with the requirements applicable to the carrying on of its business in or from the QFC.

(4) In this rule:

senior executive, of a wholesale advisory firm, means the approved individual for the firm’s senior executive function.
material conflict, in relation to an individual performing 2 or more controlled functions for a wholesale advisory firm, means:
(a) any compromise to the independence, objectivity or effectiveness of the performance of any of those functions; or
(b) any internal or external conflict of interest for the firm.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.3.2 What is a firm’s internal controls and assurance framework?
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.3 Governance — internal controls and risk management
INMA Division 9C.3.B Internal controls and assurance framework
INMA 9C.3.2 What is a firm’s internal controls and assurance framework?
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) A wholesale advisory firm’s internal controls and assurance framework consists of the following functions (each an internal control and assurance function):

(a) the firm’s risk management function; and
(b) the firm’s compliance oversight function.

(2) The framework must provide reasonable assurance of:

(a) the effectiveness and efficiency of the firm’s operations;
(b) the reliability of the firm's financial reporting; and
(c) the firm’s compliance with any applicable laws.
Note The risk management function and the compliance oversight function are not controlled functions for wholesale advisory firms, see rule 9C.2.2.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

INMA 9C.3.2 What is a firm’s internal controls and assurance framework?
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
A wholesale advisory firm’s internal controls and assurance framework consists of the policies, processes, tasks, behaviours and other aspects of the firm that, taken together

• enable the firm to respond appropriately to business, operational, financial, compliance and other risks to facilitate the firm’s effective operation
• ensure the quality of the firm’s internal and external reporting (which requires adequate records and processes that generate a flow of timely, relevant and reliable information from both internal and external sources for the firm)
• ensure the firm complies with any applicable laws and its own internal policies.

(a) the firm’s business is conducted efficiently;
(b) the firm’s financial records are accurate and complete;
(c) the firm’s financial statements are prepared in a timely manner;
(d) fraud and other unlawful acts are prevented or detected; and
(e) risk is managed effectively.

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) A wholesale advisory firm must give the Regulatory Authority an annual written statement:

(a) that attests the firm’s internal controls and assurance framework was appropriate for the firm during the previous calendar year; or
(b) if framework was not appropriate for the firm during the previous calendar year—that explains how the framework was not appropriate and the steps the firm has taken, or proposes to take, to correct the framework.

(2) A statement prepared by a firm under this rule must:

(a) be signed by the approved individual for the firm’s senior executive function; and
(b) be given to the Regulatory Authority within 1 month after the end of the calendar year to which the statement relates.

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.3.6 Firm must establish and maintain internal control and assurance functions
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.3 Governance — internal controls and risk management

INMA 9C.3.6 Firm must establish and maintain internal control and assurance functions
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
A wholesale advisory firm must establish and maintain internal control and assurance functions that are appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of the firm’s business.

Note A wholesale advisory firm’s internal control and assurance functions are:

• the risk management function; and
• the compliance oversight function, see rule 9C.3.2 (1).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.3.7 Performance of internal control and assurance function — freedom from influence
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.3 Governance — internal controls and risk management
INMA Division 9C.3.B Internal controls and assurance framework
INMA 9C.3.7 Performance of internal control and assurance function — freedom from influence
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) A wholesale advisory firm must ensure that each individual who performs an internal control and assurance function for the firm is sufficiently free from influence so as to be effective in achieving the function’s purpose.

(2) An individual is sufficiently free from influence under subrule (1) if:

(a) they are not remunerated in a way that might undermine their independence and objectivity in exercising the function;
(b) they are not involved in performing a function that generates, or is intended to generate, revenue for the firm;
(c) they are not restricted with regard to the matters they can investigate or report on in their performance of the function;
(d) they can be honest and candid in their reports and conclusions, without fear of reprisal; and
(e) no pressure or influence is exerted upon them to modify their reports or conclusions.

(3) Additionally, a wholesale advisory firm must ensure that each of its control function employees has all of the following:

(a) the necessary authority to perform the function or to carry out their duties;
(b) access to all necessary information, documents and records of the firm;
(c) appropriate access to the firm’s senior management.

(4) In this rule:

control function employee, of a wholesale advisory firm, means:
(a) an employee of the firm who performs either of the firm’s internal control and assurance functions; or
(b) any other employee of the firm who is given responsibilities within the firm’s corporate governance framework.
corporate governance framework, of a wholesale advisory firm, has the meaning given by rule 9C.2.7 (1).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.3.8 Performance of internal control and assurance function — obligation to raise matters promptly
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.3 Governance — internal controls and risk management

INMA 9C.3.8 Performance of internal control and assurance function — obligation to raise matters promptly
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) A wholesale advisory firm’s policies, procedures and controls must provide that an individual performing an internal control and assurance function for the firm must:

(a) promptly, and directly, raise significant matters with the approved individual for the firm’s senior executive function; and
(b) if the individual becomes aware of a significant risk—promptly inform any other individual performing an internal control and assurance function for the firm.

(2) In this rule:

significant risk means a risk, or several risks, taken collectively, that might have a significant effect on:
(a) a wholesale advisory firm’s risk management framework; or
(b) an individual’s performance of an internal control and assurance function for the firm.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

INMA 9C.3.9 What is the risk management function?
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
The risk management function of a wholesale advisory firm is the function of being responsible for:

(a) the firm’s risk management framework; and
(b) overseeing and reviewing the firm’s implementation of, and its compliance with, that framework.
Note For a wholesale advisory firm’s risk management framework, see Division 9C.3.D.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.3.10 Purposes of risk management function
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.3 Governance — internal controls and risk management
INMA Division 9C.3.B Internal controls and assurance framework
INMA 9C.3.10 Purposes of risk management function
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
The purposes of a wholesale advisory firm’s risk management function are to manage the firm’s risk exposure by ensuring that all reasonably foreseeable material risks to the firm are:

(a) monitored; and
(b) responded to,
appropriately and in a timely manner.
Examples of responding to a material risk
• investigating the risk
• controlling or otherwise limiting the risk
• advising or reporting on the risk

INMA 9C.3.11 When firm must appoint competent individual for risk management function
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) A firm must appoint an individual to perform the risk management function for the firm if, due to the nature, scale and complexity of the firm’s business, it is appropriate for the firm to have such an individual.

(2) An individual appointed under subrule (1) must be competent to perform the function for the firm.

Note For assessing an individual’s competence to perform the risk management function for a wholesale advisory firm, see Division 9C.4.E.

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.3.12 What is the compliance oversight function?
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.3 Governance — internal controls and risk management
INMA 9C.3.12 What is the compliance oversight function?
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
The compliance oversight function of a wholesale advisory firm:

(a) is the function of being responsible for:

(i) the firm’s compliance policies, procedures and controls; and
(ii) overseeing and reviewing the firm’s compliance with those policies procedures and controls; and

(b) consists of the following:

(i) the firm’s compliance policies, procedures and controls;
(ii) the individual who performs the compliance oversight function for the firm;
(iii) any other employees allocated responsibilities within the function;
(iv) any parts of the firm’s resources, other than the firm’s employees, that are allocated to the function;
(v) the records kept by the firm in relation to the function.
Note Appropriate records must be kept of policies and procedures, see GENE, rule 6.1.1.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.3.13 Purposes of compliance oversight function
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.3 Governance — internal controls and risk management
INMA 9C.3.13 Purposes of compliance oversight function
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) The purposes of a wholesale advisory firm’s compliance oversight function are as follows:

(a) to ensure the firm complies with:

(i) its own compliance policies, procedures and controls;
(ii) any applicable decisions of the Regulatory Authority in relation to the compliance oversight function; and
(iii) any applicable requirements or standards under the law applicable in the QFC or any other applicable law;
(b) to ensure the firm’s business is conducted ethically and responsibly;
(c) to minimise the risk of the firm, or its facilities, being used in the furtherance of a financial crime.

(2) In this rule:

financial crime means the use of the financial system for criminal, fraudulent or dishonest purposes.

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.3.15 What is a firm’s risk management framework?
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.3 Governance — internal controls and risk management
INMA 9C.3.15 What is a firm’s risk management framework?
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) A wholesale advisory firm’s risk management framework consists of the systems, structures, policies, procedures, controls and people within the firm:

(a) that identify, measure, evaluate, monitor, report on, control or mitigate any material risks for the firm; and
(b) that support the activities mentioned in paragraph (a).
(2) A firm’s risk management framework must be appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of the firm’s business.

INMA 9C.3.16 Objectives of risk management framework
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) A wholesale advisory firm’s risk management framework must:

(a) enable the firm to develop and implement appropriate strategies, policies, procedures and controls to identify and manage material risks; and
(b) provide the firm’s senior management with a comprehensive, firm-wide, view of material risks.

(2) In this rule:

manage includes measure, evaluate, monitor, report on, control and mitigate.

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.4.2 Individual must be a suitable person to perform controlled function
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.4 Individuals — competence and fitness
INMA Division 9C.4.B Assessment of individuals — controlled functions
INMA 9C.4.2 Individual must be a suitable person to perform controlled function
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) This rule applies if a wholesale advisory firm intends to make an approval application for an individual to perform a controlled function for the firm.

(2) Before making the application, the firm must be satisfied, on reasonable grounds and after making appropriate inquiries, that the individual is a suitable person to perform the controlled function for the firm.

Note FSR, article 41 (approval of persons performing controlled functions) provides that:

• the Regulatory Authority may approve an individual to perform a controlled function for an authorised firm; and
• only an approved individual may perform a controlled function for an authorised firm.

(3) The individual is a suitable person to perform the controlled function for the firm if the firm is satisfied that:

(a) the individual is competent to perform the function under rule 9C.4.3;
(b) the individual is a fit and proper person to perform the function under rule 9C.4.4; and
(c) the individual satisfies any additional requirements for the function under these or any other rules.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.4.3 How to assess individual’s suitability — competence
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.4 Individuals — competence and fitness
INMA Division 9C.4.B Assessment of individuals — controlled functions
INMA 9C.4.3 How to assess individual’s suitability — competence
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to a wholesale advisory firm in relation to:

(a) an approved individual for the firm; or
(b) an individual who is the subject of an approval application made by the firm.

(2) The individual is competent to perform a controlled function for the firm if the individual:

(a) has the elements of skills, knowledge and experience listed in Schedule 6 for the function; and

(b) possesses those elements at a level that is appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of:

(i) the role of the function in the firm; and
(ii) the firm’s regulated activities.

(3) In assessing the individual’s competence under subrule (2), the firm must consider:

(a) the following, in relation to the nature, scale and complexity of the firm’s regulated activities:

(i) the products or services the firm offers or provides, or proposes to offer or provide;
(ii) any recent or reasonably expected changes to those products or services, or to the market;
(b) the requirements and characteristics of the function within the firm;
(c) the firm’s customers;
(d) the regulatory system, including any recent or reasonably expected changes to the system; and
(e) any other relevant matter in relation to the function.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.4.4 How to assess individual’s suitability — fitness
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.4 Individuals — competence and fitness
INMA Division 9C.4.B Assessment of individuals — controlled functions
INMA 9C.4.4 How to assess individual’s suitability — fitness
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to a wholesale advisory firm in relation to:

(a) an approved individual for the firm; or
(b) an individual who is the subject of an approval application made by the firm.

(2) The individual is a fit and proper person to perform a controlled function for the firm if, after the firm has considered:

(a) the individual’s honesty, integrity and reputation under subrule (3); and
(b) the individual’s financial soundness under subrule (4),
the firm is satisfied that the individual is a fit and proper person to perform the function for the firm.

(3) The firm must consider any of the following matters that are relevant to its assessment of the individual’s honesty, integrity or reputation:

(a) any past, ongoing or pending legal proceedings, whether civil or criminal, involving or relating to the individual;
(b) any investigation undertaken, or sanction imposed, by a court or tribunal, regulatory body, government body or other professional body on, or in relation to, the individual;
(c) any contravention, or complaint of a contravention, of financial services legislation by, or involving, the individual;
(d) any complaint about the individual’s standard of conduct in relation to activities subject to regulation in any jurisdiction;

(e) any involvement the individual has had with:

(i) a business that has had an insolvency-related event, either while the individual was involved with the business or within 1 year after that involvement ended;
(ii) a business that has been refused a permission to conduct business;
(iii) a business that has had a permission to conduct business removed, restricted or suspended; or
(iv) a business that has been investigated or sanctioned by a court or tribunal, regulatory body, government body or other professional body;

(f) whether the individual has been dismissed, or has resigned at another person’s request, from a position of trust;

Example of a position of trust
a fiduciary appointment
(g) any effect that the individual’s reputation may have on the firm or on the QFC;
(h) if the individual has had any dealings with the Regulatory Authority—whether the individual has been candid and truthful in those dealings.

(4) The firm must consider any of the following matters that are relevant to its assessment of the individual’s financial soundness:

(a) whether the individual is able to pay their debts as they fall due;
(b) any arrangements the individual has made with the individual’s creditors;

(c) whether the individual has ever:

(i) filed for bankruptcy;
(ii) been served with a bankruptcy petition; or
(iii) been subject to a bankruptcy order;
(d) whether the individual’s assets have ever been seized, confiscated or frozen.

(5) In this rule:

financial services legislation includes any regulations, rules, statements of principles or codes of practice made by a professional body.
insolvency-related event means any of the following events:
(a) being wound up or put into liquidation;
(b) being placed in receivership or administration;
(c) ceasing trading;
(d) negotiating a settlement with creditors;
(e) becoming insolvent.
permission to conduct business includes an approval, an authority, a licence and a registration.
professional body includes an exchange, a clearing house and a self-regulatory body.
sanction means any form of disciplinary action and includes criticism, censures, suspensions and expulsions.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
The Regulatory Authority may withdraw its approval for an individual to perform a controlled function for a wholesale advisory firm if the Authority determines that:

(a) the individual is no longer a suitable person to perform the function; or
(b) the individual’s performance of the function has otherwise fallen below the standard at which a reasonable person, having the necessary skills, knowledge and experience for the function, would be expected to perform the function.
Note If the Authority has permitted an approved individual to perform 2 or more controlled functions for a wholesale advisory firm, the Authority may direct the firm to stop combining the functions or appoint 1 or more other individuals to perform any of the functions, see rule 9C.2.18 (2).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.4.8 Firm’s responsibilities if individual stops performing controlled function
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.4 Individuals — competence and fitness

INMA 9C.4.8 Firm’s responsibilities if individual stops performing controlled function
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) This rule applies if a wholesale advisory firm becomes aware that:

(a) an approved individual has stopped, or will stop, performing a controlled function for the firm; and
(b) the Regulatory Authority has not withdrawn, or has not been notified to withdraw, the individual’s approval to perform the function.
(2) The firm must ask the Authority to withdraw its approval for the individual to perform the controlled function for the firm.

(3) A request made under subrule (2) must be made:

(a) at least 10 business days before the day on which the individual will stop performing the function for the firm; or

(b) if a request cannot be made as required by paragraph (a)—within 2 business days after the firm becomes aware that the individual has stopped, or will stop, performing the function for the firm.

Examples for timing of request
1 If, on a business day, a firm becomes aware that an individual will stop performing a controlled function for the firm, the firm must ask the Authority to withdraw its approval for the individual to perform the function by no later than the next business day.
2 If, on a day that is not a business day, a firm becomes aware, that an individual has stopped performing a controlled function for the firm, the firm must ask the Authority to withdraw its approval for the individual to perform the function by no later than 2 business days after that day.

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.4.10 How to assess individual’s competence
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.4 Individuals — competence and fitness
INMA Division 9C.4.E Assessment of individuals — other functions
INMA 9C.4.10 How to assess individual’s competence
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to a wholesale advisory firm in relation to an individual the firm appoints, or intends to appoint, to perform:

(a) the firm’s finance function; or
(b) either of the firm’s internal control and assurance functions.

(2) The individual is competent to perform the function for the firm if the individual has a level of skill, knowledge and experience that is appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of:

(a) the role of the function in the firm; and
(b) the firm’s regulated activities.

(3) In assessing the individual’s competence under subrule (2), the firm must consider:

(a) the nature, scale and complexity of the firm’s activities in relation to:

(i) the firm’s products or services and the market; and
(ii) any recent, or reasonably expected, changes to those products or services, or to the market;
(b) the requirements and characteristics of the function within the firm;
(c) the firm’s customers;
(d) the regulatory system, including any recent, or reasonably expected, changes to the system; and
(e) any other relevant matter in relation to the function.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.4.10 Guidance
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.4 Individuals — competence and fitness
INMA Division 9C.4.E Assessment of individuals — other functions
INMA 9C.4.10 How to assess individual’s competence
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
In deciding whether an individual is competent to perform a function under this rule, a firm may have regard to any of the individual’s skills, knowledge or experience that the firm considers relevant. For example:

1 Finance function

Relevant skills may include:
• working effectively in, or with, accountancy and finance to ensure an organisation’s compliance with prudential requirements;
• displaying high standards of professional ethics in accountancy and finance;
• ensuring an organisation’s accounting records, financial accounts and statements, and auditors’ reports are maintained, reported on, audited and filed in accordance with industry standards;
• reviewing an organisation’s accounting systems; or
• implementing external audit procedures.
Relevant knowledge may include:
• having a recognised professional qualification for the finance function, or another qualification that the firm is satisfied is appropriate for the role; or
• having a membership in an appropriate professional body.
Relevant experience may include having an appropriate level of experience for the role, including experience in positions with an appropriate level of seniority for the role.

2 Risk management function

Relevant skills may include:
• researching an organisation and its requirements to inform risk management strategy and policy;
• establishing a risk management strategy or policy for an organisation;
• identifying, assessing and reporting risk management information to the senior management of an organisation;
• identifying available resources, and facilitating action planning, to manage risk within an organisation;
• facilitating business continuity planning and disaster recovery;
• developing and maintaining third-party relationships that are relevant to risk management;
• developing and maintaining effective risk management communication within an organisation; or
• monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of risk management controls in an organisation.
Relevant knowledge may include having a recognised professional qualification for the risk management function, or another qualification that the firm is satisfied is appropriate for the role.
Relevant experience may include having an appropriate level of experience for the role, including experience in a position with an appropriate level of seniority for the role.

3 Compliance oversight function

Relevant skills may include:
• researching an organisation and its requirements to inform the organisation’s compliance policy;
• developing, communicating or implementing a compliance policy, or assisting in the development of an organisation’s compliance culture;
• developing, monitoring and reporting on compliance controls;
• planning and delivering compliance training, or otherwise supporting employees in maintaining compliance;
• maintaining effective relationships with third parties and responding to requests for consultations;
• identifying, investigating and resolving non-compliant activity within an organisation;
• dealing with complaints regarding compliance;
• informing regulators of breaches in rules and regulations;
• keeping up to date with regulatory developments;
• advising on the regulatory implications of new business strategies; or
• developing and monitoring an organisation’s compliance with its training and competency programme and other resources.
Relevant knowledge may include:
• having the CISI regulatory qualification; or
• having a recognised professional qualification for the compliance oversight function, at certificate level, or another qualification that the firm is satisfied is appropriate for the role.
Relevant experience may include having an appropriate level of experience for the role, including experience in a position with an appropriate level of seniority for the role.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.5.10 Evidence of compliance
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.5 Individuals — conduct principles and ongoing obligations
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) A wholesale advisory firm must maintain all necessary records to enable the firm to:

(a) comply with this Part and Part 9C.4; and
(b) demonstrate, at all times, that the firm has complied with those Parts.

(2) Without limiting subrule (1), the firm must maintain a record of each decision the firm makes about an individual under this Part, or Part 9C.4, which includes:

(a) the inquiries the firm made before making the decision, including:

(i) the dates on which the firm made the inquiries; and
(ii) the results of the inquiries;
(b) the rules the firm considered or complied with in making the decision and, if appropriate, how the decision complied with the rules;
(c) any other matters the firm considered in making the decision; and
(d) the date on which the decision was made.

(3) The firm must retain a record made under this rule:

(a) for at least 6 years after the day on which the record was made; or
(b) if the record is about an individual who is performing, or who has performed, a controlled function for the firm—for at least 6 years after the day on which the individual last performs the function for the firm.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.6.1 Customer classification
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.6 Dealings with customers — general
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) Before conducting business with or for a customer, a wholesale advisory firm must take reasonable steps to ensure the customer is a wholesale customer.

(2) A wholesale advisory firm:

(a) must only conduct business with or for a customer that the firm is satisfied is a wholesale customer; and
(b) must have appropriate systems and controls to ensure the firm’s classification of each customer as a wholesale customer is appropriate.
Note Wholesale customer is defined in rule 9C.1.2 (1) (c).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.6.2 When is an agent a customer of a firm?
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.6 Dealings with customers — general
INMA 9C.6.2 When is an agent a customer of a firm?
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) This rule applies if:

(a) a wholesale advisory firm provides, or offers to provide, a service to a person (an agent) that the firm knows is acting as agent for another person (the principal); and
(b) the service is a regulated activity.
(2) The firm must treat the principal as the firm’s customer in relation to that service, unless the agent is another wholesale advisory firm.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.7.1 Reliance on customer information given by third parties
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.7 Dealings with customers — information handling, conflicts and liability
INMA Division 9C.7.A Third-party information and exclusion or restriction of liability
INMA 9C.7.1 Reliance on customer information given by third parties
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to a wholesale advisory firm if the firm relies on information relating to a customer of the firm:

(a) that was given to the firm by a person other than the customer (a third party); and
(b) that is of a type that the firm is required to obtain under this Part, or Part 9C.6.
(2) The firm is taken to have complied with the requirement to obtain the information if the firm can show it is reasonable for the firm to rely on the information provided by the third party.

(3) For subrule (2), it is reasonable for a firm to rely on information provided by a third party if:

(a) the information was given to the firm in writing; and

(b) the firm is satisfied, on reasonable grounds, that:

(i) the third party is competent to give the information; and
(ii) the information is accurate.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

(2) The firm is taken to have complied with the requirement to obtain the information if the firm can show it is reasonable for the firm to rely on the information provided by the third party. INMA 9C.7.2 Giving customer information to third parties

(a) directly to the customer to whom the information relates: or
(b) if the customer has given the firm written permission to disclose the information to a third party—to the third party.

(2) In this rule:

disclosable information, in relation to a customer of a wholesale advisory firm, means information that the firm is required to give to the customer under this Part or Part 9C.6.

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.7.5 Firm must have conflicts of interest and material interests policy
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.7 Dealings with customers — information handling, conflicts and liability
INMA Division 9C.7.B Managing conflicts, material interests and inducements
INMA 9C.7.5 Firm must have conflicts of interest and material interests policy
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) A wholesale advisory firm must have, and must operate in accordance with, a written policy on conflicts of interest and material interests that is:

(a) appropriate to the nature, scale and complexity of the regulated activities carried out by, or on behalf of, the firm; and
(b) approved by the approved individual for the firm’s senior executive function.

(2) The firm’s policy:

(a) must identify, with reference to the firm’s regulated activities, any circumstances that constitute, or that may give rise to, a conflict of interest or a material interest; and
(b) must include systems and controls to ensure that any circumstance identified under paragraph (a) does not cause a customer of the firm to be treated unfairly or be otherwise adversely affected.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.7.6 Management of conflicts of interest and material interests
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.7 Dealings with customers — information handling, conflicts and liability
INMA Division 9C.7.B Managing conflicts, material interests and inducements
INMA 9C.7.6 Management of conflicts of interest and material interests
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) This rule applies if a wholesale advisory firm cannot reasonably avoid either of the following in relation to the firm’s regulated activities:

(a) a conflict of interest with a customer of the firm; or
(b) holding a material interest.

(2) The firm must manage the conflict of interest, or material interest, in relation to each employee who performs a function:

(a) in connection with the interest;
(b) in relation to a regulated activity of the firm; and

(c) of a type that could, if not managed by the firm:

(i) negatively affect the interests of a customer of the firm; or
(ii) otherwise increase the firm’s risk of non-compliance with this Part or Part 9C.6.
Guidance
An employee’s performance of a function under this rule includes, for example, performing the function by carrying out an activity, providing a service, exercising a discretion or advising a customer.

(3) The firm may manage an interest, under subrule (2), in relation to an employee of the firm:

(a) by requiring the employee to disregard the conflict of interest, or material interest, when performing the function;
(b) by establishing measures to prevent or restrict any person from exercising inappropriate influence over how the employee performs the function;
(c) by arranging for the employee to be supervised by separate individuals, or within separate reporting structures, than other employees who perform the same function for the firm;
(d) by establishing measures to prevent, or to control, the employee’s performance of simultaneous or sequential steps in the function;

(e) by establishing measures to prevent, or to control the employee’s performance of simultaneous or sequential functions:

(i) in relation to the same regulated activity; or
(ii) for the same customer of the firm; or

(f) by taking any other steps that are necessary or appropriate:

(i) to manage the interest; or
(ii) to otherwise satisfy the requirements of this Part or Part 9C.6.

(4) If the firm offers its employees commission-based remuneration, the firm must ensure that offering the remuneration does not impair its ability:

(a) to act in its customers’ best interests; or
(b) to otherwise satisfy the requirements of this Part or Part 9C.6, to the extent they relate to providing suitable products or services to the firm’s customers.

(5) In this rule:

commission-based remuneration, for an employee of a wholesale advisory firm:
(a) means remuneration given under an arrangement that is connected to, and affected by, the employee providing or recommending products or services to the firm’s customers; and
(b) includes benefits of any kind.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.7.7 Disclosure of conflicts of interest and material interests
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.7 Dealings with customers — information handling, conflicts and liability
INMA Division 9C.7.B Managing conflicts, material interests and inducements
INMA 9C.7.7 Disclosure of conflicts of interest and material interests
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) Before a wholesale advisory firm may engage in a regulated activity that involves providing or offering to provide a product or service to a customer, the firm must:

(a) disclose to the customer any conflict of interest or material interest of the firm, of which the firm is aware, in relation to the activity;
(b) notify the customer of the steps the firm has taken to manage the conflict of interest or material interest; and
(c) take reasonable steps to ensure that the customer does not object to the firm’s management of the conflict of interest or material interest.
(2) If the firm cannot manage a conflict of interest or a material interest in a transaction under rule 9C.7.6, the firm must decline to act in the transaction.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.7.8 Chinese walls
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.7 Dealings with customers — information handling, conflicts and liability
INMA Division 9C.7.B Managing conflicts, material interests and inducements
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) A wholesale advisory firm must ensure there are effective Chinese walls, or other information barriers, between different business areas of the firm in relation to information that could:

(a) give rise to a conflict of interest; or
(b) be otherwise open to abuse.

(2) The firm’s procedures for maintaining Chinese walls or other information barriers within the firm must:

(a) be written;
(b) include the consequences of a breach of the procedures; and
(c) be given to each relevant employee of the firm.

(3) In this rule:

relevant employee, of a wholesale advisory firm:
(a) means any employee of the firm who, in the performance of their role, could influence the proper functioning of a Chinese wall or other information barrier within the firm; and
(b) includes the firm’s senior management.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.7.9 Inducements generally
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.7 Dealings with customers — information handling, conflicts and liability
INMA Division 9C.7.B Managing conflicts, material interests and inducements
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) A wholesale advisory firm must ensure that neither the firm, nor any of its employees:

(a) offers or gives a gift or inducement to a third party;
(b) solicits or accepts a gift or inducement from a third party; or

(c) directs or refers any actual or potential business to a third party:

(i) on the initiative of the firm, or an employee of the firm; or
(ii) on the instructions of an associate of the firm,
if doing so is likely to conflict to a significant extent with any duty the firm owes to its customers.
(2) The firm’s systems and controls must include policies and procedures to ensure the firm complies with subrule (1).
(3) The firm must ensure that every member of the firm’s senior management, and every employee of the firm, is given details of the firm’s policies and procedures about gifts, referrals, and inducements.

(4) In this rule:

associate, of a wholesale advisory firm, means:

(a) any person, including an individual, who has an interest:

(i) held in common with the firm, or with an employee of the firm; and
(ii) of a type that could give rise to a conflict of interest with a third party;
(b) a parent entity of the firm; or
(c) a direct or indirect subsidiary of the firm.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) A wholesale advisory firm must have the necessary systems and controls to ensure the firm complies with this Part and Part 9C.6.

(2) The firm’s systems and controls must be:

(a) written; and
(b) reviewed, to ensure they are fit for purpose, at least once every 12 months.
(3) The approved individual for the firm’s senior executive function must be given a written report on the outcome of each review conducted under subrule (2) (b).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA 9C.7.11 Evidence of compliance — customer information
doc_path: INMA Part 9C.7 Dealings with customers — information handling, conflicts and liability
INMA 9C.7.11 Evidence of compliance — customer information
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) A wholesale advisory firm must maintain a register containing all documents and information obtained or prepared by the firm under this Part or Part 9C.6 in relation to a customer of the firm.

(2) The register must include the following documents or information for each customer of the firm:

(a) the customer’s contact details and any other documents or information used by the firm to identify the customer;

(b) documents completed or signed by the customer in relation to the provision, or potential provision, of a product or service;

Example for paragraph (b)
an application form submitted by a customer for the provision of a service by a firm
(c) any other documents or information given to, or correspondence with, the customer in relation to the provision, or potential provision, of a product or service.

(3) The firm must retain a record under this rule:

(a) for a record of a transaction with a customer—for at least 10 years after the day on which the transaction was discontinued or completed; or

(b) for any other customer record:

(i) for at least 6 years from the day on which the firm last provided a product or service to the customer concerned; or
(ii) if another provision of this Chapter requires the firm to keep the record for a longer period—for the longer period.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

INMA 9C.8.10 Firm must have AML/CFT policy
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) A wholesale advisory firm must have a written AML/CFT policy:

(a) that sets out how the firm will comply with its obligations under the AML/CFT Law and this Part;

(b) that is risk-sensitive, appropriate and adequate, having regard to:

(i) the risk of the firm’s involvement in money laundering or terrorism financing; and
(ii) the size, complexity and nature of the firm’s business; and
(c) that includes any procedures, systems, controls, or other matters that are relevant to the firm’s compliance with the AML/CFT Law and this Part.

(2) A wholesale advisory firm’s AML/CFT policy must, at a minimum, set out the firm’s procedures for:

(a) screening individuals:

(i) during recruitment for employment by the firm; or
(ii) for existing employees—for appointment to a new or expanded role within the firm; and
(b) detecting, reporting, and keeping records of suspicious transactions of which the firm is aware; and
(c) communicating the policy to the firm’s employees and officers.
(3) A wholesale advisory firm may comply with this rule by using AML/CFT policy of the firm’s head office, if that policy satisfies the requirements of this rule.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA S2.1 Confirmation notes — general content requirements

INMA S2.1 Confirmation notes — general content requirements
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
A confirmation note for a transaction by an INMA firm for a customer must include the following information:

(a) the firm's name and address;
(b) the firm's regulatory status in a form required by GENE, Part 3.1;
(c) if the firm executed the transaction as principal or agent — that fact;
(d) the customer's name (or other means of identification) and account number if any;
(e) a description of the relevant investment, including the amount invested;
(f) whether the transaction is a sale or purchase;
(g) the price or unit price at which the transaction was executed;
(h) if the transaction involves a conversion of currency — the rate of exchange obtained;
(i) the date of the transaction;
(j) either:
(i) the time of the transaction; or
(ii) a statement that information about the time of the transaction will be provided on request;
(k) the total amount payable and the date it is payable;
(l) the remuneration of the firm and any associate (unless the associate is not obliged to disclose it to the firm because, for example, the firm is its customer) in relation to the transaction;
(m) the amount of any commission, any mark-up or mark-down, any fees, charges, taxes or duties, or any other costs (however described or applied) unless included in remuneration mentioned in paragraph (k);
(n) if the transaction involved, or will involve, the purchase of a currency with another currency — the rate of exchange involved or a statement that the rate will be supplied when the currency has been purchased, including if applicable the maturity or expiry date of any currency hedge;
(o) whether there is a right to cancel the transaction and, if there is a right to cancel, the consequences of exercising the right, and enough details to enable that right to be exercised by a retail customer.
Inserted by QFCRA RM/2019-4 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA S2.2 Confirmation notes — additional information for derivatives
doc_path: INMA Schedule 2 Content of confirmation notes
INMA S2.2 Confirmation notes — additional information for derivatives
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
A confirmation note relating to a transaction in derivatives for a customer must also include the following information:

(a) the maturity, delivery or expiry date of the derivative;
(b) for an option — the last exercise date, whether it can be exercised before maturity and the strike price;
(c) whether the exercise creates a sale or purchase in the underlying asset;
(d) if the transaction closes out an open futures position — all essential details required in relation to each contract included in the open position and each contract by which it was closed out, and the profit or loss to the customer from closing out that position;
(e) on the exercise of an option:
(i) the date of exercise, and either the time of exercise or that the customer will be notified of the time on request; and
(ii) the strike price of the option and, if applicable, the total consideration from or to the customer.
Note For a currency option, the rate of exchange will be the same as the strike price.
Inserted by QFCRA RM/2019-4 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA S2.3 Confirmation notes — additional information for collective investment schemes

INMA S2.3 Confirmation notes — additional information for collective investment schemes
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
A confirmation note relating to a transaction in units in a collective investment scheme for a customer must also include the following information:

(a) if the INMA firm is not the operator and the transaction was executed with the customer by the firm as principal — that fact;
(b) the name of the scheme and the type and number of units involved;
(c) the amount of:
(i) the operator's initial charges (if any) in cash or percentage terms; and
(ii) any subsequent charges made by the firm to the customer in relation to the transaction and, unless the subsequent charges to the customer are made on the same terms as the operator's initial charges, the basis on which the amount of the subsequent charges was decided;
(d) whether the transaction was executed on a historic-price or forward-price basis.
Inserted by QFCRA RM/2019-4 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:

(a) if the INMA firm is not the fund manager of the fund and the transaction was executed with the customer by the firm as principal — that fact;
(b) the name of the fund and the type and number of units involved;
(c) the amount of:
(i) the fund manager’s initial charges (if any) in cash or percentage terms; and
(ii) any subsequent charges made by the firm to the customer in relation to the transaction and, unless the subsequent charges to the customer are made on the same terms as the fund manager’s initial charges, the basis on which the amount of the subsequent charges was decided;
(d) whether the transaction was executed on a historic-price or forward-price basis.

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA S4.1 Investment research recommendations — additional requirements
doc_path: INMA Schedule 4 Additional obligations for investment research recommendations
INMA S4.1 Investment research recommendations — additional requirements
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) An INMA firm must take reasonable care to ensure that a research recommendation produced by it:
(a) indicates all substantially material sources (including, if appropriate, the issuer and whether the research recommendation has been disclosed to the issuer and amended after this disclosure;
(b) adequately summarises any basis of valuation or methodology used:
(i) to evaluate a security, a derivative or an issuer; or
(ii) to set a price target for a security or derivative;
(c) adequately explains the meaning of:
(i) any recommendation made (for example, 'buy' 'sell' or 'hold') and the time horizon applying to the recommendation; and
(ii) any risk warnings, including any sensitivity analysis of the relevant assumptions; and
(d) refers to:
(i) the planned frequency (if any) of updates of the research recommendation; and
(ii) any major changes in the scope of the research as previously announced; and
(e) states clearly and prominently:
(i) the date the research recommendation was first released for distribution; and
(ii) the date and time of any security or derivative price mentioned.
(2) If the substance of the research recommendation (the later recommendation) differs from the substance of an earlier research recommendation that was about the same security, derivative or issuer and was issued during the 12-month period before the day of dissemination of the later recommendation, the later recommendation must clearly and prominently indicate the difference and state the date of the earlier research recommendation.
(3) If complying with the requirements of subrule (1) (a), (b) or (c) would be disproportionate to the length of the research recommendation and there has been no change in the methodology or basis of valuation used, the INMA firm may, instead of complying with the requirements, clearly and prominently refer in the research recommendation to where the required information can be directly and easily accessed (for example, by a hyperlink to the information on an appropriate web page of the firm).
(4) Subrule (1) (a) does not apply in relation to a non-written research recommendation to the extent that complying with it would be disproportionate to the length of the research recommendation.
Inserted by QFCRA RM/2019-4 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA S4.2 Investment research recommendation — general standards for disclosure of interests etc
doc_path: INMA Schedule 4 Additional obligations for investment research recommendations
INMA S4.2 Investment research recommendation — general standards for disclosure of interests etc
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) An INMA firm must disclose, in a research recommendation produced by it:
(a) all of its relationships and circumstances that may reasonably be expected to impair the objectivity of the research recommendation, and in particular:
(i) any significant financial interest in a relevant investment that is the subject of the research recommendation;
(ii) a significant conflict of interest in relation to an issuer; and
(b) relationships and circumstances, of the kind mentioned in paragraph (a), of each person working for the firm who was involved in preparing the substance of the research recommendation, including whether the person's [individual's?] remuneration is tied to investment banking transactions performed by the firm or any affiliate of the firm.
(2) If the INMA firm is a legal person, the information disclosed must include the following:
(a) any interests or conflicts of interest of the firm or any related person that are accessible, or reasonably expected to be accessible, to the persons involved in the preparation of the substance of the research recommendation;
(b) any interests or conflicts of interest of the firm or any related person known to persons who, although not involved in the preparation of the substance of the research recommendation, had or could reasonably be expected to have had access to the substance of the research recommendation before its dissemination (other than persons whose only access to the research recommendation was to ensure compliance with relevant regulatory or statutory obligations, including the disclosures required under this Schedule).
(3) If the disclosures required by subrules (1) and (2) would be disproportionate to the length of the research recommendation, the INMA firm may, instead of complying with the requirements of the subrules, clearly and prominently refer in the research recommendation to where the required disclosures can be directly and easily accessed (for example, by a hyperlink to the disclosures on an appropriate web page of the firm).
(4) Subrules (1) and (2) do not apply in relation to a non-written research recommendation to the extent that complying with them would be disproportionate to the length of the research recommendation.
Inserted by QFCRA RM/2019-4 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA S4.3 Investment research for recommendations — additional requirements for disclosure of interests
doc_path: INMA Schedule 4 Additional obligations for investment research recommendations
INMA S4.3 Investment research for recommendations — additional requirements for disclosure of interests
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to a research recommendation produced by an INMA firm in relation to a relevant investment.
(2) The INMA firm must clearly and prominently disclose in the research recommendation the following information on its interests and conflicts of interest:
(a) major shareholdings that exist between it or any related person and the issuer (the relevant issuer) including:
(i) shareholdings exceeding 5% of the total issued share capital in the relevant issuer that are held by the firm or any related person; or
(ii) shareholdings exceeding 5% of the total issued share capital of the firm or any related person that are held by the relevant issuer;
(b) any other financial interests held by the firm or any related person in relation to the relevant issuer that are significant in relation to the research recommendation;
(c) if applicable, a statement that the firm or any related person is a market maker or liquidity provider in the securities of the relevant issuer or in any related derivatives;
(d) if applicable, a statement that the firm or any related person has been lead manager or co-lead manager, over the previous 12 months, of any publicly disclosed offer of securities of the relevant issuer or in any related derivatives;
(e) if applicable, a statement that the firm or any related person is party to any other agreement with the relevant issuer for the provision of investment banking services;
(f) if applicable, a statement that the firm or any related person is party to an agreement with the relevant issuer relating to the production of the research recommendation.
(3) Subrule (2) (e) does not apply in relation to an agreement if:
(a) disclosure of the statement would involve the disclosure of confidential information; and
(b) the agreement has been in force for at least 12 months or has given rise during that period to a payment or to the promise of payment.
(4) The INMA firm must disclose, in general terms, in the research recommendation the organisational and administrative arrangements set up within the firm to effectively prevent or deal with conflicts of interest in relation to research recommendations, including information barriers.
(5) If a person working for the INMA firm who is involved in the preparation of the research recommendation receives or buys shares of the relevant issuer before a public offering of the shares, the price at which the shares were acquired and the date of acquisition must be disclosed in the research recommendation.
(6) The INMA firm must publish the following information on a quarterly basis, and must disclose in its research recommendations:
(a) the proportion of all research recommendations published during the quarter that are 'buy', 'hold', 'sell' or equivalent terms;
(b) the proportion of relevant investments in each of those categories issued by issuers to which the firm provided material investment banking services during the last 12 months.
(7) If the disclosures required by subrules (2) to (6) would be disproportionate to the length of the research recommendation, the INMA firm may, instead of complying with the subrules, clearly and prominently refer in the research recommendation to where the required disclosures can be directly and easily accessed (for example, by a hyperlink to the disclosures on an appropriate web page of the firm).
(8) Subrules (2) to (6) do not apply in relation to a non-written research recommendation to the extent that complying with them would be disproportionate to the length of the research recommendation.
Inserted by QFCRA RM/2019-4 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.title: INMA S4.5 Investment research recommendations — requirements for dissemination of third party recommendations
doc_path: INMA Schedule 4 Additional obligations for investment research recommendations
INMA S4.5 Investment research recommendations — requirements for dissemination of third party recommendations
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) If a research recommendation produced by a third party is substantially changed before dissemination by an INMA firm, the firm must ensure that:
(a) the disseminated material clearly describes the change in detail;
(b) if the change consists of a change of the direction of the recommendation (for example, changing a 'buy' recommendation into a 'hold' or 'sell' recommendation), the firm complies with section S4.3 to the extent of the change, as if the firm were the producer of the research recommendation; and
(c) it has a formal written policy under which the persons receiving the research recommendation are directed to where they can have access to the identity of the producer of the research recommendation, the research recommendation itself, and the disclosure of the producer's interests or conflicts of interest, to the extent that they are publicly available.
(2) Subrule (1) does not apply in relation to news reporting on research recommendations produced by a third party if the substance of the research recommendation is not changed.
(3) If an INMA firm disseminates a summary of a research recommendation produced by a third party, it must ensure that the summary:
(a) is fair, clear and not misleading;
(b) identifies the source research recommendation; and
(c) identifies where the third party's disclosures (to the extent that they are publicly available) relating to the source research recommendation can be directly and easily accessed (for example, by a hyperlink to the disclosures on an appropriate web page of the firm).
Inserted by QFCRA RM/2019-4 (as from 1st January 2020).

doc_path: INMA Schedule 5 Recordkeeping — dealing and managing
INMA S5.1 Minimum records of customer orders
QFCRA Rules :: Investment Management and.document_html:
(1) An INMA firm must record the information required by table S5.1 if an event mentioned in the table happens.

Table S5.1 Minimum details for dealing and managing

  event minimum details required
1 firm receives a customer order or decides to execute a transaction for a customer order in the exercise of its discretion 1 the customer's name (or other means of identification) and account number if any

2 if relevant, the date and time the customer order is received by the firm

3 if relevant, the date and time that the firm decides to execute a transaction for the customer order in the exercise of its discretion

4 the name of the employee who received the customer order or made the decision to execute the transaction

5 the relevant investment, and the number, or total value of, the relevant investment (including any price limit or trading instructions)

6 whether the customer order is for a purchase or sale

7 any other instruction received by the firm from the customer about the carrying out of the customer order (including any amendments of the customer order or cancellation of the customer order)
2 firm executes a transaction for a customer order 1 the customer's name (or other means of identification) and account number if any

2 the name of the counterparty, if known to the firm

3 the date and time of the transaction, if available

4 the name of the employee executing the transaction

5 the relevant investment, and the number, or total value of, the relevant investment

6 the price and other significant terms (including exchange rate details, if relevant)

7 whether the transaction was a purchase or sale
3 firm passes a customer order to another person for execution of transaction 1 the name of the person instructed

2 the terms of the instructions

3 the date and time the instruction was given.
(2) However, if the INMA firm acts as an investment manager and its decision to effect a transaction of a customer is contemporaneous with the execution of the relevant customer order or its passing of the relevant customer order to another person for execution, the firm does not need to create separate records of the time of the decision to deal, and the time of execution of the customer order or passing the customer order to the other person, if the transaction record contains a note or other indication that these happened contemporaneously.
Inserted by QFCRA RM/2019-4 (as from 1st January 2020).
