QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Banking Business.title: IBANK Part 2 Definitions
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Banking Business.document_html:
absolute value of a number means the value of the number irrespective of sign.

accounting standards include accounting rules, principles, practices and conventions.

additional tier 1 capital has the meaning given by rule 3.2.10.

affiliate, of a party, means any entity of which the party holds 10% or more, but less than a majority, of the voting power.

Note This definition does not apply in rule 3.2.36 — see rule 3.2.36 (10).

approved website means a website that is approved under the Interpretation and Application Rules 2005, rule 3.1.2.

authorisation means an authorisation granted under FSR, Part 5.

authorised firm (or firm) means a person that has an authorisation.

bank exposure — see rule 4.4.9 (6).

banking book — see rule 3.1A.1.

base capital requirement has the meaning given by rule 3.2.4.

Basel III framework means the system by that name for the prudential regulation of banks, published by the BCBS and in effect as at 1 January 2023 or later.

Basel III LCR: see Part 8.4, note.

Basel Accords is the collective name for Basel I, Basel II and Basel III, which are a set of reform measures issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision to improve the regulation, supervision, risk management and capital adequacy of financial institutions.

branch means the local office in the QFC of a legal person incorporated outside the QFC.

business day means a day that is not a Friday, a Saturday, or a public or bank holiday in Qatar.

capital adequacy ratio has the meaning given by rule 3.2.6.

capital conservation buffer has the meaning given by rule 3.3.1 (2).

capital relief is the reduction, in the credit risk capital requirement for an exposure, obtained from the use of a CRM technique.

commodity means a physical or energy product that may be traded, including precious metals (other than gold), base metals, agricultural products, minerals, oil, gas and electricity.

commodity murabahah transaction (or CMT) has the meaning given by rule 1.3.6 (2).

common equity tier 1 capital (or CET 1 capital) has the meaning given by rule 3.2.8.

compliance oversight function means the function described in CTRL, rule 1.2.13.

connected, in relation to a party, has the meaning given by rule 5.1.3.

corporate exposure — see rule 4.4.9 (7).

corporate group has the meaning given by rule 9.1.2 (1).

counter-cyclical capital buffer has the meaning given by rule 3.3.1 (3).

counterparty means any person with or for whom an Islamic banking business firm conducts, or intends to conduct, Islamic banking business, Islamic investment business or associated business.

credit enhancement, of sukuk, has the meaning given by rule 10.2.16.

credit risk has the meaning given by rule 4.1.2.

credit risk capital requirement means the amount of capital that an Islamic banking business firm must have to cover its credit risk.

customer means a person to whom an Islamic banking business firm provides, has provided or offers to provide a service or product, and includes a business customer of the firm (within the meaning given in CIPR).

day means a period of 24 hours starting at midnight.

defaulted (or in default) — see rule 4.4.80.

displaced commercial risk (or DCR) has the meaning given by rule 11.2.2 (2).

eligible collateral has the meaning given by rule 4.6.12 (except in Subdivision 4.6.B.3).

Note    In that Subdivision, eligible collateral has an extended meaning — see rule 4.6.16.

eligible guarantor has the meaning given by rule 4.6.16.

eligible netting agreement has the meaning given by rule 4.6.19.

entity means any kind of entity, and includes, for example, any person.

equity participation risk has the meaning given by rule 1.3.24 (1).

excess spread has the meaning given by rule 10.2.19.

executive governance function means the function described in CTRL, rule 1.2.6.

exercise control: an entity (entity A) exercises control over another (entity B) if:

(a) entity A holds 10% or more of the shares of entity B, or is entitled to exercise or control the exercise of 10% or more of the voting power in entity B;
(b) entity A holds 10% or more of the shares in a parent entity of entity B or is entitled to exercise or control the exercise of 10% or more of the voting power in a parent entity of entity B; or
(c) entity A is able to exercise significant influence over the management of entity B or a parent entity of entity B because of entity A's shareholding or voting power, or by contractual or other arrangements.

exposure means the maximum loss that an Islamic banking business firm might suffer as a result of the default or failure of a counterparty, connected counterparties, issuer or connected issuers.

external credit rating agency — see rule 4.3.1

finance function means the function described in CTRL, rule 1.2.9.

financial asset includes:

(a) cash;
(b) a right to receive cash or another financial asset or a commodity; and
(c) an equity instrument.

financial communication, by an Islamic banking business firm, means any communication (made through any medium including brochures, telephone calls and presentations) the purpose or effect of which is:

(a) to promote or advertise the firm's services or products; or
(b) to invite or induce any person to enter into an agreement with any person in relation to those services or products.

financial group has the meaning given by rule 9.1.2 (2).

financial instrument means a contract that gives rise to a financial asset of one entity and a financial liability or equity instrument of another entity.

financial liability means an obligation to deliver cash, another financial asset or a commodity.

governing body of an entity means its board of directors, committee of management or other governing body (whatever it is called).

home jurisdiction, for an entity, means the jurisdiction where the entity's authorisation or licence was granted.

home regulator, for an entity, means the financial regulator in the jurisdiction in which the entity's authorisation or licence was granted.

IFSB–12: see Part 8.4, note.

IFSB-17 means the Core Principles for Islamic Finance Regulation (Banking Segment) published by the Islamic Financial Services Board in April 2015.

IFSB-23 means the Revised Capital Adequacy Standard For Institutions Offering Islamic Financial Services [Banking Segment] published by the Islamic Financial Services Board in December 2021.

IFSB GN 6: see Part 8.4, note.

ijarah muntahia bittamleek (or IMB) has the meaning given by rule 1.3.13.

impaired credit has the meaning given by rule 4.3.5 (1).

in default (or defaulted) — see rule 4.4.80.

internal audit function means the function described in CTRL, rule 1.2.14.

internal capital adequacy assessment process (or ICAAP) has the meaning given by rule 3.1.5.

instrument includes a financial instrument, a foreign exchange instrument and a commodity instrument.

investment fund (or fund) means an entity that is established for the purpose of investing the pooled funds of investors (held as units or shares) in assets.

investment grade means a rating of at least BBB- or equivalent.

investment risk reserve (or IRR) has the meaning given by rule 11.2.5 (5).

investments includes Islamic investments.

Islamic bank has the meaning given by rule 1.1.7.

Islamic banking business has the meaning given by rule 1.1.5.

Islamic banking business firm has the meaning given by rule 1.1.9.

Islamic collective investment fund means:

(a) an Islamic fund within the meaning of the Collective Investment Schemes Rules 2010;
(b) an Islamic fund within the meaning of the Professional Investor Funds Rules 2022; or
(c) any other collective investment fund whose entire business operations are conducted in accordance with Shari’a.

Islamic financial contract includes the contracts for raising funds or providing financing in a Shari'a-compliant manner described in Part 1.3.

Islamic financial institution means an authorised firm whose authorisation includes a condition that the whole of the firm's business must be conducted in accordance with Shari'a.

Islamic investment business has the meaning given by rule 1.1.6.

Islamic investment dealer has the meaning given by rule 1.1.8.

Islamic investments has the meaning given by rule 1.1.6 (2).

jurisdiction means any kind of legal jurisdiction, and includes, for example:

(a) the State of Qatar;
(b) a foreign country (whether or not an independent sovereign jurisdiction), or a state, province or other territory of such a foreign country; and
(c) the QFC or a similar jurisdiction.

large exposure has the meaning given by rule 5.3.1.

large exposure limit means either limit in rule 5.2.9.

legal person means an entity (other than an individual) on which the legal system of a jurisdiction confers rights and imposes duties, and includes, for example, any entity that can own, deal with or dispose of property.

long settlement transaction means a transaction in which a party undertakes to deliver a security, a commodity, or a foreign exchange amount in exchange for cash, another financial instrument, or a commodity, after a period that is longer than the shorter of:

(a) the market standard for the transaction; and
(b) 5 business days after the date on which the transaction is entered into.

liquidity facility, for sukuk, has the meaning given by rule 10.4.6 (3).

liquidity risk has the meaning given by rule 8.1.1 (3).

mark-to-market has the meaning given by rule 6.1.10 (1).

mark-to-model has the meaning given by rule 6.1.11 (1).

minimum capital requirement has the meaning given by rule 3.2.3 (2).

monetise means convert into cash (whether by sale, repo or in any other way).

month means calendar month — that is, the period beginning at the start of any day of one of the 12 named months of the year and ending:

(a) at the end of the day before the corresponding day of the next named month; or
(b) if there is no corresponding day—at the end of the last day of the next named month.

murabahah for purchase orderer contract (or MPO contract) has the meaning given by rule 1.3.4.

non-performing exposure means an exposure that is classified as non-performing in accordance with rule 4.7.10 (4).

over-the-counter: an over-the-counter transaction is one done directly between the parties, without the supervision of an exchange.

Note Over-the-counter trading is also called off-exchange trading.

parent entity, for a legal person (A), means any of the following:

(a) a legal person that holds a majority of the voting power in A;
(b) a legal person that is a member of A (whether direct or indirect, or though legal or beneficial entitlement) and alone, or together with 1 or more legal persons in the same corporate group, holds a majority of the voting power in A;
(c) a parent entity of any legal person that is a parent entity of A.

Note Legal person and corporate group are defined in this glossary.

person means:

(a) an individual (including an individual occupying an office or position from time to time); or
(b) a legal person.

problem asset has the meaning given by rule 4.1.3(3).

profit equalisation reserve (or PER) has the meaning given by rule 11.2.5 (4).

profit-sharing investment account (or PSIA) has the meaning given by rule 11.1.2.

profit rate risk in the trading book has the meaning given by rule 6.6.1

qard has the meaning given by rule 1.3.25.

qualifying central counterparty — see rule 4.6A.20.

rate of return risk (or ROR risk) has the meaning given by rule 11.2.1 (1).

recognised exchange means an exchange set out in Schedule 1 or in a notice published by the Regulatory Authority on an approved website.

regulated activity means an activity that is a regulated activity under FSR.

Regulatory Authority means the Qatar Financial Centre Regulatory Authority.

regulatory capital has the meaning given by rule 3.2.7.

related party, of an Islamic banking business firm, has the meaning given by rule 4.8.3.

restricted PSIA has the meaning given by rule 11.1.2 (3).

retained securitisation exposure has the meaning given by rule 10.4.1.

risk-based capital requirement has the meaning given by rule 3.2.5.

risk management function means the function described in CTRL, rule 1.2.12.

Rules means rules made by the Regulatory Authority under FSR, article 15 (1), and includes:

(a) any standard, principle or code of practice made by the authority; and
(b) any other instrument made or in force under any Rules.

securities financing transaction includes a repurchase agreement (“repo”), a reverse repurchase agreement (“reverse repo”) and any other securities lending or borrowing transaction where the value of the transaction depends on the market valuation of the securities.

Guidance

A securities financing transaction is typically subject to a margin agreement. Such a transaction might be:

• a repurchase transaction — selling a security and agreeing to repurchase it in the future for the original sum of money plus a return for the use of that money
• lending a security for a fee in return for a guarantee in the form of financial instruments or cash given by the borrower
• a buy-sell back transaction or sell-buy back transaction
• a margin lending transaction.

senior executive function means the function described in CTRL, rule 1.2.8.

Shari'a supervisory board, of an Islamic banking business firm, means the board appointed for the firm under rule 12.1.2.

special purpose entity or SPE has the meaning given by rule 10.2.7.

subsidiary: a legal person (A) is a subsidiary of another legal person (B) if B is a parent entity of A.

sukuk has the meaning given by rule 10.1.2.

tawarruq has the meaning given by rule 1.3.6 (1).

terms of business (of an Islamic banking business firm for a customer) means a statement or statements in writing of the terms on which the firm will conduct business with or for the customer.

tier 1 capital has the meaning given by rule 3.2.7 (2).

tier 2 capital has the meaning given by rule 3.2.12.

total risk-weighted assets has the meaning given by rule 3.2.1 (2).

trading book — see rule 3.1A.1.

unit in an Islamic collective investment fund means:

(a) a unit in an Islamic fund within the meaning of the Collective Investment Schemes Rules 2010;
(b) a unit in an Islamic fund within the meaning of the Professional Investor Funds Rules 2022;
(c) a unit in any other collective investment fund whose entire business operations are conducted in accordance with Shari’a.

unrestricted PSIA has the meaning given by rule 11.1.2 (2).

withdrawal risk has the meaning given by rule 11.2.2 (1).

writing means any form of writing, and includes, for example, any way of representing or reproducing words, numbers, symbols or anything else in legible form (for example, by printing or photocopying).

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Banking Business.content_text: absolute value of a number means the value of the number irrespective of sign. accounting standards include accounting rules, principles, practices and conventions. additional tier 1 capital has the meaning given by rule 3.2.10 . affiliate , of a party, means any entity of which the party holds 10% or more, but less than a majority, of the voting power. Note This definition does not apply in rule 3.2.36 — see rule 3.2.36 (10). approved website means a website that is approved under the Interpretation and Application Rules 2005 , rule 3.1.2 . authorisation means an authorisation granted under FSR, Part 5 . authorised firm (or firm ) means a person that has an authorisation. bank exposure — see rule 4.4.9 (6). banking book — see rule 3.1A.1 . base capital requirement has the meaning given by rule 3.2.4 . Basel III framework means the system by that name for the prudential regulation of banks, published by the BCBS and in effect as at 1 January 2023 or later. Basel III LCR : see Part 8.4 , note. Basel Accords is the collective name for Basel I, Basel II and Basel III, which are a set of reform measures issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision to improve the regulation, supervision, risk management and capital adequacy of financial institutions. branch means the local office in the QFC of a legal person incorporated outside the QFC. business day means a day that is not a Friday, a Saturday, or a public or bank holiday in Qatar. capital adequacy ratio has the meaning given by rule 3.2.6 . capital conservation buffer has the meaning given by rule 3.3.1 (2). capital relief is the reduction, in the credit risk capital requirement for an exposure, obtained from the use of a CRM technique. commodity means a physical or energy product that may be traded, including precious metals (other than gold), base metals, agricultural products, minerals, oil, gas and electricity. commodity murabahah transaction ( or CMT ) has the meaning given by rule 1.3.6 (2). common equity tier 1 capital (or CET 1 capital ) has the meaning given by rule 3.2.8 . compliance oversight function means the function described in CTRL, rule 1.2.13 . connected , in relation to a party, has the meaning given by rule 5.1.3 . corporate exposure — see rule 4.4.9 (7). corporate group has the meaning given by rule 9.1.2 (1). counter-cyclical capital buffer has the meaning given by rule 3.3.1 (3). counterparty means any person with or for whom an Islamic banking business firm conducts, or intends to conduct, Islamic banking business, Islamic investment business or associated business. credit enhancement , of sukuk , has the meaning given by rule 10.2.16 . credit risk has the meaning given by rule 4.1.2 . credit risk capital requirement means the amount of capital that an Islamic banking business firm must have to cover its credit risk. customer means a person to whom an Islamic banking business firm provides, has provided or offers to provide a service or product, and includes a business customer of the firm (within the meaning given in CIPR). day means a period of 24 hours starting at midnight. defaulted (or in default ) — see rule 4.4.80 . displaced commercial risk (or DCR ) has the meaning given by rule 11.2.2 (2). eligible collateral has the meaning given by rule 4.6.12 (except in Subdivision 4.6.B.3) . Note In that Subdivision, eligible collateral has an extended meaning — see rule 4.6.16 . eligible guarantor has the meaning given by rule 4.6.16 . eligible netting agreement has the meaning given by rule 4.6.19 . entity means any kind of entity, and includes, for example, any person. equity participation risk has the meaning given by rule 1.3.24 (1). excess spread has the meaning given by rule 10.2.19 . executive governance function means the function described in CTRL, rule 1.2.6 . exercise control : an entity ( entity A ) exercises control over another ( entity B ) if: (a) entity A holds 10% or more of the shares of entity B, or is entitled to exercise or control the exercise of 10% or more of the voting power in entity B; (b) entity A holds 10% or more of the shares in a parent entity of entity B or is entitled to exercise or control the exercise of 10% or more of the voting power in a parent entity of entity B; or (c) entity A is able to exercise significant influence over the management of entity B or a parent entity of entity B because of entity A's shareholding or voting power, or by contractual or other arrangements. exposure means the maximum loss that an Islamic banking business firm might suffer as a result of the default or failure of a counterparty, connected counterparties, issuer or connected issuers. external credit rating agency — see rule 4.3.1 finance function means the function described in CTRL, rule 1.2.9 . financial asset includes: (a) cash; (b) a right to receive cash or another financial asset or a commodity; and (c) an equity instrument. financial communication , by an Islamic banking business firm, means any communication (made through any medium including brochures, telephone calls and presentations) the purpose or effect of which is: (a) to promote or advertise the firm's services or products; or (b) to invite or induce any person to enter into an agreement with any person in relation to those services or products. financial group has the meaning given by rule 9.1.2 (2). financial instrument means a contract that gives rise to a financial asset of one entity and a financial liability or equity instrument of another entity. financial liability means an obligation to deliver cash, another financial asset or a commodity. governing body of an entity means its board of directors, committee of management or other governing body (whatever it is called). home jurisdiction , for an entity, means the jurisdiction where the entity's authorisation or licence was granted. home regulator , for an entity, means the financial regulator in the jurisdiction in which the entity's authorisation or licence was granted. IFSB–12 : see Part 8.4 , note. IFSB-17 means the Core Principles for Islamic Finance Regulation (Banking Segment) published by the Islamic Financial Services Board in April 2015. IFSB-23 means the Revised Capital Adequacy Standard For Institutions Offering Islamic Financial Services [Banking Segment] published by the Islamic Financial Services Board in December 2021. IFSB GN 6 : see Part 8.4 , note. ijarah muntahia bittamleek (or IMB ) has the meaning given by rule 1.3.13 . impaired credit has the meaning given by rule 4.3.5 (1). in default (or defaulted ) — see rule 4.4.80 . internal audit function means the function described in CTRL, rule 1.2.14 . internal capital adequacy assessment process (or ICAAP ) has the meaning given by rule 3.1.5 . instrument includes a financial instrument, a foreign exchange instrument and a commodity instrument. investment fund (or fund ) means an entity that is established for the purpose of investing the pooled funds of investors (held as units or shares) in assets. investment grade means a rating of at least BBB- or equivalent. investment risk reserve (or IRR ) has the meaning given by rule 11.2.5 (5). investments includes Islamic investments. Islamic bank has the meaning given by rule 1.1.7 . Islamic banking business has the meaning given by rule 1.1.5 . Islamic banking business firm has the meaning given by rule 1.1.9 . Islamic collective investment fund means: (a) an Islamic fund within the meaning of the Collective Investment Schemes Rules 2010 ; (b) an Islamic fund within the meaning of the Professional Investor Funds Rules 2022 ; or (c) any other collective investment fund whose entire business operations are conducted in accordance with Shari’a. Islamic financial contract includes the contracts for raising funds or providing financing in a Shari'a-compliant manner described in Part 1.3 . Islamic financial institution means an authorised firm whose authorisation includes a condition that the whole of the firm's business must be conducted in accordance with Shari'a. Islamic investment business has the meaning given by rule 1.1.6 . Islamic investment dealer has the meaning given by rule 1.1.8 . Islamic investments has the meaning given by rule 1.1.6 (2). jurisdiction means any kind of legal jurisdiction, and includes, for example: (a) the State of Qatar; (b) a foreign country (whether or not an independent sovereign jurisdiction), or a state, province or other territory of such a foreign country; and (c) the QFC or a similar jurisdiction. large exposure has the meaning given by rule 5.3.1 . large exposure limit means either limit in rule 5.2.9 . legal person means an entity (other than an individual) on which the legal system of a jurisdiction confers rights and imposes duties, and includes, for example, any entity that can own, deal with or dispose of property. long settlement transaction means a transaction in which a party undertakes to deliver a security, a commodity, or a foreign exchange amount in exchange for cash, another financial instrument, or a commodity, after a period that is longer than the shorter of: (a) the market standard for the transaction; and (b) 5 business days after the date on which the transaction is entered into. liquidity facility , for sukuk , has the meaning given by rule 10.4.6 (3). liquidity risk has the meaning given by rule 8.1.1 (3). mark-to-market has the meaning given by rule 6.1.10 (1). mark-to-model has the meaning given by rule 6.1.11 (1). minimum capital requirement has the meaning given by rule 3.2.3 (2). monetise means convert into cash (whether by sale, repo or in any other way). month means calendar month — that is, the period beginning at the start of any day of one of the 12 named months of the year and ending: (a) at the end of the day before the corresponding day of the next named month; or (b) if there is no corresponding day—at the end of the last day of the next named month. murabahah for purchase orderer contract (or MPO contract ) has the meaning given by rule 1.3.4 . non-performing exposure means an exposure that is classified as non-performing in accordance with rule 4.7.10 (4). over-the-counter: an over-the-counter transaction is one done directly between the parties, without the supervision of an exchange. Note Over-the-counter trading is also called off-exchange trading. parent entity , for a legal person ( A ), means any of the following: (a) a legal person that holds a majority of the voting power in A; (b) a legal person that is a member of A (whether direct or indirect, or though legal or beneficial entitlement) and alone, or together with 1 or more legal persons in the same corporate group, holds a majority of the voting power in A; (c) a parent entity of any legal person that is a parent entity of A. Note Legal person and corporate group are defined in this glossary. person means: (a) an individual (including an individual occupying an office or position from time to time); or (b) a legal person. problem asset has the meaning given by rule 4.1.3 (3). profit equalisation reserve (or PER ) has the meaning given by rule 11.2.5 (4). profit-sharing investment account (or PSIA ) has the meaning given by rule 11.1.2 . profit rate risk in the trading book has the meaning given by rule 6.6.1 qard has the meaning given by rule 1.3.25 . qualifying central counterparty — see rule 4.6A.20 . rate of return risk (or ROR risk ) has the meaning given by rule 11.2.1 (1). recognised exchange means an exchange set out in Schedule 1 or in a notice published by the Regulatory Authority on an approved website. regulated activity means an activity that is a regulated activity under FSR. Regulatory Authority means the Qatar Financial Centre Regulatory Authority. regulatory capital has the meaning given by rule 3.2.7 . related party , of an Islamic banking business firm, has the meaning given by rule 4.8.3 . restricted PSIA has the meaning given by rule 11.1.2 (3). retained securitisation exposure has the meaning given by rule 10.4.1 . risk-based capital requirement has the meaning given by rule 3.2.5 . risk management function means the function described in CTRL, rule 1.2.12 . Rules means rules made by the Regulatory Authority under FSR, article 15 (1), and includes: (a) any standard, principle or code of practice made by the authority; and (b) any other instrument made or in force under any Rules. securities financing transaction includes a repurchase agreement (“repo”), a reverse repurchase agreement (“reverse repo”) and any other securities lending or borrowing transaction where the value of the transaction depends on the market valuation of the securities. Guidance A securities financing transaction is typically subject to a margin agreement. Such a transaction might be: • a repurchase transaction — selling a security and agreeing to repurchase it in the future for the original sum of money plus a return for the use of that money • lending a security for a fee in return for a guarantee in the form of financial instruments or cash given by the borrower • a buy-sell back transaction or sell-buy back transaction • a margin lending transaction. senior executive function means the function described in CTRL, rule 1.2.8 . Shari'a supervisory board , of an Islamic banking business firm, means the board appointed for the firm under rule 12.1.2 . special purpose entity or SPE has the meaning given by rule 10.2.7 . subsidiary : a legal person ( A ) is a subsidiary of another legal person ( B ) if B is a parent entity of A. sukuk has the meaning given by rule 10.1.2 . tawarruq has the meaning given by rule 1.3.6 (1). terms of business (of an Islamic banking business firm for a customer) means a statement or statements in writing of the terms on which the firm will conduct business with or for the customer. tier 1 capital has the meaning given by rule 3.2.7 (2). tier 2 capital has the meaning given by rule 3.2.12 . total risk-weighted assets has the meaning given by rule 3.2.1 (2). trading book — see rule 3.1A.1 . unit in an Islamic collective investment fund means: (a) a unit in an Islamic fund within the meaning of the Collective Investment Schemes Rules 2010 ; (b) a unit in an Islamic fund within the meaning of the Professional Investor Funds Rules 2022 ; (c) a unit in any other collective investment fund whose entire business operations are conducted in accordance with Shari’a. unrestricted PSIA has the meaning given by rule 11.1.2 (2). withdrawal risk has the meaning given by rule 11.2.2 (1). writing means any form of writing, and includes, for example, any way of representing or reproducing words, numbers, symbols or anything else in legible form (for example, by printing or photocopying). QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
The glossary at the end of these rules is part of these rules.

Note 1 There are also relevant definitions in the INAP glossary. To assist the reader, the application of a definition in that glossary is usually indicated by the defined term's being in italics (other than bold italics) in these rules.

Note 2 By contrast, the application of a definition in the glossary in these rules is not indicated by the defined term's being in italics.

Note 3 For the application of definitions, see INAP, r 2.1.8 (Application of definitions).

Note 4 A note on or to these rules is explanatory and is not part of the rules (see INAP, r 2.1.6 (1) and r 2.1.7).

Note 5 However, examples and guidance are part of these rules (see INAP, r 2.1.4 (1) (b) and (2)).

Note 6 An example is not exhaustive, and may extend, but does not limit, the meaning of these rules or the particular provision of these rules to which it relates (see INAP, r 2.1.5).

Note 7 For the effect of guidance, see FSR, art 17 (4).

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI 1.2.2 What is an Islamic financial institution?
doc_path: ISFI 1.2.2 What is an Islamic financial institution?
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
An Islamic financial institution is an authorised firm whose authorisation includes a condition that the whole of the firm's business must be conducted in accordance with Shari'a.

Note For firms that conduct a part (but not the whole) of their business in accordance with Shari'a, see ch 8 (Islamic windows).

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI 3.1.3 Guidance
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
1 One of the important matters required to be disclosed by an Islamic financial institution pursuant to ISFI Rule 3.1.3(b) is the basis applied by the institution in treating any insurance deficit or surplus. Appendix B to AAOIFI FAS 13 provides some guidance as to how such a deficit or a surplus may be treated.
2 That appendix states that there are a number of ways to address an insurance deficit, including—
(a) settling the deficit from the reserve of policyholders, if any; and
(b) borrowing from the shareholders funds or from others the amount of the deficit which should be paid back from future surpluses; and
(c) asking the policyholders to meet the deficit pro rata; and
(d) increasing the future premium contribution of policyholders on a pro rata basis.
3. That appendix also states that there are a number of ways to allocate an insurance surplus, including—
(a) allocating the surplus to all policyholders, regardless of whether or not they have made claims on the policy during the financial period; and
(b) allocating the surplus only among policyholders who have not made any claims during the financial period; and
(c) allocating the surplus among those who have not made any claims and among those who have made claims of amounts less than their insurance contributions, provided that the latter category of policyholders should receive only the difference between their insurance contributions and their claims during the financial period; and
(d) allocating the surplus between policyholders and shareholders; and
(e) allocating the surplus by using other methods.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2012-3 (as from 1st February 2013)

doc_path: ISFI Chapter 5 Policies, procedures, systems and controls
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:

Amended by QFCRA RM/2012-3 (as from 1st February 2013)

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI 5.1.2 Policy and procedures manual
doc_path: ISFI Chapter 5 Policies, procedures, systems and controls
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
An Islamic financial institution must establish, implement and maintain an Islamic financial business policy and procedures manual that addresses the following matters:

(a) how the compliance oversight function will be undertaken in relation to compliance with Shari'a;
(b) how the institution's Shari'a supervisory board will oversee and advise it in regard to the institution's Islamic financial business;
(c) how fatwas, rulings and guidelines of the Shari'a supervisory board will be recorded, disseminated and implemented and the internal Shari'a review undertaken;

Note For the requirement to conduct an internal Shari'a review, see r 6.3.1.
(d) how disputes between the Shari'a supervisory board and the institution in relation to Shari'a compliance will be addressed;
(e) the process for approving the internal policies, procedures, systems and controls to ensure that—
(i) Islamic financial business is conducted in accordance with Shari'a; and
(ii) information is disseminated to investors appropriately;
(f) how conflicts of interest and potential conflicts of interest will be identified and managed.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2017-3 (as from 1st April 2017).

(d) how disputes between the Shari'a supervisory board and the institution in relation to Shari'a compliance will be addressed; (e) the process for approving the internal policies, procedures, systems and controls to ensure that— (i) Islamic financial business is conducted in accordance with Shari'a; and (ii) information is disseminated to investors appropriately; (f) how conflicts of interest and potential conflicts of interest will be identified and managed. QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI 6.1.1 Appointment of Shari'a supervisory board
doc_path: ISFI Part 6.1 Appointment and Operation of a Shari'a Supervisory Board
ISFI 6.1.1 Appointment of Shari'a supervisory board
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
An Islamic financial institution must—

(a) appoint a Shari'a supervisory board; and
(b) ensure that—
(i) its Shari'a supervisory board consists of at least 3 members; and
(ii) the members appointed to the Shari'a supervisory board are competent to perform their functions as Shari'a supervisory board members taking into account their qualifications and previous experience; and
(iii) any appointments, dismissals or changes in respect of members of the Shari'a supervisory board are approved by the governing body of the Islamic financial institution; and
(iv) no member of the Shari'a supervisory board is a director or controller of the Islamic financial institution.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2015-3 (as from 1st January 2016).

(c) the remuneration of the members of the Shari'a supervisory board.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2015-3 (as from 1st January 2016).

ISFI 6.1.4 Records of assessment of competency of Shari'a supervisory board
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
The records of the assessment of competence of Shari'a supervisory board members in ISFI rule 6.1.3(a) must include at a minimum—

(a) the factors that have been taken into account when making the assessment of competence; and
(b) the qualifications and experience of the Shari'a supervisory board members; and
(c) the basis upon which the Islamic financial institution considers that the proposed Shari'a supervisory board member is suitable; and
(d) details of any other Shari'a supervisory boards of which the proposed Shari'a supervisory board member is, or has been, a member.

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI 6.1.7 Obligation to assist Shari'a supervisory board
doc_path: ISFI Part 6.1 Appointment and Operation of a Shari'a Supervisory Board
ISFI 6.1.7 Obligation to assist Shari'a supervisory board
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
An Islamic financial institution must take reasonable steps to ensure that it and its Employees—

(a) provide such assistance as the Shari'a supervisory board reasonably requires to discharge its duties; and
(b) give the Shari'a supervisory board right of access at all reasonable times to relevant records and information; and
(c) do not interfere with the Shari'a supervisory board's ability to discharge its duties; and
(d) do not provide false or misleading information to the Shari'a supervisory board.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2015-3 (as from 1st January 2016).

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI 6.2.2 Annual Shari'a report
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
(1) An Islamic financial institution must commission an annual report from the Shari'a supervisory board which complies with the AAOIFI Standards on Governance (GSIFI No 1).
(2) An Islamic financial institution must give the Regulatory Authority a copy of each annual report of the firm's Shari'a supervisory board within 3 months after the day the relevant financial year of the institution ends.

Example

If a financial year of an Islamic financial institution ends on 31 December in a year, the annual report of the institution's Shari'a supervisory board must be given to the Regulatory Authority before 1 April in the next year.

Amended by QFCRA RM/2017-3 (as from 1st April 2017).

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI 6.2.3 Financial communication
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
(1) Before an Islamic financial institution issues or approves a financial communication, it must ensure that, in addition to the information required by the Customer and Investor Protection Rules 2019, the material states which Shari'a supervisory board has reviewed the products or services to which the material relates.
(2) Financial communication means any communication (made through any medium including brochures, telephone calls and presentations) the purpose or effect of which is:
(a) to promote or advertise:
(i) specified products; or
(ii) any regulated activity (or any activity that would be a regulated activity if it was carried on in or from the QFC); or
(b) to invite or induce any person:
(i) to enter into an agreement with any person in relation to a specified product; or
(ii) to engage in any regulated activity (or an activity that would be a regulated activity if it was carried on in or from the QFC).
Amended by QFCRA RM/2019-4 (as from 1st January 2020).
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.content_text: (1) Before an Islamic financial institution issues or approves a financial communication, it must ensure that, in addition to the information required by the Customer and Investor Protection Rules 2019 , the material states which Shari'a supervisory board has reviewed the products or services to which the material relates. (2) Financial communication means any communication (made through any medium including brochures, telephone calls and presentations) the purpose or effect of which is: (a) to promote or advertise: (i) specified products ; or (ii) any regulated activity (or any activity that would be a regulated activity if it was carried on in or from the QFC); or (b) to invite or induce any person : (i) to enter into an agreement with any person in relation to a specified product ; or (ii) to engage in any regulated activity (or an activity that would be a regulated activity if it was carried on in or from the QFC). Amended by QFCRA RM/2019-4 (as from 1st January 2020).

endnotes: Amended by QFCRA RM/2019-4 (as from 1st January 2020).

An Islamic financial institution must perform an internal Shari'a review to assess the extent to which the institution complies with fatwas, rulings and guidelines issued by its Shari'a supervisory board.

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI Chapter 8 Islamic windows
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.content_text: ISFI Chapter 8 Islamic windows

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI 8.1.1 What is an Islamic window?
doc_path: ISFI 8.1.1 What is an Islamic window?
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
If an authorised firm conducts a part (but not the whole) of its business in accordance with Shari'a, the part so conducted is an Islamic window.

Inserted by QFCRA RM/2012-3 (as from 1st February 2013)
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.content_text: If an authorised firm conducts a part (but not the whole) of its business in accordance with Shari'a, the part so conducted is an Islamic window . Inserted by QFCRA RM/2012-3 (as from 1st February 2013)

endnotes: Inserted by QFCRA RM/2012-3 (as from 1st February 2013)

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI 8.1.2 What kinds of business may be conducted by means of an Islamic window?
doc_path: ISFI 8.1.2 What kinds of business may be conducted by means of an Islamic window?
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
(1) Only insurance business (within the meaning given in PINS, rule 1.2.4) may be conducted by means of an Islamic window.
(2) An authorised firm that is a banking business firm (within the meaning given in BANK) or an INMA firm (within the meaning given in INMA) must not operate an Islamic window.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2014-3 (as from 1st January 2015)

(2) An authorised firm that is a banking business firm (within the meaning given in BANK) or an INMA firm (within the meaning given in INMA) must not operate an Islamic window. Amended by QFCRA RM/2014-3 (as from 1st January 2015)

endnotes: Amended by QFCRA RM/2014-3 (as from 1st January 2015)

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI 8.1.3 Authorisation to operate Islamic window
doc_path: ISFI 8.1.3 Authorisation to operate Islamic window
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
(1) An applicant for authorisation that proposes to operate an Islamic window must state that fact in its application.
(2) An authorised firm that proposes to operate an Islamic window must apply to the Regulatory Authority for an appropriate variation of the conditions of its authorisation.
Inserted by QFCRA RM/2012-3 (as from 1st February 2013)

Inserted by QFCRA RM/2012-3 (as from 1st February 2013)

endnotes: Inserted by QFCRA RM/2012-3 (as from 1st February 2013)

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI 8.1.4 Conditions of operating Islamic windows
doc_path: ISFI 8.1.4 Conditions of operating Islamic windows
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
(1) An authorised firm that operates an Islamic window—
(a) must identify the part or parts of its business that are to be conducted in accordance with Shari'a; and
(b) must establish and maintain policies, procedures, systems and controls that ensure that that part or those parts are so conducted.
(2) An authorised firm that operates an Islamic window must comply with—
(a) chapter 3 (except rule 3.1.1A); and
(b) chapter 5;
in relation to the part or parts of its business conducted by means of the window.
(3) For the application of chapter 3 and chapter 5 to such a firm, references to an Islamic financial institution are to be read as references to the firm.
(4) The firm must ensure that the disclosures required by AAOIFI FAS 18 are made to each customer with or for whom it conducts Islamic financial business.
Amended by QFCRA RM/2019-4 (as from 1st January 2020).

(4) The firm must ensure that the disclosures required by AAOIFI FAS 18 are made to each customer with or for whom it conducts Islamic financial business. Amended by QFCRA RM/2019-4 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI 8.1.5 Shari'a supervisory board
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
(1) An authorised firm that operates an Islamic window must comply with chapter 6 in relation to the part or parts of its business that is conducted by means of the window.
(2) For the application of chapter 6 to such a firm, references to an Islamic financial institution are to be read as references to the firm.
Inserted by QFCRA RM/2012-3 (as from 1st February 2013)

endnotes: Inserted by QFCRA RM/2012-3 (as from 1st February 2013)

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI 8.1.6 Performance of internal Shari'a review
doc_path: ISFI 8.1.6 Performance of internal Shari'a review
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
(1) An authorised firm that operates an Islamic window must, to the extent possible, perform the internal Shari'a review in accordance with the AAOIFI Standards on Governance (GSIFI No. 3).

Note An authorised firm that operates an Islamic window must perform an internal Shari'a review of the firm's compliance with fatwas, rulings and guidelines issued by its Shari'a supervisory board — see r 6.3.1, as applied by r 8.1.5.
(2) If the firm cannot perform its entire internal Shari'a review in accordance with those standards, it must document how it will perform the remainder of that review.
Inserted by QFCRA RM/2012-3 (as from 1st February 2013)

QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.title: ISFI Glossary
QFCRA Rules :: Islamic Finance Rules 200.document_html:
(see r 1.1.2)

AAOIFI means the Accounting and Auditing Organisation for Islamic Financial Institutions.

authorisation means an authorisation granted under the Financial Services Regulations, part 5.

authorised firm (or firm) means a person that has an authorisation.

BANK means the Banking Business Prudential Rules 2014.

customer means a person to whom an Islamic financial institution provides, has provided or offers to provide a service or product.

INMA means the Investment Management and Advisory Rules 2014.

Islamic financial business has the meaning given by rule 1.2.1.

Islamic financial institution has the meaning given by rule 1.2.2.

Islamic window has the meaning given by rule 8.1.1.

month means calendar month — that is, the period beginning at the start of any day of one of the 12 named months of the year and ending:

(a) at the end of the day before the corresponding day on the next named month; or
(b) if there is no corresponding day — at the end of the last day of next named month.

QFC means Qatar Financial Centre.

Regulatory Authority means the Regulatory Authority of the QFC.

Shari'a supervisory board, of an authorised firm, means the board appointed for the firm under rule 6.1.1.

Amended by QFCRA RM/2019-4 (as from 1st January 2020).

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 1.1.3 Overview of these rules
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) These rules set out the Regulatory Authority’s regulatory regime applicable to collective investment funds that are registered under these rules as professional investor funds.
(2) There are 2 types of professional investor fund — standard professional investor funds and exempt professional investor funds.
Guidance
1 Both types of fund are open only to professional investors.
2 A business customer or eligible counterparty of an authorised firm is automatically a professional investor (see rule 2.1.2 — for the meanings of business customer and eligible counterparty¸ see CIPR, rules 1.2.3 to 1.2.10). Business customers and eligible counterparties are mostly corporate bodies.
3 An individual must be a certified professional investor to invest in either type of fund, but the criteria for becoming a certified professional investor differ between a standard professional investor fund and an exempt professional investor fund.
4 A standard professional investor fund is open to individual professional investors who are certified as professional investors by the fund manager (see rule 2.1.4).
5 An exempt professional investor fund is open to individual professional investors who are self-certified (see rule 2.1.5).
6 The maximum number of investors for a fund of either type is 199.
7 There is no minimum investment for a standard professional investor fund. The minimum investment for an exempt professional investor fund is QR 400,000.
(3) A professional investor fund must have a fund manager. The fund manager may be a QFC fund manager or a State fund manager (see Part 3.1).
(4) The requirements for a QFC fund manager of a standard professional investor fund are different from those for a QFC fund manager of an exempt professional investor fund. Guidance table 1.1.3 gives an overview of the differences.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 1.1.4 Application of these rules
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
These rules apply only to professional investor funds that are established in the QFC.

Note 1 A collective investment fund that is established in the QFC may be registered under these rules as a professional investor fund or under COLL as a qualified investor scheme or retail scheme (but see note 3). COLL also deals with marketing and sale in or from the QFC of units in schemes that are not established in the QFC, including schemes that are similar or equivalent to professional investor funds established in the QFC.
Note 2 Collective investment funds are called collective investment schemes in COLL.
Note 3 Applications for the registration of certain collective investment funds of a particular description are to be accepted under the Private Placement Schemes Rules 2010 (PRIV) until 31 December 2022. Although PRIV was repealed at the same time as these rules commenced, PRIV is taken to continue to apply to those funds (see the PRIV Repeal and Consequential Amendments Rules 2022, rule 3). No other registrations of collective investment funds under PRIV are possible.

doc_path: PROF Part 1.2 Concepts about professional investor funds

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 1.2.2 Standard professional investor fund
doc_path: PROF Part 1.2 Concepts about professional investor funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
A collective investment fund is a standard professional investor fund if all of the following are true:

(a) the fund is established in the QFC;
(b) the fund is in a legal form required by or permitted under rule 1.2.4;
(c) the fund’s constitutional document provides that establishment as a standard professional investment fund is the fund’s sole purpose;
(d) the fund is registered as a standard professional investor fund in accordance with Chapter 4;
(e) units in the fund are issued only to a fund investor that is at the time:
(i) if the fund investor is an individual — a certified professional investor; or
(ii) if the fund investor is not an individual — a professional investor;
(f) the maximum number of fund investors for the fund at any time is 199.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 1.2.3 Exempt professional investor fund
doc_path: PROF Part 1.2 Concepts about professional investor funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
A collective investment fund is an exempt professional investor fund if all of the following are true:

(a) the fund is established in the QFC;
(b) the fund is in a legal form required by or permitted under rule 1.2.4;
(c) the fund’s constitutional document provides that establishment as an exempt professional investor fund is the fund’s sole purpose;
(d) the fund is registered as an exempt professional investor fund in accordance with Chapter 4;
(e) units in the fund are issued only to:
(i) individuals who are certified professional investors for the fund; and
(ii) persons (other than individuals) that are professional investors;
(f) the minimum investment in the fund of a fund investor is QR 400,000;
(g) the maximum number of fund investors for the fund at any time is 199.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 1.2.5 Professional investor funds — open-ended or closed-ended
doc_path: PROF Part 1.2 Concepts about professional investor funds
PROF 1.2.5 Professional investor funds — open-ended or closed-ended
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) A professional investor fund may be an open-ended fund or a closed-ended fund.
(2) An open-ended fund is a professional investor fund that permits its units to be redeemed, either continuously or periodically.
(3) A closed-ended fund is a professional investor fund that does not permit its units to be redeemed.
(4) An open-ended fund that is a QFC company must be an open-ended company with variable share capital.
Guidance
“Open-ended company with variable share capital”: such a company does not have an authorised share capital specified at its incorporation. The Companies Regulations 2005, articles 17 (1) (H) and 17 (6) and (7), permit the incorporation of a company without a fixed share capital if, on incorporation, the company will be a collective investment fund.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 1.2.6 Professional investor funds — umbrella funds and subfunds
doc_path: PROF Part 1.2 Concepts about professional investor funds
PROF 1.2.6 Professional investor funds — umbrella funds and subfunds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) An umbrella fund is a professional investor fund in which the contributions by fund investors, and the profit or income out of which payments are to be made to fund investors, are pooled separately in relation to separate parts of the fund property.
(2) A subfund of an umbrella fund is a part of the fund property that is pooled separately.
(3) An umbrella fund may be either a standard professional investor fund or an exempt professional investor fund.
(4) Each subfund of an umbrella fund must meet the requirements for a standard professional investor fund or an exempt professional investor fund. However, the requirement relating to the maximum number of fund investors for the fund in rule 1.2.2 (f) or 1.2.3 (g) must be met for the umbrella fund as a whole.
(5) Units in a subfund of an umbrella fund may be denominated in a different currency from the base currency of the umbrella fund.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF Chapter 2 Key concepts
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
Introductory notes for Chapter 2

1 The purpose of this Chapter is to set out the key prohibitions on fund managers of professional investor funds and authorised firms in relation to professional investor funds.
2 Under FSR, article 105, the Regulatory Authority has the power to give certain directions in relation to collective investment funds if there is a breach of rules, or to protect the interests of fund investors.
3 Part 2.1 introduces a new concept —the certified professional investor — which applies only to individuals. An individual who wishes to invest in a standard professional investor fund must meet the conditions set out in rule 2.1.4. An individual who wishes to invest in an exempt professional investor fund must meet the conditions set out in rule 2.1.5. The key difference between the two is that for a standard professional investor fund the manager is obliged to be satisfied that the individual meets the criteria, but for an exempt professional investor fund the manager may rely on a statement signed by the individual. All investors in a standard or exempt professional investor fund who are not individuals must be professional investors (as defined in rule 2.1.2).

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 2.1.1 Fund investor
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) A fund investor for a professional investor fund is a person who invests in the fund. A fund investor for such a fund must be:
(a) in the case of a person other than an individual — a professional investor; or
(b) in the case of a person who is an individual — a certified professional investor.
(2) Fund investor includes a person referred to as a participant in the definition of collective investment fund in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 3, paragraphs 6.2. to 6.6.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 2.1.2 Professional investor
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
A person is a professional investor for a professional investor fund if, in relation to dealings in investments that consist of (or include) units in the fund, the person:

(a) would be a business customer or eligible counterparty of the fund if the fund were an authorised firm and the person were a customer of the fund; or
(b) is a business customer or eligible counterparty of an authorised firm.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 2.1.4 Certified professional investor for standard professional investor fund
doc_path: PROF 2.1.4 Certified professional investor for standard professional investor fund
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) An individual is a certified professional investor for a standard professional investor fund if the fund’s fund manager is satisfied that the individual:
(a) has at least QR 4 million in net assets (excluding the value of his or her primary family residence, but including assets in which he or she has a beneficial interest); or
(b) earned income (including bonuses) of QR 750,000 or more in each of the previous 2 calendar years and reasonably expects to do so in the current calendar year.
(2) When the fund manager of a standard professional investor fund is considering whether to classify an individual as a certified professional investor on the basis of the individual’s net worth or income, the fund manager must make reasonable efforts to obtain evidence showing that the individual meets:
(a) the minimum asset requirement in paragraph (1) (a); or
(b) the minimum income requirement in paragraph (1) (b).

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.content_text: (1) An individual is a certified professional investor for a standard professional investor fund if the fund’s fund manager is satisfied that the individual: (a) has at least QR 4 million in net assets (excluding the value of his or her primary family residence, but including assets in which he or she has a beneficial interest); or (b) earned income (including bonuses) of QR 750,000 or more in each of the previous 2 calendar years and reasonably expects to do so in the current calendar year. (2) When the fund manager of a standard professional investor fund is considering whether to classify an individual as a certified professional investor on the basis of the individual’s net worth or income, the fund manager must make reasonable efforts to obtain evidence showing that the individual meets: (a) the minimum asset requirement in paragraph (1) (a); or (b) the minimum income requirement in paragraph (1) (b). Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

endnotes: Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 2.1.5 Certified professional investor for exempt professional investor fund
doc_path: PROF 2.1.5 Certified professional investor for exempt professional investor fund
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
An individual is a certified professional investor for an exempt professional investor fund if:

(a) the individual has signed, and has given to the fund’s fund manager, a statement in the terms set out in Schedule 3;
(b) the individual signed the statement within the period of 12 months ending with the day on which the application for registration of the fund is made; and
(c) the fund manager has no reasonable grounds to doubt the accuracy of the statement.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

PROF 2.2.1 Issue or transfer of units — standard professional investor funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a standard professional investor fund must not issue a unit in the fund to a person who is not a professional investor or a certified professional investor.
(2) The fund manager of a standard professional investor fund must not accept the transfer of a unit in the fund to a person who is not a professional investor or a certified professional investor.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 2.2.2 Issue or transfer of units — exempt professional investor funds
doc_path: PROF Part 2.2 Conduct by fund managers
PROF 2.2.2 Issue or transfer of units — exempt professional investor funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of an exempt professional investor fund must not issue a unit in the fund to a person:
(a) if the person is not an individual — that is not a professional investor; or
(b) if the person is an individual — who is not a certified professional investor for the fund.
(2) The fund manager of an exempt professional investor fund must not accept the transfer of a unit in the fund to a person:
(a) if the person is not an individual — that is not a professional investor; or
(b) if the person is an individual — who is not a certified professional investor for the fund.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

PROF 2.2.4 Registering fund investors — exempt professional investor funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:

(a) if the person is not an individual — the person was a professional investor at the time that the unit was issued or transferred to the person; or

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 2.3.1 Dealings in funds only to be done for professional investors
doc_path: PROF Part 2.3 Conduct by authorised firms
PROF 2.3.1 Dealings in funds only to be done for professional investors
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) This rule applies if:
(a) an authorised firm provides, has provided or offers to provide a service or product to a person;
(b) the service or product includes the conduct of 1 or more of the following regulated activities for the person in or from the QFC:
(i) dealing in investments;
(ii) arranging deals in investments (as described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 2, paragraph 5);
(iii) advising on investments (as described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 2, paragraph 11); and
(c) the service or product is to be provided in relation to units in a professional investor fund.
(2) If the fund concerned is a standard professional investor fund, the firm may provide the service or product to the person only if:
(a) the person is a business customer or eligible counterparty of the firm; or
(b) the firm believes, on reasonable grounds, that the person could be classified (in accordance with CIPR) as a business customer or eligible counterparty of the firm.
(3) If the fund concerned is an exempt professional investor fund, the firm may provide the service or product to the person only if the person is a certified professional investor for the fund.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.content_text: (1) This rule applies if: (a) an authorised firm provides, has provided or offers to provide a service or product to a person; (b) the service or product includes the conduct of 1 or more of the following regulated activities for the person in or from the QFC: (i) dealing in investments; (ii) arranging deals in investments (as described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 2 , paragraph 5); (iii) advising on investments (as described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 2 , paragraph 11); and (c) the service or product is to be provided in relation to units in a professional investor fund. (2) If the fund concerned is a standard professional investor fund, the firm may provide the service or product to the person only if: (a) the person is a business customer or eligible counterparty of the firm; or (b) the firm believes, on reasonable grounds, that the person could be classified (in accordance with CIPR) as a business customer or eligible counterparty of the firm. (3) If the fund concerned is an exempt professional investor fund, the firm may provide the service or product to the person only if the person is a certified professional investor for the fund. QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF Chapter 3 Fund managers
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
Introductory notes for Chapter 3

1 The purpose of this Chapter is to set out the role of fund managers in operating a professional investor fund.
2 Parts 3.1 to 3.4 are about the fund manager of a professional investor fund. There are two types of fund managers for funds: QFC fund managers and State fund managers.
3 Part 3.5 requires fund managers to have certain key personnel and sets out the way that other QFC rules apply to those personnel.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 3.1.1 Meaning of fund manager
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund is the person responsible for complying with the requirements imposed by these rules in relation to establishing, operating, managing or winding up the fund.
(2) The activities involved in operating a professional investor fund include the activities mentioned in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 2, paragraph 12.1 (2).
(3) Fund manager includes a person referred to as the operator in the definition of collective investment fund in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 3, paragraphs 6.2. to 6.6.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
Introductory notes for Part 3.2

1 The purpose of this Part is to set out the qualifications for a QFC fund manager of a professional investor fund, the general and specific functions of QFC fund managers and specific principles of conduct that apply to them in performing those functions.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 3.2.1 Qualifications of QFC fund manager
doc_path: PROF Division 3.2.A QFC fund manager qualifications
PROF 3.2.1 Qualifications of QFC fund manager
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
A QFC fund manager of a professional investor fund is an authorised firm to which all of the following apply:

(a) the firm is a corporation;
(b) the firm is a separate legal person from the fund;
(c) the firm has an authorisation to conduct each of the following regulated activities:
(i) operating a collective investment fund;
(ii) managing investments;
(iii) dealing in investments;
(d) the firm is permitted under the scope of the authorisation to be the fund manager of:
(i) the fund;
(ii) professional investor funds of that kind; or
(iii) any professional investor fund registered under these rules;
(e) if the firm will provide custody services to the fund — the firm has an authorisation to conduct the regulated activity of providing custody services (as described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 2, paragraph 8);
(f) the firm meets the minimum capital and liquid assets requirements in INMA, Part 3.3 (as modified by rule 3.2.2, if applicable).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 3.2.3 Legal and regulatory requirements for QFC fund managers
doc_path: PROF Division 3.2.B QFC fund manager functions
PROF 3.2.3 Legal and regulatory requirements for QFC fund managers
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) A QFC fund manager of a professional investor fund may perform all of the functions in relation to operating the fund that are set out in the fund’s constitutional document.
(2) A QFC fund manager of a professional investor fund must comply with every legal and regulatory requirement applying to the fund manager:
(a) in relation to the fund;
(b) as a fund manager of a professional investor fund;
(c) as an operator of a collective investment fund; and
Note Collective investment funds are called collective investment schemes in COLL.
(d) as an authorised firm.
(3) Without limiting subrule (2), a QFC fund manager of a professional investor fund must act in accordance with the following:
(a) these rules;
(b) any regulations under which the fund is established, including any law that is applied by, or that supplements, those regulations;
(c) the other provisions of the law applying in the QFC in relation to:
(i) the fund;
(ii) the fund manager as a fund manager of a professional investor fund;
(iii) the fund manager as an operator of a collective investment fund; and
(iv) the fund manager as an authorised firm;
(d) the scope of the fund manager’s authorisation, including any conditions, restrictions or requirements;
(e) the scope of the fund’s registration, including any conditions, restrictions or requirements;
(f) the fund’s constitutional document, including any stated conditions to which the exercise of a function is subject;
(g) the fund’s offer document, including any stated conditions to which the exercise of a function is subject.
(4) Subrule (3) applies even if another rule imposes additional conditions or limitations on the exercise of a function by a QFC fund manager of a professional investor fund.
Guidance
Other Regulatory Authority rules that may apply to a QFC fund manager of a professional investor fund include:
• AML/CFTR, in relation to the fund manager’s AML/CFT obligations
• CDRS, for fund investors for standard professional investor funds
• CIPR, subject to Division 3.2.C
• CTRL, in relation to controlled functions and the outsourcing of functions by the fund manager
• GENE, in relation to protected reporting, controllers, audit requirements and records
• INAP, in relation to the interpretation of the rules
• INDI, in relation to the assessment, training and competency of individuals who exercise controlled functions
• INMA, subject to rule 3.2.2.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 3.2.4 Application of CIPR generally
doc_path: PROF Division 3.2.C QFC fund managers’ conduct — application of CIPR
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) CIPR contains general principles of conduct for authorised firms in their interactions with customers. CIPR applies to a QFC fund manager of a professional investor fund in accordance with this Division.
(2) For that application:
(a) references in CIPR to an authorised firm are taken to be references to a QFC fund manager of a professional investor fund; and
(b) references in CIPR to a customer of an authorised firm are taken to be references to a fund investor for a professional investor fund.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 3.2.5 Application of CIPR — standard professional investor funds
doc_path: PROF Division 3.2.C QFC fund managers’ conduct — application of CIPR
PROF 3.2.5 Application of CIPR — standard professional investor funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) Subject to subrule (2), CIPR applies to a QFC fund manager of a standard professional investor fund in the fund manager’s capacity as an authorised firm.
(2) The requirements in CIPR, rules 3.3.3 (7) and 3.3.6, do not apply in relation to dealings in investments that consist of (or include) units in the fund.
Note The requirements in CIPR, rules 3.3.3 (7) and 3.3.6, are requirements for the continuing verification of customer classification. They continue to apply in relation to any other business that an authorised firm conducts for a professional investor.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 3.2.6 Application of CIPR — exempt professional investor funds
doc_path: PROF Division 3.2.C QFC fund managers’ conduct — application of CIPR
PROF 3.2.6 Application of CIPR — exempt professional investor funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The only provisions of CIPR that apply to a QFC fund manager of an exempt professional investor fund in relation to the management of the fund are the following:
(a) Chapter 2;
(b) Part 3.2;
(c) rules 3.5.1 and 3.5.2;
(d) rule 4.2.4 (1) (a) in relation to an advertisement (within the meaning of CIPR) about the fund.
(2) In the application of a provision of CIPR mentioned in subrule (1) to the fund manager of an exempt professional investor fund, a reference to these rules is a reference to those provisions of CIPR.

Guidance

1 An authorised firm that is the manager of an exempt professional investor fund and is authorised to conduct other regulated activities must comply fully with CIPR in relation to those other activities. Rule 3.2.6 (1) exempts the firm from complying fully with CIPR only in the performance of its functions as the manager of an exempt professional investor fund.
2 If an authorised firm that is a QFC fund manager of an exempt professional investor fund becomes authorised to conduct other regulated activities, CIPR applies to the firm in relation to those other activities.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.content_text: (1) The only provisions of CIPR that apply to a QFC fund manager of an exempt professional investor fund in relation to the management of the fund are the following: (a) Chapter 2 ; (b) Part 3.2 ; (c) rules 3.5.1 and 3.5.2 ; (d) rule 4.2.4 (1) (a) in relation to an advertisement (within the meaning of CIPR) about the fund. (2) In the application of a provision of CIPR mentioned in subrule (1) to the fund manager of an exempt professional investor fund, a reference to these rules is a reference to those provisions of CIPR. Guidance 1 An authorised firm that is the manager of an exempt professional investor fund and is authorised to conduct other regulated activities must comply fully with CIPR in relation to those other activities. Rule 3.2.6 (1) exempts the firm from complying fully with CIPR only in the performance of its functions as the manager of an exempt professional investor fund. 2 If an authorised firm that is a QFC fund manager of an exempt professional investor fund becomes authorised to conduct other regulated activities, CIPR applies to the firm in relation to those other activities. QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF Part 3.3 State fund managers
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
Introductory notes for Part 3.3

1 The purpose of this Part is to set out the qualifications for a State fund manager of a professional investor fund, and the general and specific functions of State fund managers of such a fund.
2 A State fund manager of a professional investor fund is licensed or authorised by the Qatar Central Bank, the Qatar Financial Markets Authority or another regulatory or governmental authority in the State of Qatar.
3 The State fund manager of a professional investor fund is obliged under a contract with the fund to perform the functions imposed on fund managers by these rules.
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.content_text: Introductory notes for Part 3.3 1 The purpose of this Part is to set out the qualifications for a State fund manager of a professional investor fund, and the general and specific functions of State fund managers of such a fund. 2 A State fund manager of a professional investor fund is licensed or authorised by the Qatar Central Bank, the Qatar Financial Markets Authority or another regulatory or governmental authority in the State of Qatar. 3 The State fund manager of a professional investor fund is obliged under a contract with the fund to perform the functions imposed on fund managers by these rules.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 3.3.1 Qualifications of State fund manager
doc_path: PROF 3.3.1 Qualifications of State fund manager
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) A State fund manager of a professional investor fund is a bank, insurance company or investment manager that:
(a) is authorised or licensed by the Qatar Central Bank, the Qatar Financial Markets Authority or any other regulatory or governmental authority in the State of Qatar;
(b) is not an authorised firm; and
(c) has a contract with the fund that complies with subrule (2) (a QFC fund management contract).
(2) A contract complies with this subrule if:
(a) the governing law of the contract is the law of the QFC and the jurisdiction of the contract is the QFC;
(b) the contract requires the State fund manager to fulfil the obligations that would be imposed on a QFC fund manager in relation to the fund by:
(i) these rules;
(ii) any regulations under which the fund is established, including any law applied by, or that supplements, those regulations;
(iii) the other provisions of the law applying in the QFC in relation to:
(A) the fund;
(B) the fund manager as the fund manager of a professional investor fund; or
(C) the fund manager as a party to the contract;
(iv) the scope of the fund’s registration, including any conditions, restrictions or requirements;
(v) the fund’s constitutional document, including any stated conditions to which the exercise of a function is subject; and
(vi) the fund’s offer document, including any stated conditions to which the exercise of a function is subject; and
(c) if the fund is a standard professional investor fund, the contract requires the State fund manager:
(i) to participate in the scheme established by the Customer Dispute Resolution Scheme Rules 2019;
(ii) to treat those Rules as binding on it; and
(iii) to comply with any ruling of the Independent Adjudicator under the scheme.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)
