(2) A contract complies with this subrule if: (a) the governing law of the contract is the law of the QFC and the jurisdiction of the contract is the QFC; (b) the contract requires the State fund manager to fulfil the obligations that would be imposed on a QFC fund manager in relation to the fund by: (i) these rules; (ii) any regulations under which the fund is established, including any law applied by, or that supplements, those regulations; (iii) the other provisions of the law applying in the QFC in relation to: (A) the fund; (B) the fund manager as the fund manager of a professional investor fund; or (C) the fund manager as a party to the contract; (iv) the scope of the fund’s registration, including any conditions, restrictions or requirements; (v) the fund’s constitutional document, including any stated conditions to which the exercise of a function is subject; and (vi) the fund’s offer document, including any stated conditions to which the exercise of a function is subject; and (c) if the fund is a standard professional investor fund, the contract requires the State fund manager: (i) to participate in the scheme established by the Customer Dispute Resolution Scheme Rules 2019 ; (ii) to treat those Rules as binding on it; and (iii) to comply with any ruling of the Independent Adjudicator under the scheme. QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 3.3.2 Legal and regulatory requirements on State fund manager
doc_path: PROF 3.3.2 Legal and regulatory requirements on State fund manager
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) A State fund manager of a professional investor fund may perform all of the functions in relation to operating the fund that are set out in the constitutional document for the fund.
(2) A State fund manager of a professional investor fund must fulfil the obligations that are imposed by the QFC fund management contract with the fund to comply with the requirements that are imposed by these rules in relation to establishing, operating, managing or winding up the fund.
(3) Without limiting subrule (2), a State fund manager of a professional investor fund must fulfil the obligations that are imposed by the QFC fund management contract with the fund in relation to the following:
(a) these rules;
(b) any regulations under which the fund is established, including any law that is applied by, or that supplements, those regulations;
(c) the other provisions of the law applying in the QFC in relation to:
(i) the fund;
(ii) the fund manager as the fund manager of a professional investor fund; or
(iii) the fund manager as a party to the QFC fund management contract;
(d) the scope of the fund’s registration, including any conditions, restrictions or requirements;
(e) the constitutional document for the fund, including any stated conditions to which the exercise of a function is subject;
(f) the offer document for the fund, including any stated conditions to which the exercise of a function is subject.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF Part 3.4 Changing fund managers
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
Introductory note for Part 3.4

The purpose of this Part is to set out the rules that apply when the fund manager of a professional investor fund is changed.
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.content_text: Introductory note for Part 3.4 The purpose of this Part is to set out the rules that apply when the fund manager of a professional investor fund is changed.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 3.4.1 Change of fund manager — replacement by fund investors
doc_path: PROF 3.4.1 Change of fund manager — replacement by fund investors
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) In accordance with the constitutional document for a professional investor fund, the fund investors for the fund:
(a) may remove the fund manager; and
(b) may appoint a new fund manager.
Note A professional investor fund must have a fund manager at all times (see rule 3.1.2 (1)).
(2) If the fund investors for a professional investor fund appoint a new fund manager, the new fund manager must tell the Regulatory Authority about the change within 1 business day after the day on which the new fund manager is appointed.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 3.4.2 Replacement of fund manager after regulatory action
doc_path: PROF 3.4.2 Replacement of fund manager after regulatory action
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) This rule applies if the fund manager of a professional investor fund ceases to be qualified as a fund manager because of action taken by the Regulatory Authority under FSR.
(2) If this rule applies, the fund investors for the fund must appoint a new fund manager who is qualified under rule 3.2.1 (for a QFC fund manager) or 3.3.1 (for a State fund manager).

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 3.4.3 Change of fund manager — retirement
doc_path: PROF 3.4.3 Change of fund manager — retirement
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund may retire as the fund’s fund manager, in accordance with the fund’s constitutional document, in favour of another person if:
(a) the other person is qualified under rule 3.2.1 or 3.3.1; and
(b) the retiring fund manager appoints the other person as the fund’s fund manager.
(2) If the fund manager of a professional investor fund retires, the fund’s new fund manager must tell the Regulatory Authority about the retirement and appointment within 1 business day after the day on which the new fund manager is appointed.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 3.4.4 Consequences of change of fund manager — requirements cease applying
doc_path: PROF 3.4.4 Consequences of change of fund manager — requirements cease applying
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) This rule applies in relation to the legal and regulatory requirements under legislation that applies in the QFC to a person who is the fund manager of a professional investor fund.
(2) Those requirements cease to apply to the person on and from the time at which the person ceases to be the fund’s fund manager.

(2) Those requirements cease to apply to the person on and from the time at which the person ceases to be the fund’s fund manager. Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 3.4.5 Consequences of change of fund manager — rights and property
doc_path: PROF 3.4.5 Consequences of change of fund manager — rights and property
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) A person that ceases to be the fund manager of a professional investor fund is entitled to continue to be recorded in the fund’s register of fund investors for any units in the fund that the person holds.
(2) Subrule (1) is subject to any restriction in the fund’s offer document in relation to the permitted categories of fund investors for the fund.
(3) A person who ceases to be the fund manager of a professional investor fund must do everything reasonably necessary:
(a) to assign all of the person’s rights and functions as the fund’s fund manager to the fund’s new fund manager; and
(b) to transfer or deliver the fund property held by the person to the new fund manager.
(4) Until all the fund property has been transferred or delivered, the person remains accountable for it to the fund investors for the fund.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 3.4.6 Consequences of change of fund manager — preservation of liability
doc_path: PROF 3.4.6 Consequences of change of fund manager — preservation of liability
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
A change in the fund manager of a professional investor fund does not affect the rights of a person (including the former fund manager) in relation to an act or omission of the former fund manager.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF Chapter 4 Registration process
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
Introductory notes for Chapter 4

1 This Chapter sets out the rules for the registration of professional investor funds.
2 Professional investor funds are a type of collective investment fund.
3 Collective investment funds must be registered either under these rules or under COLL (see COLL, rule 2.1.1).
4 A professional investor fund is registered as either a standard professional investor fund or an exempt professional investor fund.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.content_text: Introductory notes for Chapter 4 1 This Chapter sets out the rules for the registration of professional investor funds. 2 Professional investor funds are a type of collective investment fund. 3 Collective investment funds must be registered either under these rules or under COLL (see COLL, rule 2.1.1 ). 4 A professional investor fund is registered as either a standard professional investor fund or an exempt professional investor fund. Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

endnotes: Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 4.1.1 Application for registration
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The person who is to become the initial fund manager of a professional investor fund may apply to the Regulatory Authority to register the fund as either:
(a) a standard professional investor fund; or
(b) an exempt professional investor fund.
(2) An application under subrule (1) must be in a form approved by the Authority, and must be accompanied by all of the following:
(a) a copy of the fund’s constitutional document;
(b) a copy of the fund’s offer document;
(c) if the Authority so requires — a completed checklist, in terms specified by the Authority, signed by the fund manager, certifying that the fund documents for the fund meet the requirements of Parts 5.1 and 5.2;
(d) any other document or other information that the Authority reasonably requires.
Note The applicant must pay the application fee when the application is filed with the Authority (see rule 10.1.1). The application is taken not to have been made until the fee is paid (see rule 10.1.1 (4)).
(3) The fund’s constitutional document must not contain a provision that:
(a) conflicts with a provision of these rules; or
(b) is unfairly prejudicial to the interests of fund investors for the fund generally or to the fund investors for a class of units in the fund.
(4) The Authority may request the applicant, in writing, to give the Authority additional information or documents that the Authority reasonably needs to decide the application.
(5) If the applicant does not comply with a request under subrule (4), the Authority may refuse to consider the application.
(6) The applicant may withdraw the application by notice to the Authority at any time before the application is decided.
(7) If the applicant becomes aware, at any time after the application is made but before it is withdrawn or decided, of a material change that is reasonably likely to be relevant to the Authority’s consideration of the application, the applicant must tell the Authority about the change by no later than the next business day.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 4.1.2 Decision on application for registration
doc_path: PROF 4.1.2 Decision on application for registration
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) For a fund to be registered as a professional investor fund, the applicant must satisfy the Regulatory Authority that it is appropriate for the fund to be registered, particularly having regard to the interests of people who are, or might become, fund investors for the fund.

(2) In particular, the Regulatory Authority may refuse an application to register a fund as a professional investor fund if the Authority considers that any of the following applies:

(a) the fund is not eligible for registration as a professional investor fund of the type for which the applicant has applied;

Note See rules 1.2.2 and 1.2.3 for the eligibility requirements for each type of fund.
(b) the name of the fund is not appropriate to describe the fund, or is undesirable or misleading;
(c) the person named in the application as the person who is to become the fund’s fund manager is not qualified (or, at the time of registration, will not be qualified) to be the fund’s fund manager under rule 3.2.1 or 3.3.1;
(d) the person named in the application as the person who is to become the fund’s initial auditor does not meet (or, at the time of registration, will not meet) the requirements of rule 8.6.1 (3);
(e) the Authority has required the fund’s fund manager to sign a checklist certifying that the fund documents for the fund meet the requirements of Parts 5.1 (for the constitutional document) and 5.2 (for the offer document), and the fund manager has not done so;

(f) there is reason to believe that the constitutional document contains a provision that:

(i) conflicts with a provision of these rules; or
(ii) is unfairly prejudicial to the interests of fund investors for the fund generally or to the fund investors for a class of units in the fund;
(g) the fund documents for the fund do not meet the requirements of Part 5.1 or Part 5.2;
(h) the fund otherwise does not comply with these rules;

(i) the proposed arrangements for safeguarding the fund property do not provide an appropriate level of protection for people who are, or might become, fund investors for the fund;

Guidance
The Authority would usually expect the fund property to be held by an independent custodian that is authorised in the QFC or another jurisdiction that would provide an appropriate level of protection for fund investors for the fund.
(j) if the fund is to be a closed-ended fund — it is inappropriate for the fund to be a closed-ended fund;
(k) the Authority considers that the dominant purpose of registering the fund under these rules is to avoid the application of provisions of COLL that should apply to the fund in the interests of people who are, or might become, fund investors for the fund.

(3) To avoid doubt, the fund may be registered even if the constitutional document contains 1 or more provisions of a kind mentioned in paragraph (2) (f).

Note Under rule 5.1.3, such provisions have no effect in relation to the fund.

(4) The Authority may register the fund either:

(a) without conditions, restrictions or requirements; or
(b) with the conditions, restrictions or requirements that it considers appropriate.
(5) The Authority must notify the applicant in writing of its decision to register, or to refuse the application to register, a fund as a professional investor fund.

(6) If the Authority refuses the application, or registers the fund with conditions, restrictions or requirements not agreed to by the applicant, the notice under subrule (5):

(a) must give reasons for the decision; and
(b) must state that the applicant may appeal to the Regulatory Tribunal against the decision.
(7) On the fund’s registration, the person named in the application as the person who is to become the fund’s fund manager becomes the fund’s fund manager.

Amended by QFCRA RM/2026-2 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 4.1.3 Variation of conditions, restrictions or requirements
doc_path: PROF 4.1.3 Variation of conditions, restrictions or requirements
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) At any time after a professional investor fund is registered, the Regulatory Authority may vary any condition, restriction or requirement imposed on the fund, if the Authority considers it appropriate to do so.
(2) The Authority must notify the fund’s fund manager in writing of a decision under subrule (1).
(3) If the Authority varies a condition, restriction or requirement imposed on a professional investor fund, and the fund’s fund manager has not agreed to the variation, the notice under subrule (2):
(a) must give reasons for the decision; and
(b) must state that the fund manager may appeal to the Regulatory Tribunal against the decision.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF Chapter 5 Fund documents
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
Introductory notes for Chapter 5

1 This purpose of this Chapter is to set out the requirements for what the fund documents for a professional investor fund must contain.
2 The constitutional document for such a fund is created when the fund is established. Part 5.1 contains detailed provisions about constitutional documents.
3 The offer document for such a fund is a document used to market the fund to fund investors. Part 5.2 contains detailed provisions about offer documents.
4 In these rules, those documents are collectively referred to as the fund documents.
5 Part 5.3 contains provisions that apply to all fund documents.

(a) if the fund is a QFC company — the company’s articles of association;
(b) if the fund is a QFC limited partnership — the partnership’s partnership agreement; and
(c) if the fund is of another legal form permitted by the Regulatory Authority under rule 1.2.4 (2) — the corresponding instrument for that legal form.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 5.1.3 Relationship between constitutional documents and these rules
doc_path: PROF 5.1.3 Relationship between constitutional documents and these rules
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) A provision of the constitutional document for a professional investor fund has no effect to the extent that:
(a) it conflicts with a provision of these rules; or
(b) it is unfairly prejudicial to the interests of fund investors for the fund generally or a class of units in the fund.
(2) However, a provision of the constitutional document for a professional investor fund must not be taken to conflict with a provision of these rules to the extent that the provision of the constitutional document can operate concurrently with the provision of these rules.
(3) So far as possible, a provision of the constitutional document must be read and given effect to in a way that is compatible with these rules.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 5.2.1 Offer documents for professional investor funds
doc_path: PROF 5.2.1 Offer documents for professional investor funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The offer document for a professional investor fund is a document, made in accordance with these rules, containing information about the fund.
Note The requirements in these rules apply to professional investor funds in addition to the requirements in CIPR about disclosure documents (see Division 3.2.C).
(2) The offer document for a professional investor fund must be entitled offer document. No other title may be used.
(3) The fund manager of a professional investor fund is responsible for the fund’s offer document.
(4) The offer document for a professional investor fund must contain all the information that fund investors for the fund and their professional advisers would reasonably require (and would reasonably expect to have drawn to their attention) in a document of that kind, for the purpose of making an informed judgment about:
(a) the merits and risks of investing in the fund; and
(b) the extent and characteristics of the risks accepted by investing in the fund.
(5) A reference in these rules to a professional investor fund’s offer document is a reference to the offer document as first made, and as amended in accordance with these rules from time to time, and includes any document that is prepared to supplement the offer document.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 5.2.2A Tokenised funds and token investing funds – additional matters to be included in offer document
doc_path: PROF 5.2.2A Tokenised funds and token investing funds – additional matters to be included in offer document
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) If a professional investor fund is a tokenised fund or a token investing fund, the offer document for the fund must also include the statements and provisions required by Schedule 2A.

(2) For these Rules, a professional investor fund is:

(a) atokenised fund if any of the units in the fund are investment tokens;
(b) atoken investing fund if the fund’s constitutional document states that it is an object of the fund to invest in tokens.

(3) In these Rules:

(a)investment token andtoken have the same meanings as in the Investment Token Rules 2024; and
(btokenised has the same meaning as in the Digital Asset Regulations 2024.
Note The fact that a fund is a tokenised fund or a token investing fund (or both) does not affect any requirements on the fund applicable by virtue of the nature of the underlying of any tokenised fund units or tokens held, or proposed to be held, as fund property. The fund must comply with those requirements.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2024-3 (as from 1st September 2024)

(3) In these Rules: (a) investment token and token have the same meanings as in the Investment Token Rules 2024 ; and (b tokenised has the same meaning as in the Digital Asset Regulations 2024. Note The fact that a fund is a tokenised fund or a token investing fund (or both) does not affect any requirements on the fund applicable by virtue of the nature of the underlying of any tokenised fund units or tokens held, or proposed to be held, as fund property. The fund must comply with those requirements. Derived from QFCRA RM/2024-3 (as from 1st September 2024)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 5.2.3 Making and updating offer document
doc_path: PROF 5.2.3 Making and updating offer document
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must ensure that:
(a) the first offer document for the fund is drawn up; and
(b) the fund’s offer document is kept up to date.
Guidance
The Regulatory Authority expects the fund manager of a professional investor fund to revise the fund’s offer document if a material change happens (for example, a change in the fund’s investment objectives, strategy or policy) and the change affects a statement that must be included in the offer document.

(2) If a professional investor fund is a closed-ended fund, paragraph (1) (b) ceases to apply to the fund on the fund’s final closing.

Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 5.2.4 Formal requirements for offer document
doc_path: PROF 5.2.4 Formal requirements for offer document
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must ensure that the fund’s offer document:
(a) is in English;
(b) presents information about the fund in language that is plain and easy to understand;
(c) does not contain any untrue or misleading statement; and
(d) otherwise complies with these rules.
(2) Subrule (1) (a) does not prevent the fund manager of a professional investor fund preparing, or arranging for the preparation of, a translation of the fund’s offer document into any other language, but the English version of the offer document remains the authoritative version.
(3) The offer document for a professional investor fund must provide that in the event of any discrepancy between the English text of the offer document and any other version, the English text prevails.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 5.3.1 Fund documents to be made available
doc_path: PROF Part 5.3 General provisions applying to fund documents
PROF 5.3.1 Fund documents to be made available
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must make the fund documents for the fund available free of charge to a fund investor for the fund or a person that proposes to become a fund investor for the fund.
(2) The fund manager must do so:
(a) in the case of a fund investor for the fund:
(i) before the fund investor acquires, or contracts to acquire, a further unit in the fund; or
(ii) at any other time, on the fund investor’s request; and
(b) in the case of a person that proposes to become a fund investor for the fund — before the person acquires, or contracts to acquire, a unit in the fund.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 5.3.2 Amendment of fund documents
doc_path: PROF Part 5.3 General provisions applying to fund documents
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) This rule applies if a fund document for a professional investor fund is amended.
(2) The fund’s fund manager must file the following documents with the Regulatory Authority:
(a) a copy of the amendment;
(b) a copy of the fund document as amended;
(c) if the Authority so requires — a completed checklist, in terms set out by the Authority, signed by the fund manager, certifying that the fund document as amended meets the requirements of Part 5.1 (for the constitutional document) or Part 5.2 (for the offer document).
(3) The fund manager must file the documents required by subrule (2):
(a) in the case of an amendment of the constitutional document — within 21 days after the amendment; and
(b) in the case of an amendment of the offer document — within 1 business day after the amendment.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.content_text: PROF Part 6.1 Key concepts

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 6.1.1 Interpretation
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) A unit in a professional investor fund is a unit representing the rights or interests (however described) of a fund investor for the fund.
(2) In working out how many fund investors that a professional investor fund has at any time:
(a) the joint holding of a unit in the fund by 2 or more fund investors counts as a single holding; and
(b) a unit in the fund that is held on trust for a beneficiary is taken to be held by the beneficiary (rather than the trustee) if:
(i) the beneficiary is currently entitled to a share of the trust estate or the income from it; or
(ii) the beneficiary (separately or together with other beneficiaries) is able to control the trustee.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 6.2.2 Initial offer period
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The period of the initial offer for a professional investor fund, and how it ends, must be set out in the fund’s offer document. The period must not be unreasonably long.
(2) In these rules, initial offer means:
(a) for a professional investor fund — an offer of the sale of units in the fund if all or part of the consideration paid for the units is to be used to acquire the initial fund property; and
(b) for a subfund of an umbrella fund — an offer of the sale of units in the subfund if all or part of the consideration paid for the units is to be used to acquire the initial fund property that is to be attributable to the subfund.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 6.2.3 Issue of units under constitutional document
doc_path: PROF 6.2.3 Issue of units under constitutional document
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The constitutional document for a professional investor fund may do 1 or more of the following:
(a) authorise the fund to issue fractions of units in the fund;
(b) provide that the issue of units in the fund may be limited;
(c) provide that units in the fund may be issued in classes specified in the document.
(2) If the constitutional document provides that units in the fund may be issued in classes, then, unless the document requires or permits otherwise, the fund’s fund manager:
(a) must equally treat fund investors who hold units in the fund in the same class; and
(b) must fairly treat fund investors who hold units in the fund in different classes.
(3) If subrule (1) (c) applies to a professional investor fund, a fund investor for the fund has the right to convert units in the fund from one class to another, if converting the units does not breach the fund’s offer document.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

(2) If the constitutional document provides that units in the fund may be issued in classes, then, unless the document requires or permits otherwise, the fund’s fund manager: (a) must equally treat fund investors who hold units in the fund in the same class; and (b) must fairly treat fund investors who hold units in the fund in different classes. QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 6.2.4 Number of issued units to correspond with units registered to fund investors
doc_path: PROF 6.2.4 Number of issued units to correspond with units registered to fund investors
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must ensure that, at a time at which the fund property is valued, there are at least as many units in issue in a class of units in the fund as there are units of that class registered to fund investors of the fund.
(2) If the fund manager of a professional investor fund breaches subrule (1), the fund manager:
(a) must correct the breach as quickly as possible; and
(b) must reimburse the fund for any costs that the fund incurred in correcting the breach, subject to any reasonable minimum level of reimbursement provided in the fund’s offer document.
Note The fund manager may also have an obligation under rule 7.2.2 to notify the Regulatory Authority about the breach.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 6.2.5 Units in QFC companies — share rights and denominations
doc_path: PROF 6.2.5 Units in QFC companies — share rights and denominations
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to a professional investor fund that is a QFC company.
(2) The constitutional document for such a fund may provide that the rights attached to shares of a specified class are to be expressed in 2 denominations, one of which (the smaller denomination) is to be in a specified proportion to the other (the larger denomination) fixed by the document.
(3) For a class of shares of a fund to which subrule (2) applies, a share with rights expressed in the smaller denomination is a smaller denomination share, and a share with rights expressed in the larger denomination is a larger denomination share.
(4) If the rights for a class of shares of such a fund are not expressed in 2 denominations, all shares of the class have the same rights.
(5) If the rights for a class of shares of such a fund are expressed in 2 denominations:
(a) all shares of a particular denomination have the same rights; and
(b) the rights that attach to a smaller denomination share of the class are in the proportion fixed by the constitutional document to the rights that attach to a larger denomination share of the class.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.content_text: (1) This rule applies to a professional investor fund that is a QFC company. (2) The constitutional document for such a fund may provide that the rights attached to shares of a specified class are to be expressed in 2 denominations, one of which (the smaller denomination ) is to be in a specified proportion to the other (the larger denomination ) fixed by the document. (3) For a class of shares of a fund to which subrule (2) applies, a share with rights expressed in the smaller denomination is a smaller denomination share , and a share with rights expressed in the larger denomination is a larger denomination share . (4) If the rights for a class of shares of such a fund are not expressed in 2 denominations, all shares of the class have the same rights. (5) If the rights for a class of shares of such a fund are expressed in 2 denominations: (a) all shares of a particular denomination have the same rights; and (b) the rights that attach to a smaller denomination share of the class are in the proportion fixed by the constitutional document to the rights that attach to a larger denomination share of the class. QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 6.3.1 Requirement to maintain register of fund investors
doc_path: PROF Part 6.3 Register of fund investors
PROF 6.3.1 Requirement to maintain register of fund investors
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must ensure that a register of fund investors for the fund is established and maintained as part of the fund manager’s records.
(2) For subrule (1), the obligation to ensure that the register is maintained requires the fund manager to take all reasonable steps to ensure that the register is accurate, complete and up to date. Those steps must include:
(a) taking reasonable steps to update the register on receiving written notice of a change of the name or address of a fund investor for the fund;
(b) ensuring that the register, or a copy of the register, is available in the QFC during ordinary business hours for inspection by or on behalf of:
(i) any fund investor for the fund;
(ii) the Regulatory Authority; or
(iii) the fund’s auditor;
(c) on request by or on behalf of any fund investor for the fund, giving the fund investor a copy of the register entries relating to that fund investor; and
(d) recording the conversion of units from one class in the fund to another.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 6.3.2 Contents of register
doc_path: PROF Part 6.3 Register of fund investors
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must ensure that the register of fund investors for the fund includes:
(a) the number or percentage of units in the fund in each class that are currently in issue; and
(b) for each person who is or has been a fund investor for the fund — all of the following information:
(i) the person’s name and address (but for joint holdings of units by 5 or more fund investors, the names and addresses of no more than 4 of them need be included);
(ii) the number or percentage of units (including fractions of a unit) in each class in the fund that the person holds or has held;
(iii) the date on which the person was registered for the units;
(iv) if relevant, the date on which the person ceased to be so registered.
(2) The fund manager:
(a) must not enter notice of any trust (whether express, implied or constructive) on the register; and
(b) is not bound by notice of any trust.
(3) The fund manager must rely on the register as conclusive evidence of the persons entitled to the units in the fund entered on it.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 6.3.3 Transfer of registration by fund investor
doc_path: PROF Part 6.3 Register of fund investors
PROF 6.3.3 Transfer of registration by fund investor
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) Every fund investor for a professional investor fund is entitled to transfer units in the fund that are entered in the fund’s register of fund investors in the fund investor’s name.
(2) The transfer must be done by an instrument in the form that the fund’s fund manager approves.
(3) The fund manager is under no duty to accept a transfer unless the transfer is permitted by the fund documents for the fund.
(4) The transferor must be treated as the fund investor for the fund until the transferee’s name is entered in the register of fund investors.
(5) An instrument of transfer must be left for registration with the fund manager and must be accompanied by:
(a) any other document required by the law applying in the QFC; and
(b) any other evidence that the fund manager reasonably requires.
(6) The fund manager must keep an instrument of transfer for at least 10 years after the day on which it is registered.
(7) On the registration of an instrument of transfer, the fund manager must make a record of the transferor, the transferee and the date of transfer in the register of fund investors.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 6.3.4 Certificates
doc_path: PROF Part 6.3 Register of fund investors
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) If units in a professional investor fund are issued or transferred, the fund’s fund manager may issue, in accordance with the fund’s constitutional document, a document or other means of evidencing title to the units (a certificate).
(2) If such a fund’s fund manager issues certificates, and the fund’s procedures for redeeming units require fund investors for the fund to surrender any existing certificate, the fund manager must issue a certificate for units in the fund as soon as practicable after issuing or transferring the units.
(3) If the fund manager receives written notice of a change of the name of a fund investor for the fund and a certificate has been issued for the fund investor’s units, the fund manager must either endorse the existing certificate appropriately, or issue an updated certificate.
(4) Bearer certificates (that is, certificates that indicate that the bearer is entitled to specified units in the fund) may not be issued for units in a professional investor fund.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 6.4.3 Issue and redemption — avoiding undue benefit or advantage
doc_path: PROF Part 6.4 Issue and redemption of units
PROF Division 6.4.B Issue and redemption of units — all professional investor funds
PROF 6.4.3 Issue and redemption — avoiding undue benefit or advantage
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) In issuing or redeeming units in a professional investor fund, the fund’s fund manager must not do (or fail to do) anything if the result of the action or failure would or might be to give either the fund manager or an associated person of the fund manager a benefit or advantage at the expense of:
(a) a fund investor for the fund; or
(b) a person who might become a fund investor for the fund.
(2) If the fund manager of a professional investor fund breaches subrule (1), the fund manager:
(a) must correct the breach as quickly as possible; and
(b) must reimburse the fund for any costs that the fund incurred in correcting the breach, subject to any reasonable minimum level of reimbursement provided for in the fund’s offer document.
Note The fund manager may also be required to notify the Regulatory Authority about the breach — see rule 7.2.2.

PROF 6.4.5 Issue and redemption — multiple classes of units
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to an open-ended fund that has 2 or more classes of units in issue.
(2) The fund’s fund manager may treat all, or any 2 or more, of the classes as a single class in deciding how many units in the fund are to be issued or redeemed by reference to a particular point in time if either:
(a) the classes have the same entitlement to participate in the fund property, and the same liability for charges, expenses, and other payments that may be recovered from the fund property; or
(b) the classes differ only as to whether income is distributed or accumulated by periodic credit to capital, and the price of the units in each class is calculated by reference to undivided shares in the fund property.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
Introductory notes for Chapter 7

1 This Chapter sets out the requirements on the fund manager of a professional investor fund in relation to operating the fund.
2 Part 7.1 is about investing, borrowing and spending for the fund.
3 Part 7.2 is about the requirements on the fund manager to safeguard the property of the fund, and to notify the Regulatory Authority if unlawful activity might have an adverse effect on the fund or its investors.
4 Part 7.3 is about valuing and pricing the fund and units in the fund.
5 Part 7.4 requires the fund manager to make certain records if the fund is an open-ended fund, and there is a policy to require a dilution adjustment or dilution levy.
6 Part 7.5 sets out provisions for managing conflicts or potential conflicts of interest when the fund manager conducts transactions in relation to the fund property with particular people.
7 In relation to standard professional investor funds, Part 7.5 applies to QFC fund managers in addition to the rules in CIPR, Part 3.5, about managing conflicts, material interests and inducements. QFC fund managers have an overarching obligation under CIPR, Chapter 2, to seek to avoid conflicts of interest. The only provisions of CIPR, Part 3.5, that apply in relation to an exempt professional investor fund (whether the fund’s fund manager is a QFC fund manager or a State fund manager) are rules 3.5.1 and 3.5.2 (which deal with conflicts of interest).
8 Part 7.6 permits the fund manager of an open-ended fund to suspend dealings in the fund in certain circumstances.
9 Part 7.7 is about the circumstances in which the fund manager of a professional investor fund winds up the fund, and the procedural requirements for doing so.
10 Part 7.8 modifies FSR, Part 16 about business transfers.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must ensure that the fund does not incur any expense in relation to any property unless:
(a) investing in the property is in accordance with the fund’s investment objectives, strategies and policy; or
(b) the property is necessary for the direct pursuit of the fund’s business of investing in any investments to which it is dedicated.
(2) The fund manager of a professional investor fund may make payments out of the fund property from capital rather than from income if the basis for doing so is set out in the fund’s offer document.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.2.1 Property safeguarding functions of fund manager
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF Part 7.2 Protecting professional investor funds
PROF 7.2.1 Property safeguarding functions of fund manager
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund is responsible for safeguarding the fund property.
(2) Without limiting subrule (1), the fund manager of a professional investor fund must do all of the following:
(a) ensure that the fund property:
(i) is properly accounted for;
(ii) is clearly identified as fund property; and
(iii) is held separately from the fund manager’s own property and the property of any other person;
Guidance
The Regulatory Authority would regard subparagraph (a) (iii) as satisfied if the fund property is held by an appropriate independent custodian (see rule 4.1.2 (2) (i)).
(b) ensure that any fund property in registrable form is appropriately registered as soon as practicable;
(c) ensure that all means of evidencing title to fund property, other than in relation to derivatives and forward positions, are taken into custody or control by the appropriate person;
(d) ensure that any resulting benefit of a derivative or forward transaction is received by the fund manager for the fund property;
(e) collect, hold and deal with income in relation to the fund property.
(3) If the fund manager of a professional investor fund is of the opinion that a deal in relation to the fund breaches these rules, then, subject to the fund’s constitutional document, the fund manager:
(a) must cancel the transaction, or make a disposal or acquisition to restore the previous situation; and
(b) must meet any resulting loss or expense.
Note The fund manager may also be required to notify the Regulatory Authority about the breach — see rule 7.2.2.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.content_text: (1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund is responsible for safeguarding the fund property. (2) Without limiting subrule (1), the fund manager of a professional investor fund must do all of the following: (a) ensure that the fund property: (i) is properly accounted for; (ii) is clearly identified as fund property; and (iii) is held separately from the fund manager’s own property and the property of any other person; Guidance The Regulatory Authority would regard subparagraph (a) (iii) as satisfied if the fund property is held by an appropriate independent custodian (see rule 4.1.2 (2) (i)). (b) ensure that any fund property in registrable form is appropriately registered as soon as practicable; (c) ensure that all means of evidencing title to fund property, other than in relation to derivatives and forward positions, are taken into custody or control by the appropriate person; (d) ensure that any resulting benefit of a derivative or forward transaction is received by the fund manager for the fund property; (e) collect, hold and deal with income in relation to the fund property. (3) If the fund manager of a professional investor fund is of the opinion that a deal in relation to the fund breaches these rules, then, subject to the fund’s constitutional document, the fund manager: (a) must cancel the transaction, or make a disposal or acquisition to restore the previous situation; and (b) must meet any resulting loss or expense. Note The fund manager may also be required to notify the Regulatory Authority about the breach — see rule 7.2.2 . Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

endnotes: Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.2.2 Duty to report breaches with adverse effect on fund or fund investors
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF Part 7.2 Protecting professional investor funds
PROF 7.2.2 Duty to report breaches with adverse effect on fund or fund investors
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) This rule applies if:

(a) the fund manager of a professional investor fund becomes aware, or suspects on reasonable grounds, that there has been, may be, or may be about to be, in relation to the fund, a breach of a law; and
(b) the breach has had, would have, or is likely to have a material adverse effect on the fund or the interests of fund investors for the fund.

(2) In subrule (1):

law includes:
(a) a law of any jurisdiction (including the QFC); and
(b) any regulations, rules or other instruments (however described and whether legislative or administrative) made or in force under a law of any jurisdiction (including the QFC).
(3) The fund manager must tell the Regulatory Authority about the breach within 1 business day.

(4) The fund manager must give the Authority any information about the breach that the Authority reasonably requires.

Note Under GENE, Part 4.2, an authorised firm must also notify the Authority of any significant breach of an applicable rule, regulation, or other law by the firm or an employee of the firm (see GENE, rule 4.2.2 (1) (b)).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)
Amended by QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.3.2 Net asset value
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF Division 7.3.A Valuation and pricing — general
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
The net asset value of the fund property of a professional investor fund, at any time, is the value of the fund’s assets (including current assets) at that time after deducting:

(a) the fund’s current liabilities (including accrued expenses) at that time; and
(b) the fund’s longer-term liabilities.

PROF 7.3.3 Net asset value per unit

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.3.4 Valuation
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF Division 7.3.A Valuation and pricing — general
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must ensure that policies and procedures are established for the purpose of conducting proper valuations of the fund property.
(2) The policies and procedures must be appropriate for, and must apply consistently to, the fund property.
(3) The fund manager must value the fund property in accordance with:
(a) these rules; and
(b) the policies and procedures mentioned in subrule (1).
(4) Without limiting subrules (1) to (3), valuations of the fund property must be performed by:
(a) a person that is independent from the fund manager, and holds appropriate professional qualifications to conduct property valuations; or
(b) the fund manager, or another person in the same corporate group as the fund manager, but only if:
(i) the function of valuation of the fund property is independent of the function of investment management for the fund; and
(ii) the fund manager has made appropriate arrangements to effectively manage any conflicts of interest that may arise (for example, by avoiding or mitigating such a conflict, or disclosing the conflict to the fund investors for the fund).
(5) If the valuation of the fund property is not performed by a person mentioned in subrule (4) (a), the Regulatory Authority may require the fund manager to have the valuation verified by an auditor or independent third party.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.3.5 Valuation — open-ended funds
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF Division 7.3.B Valuation and pricing — open-ended funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) An open-ended fund must have a point in time (a valuation point) on each dealing day (other than a dealing day during the fund’s initial offer period) at which the fund property is to be valued.
(2) Dealing day, for an open-ended fund, means the period (if any) in a business day during which the fund’s fund manager is open to deal in units in the fund, in accordance with the fund’s offer document.
(3) The fund manager of an open-ended fund must prepare a valuation of the fund property at each valuation point.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.3.6 Prices of units — open-ended funds
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF Division 7.3.B Valuation and pricing — open-ended funds
PROF 7.3.6 Prices of units — open-ended funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of an open-ended fund must calculate the price of a unit in the fund at a valuation point, or for the issue or redemption of such a unit:
(a) on the basis of the calculation of the fund’s net asset value per unit (see rule 7.3.3) at the valuation point;
(b) in a way that is fair and reasonable as between fund investors for the fund;
(c) using forward prices (that is, prices calculated by reference to the next valuation point after the fund manager receives the relevant instructions to issue or redeem the units); and
(d) otherwise in accordance with the fund documents for the fund.
Guidance
The price of a unit may be reduced (for sales or issues) or increased (for acquisitions or redemptions) by duties and charges.
(2) For any unit in the fund, there must be only 1 forward price calculated from time to time by reference to a particular valuation point.
(3) If a fund investor for the fund so requests at any time, the fund manager must tell the fund investor the price of any class of unit in the fund, based on the latest valuation under rule 7.3.5 (3).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.4.1 Meaning of dilution and related terms
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF 7.4.1 Meaning of dilution and related terms
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
In these rules:

dealing costs means any costs that result from, or are reasonably expected to result from, the acquisition, holding, management or disposal of investments by the fund manager of a professional investor fund.

Guidance

Dealing costs includes:

• the costs of dealing in investments, and professional fees incurred, or expected to be incurred, in relation to the acquisition or disposal of an immovable; and
• if there is a spread between the buying and selling prices of the investment — the indirect cost resulting from the difference between the prices.

dilution adjustment, for a professional investor fund, means an adjustment to the price of a unit in the fund required by the fund fund’s manager for the purpose of reducing the effect of dilution.

dilution levy, for a professional investor fund, means a charge at the rate, or of the amount, required by the fund’s fund manager for the purpose of reducing the effect of dilution.

effect of dilution, for a professional investor fund, means the increase or decrease of the fund’s cash resources resulting from the issue or redemption of units in the fund over a period (whether or not the increase or decrease occurs in the period or otherwise).

Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.4.2 Required records in respect of dilution
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF 7.4.2 Required records in respect of dilution
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
If a professional investor fund is an open-ended fund, and the fund’s offer document states that the fund manager’s policy is to require a dilution adjustment or dilution levy, the fund’s fund manager must make a record of:

(a) how it calculates and estimates dilution; and
(b) its policy and method for deciding the rate or amount of any dilution adjustment or dilution levy.

Note Records must be kept for 10 years (see rule 8.1.2 (2)).

Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.5.1 Meaning of affected person
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF Part 7.5 Avoiding conflicts of interest
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
An affected person for a professional investor fund is any of the following:

(a) the fund’s fund manager;
(b) a member (however described) of the fund manager’s governing body;
(c) a member (however described) of the fund’s governing body;
(d) an investment adviser for the fund;
(e) a person to whom functions of the fund’s fund manager are outsourced under CTRL, Part 8.4;
(f) the fund’s auditor (see Part 8.6);
(g) an associated person of a person mentioned in any of paragraphs (a) to (f);
(h) a fund investor for the fund with 5% or more in value of all the units in the fund then in issue.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)
Amended by QFCRA RM/2024-4 (as from 1st October 2025)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.5.2 Meaning of investment adviser
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF Part 7.5 Avoiding conflicts of interest
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
Investment adviser, for a professional investor fund, means a person who is retained by the fund’s fund manager under a commercial arrangement (but who is not an employee of the fund manager) to provide the fund manager with:

(a) advice about the merits of investment opportunities for the fund; or
(b) information relevant to the making of judgments about the merits of investment opportunities for the fund.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.5.3 Prior notice of transactions with affected person
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF Part 7.5 Avoiding conflicts of interest
PROF 7.5.3 Prior notice of transactions with affected person
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to a proposed transaction by the fund manager of a professional investor fund in relation to the fund property if the transaction is with an affected person for the fund.
(2) The fund manager must not enter into the transaction unless the fund manager has given the fund investors for the fund prior written notice of the transaction (or transactions that include the transaction), including an explanation of how rule 7.5.4 is complied with in relation to the transaction or transactions.
Example of written notice
notice given in the offer document for the fund.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

(2) The fund manager must not enter into the transaction unless the fund manager has given the fund investors for the fund prior written notice of the transaction (or transactions that include the transaction), including an explanation of how rule 7.5.4 is complied with in relation to the transaction or transactions. QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.5.4 Conduct of transactions with affected person
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF Part 7.5 Avoiding conflicts of interest
PROF 7.5.4 Conduct of transactions with affected person
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to a transaction by the fund manager of a professional investor fund in relation to the fund property if the transaction is with an affected person for the fund.
(2) The fund manager must ensure that:
(a) the terms of the transaction are at least as favourable to the fund as those of any comparable transaction on normal commercial terms that were negotiated at arm’s length with an independent third party; and
(b) the transaction:
(i) does not breach any other provision of this Part; and
(ii) is not prohibited by the fund documents for the fund.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.5.5 Reporting requirements for transactions with affected persons
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF Part 7.5 Avoiding conflicts of interest
PROF 7.5.5 Reporting requirements for transactions with affected persons
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) If the fund manager of a professional investor fund enters into a transaction in relation to the fund property with an affected person for the fund, the fund’s annual report for the accounting period in which the transaction takes place must include the following:
(a) a summary of the total value of transactions with affected persons for the fund in relation to the fund property during the accounting period;
(b) a summary of the nature of the transactions;
(c) a list of the names of the affected persons for the fund;
(d) if the fund investors for the fund voted at a general meeting held during the accounting period to approve a transaction with an affected person for the fund — details of the approval and the results of the voting in relation to the approval.
(2) If the fund manager of a professional investor fund does not enter into any transaction in relation to the fund property with an affected person for the fund during an annual accounting period of the fund, the fund’s annual report for the accounting period must include a statement to that effect.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.6.1 Suspension and restart of dealings — open-ended funds
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF 7.6.1 Suspension and restart of dealings — open-ended funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) This rule applies to the fund manager of an open-ended fund.
(2) The fund manager may temporarily suspend dealings in all units, or a class of units, in the fund. However, the fund manager may do so only within any limits that are fair and reasonable to all fund investors for the fund and are set out in the fund’s offer document.
(3) The fund manager may suspend dealings under subrule (2) only if the fund manager has decided that there is a good and sufficient reason for the suspension in the interests of fund investors, or persons that might become fund investors, for the fund.
(4) If the fund manager decides to suspend dealings, the fund manager must tell the Regulatory Authority about the suspension and the reasons for it within 1 business day after the day on which the fund manager makes the decision.
(5) The fund manager must also notify the fund investors for the fund about the suspension as soon as practicable after the suspension starts.
(6) The fund manager must ensure that the suspension continues only for as long as it is justified having regard to the interests of all the fund investors for the fund.
(7) The suspension of dealings must end as soon as the suspension ceases to be justified in the interests of all the fund investors for the fund.
(8) The fund manager:
(a) must review the suspension at least every 28 days; and
(b) must tell the Regulatory Authority about the result of such a review within 1 business day after conducting it.
(9) If the fund manager becomes aware of any material change in circumstances that may affect the continuation of the suspension, the fund manager must tell the Authority about the change within 1 business day.
(10) The Authority may, at any time, direct the fund manager to end the suspension.
(11) The fund manager must immediately comply with the direction.
(12) If the suspension ends, the fund manager must tell the Authority about the restart of dealings within 1 business day after the day dealings restart.
Note Under FSR, article 105, the Authority has power to give certain directions in relation to collective investment funds, including a direction to cease issuing or redeeming units in the fund and to wind up the fund.

PROF 7.7.1 Application of Part 7.7 to subfunds of umbrella funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
This Part applies to a subfund of an umbrella fund as if:

(a) a reference to a fund were a reference to the subfund;
(b) a reference to units were a reference to units in the class or classes related to the subfund;
(c) a reference to a meeting of fund investors were a reference to a meeting of fund investors for the fund of the class or classes referred to in paragraph (b);
(d) a reference to a special resolution were a reference to a special resolution passed at a meeting of fund investors for the fund referred to in paragraph (c);
(e) a reference to the fund property were a reference to the fund property attributed to the subfund;
(f) a reference to liabilities were a reference to liabilities of the fund attributable to the subfund; and
(g) all other necessary changes were made.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.7.2 Winding up — general
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
A professional investor fund may be wound up in one of the following ways:

(a) by order of the QFC Court under the Insolvency Regulations 2005 or any other regulations in force in the QFC;
(b) if not inconsistent with any regulations in force in the QFC or these rules — in the way and circumstances provided in the constitutional document for the fund;
(c) in the way and in any other circumstances provided by these rules or any other rules made by the Regulatory Authority.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.7.4 Notice to Regulatory Authority that fund not commercially viable or purpose cannot be accomplished
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF 7.7.4 Notice to Regulatory Authority that fund not commercially viable or purpose cannot be accomplished
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) If the fund manager of a professional investor fund believes, on reasonable grounds, that the fund is not commercially viable or that the fund’s purpose cannot be accomplished, the fund manager must give the Regulatory Authority notice about the matter within 1 business day after the day the fund manager forms the belief.
(2) The notice must include the following information:
(a) the fund’s name;
(b) the fund’s size and type;
(c) the number of fund investors for the fund;
(d) if the fund is an open-ended fund — whether dealing in the fund’s units has been suspended;
(e) why the fund manager believes that the fund is not commercially viable or that the fund’s purpose cannot be accomplished;
(f) what consideration has been given to the fund entering into a transfer scheme (see Part 7.8) with a substitute fund and the reasons why a transfer scheme is not possible;
Note Substitute fund is defined in the glossary.
(g) whether fund investors for the fund have been told of the intention to seek winding-up and, if not, whether and when they will be told of the intention;
(h) details of any proposed rebate of charges to be made to fund investors for the fund who recently purchased units in the fund;
(i) the preferred date for the start of the winding-up.
(3) The Authority may, in writing, require the fund manager to provide any further information or documents that the Authority reasonably needs in relation to the fund.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.7.5 Winding-up by fund manager
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) This rule applies if any of the following circumstances exists in relation to a professional investor fund:
(a) the fund’s fund manager has requested the Regulatory Authority to cancel the fund’s registration, and the Authority has agreed in principle that it will do so when the winding-up of the fund is completed;
(b) the fund manager believes, on reasonable grounds, that the fund is not commercially viable or that the fund’s purpose cannot be accomplished;
(c) if the constitutional document for the fund states that the fund’s duration is limited — the fund’s duration ends;
(d) under the fund’s constitutional document, the fund investors for the fund direct the fund manager to wind up the fund;
(e) if the fund is subject to a transfer scheme that was approved under Part 7.8, and under the scheme the fund is to be left with no property — the transfer scheme commences.
(2) If any of the circumstances mentioned in subrule (1) apply in relation to a professional investor fund, the fund’s fund manager:
(a) must cease:
(i) dealing in the fund’s units; and
(ii) investing or borrowing for the fund; and
(b) must take the steps necessary to wind up the fund in accordance with:
(i) any regulations in force in the QFC that apply to the winding-up;
(ii) these rules; and
(iii) any other rules made by the Authority that apply to the winding-up.
(3) If any of the circumstances mentioned in subrule (1) (a) to (d) apply in relation to a professional investor fund:
(a) the fund’s fund manager must realise the fund property as soon as practicable;
(b) after meeting or making provision for all the fund’s liabilities and the costs of the winding-up, the fund manager must distribute the proceeds of the realisation to the fund investors for the fund in accordance with the fund’s constitutional document; and
(c) if the fund manager holds any unclaimed net proceeds or other cash (including unclaimed distribution payments) after the end of 12 months from the day they became payable, the fund manager must pay them into the QFC Court, after meeting or making provision for the costs of doing so.
(4) If the fund manager of a professional investor fund and 1 or more fund investors for the fund agree, the requirement to realise the fund property does not apply to the part of the fund property proportionate to those investors’ entitlement.
(5) The fund manager of a professional investor fund may distribute the part of the fund property mentioned in subrule (4) to the fund investors mentioned in that subrule, after making the adjustments or provisions that appear appropriate to ensure that those fund investors bear a proportionate share of the fund’s liabilities and the costs of the winding-up.
(6) If the circumstance mentioned in subrule (1) (e) applies in relation to a professional investor fund, the fund’s fund manager must wind up the fund in accordance with the approved transfer scheme.
(7) As soon as practicable after starting the winding-up of a professional investor fund, the fund’s fund manager:
(a) must tell the fund investors for the fund about the winding-up; and
(b) must publish notice of the winding-up in an English-language and an Arabic-language national newspaper and, if the fund has a website, on the fund’s website.
(8) Not later than 5 business days after the day the winding-up of a professional investor fund is completed, the fund’s fund manager:
(a) must tell the Authority about the completion of the winding-up; and
(b) must ask the Authority to cancel the fund’s registration.
(9) This rule is subject to any order of the QFC Court.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.7.6 Accounting and reports during winding-up
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF 7.7.6 Accounting and reports during winding-up
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) While a professional investor fund is being wound up, whether under rule 7.7.5 or otherwise:
(a) the annual accounting periods and half-yearly accounting periods continue to run;
(b) the provisions of these rules about annual and interim allocation of income continue to apply to the fund; and
(c) reports to fund investors for the fund and the Regulatory Authority about the fund continue to be required.
(2) However, if the fund’s fund manager decides that the interests of the fund investors for the fund or the Authority do not require the timely preparation of a report for an annual accounting period or half-yearly accounting period, the fund manager may delay the preparation of the report, but only until the end of the next annual accounting period or half-yearly accounting period.
(3) The fund manager may make a decision under subrule (2) only after consulting the fund’s auditor and the Authority, and must have reasonable grounds for the decision.
(4) If the preparation of a report has been delayed under subrule (2), the annual accounting period or half-yearly accounting period for which the report was delayed must be covered in the report for the next annual accounting period or half-yearly accounting period.
(5) At the completion of the winding-up, the annual accounting period then running is regarded as the final annual accounting period for the fund.
(6) Within 2 months after the end of the final annual accounting period, the fund manager must send the report for that period to:
(a) the Authority; and
(b) each person who was a fund investor for the fund immediately before the end of the period.
(7) This rule is subject to any order of the QFC Court.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 7.8.3 Modification of FSR, Part 16, in relation to fund business transfers
doc_path: PROF Chapter 7 Operating professional investor funds
PROF 7.8.3 Modification of FSR, Part 16, in relation to fund business transfers
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
In relation to a fund business transfer, FSR, Part 16 is modified by the insertion of the following article:

“94A Transfers of property of professional investor funds

(1) In this article, expressions defined in the Professional Investor Funds Rules 2022 have the respective meanings so defined.
(2) If, for the purpose of a fund business transfer, it is proposed that all of the fund property of a professional investor fund should become the property of a substitute fund, the proposal must not be implemented without the approval of a special resolution of the fund investors for the fund, unless article 94A (3) applies.
Note Substitute fund is defined in the glossary to the Professional Investor Funds Rules 2022.
(3) If, for the purpose of a fund business transfer, it is proposed that all of the fund property attributable to a subfund (the first subfund) of an umbrella fund should become the property of a substitute fund (whether or not the substitute fund is another subfund of the umbrella fund), the proposal must not be implemented without the approval of:
(a) a special resolution of the fund investors for the first subfund; and
(b) unless the implementation of the transfer scheme is not likely to result in any material prejudice to the interests of the fund investors in any other subfund of the umbrella fund — a special resolution of the fund investors for the fund of units in the umbrella fund.
(4) If it is proposed that a professional investor fund or a subfund of an umbrella fund should receive property (other than its first property) under a fund business transfer, or an arrangement equivalent to a scheme of arrangement (see article 94A (6)), that is entered into by a substitute fund, the proposal must not be implemented without the approval of a special resolution of the fund investors of the substitute fund or of the class or classes of units related to the subfund of the umbrella fund (as appropriate).
(5) However, if the fund manager of a professional investor fund agrees that the receipt of the property by the substitute fund as mentioned in article 94A (4):
(a) is not likely to result in any material prejudice to the interests of the fund investors for the fund; and
(b) is consistent with the investment objectives, strategies and policy of the fund or subfund;
the property may be transferred to the fund or subfund, and units in the fund or subfund may be issued in exchange for the property, as part of the fund business transfer without the approval of a special resolution.
(6) In article 94A (4):
scheme of arrangement means an arrangement relating to a professional investor fund (the transferor fund), or to a subfund of an umbrella fund (the transferor subfund), under which:
(a) either:
(i) all or part of the property of the transferor fund, or all or part of the property attributed to the transferor subfund, is to become property of 1 or more substitute funds registered in the QFC (the transferee fund or transferee funds); or
(ii) all or part of the property attributed to the transferor subfund is to become property attributed to 1 or more other subfunds of the same umbrella fund that is a substitute fund (the transferee subfund or transferee subfunds); and
(b) fund investors for the transferor fund or transferor subfund are to receive, in exchange for their respective interests in the property being transferred or reattributed, either:
(i) units in the transferee fund, or 1 or more of the transferee funds, to which the property is transferred; or
(ii) units in the transferee subfund, or 1 or more of the transferee subfunds, to which the property is reattributed.”.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

(4) If it is proposed that a professional investor fund or a subfund of an umbrella fund should receive property (other than its first property) under a fund business transfer, or an arrangement equivalent to a scheme of arrangement (see article 94A (6)), that is entered into by a substitute fund, the proposal must not be implemented without the approval of a special resolution of the fund investors of the substitute fund or of the class or classes of units related to the subfund of the umbrella fund (as appropriate). (5) However, if the fund manager of a professional investor fund agrees that the receipt of the property by the substitute fund as mentioned in article 94A (4): (a) is not likely to result in any material prejudice to the interests of the fund investors for the fund; and (b) is consistent with the investment objectives, strategies and policy of the fund or subfund; the property may be transferred to the fund or subfund, and units in the fund or subfund may be issued in exchange for the property, as part of the fund business transfer without the approval of a special resolution. (6) In article 94A (4): scheme of arrangement means an arrangement relating to a professional investor fund (the transferor fund ), or to a subfund of an umbrella fund (the transferor subfund ), under which: (a) either: (i) all or part of the property of the transferor fund, or all or part of the property attributed to the transferor subfund, is to become property of 1 or more substitute funds registered in the QFC (the transferee fund or transferee funds ); or (ii) all or part of the property attributed to the transferor subfund is to become property attributed to 1 or more other subfunds of the same umbrella fund that is a substitute fund (the transferee subfund or transferee subfunds ); and (b) fund investors for the transferor fund or transferor subfund are to receive, in exchange for their respective interests in the property being transferred or reattributed, either: (i) units in the transferee fund, or 1 or more of the transferee funds, to which the property is transferred; or (ii) units in the transferee subfund, or 1 or more of the transferee subfunds, to which the property is reattributed.”. Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF Chapter 8 Records, accounts and reports
doc_path: PROF Chapter 8 Records, accounts and reports
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
Introductory notes for Chapter 8

1 This Chapter is about the records that must be kept, and reports that must be prepared, for professional investor funds.
2 The fund manager of a professional investor fund is responsible for ensuring that records are kept and reports are prepared.
3 The fund manager of a professional investor fund must prepare an annual report for the fund. The annual report must include the accounts for the fund.
4 The fund manager of a professional investor fund must prepare the accounts for the fund. The accounts must be prepared in accordance with internationally accepted accounting standards. The fund manager must ensure the accounts give a true and fair overview of the finances of the fund and its operations throughout the period covered by the report.
5 The fund manager of a professional investor fund is responsible for ensuring that there is an auditor appointed at all times. The auditor must be a QFC approved auditor who is eligible under GENE, Part 9.7. The fund’s auditor must audit the accounts.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)
