QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 8.1.3 Accounting periods
doc_path: PROF Chapter 8 Records, accounts and reports
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) A professional investor fund must have a half-yearly accounting period and an annual accounting period that satisfy these rules.
(2) A half-yearly accounting period starts on the first day of an annual accounting period and ends:
(a) on the day that is 6 months before the last day of the annual accounting period; or
(b) on another reasonable date stated in the fund’s offer document.
(3) The first annual accounting period:
(a) starts on:
(i) the first day of the initial offer period; or
(ii) if there is no initial offer period for the fund — the date the fund is registered; and
(b) ends on the next accounting reference date, unless subrule (4) applies.
(4) If the first accounting reference date falls less than 6 months after the start of the first annual accounting period, the fund’s fund manager may extend the first annual accounting period to the next accounting reference date.
(5) Each annual accounting period after the first is for 12 months, starting on the day after an accounting reference date and ending on the next accounting reference date, unless subrule (7) applies.
(6) Each annual accounting period or half-yearly accounting period ends at the end of the day worked out under this rule, or, if the fund manager so decides, at the last valuation point on that day at which the fund property is valued.
(7) If the accounting reference date stated in the fund’s offer document is changed, the fund manager may lengthen or shorten the fund’s annual accounting period by up to 6 months to end on the next accounting reference date.
(8) Before lengthening or shortening an annual accounting period under subrule (4) or (7), the fund manager:
(a) must consult the fund’s auditor; and
(b) must give the Regulatory Authority reasonable notice.
(9) If the annual accounting period for a professional investor fund is extended under subrule (4) or (7) and the result is a longer than usual period before the publication of reports to fund investors for the fund, the fund’s fund manager must, during the extended period, make summary information about the fund’s investment activities available to the fund investors.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 8.2.1 Legal and regulatory requirement to keep records
doc_path: PROF Chapter 8 Records, accounts and reports
PROF 8.2.1 Legal and regulatory requirement to keep records
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must make the records necessary to enable the fund manager:
(a) to comply with:
(i) these rules;
(ii) the other provisions of the law applying in the QFC in relation to the fund; and
(iii) the other provisions of the law applying in the QFC in relation to the fund manager as a fund manager of a professional investor fund or as an operator of a collective investment fund;
(b) in the case of a QFC fund manager — to comply with any other provisions of the law applying in the QFC to the fund manager as an authorised firm; and
(c) to demonstrate, at all times, whether the fund manager has complied with the requirements set out in paragraphs (a) and (b).
(2) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must keep a record made for this rule for at least 10 years after the day the record is made.
(3) At the request of the Regulatory Authority or the auditor of a professional investor fund, the fund’s fund manager:
(a) must make records kept under this rule available for inspection by the Authority or the fund’s auditor within a reasonable period that is no longer than 3 days; and
(b) must provide a copy of any of the records to the Authority or the auditor in the requested form (if any), within a reasonable period that is no longer than 3 days.
(4) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must not charge for making records available, or providing a copy of any records, under subrule (3).
Note 1 GENE, Chapter 6 contains provisions about record-keeping and how records must be maintained. These requirements apply to all QFC fund managers.
Note 2 CIPR, Chapter 8 requires authorised firms to maintain complete and readily accessible records about instructions from customers. These requirements apply to QFC fund managers of standard professional investor funds.

PROF 8.3.1 Fund manager of professional investor fund must prepare annual and half-yearly reports
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must prepare a report, in accordance with this Part, for each annual accounting period and each half-yearly accounting period.
(2) However, if the first annual accounting period is less than 12 months, a half-yearly report need not be prepared for that period.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 8.3.3 Contents of annual reports — funds other than umbrella funds
doc_path: PROF Chapter 8 Records, accounts and reports
PROF 8.3.3 Contents of annual reports — funds other than umbrella funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
An annual report for an annual accounting period of a professional investor fund (other than an umbrella fund) must contain the following:

(a) the audited accounts for the period;
(b) the fund manager’s report (see rule 8.5.1) for the period;
(c) the auditor’s report (see rule 8.6.2) for the period.
Note See also rule 7.5.5 about reporting requirements for transactions with affected persons.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 8.3.4 Contents of annual reports — umbrella funds
doc_path: PROF Chapter 8 Records, accounts and reports
PROF 8.3.4 Contents of annual reports — umbrella funds
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) An annual report for an annual accounting period of an umbrella fund must be prepared for the umbrella fund as a whole, and must contain the following:
(a) for each subfund of the umbrella fund:
(i) the audited accounts for the period; and
(ii) the fund manager’s report (see rule 8.5.1) for the period;
(b) an aggregation of all the accounts required by paragraph (a);
(c) the auditor’s report (see rule 8.6.2) for the umbrella fund for the period.
(2) If the Regulatory Authority so approves, such a report need not comply with subrule (1) (b).
(3) In addition to complying with subrule (1), the fund manager of the umbrella fund may prepare a further annual report for any 1 or more individual subfunds.
(4) A report under subrule (3) for an annual accounting period of a subfund must contain the following:
(a) the audited accounts for the subfund for the period;
(b) the fund manager’s report (see rule 8.5.1) for the subfund for the period;
(c) the auditor’s report (see rule 8.6.2) for the umbrella fund for the period.

(2) If the fund is an umbrella fund, the fund manager may prepare the half-yearly report for the fund as a whole, for each individual subfund, or for both.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 8.3.7 Providing copies of reports to fund investors and other interested persons
doc_path: PROF Chapter 8 Records, accounts and reports
PROF 8.3.7 Providing copies of reports to fund investors and other interested persons
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must make reports, prepared in accordance with this Part, available free of charge to a fund investor for the fund or a person that proposes to become, a fund investor for the fund.
(2) The fund manager must do so:
(a) in the case of a fund investor for the fund:
(i) before the fund investor acquires, or contracts to acquire, a further unit in the fund; or
(ii) at any other time, on the fund investor’s request; and
(b) in the case of a person that proposes to become a fund investor for the fund — before the person acquires, or contracts to acquire, a unit in the fund.
(3) If the fund is an umbrella fund, a report that is made available under subrule (1) may be a report prepared under rule 8.3.4 (3) for the relevant subfund. However, the fund manager must also make available to the person a copy of the report prepared under rule 8.3.4 (1) for the fund as a whole if the person asks for it.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 8.5.1 Fund manager’s report
doc_path: PROF Chapter 8 Records, accounts and reports
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
The fund manager of a professional investor fund must prepare, for an accounting period, a report (the fund manager’s report) that includes the following:

(a) a review comparing the investment activities of the fund (or, if the fund is an umbrella fund, each subfund) during the period with those set out in the offer document for the fund applying to the period;
(b) particulars of any fundamental or significant change in relation to the fund (or, if the fund is an umbrella fund, each subfund) since the fund manager’s last report;
(c) any other information that would enable fund investors for the fund to make an informed judgment on the development of the activities of the fund (or, if the fund is an umbrella fund, each subfund) during the period and the results of those activities as at the end of the period.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 8.6.1 Appointment and removal of auditor
doc_path: PROF Chapter 8 Records, accounts and reports
PROF 8.6.1 Appointment and removal of auditor
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must ensure that there is, at all times, an auditor of the fund.
(2) Accordingly, a person must be appointed from time to time as the fund’s auditor in accordance with the fund’s constitutional document.
(3) The fund’s auditor must be an eligible auditor:
(a) who is approved by the QFC Authority to act as an auditor; and
(b) whose name is entered in the register of auditors maintained by the QFC Companies Registration Office.
(4) For subrule (3), a person is an eligible auditor for a professional investor fund if the person is eligible to be the fund’s auditor under GENE, Part 9.7, as applied by subrule (8).
(5) The auditor’s audit fees are as the fund manager decides.
(6) The fund manager may remove the auditor at any time.
Note Under GENE, rule 9.7.3A, as applied by subrule (8), an auditor’s term is limited to 5 years.
(7) The power in subrule (6) has effect despite anything in any agreement between the auditor and either the fund manager or the fund.
(8) GENE, Part 9.7, applies to the appointment and removal of the auditor as if the fund were an authorised firm.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 8.6.2 Auditor’s report
doc_path: PROF Chapter 8 Records, accounts and reports
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
The fund manager of a professional investor fund must ensure that, for each annual accounting period of the fund, the fund’s auditor prepares a report (the auditor’s report) to the fund investors for the fund that includes the following statements:

(a) whether, in the auditor’s opinion, the accounts have been properly prepared in accordance with these rules and the fund documents for the fund;
(b) whether, in the auditor’s opinion, the accounts give a true and fair view of:
(i) the net income and the net gains or losses of the fund property for the relevant annual accounting period; and
(ii) the fund’s financial position as at the end of the accounting period;
(c) whether the auditor is of the opinion that proper accounting records for the fund have been kept and whether the accounts are in agreement with the accounting records;
(d) whether the auditor has been given all the information and explanations that, to the best of the auditor’s knowledge and belief, are necessary for the purposes of the audit;
(e) whether the auditor is of the opinion that the information given in the fund manager’s report for the accounting period is consistent with the accounts.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 9.1.2 Islamic fund must have Shari’a supervisory board
doc_path: PROF 9.1.2 Islamic fund must have Shari’a supervisory board
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of an Islamic fund must ensure that there is, at all times, a Shari’a supervisory board for the fund.
(2) CTRL, Part 9.3, applies to an Islamic fund as if:
(a) the fund were an Islamic financial institution (within the meaning given by CTRL);
(b) a reference to an Islamic financial institution was a reference to the fund;
(c) a reference to the governing body of an Islamic financial institution were a reference to the fund manager;
(d) rule 9.3.2 (2) were omitted; and
(e) all other necessary changes were made.
(3) A decision relating to the appointment or dismissal of a member of the fund’s Shari’a supervisory board, or to a change affecting the board, must be made by the fund’s fund manager.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 10.1.1 Fees
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) An applicant for the registration of a professional investor fund must pay the Regulatory Authority an application fee of the relevant amount.
(2) The fee must be paid when the application is filed with the Authority.
(3) The Authority may also, by written notice given to the applicant, require the applicant to pay a supplementary fee to the Authority not later than the time stated in the notice if the Authority expects to incur substantial costs in processing the application.
(4) If subrule (2), or a notice under subrule (3), is not complied with, the application is taken not to have been made until the fee is paid.
(5) The fee is non-refundable, whether or not the application is successful.
(6) In this rule:
relevant amount, for a fund, means:
(a) if the fund is not an umbrella fund, or is an umbrella fund with only 1 subfund — US$ 2,000; or
(b) if the fund is an umbrella fund with 2 or more subfunds — whichever is the lesser of the following:
(i) US$ 1,000 x number of subfunds;
(ii) US$ 10,000.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 10.1.2 Annual fees
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The fund manager of a professional investor fund must pay the Regulatory Authority an annual fee for each year that the fund is registered.
(2) The annual fee for the first year of registration is the amount calculated as follows:
where:
F is the appropriate annual fee for the fund for a subsequent year, as specified in subrule (4).
W is the number of whole months remaining, after the date of the fund’s registration, in the year.
(3) The annual fee for the first year of registration must be paid within 21 days after the day the fund is registered.
(4) The annual fee for a subsequent year of registration is:
(a) if the fund is not an umbrella fund, or is an umbrella fund with only 1 subfund — US$ 2,000; or
(b) if the fund is an umbrella fund with 2 or more subfunds — whichever is the lesser of the following:
(i) US$ 1,000 x number of subfunds;
(ii) US$ 10,000.
(5) The annual fee for a subsequent year of registration must be paid on or before 1 January in the year.
(6) If the annual fee is not paid in accordance with this rule, the amount of the fee is increased by 1% for each month, or part of a month, that it remains unpaid after the date it became payable.
(7) Subrule (6) does not limit any action that the Authority may take if an annual fee is not paid in accordance with this rule.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 11.1.1 Restitution orders for breach of relevant requirement
doc_path: PROF 11.1.1 Restitution orders for breach of relevant requirement
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) A person may apply to the QFC Court for a restitution order if:
(a) the person suffers loss or damage as a result of a breach of a relevant requirement in relation to a professional investor fund; and
(b) the person is:
(i) an individual acting otherwise than in the course of conducting a regulated activity; or
(ii) another person acting otherwise than in the course of conducting business of any kind.
Note This rule is made under FSR, article 65.
(2) In subrule (1), a person breaches a relevant requirement in the circumstances described in FSR, article 84.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF 11.1.2 Requirement for notices
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) If a provision of these rules authorises or requires a notice or other document to be served on, or information to be given to, any person (other than the Regulatory Authority), (whether the word ‘serve’, ‘give’, ‘notify’, ‘send’ or ‘tell’, or some other word, is used), the document or information must be served or given in a legible form.
(2) For subrule (1), any form is a legible form if it meets the following requirements:
(a) it is consistent with the knowledge that the person serving the document, or giving the information, has about how the recipient of the document or information wishes or expects to receive it;
(b) it can be provided in a durable medium by the person serving the document or giving the information;
(c) it enables the recipient to know or record the time of receipt;
(d) it is reasonable in the context.
(3) In these rules, a requirement that a document be signed may be satisfied by an electronic signature or electronic evidence of assent.

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF S2.1 Contents of offer document
doc_path: PROF S2.1 Contents of offer document
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
The offer document must include information about the fund, including the following:

(a) the fund’s name, and the address of its registered office in the QFC;
(b) the date of the fund’s incorporation or establishment (indicating whether or not the duration is limited);
(c) if the fund is an exempt professional investor fund — that the minimum investment of a fund investor for the fund is QR 400,000 (or a specified higher amount);
(d) that the maximum number of fund investors for the fund is 199 (or a specified lesser number);
(e) a statement of the place where copies of the constitutional document and any annual reports may be inspected and obtained;
(f) the fund’s accounting reference date;
(g) if the fund is a QFC company — details of the authorised and issued shares including (if applicable) any existing initial, founder or management equity interests;
(h) details of the principal rights and restrictions attaching to the units in the fund, including with respect to currency, voting rights, circumstances of winding up or dissolution, certificates, and entry in registers;
(i) if applicable, an indication of stock exchanges or markets where the equity interests are, or are to be, listed or dealt in;
(j) the procedures and conditions for the issue and sale of units in the fund;
(k) the procedures and conditions for the redemption or purchase of units in the fund and the circumstances in which dealing in units may be suspended;
(l) a description of the intentions in relation to the declaration of dividends or distributions on the units in the fund;
(m) a description of the fund’s investment objectives, investment policy and any limitations on that investment policy;
(n) a description of the fund’s material risks and an indication of any techniques and instruments or borrowing powers which may be used;
(o) a description of the policy and procedures for calculating the fund’s net asset value;
(p) disclosure of any expected material involvement by the fund manager or investment adviser in the valuation of the fund property;
(q) a description of the rules applicable to the determination of prices for issue (or sale) and redemption (or purchase), the frequency of dealings and the places where information about the prices may be obtained;
(r) information about the manner or calculation of remuneration of the fund manager, the fund’s investment adviser and any other service providers receiving or likely to receive fees from the fund;
(s) a description of the potential conflicts of interest between the fund, the fund manager and the fund’s service providers;
(t) a statement confirming the power to enter into side letters:
(i) that bind the fund;
(ii) that contain any terms the effect of which is to provide a fund investor for the fund (investor A) with more favourable treatment than other fund investors for the fund who hold units in the fund in the same class as investor A;
(iii) the terms of which enhance investor A’s ability to redeem units of that class, or make a determination as to whether to redeem units of that class; and
(iv) the terms of which might reasonably be expected to put the other fund investors for the fund at a material disadvantage in connection with the exercise of their rights to redeem units in the fund;
(u) whether the fund is registered or licensed (however described), or intends to be registered or licensed, in any jurisdiction or with any supervisory or regulatory authority outside the QFC;
(v) details of the nature and frequency of financial reports to be distributed to fund investors for the fund;
(w) the principles or standards in accordance with which the fund’s fund manager must prepare and maintain the accounts for the fund;
(x) if the fund is an Islamic fund — that the fund is an Islamic fund and that all of the fund’s operations will be conducted in accordance with Shari’a.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2022-1 (as from 1st April 2022)

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF S2.4 Details of entities involved with fund’s affairs
doc_path: PROF S2.4 Details of entities involved with fund’s affairs
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(1) The following information:
(a) the following information in relation to the fund’s fund manager, and (if applicable) each of the fund’s investment managers and investment advisers:
(i) its name and address;
(ii) whether it is an authorised firm;
(iii) for an investment adviser — the name, and details of the experience, of each individual who is a director or principal, or otherwise occupies a senior management role in the investment adviser;
(iv) for an investment adviser — if it conducts a significant activity other than providing advice to the fund as an investment adviser, details of the activity;
(v) for an investment adviser — a summary of the material provisions of the contracts to which it is a party in relation to the fund that may be relevant to fund investors for the fund, including provisions (if any) relating to remuneration, remuneration sharing, termination, compensation on termination and indemnity engaging the services of the investment adviser;
(b) the name and address of the fund’s auditor;
(c) the name and address of the fund’s legal advisers;
(d) the name and address of the entity that is responsible for calculating and producing the fund’s net asset value;
(e) the name and address of the entity that is responsible for registrar and transfer services for the fund;
(f) the name, address and main business activity of any custodian or sub-custodian for the fund, and the name of any regulatory authority under which it operates;
(g) the name and address of the fund’s principal prime broker, and the name of any regulatory authority under which it operates;
(h) the name, address and duties of any other person with significant involvement in the fund’s affairs.
(2) In subclause (1):
address, for an entity, means the address of the entity’s principal place of business.

PROF S2A.6 Description of token infrastructure
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
The offer document must include a description of the token infrastructure on which the tokenised units, or tokens held as fund property, are stored, including:

(a) details of any licences issued by the QFC Authority to token generators who generate tokens on the infrastructure;
(b) a description of the governance arrangements relating to the infrastructure, including a description of the manner in which the fund manager ensures that fund units are held only by, and transferred only to, persons who are professional investors;
(c) an explanation of the potential risks associated with use of the infrastructure, including the cyber-attack risks and risks of loss of tokens; and
(d) a description of the measures taken to mitigate those risks.

I, ___________________________(name) confirm that I have received and read the offer document for the ____________________________________________________ (name of exempt professional investor fund).

I confirm that I am eligible to be a fund investor in an exempt professional investor fund because:

QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.title: PROF Glossary
QFCRA Rules :: Professional Investors Fu.document_html:
(see rule 1.1.5)

accounting reference date has the meaning given by rule 8.1.2.

accounts has the meaning given by rule 8.1.1.

affected person, for a professional investor fund, has the meaning given by rule 7.5.1.

AML/CFTR means the Anti-Money Laundering and Combatting the Financing of Terrorism Rules 2019.

annual accounting period of a professional investor fund has the meaning given by rule 8.1.3.

annual report, for a professional investor fund for an annual accounting period of the fund, means a report for the fund and the period prepared in accordance with Chapter 8.

articles of association, for a professional investor fund that is a QFC company, means the articles of association of the company as amended from time to time.

associated person, for a person (A), means any of the following:

(a) if A is a legal person — a legal person in the same group as A;
(b) any other person whose business or domestic relationship with A might reasonably be expected to give rise to a community of interest between them that may involve a conflict of interest in engaging with third parties.

audited accounts has the meaning given by rule 8.1.4.

auditor’s report has the meaning given by rule 8.6.2.

authorisation means an authorisation granted under FSR, Part 5.

authorised firm means a person that has an authorisation.

base currency, for a professional investor fund, means the currency stated in the fund’s constitutional document as the fund’s base currency.

borrowing, for a professional investor fund, includes any arrangement (including a combination of derivatives) designed to achieve a temporary injection of money into the fund property in the expectation that the amount will be repaid.

breach includes fail or refuse to comply with.

business day means a day that is not a Friday, Saturday, or a public holiday or bank holiday in Qatar.

CDRS means the Customer Dispute Resolution Scheme Rules 2019.

certified professional investor has the meaning given by rule 2.1.4.

exempt professional investor fund has the meaning given by rule 1.2.3.

CIPR means the Customer and Investor Protection Rules 2019.

class, for a professional investor fund, means:

(a) a particular class of units in the fund; or
(b) if the fund is an umbrella fund:
(i) all the units relating to a single subfund of the fund; or
(ii) a particular class of units relating to a single subfund of the fund.

closed-ended fund has the meaning given by rule 1.2.5 (2).

COLL means the Collective Investment Schemes Rules 2010.

collective investment fund is an arrangement that is a collective investment fund under FSR, other than an arrangement that is not a collective investment scheme under COLL, Schedule 1.

Note 1

FSR, Schedule 3, Part 3, paragraphs 6.2 to 6.6 provide as follows:

6.2 Subject to paragraphs 6.5 and 6.6, a collective investment fund is any arrangement:
(1) the purpose or effect of which is to enable persons taking part in the arrangements (the participants) to participate in or receive profits or income arising from the acquisition, holding, management or disposal of property or sums paid out of such profits or income;
(2) that meets the property condition in paragraph 6.3 and the investment condition in paragraph 6.4.
6.3 An arrangement will meet the property condition referred to in paragraph (2) if:
(1) the arrangement is made with respect to property of any description, including money, whether the participants become owners of the property or any part of it or otherwise; and
(2) any of the participants do not have day-to-day control over the management of the property, whether or not they have the right to be consulted or give directions in respect of the property.
6.4 An arrangement will meet the investment condition referred to in paragraph 6.2 if:
(1) the contributions of the participants and the profits or income out of which payments to be made are pooled; or
(2) the property is managed as a whole by or on behalf of the operator of the scheme.
6.5 Arrangements for such pooling as is mentioned in paragraph 6.4 (1) in relation to separate parts of the property are not to be regarded as constituting a single collective investment fund unless the participants are entitled to exchange rights in one part for rights in another.
6.6 The Regulatory Authority may make rules specifying the circumstances in which particular arrangements do not constitute a collective investment fund for the purposes of paragraph 6.1.
Note 2 Schedule 1 of COLL specifies circumstances in which particular arrangements do not constitute collective investment schemes (referred to as funds in FSR).
Note 3 The participants referred to in FSR are referred to as fund investors in these rules.

constitutional document, for a professional investor fund, has the meaning given by rule 5.1.1.

contract for differences means the specified product described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 3, paragraph 9.

contract of insurance means the specified product described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 3, paragraph 10.

controlled function has the meaning given by FSR, article 41 (2).

corporation includes all of the following:

(a) a company;
(b) a limited partnership;
(c) a limited liability partnership.

CTRL means the Governance and Controlled Functions Rules 2020.

customer has the meaning given by CIPR.

day means a period of 24 hours starting at midnight.

deal means buy, sell, otherwise acquire, subscribe for or underwrite property or offer or agree to do so, either as principal or agent, and includes, for an investment that is a contract of insurance, carry out the contract.

dealing costs has the meaning given by rule 7.4.1.

dealing day has the meaning given by rule 7.3.5 (2).

dealing in investments means the regulated activity described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 2, paragraph 4.

debt instrument means the specified product described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 3, paragraph 2.

dedicated, for investments of a professional investor fund, means intended that the fund investors for the fund should participate or receive:

(a) profits or income arising from the acquisition, holding, management or disposal of investments of that kind; or
(b) amounts paid out of profits or income mentioned in paragraph (a).

derivative means a future, option or contract for differences.

distribution account, for a professional investor fund, means the account (if any) to which the income property must be transferred as at the end of each annual accounting period.

document means a record of information in any form (including electronic form), and includes, for example, all of the following:

(a) anything in writing or on which there is writing;
(b) anything on which there are figures, marks, numbers, perforations, symbols or anything else having a meaning for individuals qualified to interpret them;
(c) a drawing, map, photograph or plan;
(d) any other item or matter (in whatever form) that is, or could reasonably be considered to be, a record of information.

employee of a person (A), means an individual:

(a) who is employed or appointed by A, whether under a contract of service or services or otherwise; or
(b) whose services are, under an arrangement between A and a third party, placed at the disposal and under the control of A.

entity means any kind of entity, and includes, for example, any person.

exercise a function means exercise or perform the function.

forward price has the meaning given by rule 7.3.6 (4).

function means any function and includes any authority, obligation, duty or power.

fund document, for a professional investor fund, means either or both of the following:

(a) the fund’s constitutional document;
(b) the fund’s offer document.

fund investor, for a professional investor fund, has the meaning given by rule 2.1.1.

fund manager of a professional investor fund has the meaning given by rule 3.1.1.

fund manager’s report has the meaning given by rule 8.5.1.

fund property: the fund property of a professional investor fund is the property held for or in the fund.

future means the specified product described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 3, paragraph 8.

GENE means the General Rules 2005.

governing body, of an entity, means its board of directors, committee of management or other governing body (whatever it is called).

group means the following:

(a) a legal person (A);
(b) any parent entity of A;
(c) any subsidiary (direct or indirect) of A or of any parent entity of A.

half-yearly accounting period, for a standard professional investor fund, has the meaning given by rule 8.1.3.

half-yearly report, for a standard professional investor fund and a half-yearly accounting period, means a report prepared in accordance with Chapter 8.

income equalisation, for a professional investor fund, means a capital amount that, in accordance with a power in the fund’s constitutional document, is included in an allocation of income for a unit in the fund issued during the accounting period in relation to which the income allocation is made.

income property, for a professional investor fund, means all amounts considered by the fund’s fund manager, after consultation with the fund’s auditor, to be of the nature of income received or receivable in relation to the fund property, other than any amount in the distribution account (if any).

INAP means the Interpretation and Application Rules 2005.

INDI means the Individuals (Assessment, Training and Competency) Rules 2014.

initial offer has the meaning given by rule 6.2.2 (2).

initial offer period means the period determined as set out in rule 6.2.2 (1).

INMA means the Investment Management and Advisory Rules 2014.

instrument means an instrument of any kind, and includes (for example) any writing or other document.

investment means any investment, including any asset, right or interest.

investment adviser has the meaning given by rule 7.5.2.

Islamic fund has the meaning given by rule 9.1.1.

issue, of a unit in a professional investor fund, means the issue of a new unit in the fund by the fund’s fund manager.

jurisdiction means any kind of legal jurisdiction, and includes all of the following:

(a) the State of Qatar;
(b) a foreign country (whether or not an independent sovereign jurisdiction), or a state, province or other territory of such a foreign country;
(c) the QFC or a similar jurisdiction.

larger denomination share has the meaning given by rule 6.2.5 (3).

legal person means an entity (other than an individual) on which the legal system of a jurisdiction confers rights and imposes duties, and includes, for example, any entity that can engage in property transactions.

Examples

1 a company
2 any other corporation
3 a partnership, whether or not incorporated
4 an association or other undertaking, whether or not incorporated.

managing investments means the regulated activity described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 2, paragraph 10.

money means any form of money, including cheques and other payable orders.

month means calendar month.

net asset value has the meaning given by rule 7.3.2.

net asset value per unit has the meaning given by rule 7.3.3.

offer document, for a professional investor fund, has the meaning given by rule 5.2.1.

open-ended fund has the meaning given by rule 1.2.5 (1).

operating a collective investment fund means the regulated activity described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 2, paragraph 12.

option means the specified product described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 3, paragraph 7.

ordinary resolution, for a professional investor fund or a class of units in a fund, means a resolution passed at a general meeting of the fund or a separate meeting of the fund investors of that class of units, if:

(a) notice indicating the intention to propose the resolution was properly given; and
(b) the resolution passed by a simple majority of the votes validly cast (whether as a show of hands or on a poll) for or against the resolution at the meeting.

parent entity, for a legal person (A), means any of the following:

(a) a legal person that holds a majority of the voting power in A;
(b) a legal person that is a member of A (whether direct or indirect, or though legal or beneficial entitlement) and alone, or together with 1 or more legal persons in the same group, holds a majority of the voting power in A;
(c) a parent entity of any legal person that is a parent entity of A.

partnership agreement, for a professional investor fund that is a QFC limited partnership, means the partnership agreement of the partnership as amended from time to time.

person means:

(a) an individual (including an individual occupying an office or position from time to time); or
(b) a legal person.

price, of a unit in a professional investor fund, means the price of the unit calculated in accordance with these rules.

professional investor has the meaning given by rule 2.1.2.

professional investor fund has the meaning given by rule 1.2.1.

property means any estate or interest (whether present or future, vested or contingent, or tangible or intangible) in immovables or property of any other kind, and includes, for example:

(a) money of any currency;
(b) bonds, securities, shares, and other negotiable or non-negotiable instruments of any kind;
(c) any right to interest, dividends, or other income, on or accruing from or generated by immovables or property of any other kind;
(d) any other things in action;
(e) any other charge, claim, demand, easement, encumbrance, lien, power, privilege, right, or title, recognised or protected by the law of any jurisdiction over, or in relation to, immovables or property of any other kind; and
(f) any other documents evidencing title to, or to any interest in, immovables or property of any other kind.

QFC means the Qatar Financial Centre.

QFC company means a company that is incorporated under the Companies Regulations 2005.

QFC Court means the Qatar Financial Centre Civil and Commercial Court.

QFC fund manager of a professional investor fund has the meaning given by rule 3.2.1 (1).

QFC limited partnership means a limited partnership that is incorporated under the Partnership Regulations 2007.

redemption, of a unit in a professional investor fund, means the redemption of an existing unit by the fund’s fund manager on behalf of the fund.

register of fund investors has the meaning given by rule 6.3.1.

regulated activity means an activity that is a regulated activity under FSR.

Regulatory Authority means the Qatar Financial Centre Regulatory Authority.

remuneration means any form of remuneration, and includes benefits of any kind.

rules means any rules made by the Regulatory Authority, and includes:

(a) any standard, principle or code of practice made by the Regulatory Authority; and
(b) any other instrument made or in force under any rules, standard, principle or code of practice made by the Regulatory Authority.

security means any of the following:

(a) a share;
(b) a debt instrument;
(c) a warrant;
(d) a securities receipt;
(e) a unit in a collective investment fund.

securities receipt means the specified product described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 3, paragraph 5.

sell an investment means sell the investment in any way, and includes the following:

(a) dispose of the investment for valuable consideration;
(b) for an investment consisting of rights under a contract:
(i) surrender, assign or convert the rights for valuable consideration; or
(ii) assume the corresponding rights under the contract for valuable consideration;
(c) for an investment consisting of rights under an arrangement — assume the corresponding liabilities under the arrangement for valuable consideration;
(d) for any other investment — issue or create the investment or grant the rights or interests of which it consists.

share means the specified product described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 3, paragraph 1.

Shari’a supervisory board, of an Islamic fund, means the board constituted for the fund under rule 9.1.2.

smaller denomination share has the meaning given by rule 6.2.5 (3).

special resolution, for a professional investor fund, or a class of units in a professional investor fund, means a resolution passed at a general meeting of the fund or a separate meeting of fund investors for the fund for that class of units in the fund if:

(a) notice indicating the intention to propose the resolution as a special resolution was properly given; and
(b) the resolution was passed by a majority of at least 75% of the votes validly cast (whether as a show of hands or on a poll) for or against the resolution at the meeting.

specified product means an investment or other type of product that is a specified product under FSR.

standard professional investor fund has the meaning given by rule 1.2.2.

State fund manager of a professional investor fund has the meaning given by rule 3.3.1.

subfund, of an umbrella fund, has the meaning given by rule 1.2.6 (2).

subsidiary: a legal person (A) is a subsidiary of another legal person (B) if B is a parent entity of A.

substitute fund: a collective investment fund is a substitute fund in relation to a professional investor fund if the collective investment fund is any of the following:

(a) another professional investor fund;
(b) a subfund of an umbrella fund;
(c) a collective investment scheme registered in the QFC;
(d) a subscheme of an umbrella scheme registered in the QFC.

umbrella fund has the meaning given by rule 1.2.6 (1).

unit, in a professional investor fund, has the meaning given by rule 6.1.1 (1).

valuation point has the meaning given by rule 7.3.5 (1).

warrant means the specified product described in FSR, Schedule 3, Part 3, paragraph 4.

writing means any form of writing, and includes, for example, any way of representing or reproducing words, numbers, symbols or anything else in legible form (for example, by printing or photocopying).

year means calendar year.

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 1.1.5 Operating representative office to be regulated activity
doc_path: REPO 1.1.5 Operating representative office to be regulated activity
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
(1) For FSR, article 23 (2), the activity of operating a representative office is a regulated activity.

(2) The regulated activity of operating a representative office consists of doing any 1 or more of the following in or from the QFC:

(a) subject to subrule (3), providing information (but not advice) in relation to financial services or financial products offered by the representative office’s head office if (and only if) the information is general in nature (such as, for example, providing a general market or risk study, investment research or a published prospectus);

(b) on behalf of the representative office’s head office or a member of the same corporate group, doing any of the following:

(i) acting as a channel of communication between the head office or member and actual or potential customers of the head office or member in Qatar;
(ii) carrying out market research or feasibility studies in relation to financial products or financial services on behalf of the head office or member;
(iii) reporting to the head office or member on business trends, opportunities and developments in the Qatari market;
(c) subject to subrule (3), marketing 1 or more financial products or financial services offered by the head office or member.
Note For the meaning, in these rules, of marketing a financial product or financial service, see the Glossary.

(3) Providing information about, or marketing, a financial product or financial service by a representative office is within the regulated activity of operating a representative office if and only if the product or service falls within the description of a specified product or specified activity.

Note 1 For the description of the specified products and specified activities, see FSR, Schedule 3, Part 3 and Schedule 3, Part 2 respectively.
Note 2 Chapter 5 disapplies certain rules. Therefore, other rules including the Schedules to the rules apply, in particular GENE Schedule 4, Fees table.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)
Amended by QFCRA RM/2026-2 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 2.2.2 Disclosures of status required on certain business documents
doc_path: REPO 2.2.2 Disclosures of status required on certain business documents
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
(1) A representative office must take reasonable care to ensure that every significant business document that it uses in connection with its operation includes either of the following disclosures:
(a) “Authorised by the Qatar Financial Centre Regulatory Authority as a representative office”;
(b) “Authorised by the QFC Regulatory Authority as a representative office”.
(2) For this rule, significant business document includes letterhead (whether issued by post, fax or electronic means), marketing material, business cards, and websites, but does not include with-compliments slips or text messages.
(3) The Regulatory Authority’s logo may be reproduced only with the Authority’s express written permission and in accordance with any conditions for the logo’s use that the Authority issues from time to time.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 2.2.3 Products or services that may not be marketed etc
doc_path: REPO 2.2.3 Products or services that may not be marketed etc
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
(1) A representative office must not provide information about, or market, a product or service unless the product or service falls within the description of a specified product or specified activity.
(2) To avoid doubt, a representative office must not provide information about or market a product or service that may not be lawfully marketed or provided in Qatar generally.
(3) A representative office must not market a financial product issued by, or a financial service provided by or on behalf of, a government or a non-commercial government entity.

Amended by QFCRA RM/2026-2 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 2.2.4 Marketing material
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
(1) In these rules:
marketing material means material communicated to a person in the course of providing information on financial services or financial products or making introductions or referrals.
(2) When marketing a financial product or financial service, a representative office must take reasonable care to ensure that the marketing material that it uses is clear, fair and not misleading.
(3) A representative office must ensure that any marketing material that it communicates to a person contains, in addition to either of the disclosures required by rule 2.2.2:
(a) the names of the representative office and the entity on behalf of which the marketing material is being communicated; and
(b) if the marketing material is directed to a particular class or category of person, clear statements to that effect and that no other person should act on it.
(4) The representative office must ensure that the marketing material contains in a prominent position, or has attached to it:
(a) a statement that clearly sets out the following:
(i) the name of the jurisdiction in which the relevant financial product or financial service is regulated and the legislation in that jurisdiction that applies to the product or service;
(ii) the name of the regulator that regulates the product or service;
(iii) the regulatory status of the product or service, according to that regulator; and
(b) the following warning:
Warning: This document is about a financial product [or service] that is not regulated nor approved by the Qatar Financial Centre Regulatory Authority. The Regulatory Authority is not responsible for reviewing or verifying any prospectus or other document in relation to this financial product [or service].
(5) A representative office must ensure that any document that contains information on past performance contains the following warning:
Warning: Past performance is not a reliable guide to future performance.
The warning must appear near the information on past performance, and may not be provided by way of a footnote.
(6) A representative office must not distribute marketing material for a financial product or financial service if it becomes aware that the entity that offers the product or service is in breach of a regulatory or legal requirement in relation to it.
(7) A representative office must take reasonable steps to ensure that no person uses its marketing material on its behalf in a way that contravenes this rule.
(8) Nothing in this rule applies to any material communicated in the course of any other regulated activity.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 2.2.5 No advertising of particular products or particular services
doc_path: REPO 2.2.5 No advertising of particular products or particular services
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
(1) A representative office must not advertise a particular financial product or a particular financial service.
(2) In subrule (1):
advertise means communicate in any medium (for example, brochure, telephone call, the internet, email and presentation) if the purpose or effect of the communication is:
(a) to promote:
(i) 1 or more financial products or financial services; or
(ii) a regulated activity (or an activity that would be a regulated activity if it was carried on in or from the QFC); or
(b) to invite or induce a person:
(i) to enter into an agreement with any person in relation to a financial product or financial service; or
(ii) to engage in a regulated activity (or an activity that would be a regulated activity if it were carried on in or from the QFC).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 3.1.1 Eligibility to apply for authorisation
doc_path: REPO 3.1.1 Eligibility to apply for authorisation
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
A person may apply for authorisation to operate a representative office only if the person is a body corporate that is:

(a) incorporated in a jurisdiction other than the QFC or the State; and

(b) regulated by a financial services regulator in a jurisdiction other than the QFC or the State, in a way that is substantially equivalent to the QFC regulatory framework.

Note The effect of rule 3.1.1 (a) is that the applicant must be registered in the QFC as a branch.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)
Amended by QFCRA RM/2026-2 (as from 1st May 2026).

Note The effect of rule 3.1.1 (a) is that the applicant must be registered in the QFC as a branch. QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 3.1.2 Application for authorisation
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
(1) An application for authorisation to operate a representative office must be in the approved form.

(2) The applicant must submit with the application:

(a) a business strategy;
(b) evidence from the financial services regulator responsible for the supervision of the applicant, that that financial services regulator has no objection to the establishment of the representative office in the QFC; and
(c) a statement of the applicant’s proposed principal place of business in the QFC.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)
Amended by QFCRA RM/2026-2 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 3.1.2 Guidance
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
In assessing an application for authorisation as a representative office, the Regulatory Authority will consider at least the following factors:

• the applicant’s business model, to ensure that the proposed activities are within the scope of the authorisation sought;
• the legal form of the applicant;
• the fitness and propriety of the applicant;
• the quality of regulation that applies to the applicant’s head office, and the substantial equivalence of that regulation to the QFC regulatory framework;
• the applicant’s financial standing;
• the applicant’s controllers;
• the applicant’s proposed principal place of business in the QFC, to be satisfied that the premises demonstrate a commitment to doing business in the QFC and are operational.

In deciding whether a firm in another jurisdiction is regulated in a substantially equivalent way, the Authority would look, in particular, at the home jurisdiction’s risk-based capital requirements and consolidated supervision. The Authority may also consider the capacity of the home regulator to enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Authority.

Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 3.1.2A Business strategy
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
(1) The business strategy must be in the form specified by the Regulatory Authority.

(2) The business strategy must include:

(a) the applicant’s short and long-term objectives with respect to operating in the QFC; and
(b) details of how the applicant’s objectives under paragraph (a) align with the QFC’s objectives and support Qatar’s broader economic objectives.

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 3.1.2B Approval of application
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
The Regulatory Authority may approve an application for authorisation to operate a representative office only if:

(a) the Regulatory Authority is satisfied that the applicant is eligible to apply for authorisation; and

(b) the applicant provides evidence satisfying the Regulatory Authority that:

(i) the financial services regulator responsible for the supervision of the applicant has no objection to the establishment of the representative office in the QFC;
(ii) the applicant’s business strategy aligns with the QFC’s objectives and Qatar’s broader economic objectives; and
(iii) the applicant is genuinely committed to doing business in the QFC.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-2 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 3.1.2B Guidance
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
In assessing an application for authorisation as a representative office, the Regulatory Authority considers factors including:

1. the applicant’s business model, to ensure that the proposed activities are within the scope of the authorisation sought;
2. the applicant’s business strategy;
3. the applicant’s legal form;
4. the applicant’s fitness and propriety;
5. the quality of regulation that applies to the applicant’s head office and the substantial equivalence of that regulation to the QFC regulatory framework;
6. the applicant’s financial standing;
7. the applicant’s controllers; and
8. the applicant’s proposed principal place of business in the QFC, to be satisfied that the premises demonstrate a commitment to doing business in the QFC and are operational.

In deciding whether a firm in a jurisdiction other than the QFC or the State is regulated in a way that is substantially equivalent to the QFC regulatory framework, the Regulatory Authority would look, in particular, at the risk-based capital and conduct of business requirements and the consolidated supervision of the applicant’s financial services regulator. The Regulatory Authority may also consider the capacity of the applicant’s financial services regulator, to enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Regulatory Authority.

Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-2 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 3.1.2C Two-year limit on authorisation
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
(1) If a firm is granted authorisation to operate a representative office on or before 1 May 2026, that authorisation is valid for a maximum of two years from 1 May 2026.
(2) If a firm is granted authorisation to operate a representative office after 1 May 2026, that authorisation is valid for a maximum of two years from the date authorisation is granted.
(3) To avoid doubt, a two-year authorisation period granted by the Regulatory Authority under these rules is non-renewable.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2026-2 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 3.1.3 Senior executive function
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
(1) The senior executive function for a representative office is the function of being responsible for the whole business of the office carried on in or from the QFC. That function is a controlled function for the purposes of FSR, article 41 (2).
(2) A representative office must have an individual who is approved to exercise the senior executive function for the office. The individual must be ordinarily resident in Qatar.
(3) To avoid any doubt, references to the senior executive function in the provisions of INDI that apply to a representative office apply to the senior executive function referred to in subrule (1).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 3.1.4 MLRO function
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
(1) The MLRO function for a representative office is the function of being responsible for overseeing compliance with the office’s responsibilities under the AML/CFT Law. That function is a controlled function for the purposes of FSR, article 41 (2).

(2) Subject to subrule (3), the individual who exercises the MLRO function for a representative office must be:

(a) the individual who exercises that function or an equivalent function in the office’s head office; or
(b) an individual who is ordinarily resident in Qatar.
(3) If the Regulatory Authority considers that the MLRO function for a representative office cannot be adequately exercised by an individual who is not resident in Qatar, the Authority may direct the office to appoint as MLRO an individual who is ordinarily resident in Qatar.

(4) To avoid any doubt, references to the MLRO function in the provisions of INDI that apply to a representative office apply to the MLRO function referred to in subrule (1).

Note INDI, Schedule 1, SI. 7.21 (which specifies the qualifications required of an individual who exercises the MLRO function), does not apply to the controlled function referred to in rule 3.1.4 – see rule 5.1.1 (i).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)
Amended by QFCRA RM/2026-2 (as from 1st May 2026).

doc_path: REPO 3.1.5 Representative offices not to hold money etc
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
A representative office must not hold or control money or property unless the money or property:

(a) is necessary to deal with its ordinary business operating expenses; and
(b) belongs to the representative office or the member of its corporate group that it represents.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 3.1.8 Information supplied to other regulators
doc_path: REPO 3.1.8 Information supplied to other regulators
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
If requested by the Regulatory Authority, a representative office must provide the Authority with information that it or another member of its corporate group has provided to a financial services regulator.

Note In common with all other authorised firms, representative offices must notify the Regulatory Authority of particular events under GENE, Chapter 4. Including, for example:

• changes to a firm’s basic details such as its name or business address (GENE, rule 4.1.1)
• significant matters that could adversely affect a firm’s solvency or reputation (GENE, rule 4.2.2)
• any fraud or significant accounting irregularity that relates to a firm (GENE, rule 4.2.3)
• certain actions taken against a firm by a regulator other than the Authority (GENE, rule 4.2.4)
• any solvency-related event that affects a firm (GENE, rule 4.2.6).
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)
Amended by QFCRA RM/2026-1 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 3.1.9 Records to include marketing material
doc_path: REPO 3.1.9 Records to include marketing material
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
The records that a representative office retains must include any marketing material issued, distributed or otherwise communicated by it or on its behalf.

Note 1 The general record-keeping obligations of an authorised firm are set out in GENE Chapter 6. The whole of GENE Chapter 6, applies to a representative office. In relation to records of AML/CFT matters, see rules 4.1.3 and 4.1.5.
Note 2 In relation to ownership information, see the particular record-keeping requirement in the QFCA Rules, rule 8A.17.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO Chapter 4 AML/CFT
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.content_text: REPO Chapter 4 AML/CFT

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 4.1.1 AML/CFT policy
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
(1) A representative office must have a written policy setting out how it will comply with the office’s obligations under the AML/CFT Law.
(2) The policy must include the office’s procedures, systems and controls. It must be risk-sensitive, appropriate and adequate having regard to the risk of money-laundering and terrorism financing and the size, complexity and nature of the office’s business.

(3) The policy must set out appropriate procedures for at least the following:

(a) screening procedures for the appointment or employment of officers and employees;
(b) the detection and reporting of suspicious transactions and the keeping of records, in accordance with the instructions issued by the FIU; and
(c) the detection and reporting of activity related to funds or a transaction or potential transaction which, if it involved an authorised firm, would constitute a suspicious transaction that the authorised firm would be required to report.

(4) The policy must also cover:

(a) communication of the policy to the office’s officers and employees; and
(b) anything else that is relevant and appropriate to the office’s activities and is required under the AML/CFT Law or these rules.
(5) A representative office may comply with this rule by using its head office’s AML/CFT policies, if those policies satisfy the requirements of this rule.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)
Amended by QFCRA RM/2026-2 (as from 1st May 2026).

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 4.1.2 AML/CFT training programme
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
(1) A representative office must design, deliver and maintain an appropriate AML/CFT training programme for its officers and employees.
(2) A representative office may comply with this rule by taking part in its head office’s AML/CFT training programme, if that programme satisfies the requirements of this rule.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 4.1.3 Reporting records to be made by MLRO
doc_path: REPO 4.1.3 Reporting records to be made by MLRO
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
The MLRO of a representative office must make and keep records of the details of each suspicious transaction report that the office makes to the FIU.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)

doc_path: REPO 4.1.4 Annual reports to Regulatory Authority
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO 4.1.5 How long AML/CFT records must be kept
doc_path: REPO 4.1.5 How long AML/CFT records must be kept
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
A record that is made by a representative office for the AML/CFT Law or this Chapter must be kept for at least 10 years after the day it is made.
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)

REPO 5.1.1 Disapplication of certain other provisions of Rules
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
The following Rules or provisions of Rules do not apply to a representative office:
(a)the Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism Rules 2019;
(b) the Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism (General Insurance) Rules 2019;
(c) the Banking Business Rules 2014;
(d) the Captive Insurance Business Rules 2011;
(e) the Collective Investment Schemes Rules 2010;
(f) the Customer and Investor Protection Rules 2019;
(g) GENE, Parts 1.2, 2.4 and 3.1 and Chapter 9;
(h) the Governance and Controlled Functions Rules 2020.
(i) INDI, Chapters 4 and 5 and Schedule 1, rule S1.7.21;
(j) the Insurance Mediation Business Rules 2014;
(k) the Investment Management and Advisory Rules 2014;
(l) the Islamic Banking Business Prudential Rules 2015;
(m) the Insurance Business Rules 2006;
(n) the Professional Investor Funds Rules 2022.
 
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)
Amended by QFCRA_RM2023-3 (as from 1st August 2023).

QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.title: REPO Glossary
QFCRA Rules :: Representative Office Rul.document_html:
(see rule 1.1.4)
AML/CFT Law means Law No. (20) of 2019 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing, and includes Regulations made under that Law.
authorisation means an authorisation granted under FSR, Part 5.
authorised firm means a person that has been granted an authorisation.
employee means an individual:
(a) who is employed or appointed by a person in connection with that person’s business, whether under a contract of service or for services or otherwise; or
(b) whose services, under an arrangement between that person and a third party, are placed at the disposal and under the control of that person.
entity means a body corporate or partnership or un-incorporated association carrying on a trade or business with a view to profit.
financial services regulator means a regulator of financial services in a jurisdiction other than the QFC.
FIU means the Financial Intelligence Unit established under the AML/CFT Law.
FSR means the Financial Services Regulations.
GENE means the General Rules 2005.
INDI means the Individuals (Assessment, Training and Competency) Rules 2014.
marketing a financial product or financial service means doing either or both of the following:
(a) providing general information on the availability of the product or service;
(b) making introductions or referrals in connection with the offer of the product or service.
marketing material has the meaning given by rule 2.2.4 (1).
operating a representative office has the meaning given by rule 1.1.5 (2).
person means:
(a) an individual (including an individual occupying an office or position from time to time); or
(b) a legal person.
Qatar means the State of Qatar including the QFC.
QFC means the Qatar Financial Centre.
regulated activity has the meaning given by FSR, article 23.
Regulatory Authority means the Regulatory Authority of the QFC.
representative office means an authorised firm that has an authorisation to conduct the regulated activity of operating a representative office.
specified activity has the meaning given by FSR, article 110.
specified product has the meaning given by FSR, article 110.
State means the State of Qatar excluding the QFC. 
Derived from QFCRA RM/2020-5 (as from 1st October 2020)
Amended by QFCRA RM/2026-2 (as from 1st May 2026).
